# House terminology in the v3 manuscript: dictionary

**Status:** regenerated on 25 November 2026 against the converted text (the fork branch `claude/v3-terminology-dictionary` after its third review). Until then this file described the manuscript as it stood before the vocabulary conversion (commit `4f462ac5`); that version is in the history of this file. Later the same day the entries were brought up to date with the 125 lines changed by commits `c5bd232d`, `d869e433` and `080d934e` (sentence repairs, chapter 11 adapted to the average over the forests, the polynomial route of 17c; decisions in Appendix J of the records file, "Decisions of 25 November 2026"). **Updated on 27 November 2026** against the text after the merge of upstream `275862c2` (commit `4ad8a726`, with the merge corrections of the same day) and the decisions of 26 November 2026 (titles, defining sentences, coined terms, definitions from the sources, the seventeen further titles with the body), all as recorded in `audit/merge-2026-11-26.md`. The line references were first remapped by a script from the text of `a74c610b` to the current text, using a diff-based line map; the entries named in that record and the entries whose word counts changed were then checked by grep against the current text and corrected, and 16 entries were added for the new terms. A reference whose sentence was rewritten by upstream and is not among these may still point a few lines off. **Scope:** all chapter files under `chapters/`, plus `main-theorem.tex` and `reading-guide.tex` (not `notation-index.tex`, which was converted separately on 26 November 2026). Line numbers are those of the current text; upstream's merge changed the line count of the files, so they are no longer those of upstream commit `7bec3925`.

**Purpose.** The manuscript uses many words as technical terms that are not standard mathematical vocabulary. This file lists them alphabetically, one entry per term for the whole book. Each entry states what the term means in the text, where it occurs, on what basis the meaning is given, and a proposed standard equivalent. It extends the translation table in `blueprint/notation.md`.

- [Dictionary](#dictionary): 1433 entries, A to Z. 152 carry a term introduced by the conversion or by the decisions of 26 November 2026 as headword, with the former house word under *Formerly*; 589 are pointers (a former word pointing to its successor, a new term pointing to the entries of the words it replaced, or a variant). Added on 27 November 2026: 16 entries for the terms of the decisions of 26 November 2026 and of upstream's merge, each marked "*Now:* new on 26 November 2026" (all in pointer form, 14 of them with the former word under *Formerly*).
- [Appendix A](#appendix-a). How the vocabulary is distributed over the book.
- [Appendix B](#appendix-b). Concepts with several names.
- [Appendix C](#appendix-c). Symbols with several meanings, and symbols used without definition.
- [Appendix D](#appendix-d). Damaged sentences.
- [Appendix E](#appendix-e). Jargon in label names.
- [Appendix F](#appendix-f). Equivalents that must not be used, and three that need a mathematician.
- [Appendix G](#appendix-g). Terms whose meaning the text does not determine.
- [Appendix H](terminology-records.md#appendix-h). Open questions. In the companion file [terminology-records.md](terminology-records.md).
- [Appendix I](#appendix-i). Method and limits.

- [Appendix L](terminology-records.md#appendix-l). Names in the papers of Bałaban and Dimock. In the companion file [terminology-records.md](terminology-records.md).

## How to read an entry

- **Headword and variants.** Compound forms and spelling variants that mean the same thing are listed under *Variants*. A term that is only a variant of another has a pointer entry ("See …").
- **Now, Formerly, In the text.** Every entry records what the converted text does with the term. *Now: unchanged* — it stands as before. *Now: replaced by …* or *partly replaced by …* — the term that stands in its place, and the lines where the old word remains. *Now: removed* — the word was deleted without a successor. *Now: not applied* — the entry proposed a change and the text still has the old term. Where a house word was replaced everywhere by one new term, the entry stands under the new term, with the old word under *Formerly* and the present wording under *In the text*; the old word keeps a pointer entry. Where the replacement differs by sense or place, the entry stays under the old word and each new term has a pointer entry ("Stands in the text where these former terms stood").
- **Adopted, Proposed.** *Adopted*: the equivalent is now in the text. *Proposed*: it is not, or only in part.
- **Senses.** A term with one meaning has a single *Meaning* paragraph. A term whose meaning changes has numbered senses, each with its own references.
- **Basis.** **D**: the text defines the term at the cited line. **R**: the meaning is read off an explicit sentence or formula. **I**: inferred from context; check before using the proposed equivalent. **?**: the text does not determine the meaning. **S**: the v3 text does not determine the meaning; it is taken from the manuscripts v3 was written from, or from the Lean definition, cited under *Source*.
- **Literature.** Present where the object was found in papers of Bałaban or Dimock: the name and symbol used there, with paper and page (abbreviations in Appendix L of the records file), how close the match is, and what would make the literature's name misleading here. The papers were read in part, often from an OCR text layer; Appendix L of the records file states the coverage.
- **Source.** Present where the meaning was traced beyond the v3 text. "Scott" is `manuscript/HumanizeYM_v2/`, "Martin" is `manuscript/existence/`. Lean declarations are cited by fully qualified name and path in the formal source at revision `3456e5e75cf8d4cd558955a5c7638fba2d68f464`; "(definition read)" or "(statement read)" means the declaration was read as source text and matched to the manuscript on its formulas. Nothing was elaborated or built, and Lean identifiers are not mathematical words, so a name alone is never evidence.
- **Where.** References are `chapter:line`. Counts are occurrences in prose, with label names stripped.
- **Proposed.** The standard equivalent, the same for the whole book. "Keep, define once" means the term should stay with one definition; "delete" means the word carries no content. Proposals rest on the agents' general mathematical knowledge and were not checked against the literature.
- **Across chapters.** Says whether the term has one sense throughout, where the meaning changes, and which readings were rejected. "(text read)" marks lines opened during the last revision to decide between conflicting readings.

**File abbreviations.** `1` 01-lattice, `2` 02-observables, `2e` 02-equation-section, `3` 03-maxwell, `4` 04-blocking, `5` 05-gaussian, `6` 06-large-fields, `7` 07-matching, `8` 08-polymers, `9` 09-renormalization, `9s` 09-stationary-remainder, `10` 10-common-trajectory, `11` 11-marked-insertions, `11R` 11-restarted-history, `11E` 11-equation-calibration, `12` 12-ultraviolet-limit, `13` 13-continuum-fields, `13sb` 13-sharp-bounds, `13ba` 13-bounded-approximations, `18gq` 18-graded-quotient, `18lp` 18-lattice-products, `14` 14-reflection-ward, `14lc` 14-lattice-comparison, `15` 15-phases, `15sp` 15-sharp-phase-bounds, `16` 16-reconstruction, `17` 17-trace-law, `17w` 17-variable-windows, `17t` 17-trace-transfer, `17c` 17-current-contraction, `17m` 17-marked-trace-rates, `18` 18-operator-products, `18r` 18-raw-replacement, `19` 19-assembly, `MT` main-theorem, `RG` reading-guide. The files `18gq` and `18lp` are input from chapter 13. The draft `chapters/09-forest-average.tex`, input into chapter 9, is cited as `9f` (in a few entries by its file name or as `FA`).

**Book-wide word choices.** Decided by the author on 23 November 2026 (issue 1 of the fork): Bałaban's vocabulary is adopted wherever the object is the same; where v3's construction differs, his name is kept and the difference stated at first use. These choices are applied in the *Proposed* fields.

| Object | Word |
|---|---|
| lattice spacing `a_m`; the integer `m` | *scale*; *scale index `m`* (Bałaban, B87 p. 256). His index `k` runs the other way: `k = 0` is the finest lattice |
| one block transformation | *step*; at first use "renormalization transformation, called a step" |
| the stationary field `ρ(v)` | *critical configuration* (Bałaban's "minimal configuration" where a minimum is proved; in v3 a stationary point of action plus penalty) |
| a configuration about which one expands, or in which operators are differentiated | *background field* |
| the Gaussian integration variables of one step | *fluctuation field* |
| the operator `W` | *the linearization `W` of the critical configuration*, naming the representative: `W_s` (straight average), `W_a` (smooth), `W_F` (forest). The derivative of the stationary substitution is `W_F`; chapter 17 computes with `W_a`, which differs from it by a fine gradient (17c:49–54, as reworded on 24 November 2026), and, for the exact Taylor-order statement, passes on to `W_s` (17c:56–69, rewritten on 25 November 2026). Write the representative wherever `W` is unqualified: `W_s` at 5:527–535, `W_F` at 11:642 |
| failure of a smooth cutoff on a small-field region | *large fluctuation-field event*, against the *large-field* set proper. Bałaban makes the same split (large plaquette fields, large fluctuation fields), as chapter 6 does (6:7–11) |
| tree gauge, tree slice | *axial gauge* (*block axial gauge*) |
| small-field condition | *regularity condition* on the plaquette variables |
| regular activity | *localized term* of the regular part of the action, on a *localization domain* |
| block average | *averaging operation* (nonlinear, an analogue of Bałaban's `Ū`); *linear averaging operator* (`M`) |
| gauge completion | *gauge-fixing term* |
| route | *contour*; *contour variable* |
| reset | *coupling constant renormalization*; *vacuum energy renormalization* |
| first expansion; second cluster expansion | *Mayer expansion*; *exponentiation* (*exponentiated cluster expansion*) |
| the constant `b` | *the penalty parameter `b`* (MT:12). Bałaban's gauge papers have a delta function instead; the penalty term of chapter 7 is a different object |
| the choice of orders, exponents, widths and bounds of 10:25 | *stage `j`*, for this only, and not called a "regularity class": "regular" is kept for the regular part of the action and for the regularity condition. No counterpart in Bałaban; in Dimock "stage" means a step |
| extraction of the local polynomial part of an insertion (chapter 11) | *the localization operator* (*Taylor localization*). Bałaban's sense of the word appears only in *localized term* and *localization domain*; he calls v3's operation imposing renormalization conditions |
| number of box convolutions in the averaging weight | *smoothing order `j`* (4:16); not "order", which in Bałaban counts composed steps |
| the other fields in a correlation | *spectators*, defined once |
| family of functionals separating fields | *separating family* |
| "unit" | *identity field* |
| moving a density, coefficient or current through the block steps | *transfer* |
| "history" (11:18–19) | kept, defined once; not "trajectory" or "schedule". *Restarted history* for the one with the coupling frozen below the comparison scale |
| the index `d` of `V_d` | *filtration index `d`* (the name in `blueprint/notation.md`); not "tag", which is the random index in chapters 4–11 |
| the algebra `𝔄` | *compression algebra* |
| the identity of 9:653–669 | *exact regrouping*, cited by number |
| index neighbourhood on which a matrix is inverted (6:525–532) | *window `Ω_i`*, for this sense only |
| a lattice path along which links are multiplied; the product | *contour*; *contour variable*. *Holonomy* for a closed contour only; *path* only in "path action", "path coefficients" and for paths merely counted |
| spelling | American, as in the manuscript (renormalization, normalization, localization, neighborhood) |
| "graph" (11:379–382; 12:82–95) | kept: the graph transform of invariant-manifold theory |

## Dictionary

### A

#### absorb
*Now:* not applied; the verb stands at all its places, also where no inequality is displayed.
- **Meaning.** "Is bounded using a spare factor": a constant or error factor is dominated by slack kept in another factor of the same estimate ("The first term absorbs the coefficient and small-field remainder", 11:943; "The difference of the exponents, `19/16 − 23/20 = 3/80`, absorbs the remaining subpower factor", 9:191).
  *Basis:* I (11:219, 296, 322, 420). *Where:* 5:1284; ch. 6, 15 (6:250–1482); ch. 7, 7; 8:322, 334; ch. 9, 6 (among them 9:191); ch. 10, 8; ch. 11, 16; 11R, 3; 11E, 0 (examples 11:219, 296, 322, 420, 943, 1619); 12:282; 13sb:62, 93; 18gq, 3; 18lp, 6; ch. 17–19 (lines not listed). *Proposed:* *is bounded by*; keep the verb only where the inequality that does the absorbing is displayed.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout; ordinary usage in analysis, listed because chapters 10–11 use it in place of the inequality.
*See also:* reserve; cost; gain; loss.

#### absorbing the larger source weight
*Formerly:* *weight restoration*.
*In the text:* (title 11:1380; 17w:89) and by the lemma titles "Regular remainders at the larger source weight" (11:1442) and "Large-field activities at the larger source weight" (11:1477); the label `ch11:weight-restoration` is unchanged. Since 26 November 2026 "larger source weight" is glossed at its first use: "a larger source weight (the weight `ω` of the source variables in place of `ω_−`, Section ch11:weight-restoration)" (11:29).
*Variants:* absorbing the larger source weight; larger source weight; no longer in the text: regular weight restoration; large-field weight restoration; regular-restoration bounds; restored weight.
- **Meaning.** The passage from a bound at the source weight `ω_−` and exponent `e+2` to one at the larger source weight `ω = H^U ω_−` and smaller exponent `e` (11:1386–1394, 1442–1448). Subsection "Absorbing the larger source weight" (11:1380–1381, label `ch11:weight-restoration`) with the lemmas "Regular remainders at the larger source weight" (11:1442) and "Large-field activities at the larger source weight" (11:1477); "Lemma (ch11:restore-regular) therefore gives `H^{-1}`" (11:2136).
  *Basis:* R (11:1386–1394, 1442–1448). *Where:* 11:1380–1596 (lemmas at 11:1442, 1477), 2131; 17w:89 ("Absorbing the larger source weight"), 93 ("bounds of Lemma (ch11:restore-regular)"). *Proposed:* *change of the source weight from `ω_−` to `ω`*.
*Across chapters:* one sense; chapter 17 cites the chapter 11 lemmas.
*See also:* weight.

#### accumulated noise
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* no longer in the text: suffix noise.
- **Meaning.** The propagated contribution of the Gaussian term `b^{-1/2}ξ` of the block kernel: "The independent noise introduced at step `h` is propagated only through the subsequent, coarser steps `h+1,…,n`" (5:378–379).
  *Basis:* R (5:378–379). *Where:* 5:280, 377–379, 775, 778. *Proposed:* as for *noise* (sense 1).
*Across chapters:* chapter 5; a compound of *noise*.
*See also:* noise.

#### action-gradient terms
*Now:* replaced by *derivatives of the actions* (decision of 26 November 2026, 17t: subsection title 17t:289 "Cancellation of the derivatives of the actions"; 17t:335 "both derivatives of the actions"; 17t:405 "the derivatives of the actions in (ch17:contact)"; 17t:476 "The derivative of the action `DS[Z_b′]`") (grep).
- **Meaning.** The two terms `DΓ[Y]` and `DS[Z]` on the right of the contact identity (17.contact), `½ tr(R D²(DS[Y])) − div_Haar Y = DΓ[Y] − μ² tr(RV) + DS[Z]` (17t:236–238); generically `DF[Z]`, the derivative of a gauge-invariant action `F` (here `S` or `Γ`) in the direction of a gauge-covariant vector field `Z` with a base point (17t:297–302, 402–403).
  *Basis:* R (17t:335, 403–405, 476). *Where:* 17t:289 (title), 335, 405, 476. *Adopted:* *derivatives of the actions* (decision of 26 November 2026; the dictionary had proposed *the terms `DS[Z]`, `DΓ[Y]`*).
*Across chapters:* one sense; chapter 17 only.

#### active coordinates
*Now:* not applied; the term is kept and glossed at 6:448 ("*Active* coordinates, the integration variables, are logarithms (Lie-algebra coordinates) of the remaining non-tree links").
*Variants:* inactive coordinates; active / inactive (Haar) variables.
- **Meaning.** The logarithms of the non-tree links outside the `10B`-neighbourhood, that is, the variables over which the step integrates; the inactive ones are held fixed ("after the inactive Haar variables have been frozen", 9:72–73).
  *Basis:* D (6:448). *Where:* 6:448; 9:51, 58, 72–73. *Proposed:* *integration variables*; *variables held fixed*.
*Literature:* see *free* (the non-tree links) and *logarithm* (the coordinates relative to `rep V`).
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 6 and 9.
*See also:* dummy Gaussian coordinates.

#### activity
*Now:* partly replaced by *localized term* (the regular activity of sense 1); remains, as adopted, for the large-field activity (4:484), for the polymer activity of sense 2 (8:288; 9:89) and in *activity array* (10:424, glossed there as "the family of localized terms and large-field activities"; since 26 November 2026 also glossed at its first use, 10:6).
*Variants:* activities; large-field activity; polymer activity; activity array; no longer in the text: regular activity.
1. **Term of the local representation of a density (chapters 4, 9–13, 17).** One of the local terms by which a density is represented, of two kinds (Definition "Localized terms and large-field activities", 4:476–495). A localized term (formerly regular activity) is a triple `(X_i, o_i, E_i^reg)`: a localization domain, a base point and a real Borel gauge-invariant function local on `X_i`; it enters the exponent additively. A large-field activity has an exclusion support `Y_i`, a nonempty prescribed large-field set `I_i^bad ⊂ Y_i`, an additional condition, an event `𝓔_i^extra`, and a value `K_i^lf`. The localized terms are not polymer activities. "Here `x_m` is the activity array, the family of localized terms and large-field activities" (10:424).
   *Basis:* D (4:476–495). *Where:* 4:477–494, 496, 597; 9:133, 869 ("localized term"); 10:424; 12:33 ("arrays of localized terms and large-field activities"), 70–77; 13ba:151–152; chapter 17 through `E_reg`. *Adopted:* *large-field activity*, defined in chapter 4; *localized term* (of the regular part of the action) for the regular one.
2. **Polymer activity (chapter 8, parts of chapter 9).** The activity `z_γ` of a polymer in the gas, the standard sense: "In addition to the polymer activities `z_γ`, introduce large-field activities `K_η` with supports `Y_η` and nonempty sets `I_η ⊂ D ∩ Y_η`" (8:288–290). The "rescaled activities" (8:171; 9:181), the "source-dependent activities" (8:271, 367) and the "polymer activities of the Mayer expansion" (9:88–89) are of this kind.
   *Basis:* R (8:288–290). *Where:* 8:171–172, 271, 288–290, 321–336, 367; 9:88–89, 149–154, 181. *Adopted:* *polymer activity* (standard).
*Literature:* **activities** of a **polymer expansion** (B88a p. 14: "Thus finally we obtain the polymer expansion … If the activities H(Z) of the above polymer expansion are sufficiently small, then the polymer expansion can be exponentiated according to the well-known formula"; B89b pp. 387–388, (1.90)–(1.91): "the activities `F(X')`"). Sense 2 (the polymer activity `z_γ`) is the same object; the incompatibility relation is Bałaban's function `ζ(Z,Z′)` (B88a p. 14: "ζ(Z,Z′) = 0 if Z ∩ Z′ contains a cube, or a wall of a cube, and ζ(Z,Z′) = 1 otherwise"). Dimock does not use the word: his **M-polymers** are connected unions of `M`-cubes, class `D_k`, with "small polymers" and "large polymers" (D1 pp. 1330010-17, -22), and he has no gas language; v3's supports need not be connected. For sense 1 the word is a name clash with the literature: what v3 calls a regular activity Bałaban calls a localized term (see *regular activity*), and the large-field activity is an operation `T_k(X)` (see *large-field activities*). Adopted (23 November 2026): *polymer activity* for sense 2; in sense 1 the regular activity becomes *localized term* (see *regular activity*), and "activity" remains v3's word for the large-field one only, to be said once.
*Across chapters:* the large-field activities are the same objects in both senses (4:484–487; 8:288–295). The regular ones are not, and now carry different names: in chapter 8 the polymer activity `z_γ` (8:288), in chapters 4 and 9 the localized term, an additive term of the exponent; chapter 9 says "polymer gas" (9:151) and "small-field polymers", "small-field factor" (9:154, 173). 4:496 states that "activity" for the large-field terms is particular to the book. Text read at 4:476–496 and 8:287–291; the conflict is recorded under *regular activity*.
*See also:* regular activity; large-field activities; array; inflated activities; source-deformed activities; preliminary large-field activities; prescribed set of large-field sites; first expansion; density coordinates.

#### activity arrays
*Now:* unchanged; since 25 November 2026 also at 10:6, where it replaces "coefficient arrays" (decision 45), and since 26 November 2026 glossed there: "a consistent choice of activity arrays (the families of localized terms and large-field activities)" (10:6).
See *array*.

#### actual
*Now:* partly replaced by *non-flat* (sense 2); *averaging operation* (sense 3); *the inverse coupling `β`* (sense 4; "the coupling `β`" until 25 November 2026); *original* (sense 9); *modified metric* (sense 10); deleted without successor in most places of senses 1, 5, 6 and 8; remains at 6:1168 ("actually"); 9s:307 ("actual-sector inputs"); 11:415, 558, 1164, 1619. #### actual stationary tangent
*Now:* replaced by *linearization of the critical configuration* (written `W`; its smooth representative `W_a`, sense 1; its representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge, sense 2).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: actual tangent; actual smooth tangent (7:1055); smooth actual lift (9s:194–196); actual stationary pullback (17t:160); actual response (17m:193).
1. **The operator `W_a = W_s − d_{0,f} E R W_s`,** the smooth representative of the derivative of the stationary map ("The smooth representative of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration is `W_a` from (ch05:corrected-transport); its representative in the block axial gauge is `W_F`", 7:583; "The smooth representative of the linearization of the critical configuration is `W_a = W_s − d_f E R W_s`", 17m:263–264).
   *Basis:* R (7:583; 17m:263–264; symbol defined 5:1118). *Where:* 7:583, 1056 ("the smooth representative `W_a`"); 9s:196 ("smooth representative `W_a`"), 230; 17m:193 ("the linearization of the critical configuration"), 263. *Adopted:* *the smooth representative `W_a` of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration*. The derivative of the critical configuration with respect to the coarse field is `W_F` (sense 2).
   *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:386–390` "`W_r = W_s − d_f I_ℓ(𝓕_m W_s)` … We take `W_0 = W_r`" (v3's `W_a`, with `I_ℓ = E`, `𝓕_m = R`); `B-section.tex:473` "retain `W_0` for the smooth free interpolation before axial gauge". No Lean declaration corresponding to `W_a` was found (not searched exhaustively).
2. **The derivative of the stationary substitution (17c:49–51), which is the forest representative `W_F`.** "The first derivative of the nonlinear critical-configuration map, from coarse to fine link variables with block ratio `L`, is the forest representative `W_F` of (ch05:stationary-tangent) … Since `W_F − W_a` is a fine gradient, the Ward identities of `E_b` allow us to compute with the smooth representative `W = W_a`" (17c:49–54). The composition with the critical configuration is `𝓘F = F(U_stat(V))` (17t:31), so the derivative is `D U_stat(0)`. The critical configuration is constructed in the block axial chart, where its derivative is `W_F`: `rep v + ι_F Dρ(0)v = W_F v` (5.stationary-tangent, 5:1157–1160); "Let `𝒰(x) = 𝒟_x(ρ(x))` be the critical configuration as a physical fine field. Its linearization is the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge" (9s:193–194). It is not `W_a`: `W_a` differs from `W_F` by a fine gradient `d_{0,f}φ` with `φ = 0` at the block roots (5:1149–1153), which is why chapter 17c may compute with `W_a`: "Recall that `W = W_a` is the smooth representative; the quadratic Ward identities annihilate its gradient difference from `W_F`" (17c:113–114).
   *Basis:* D for the derivative of the critical-configuration map, which the text states to be `W_F` (17c:49–51); R that the derivative of the critical configuration in the block axial chart is `W_F` (5:1157–1160), and that `W_F` is its representative in the block axial gauge (9s:193–194); S for the statement that the field `U_stat` of chapter 17 is that field. *Where:* 17c:8 ("the linearization of the critical configuration"), 48 ("the forest representative `W_F`"), 112; 11:642 ("the linearization `W` of the critical configuration, taken in its representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge"). *Adopted:* *the linearization `W_F` of the critical configuration, that is, the derivative of the critical-configuration map `ρ` with respect to the coarse field (5.stationary-tangent)*; in `17-current-contraction.tex` the computation uses its smooth representative `W_a`, and the representative is written wherever `W` is unqualified there.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:162` "For Lemma B3's stationary background `U_stat(V)`, stationary substitution is `𝓘F(V) = F(U_stat(V))`"; `part2/B-section.tex:473` "Write `W_ax v = (v, Dψ(0)v)` for the axial tangent, and retain `W_0` for the smooth free interpolation before axial gauge. They are distinct coordinate representatives"; `B-section.tex:483` (Lemma B3(ii)) "`rep v + ι_ax Dψ(0)v` is the tree representative of `W_0 v`". Lean, in `YM/PREC/TreeMatch.lean`: `YM.Precision.extracted S F W := W + d 0 f * straighten S F W` (definition read); `YM.Precision.stays` (statement and proof read: `extracted` vanishes on every tree link); `YM.Precision.Inputs` (definition read: `K H * W = (mean S)ᵀ * K H'`, `mean S * W = 1 − penalty⁻¹ • K H'`, the two identities of 5:1097 for `W_s`); `YM.Precision.stationed` (statement and proof read: under `Inputs`, `probe * extracted = 1 − penalty⁻¹ • K H'` and `K H * extracted = probeᵀ * K H'`, with `probe = mean + d 0 c * fixRoot` in `YM/PREC/FrameResponse.lean`, definition read). In `YM/PCalc/Chart.lean`: `YM.Precision.Critical` and `YM.Precision.Guessed` (definitions read: `ρ` is an analytic germ with `ρ 0 = 0` at which the derivative in the forest-chart variable of path action plus penalty vanishes; `Guessed B W ρ` says `d/dt ρ(t x)|₀ = extracted S B W x − linearCopy x`, componentwise in the colour index). `YM.Work.F04.tangent`, `YM/Work/F04.lean` (statement read; proof not read): `fderiv ρ 0 x = relative H U x` under `Inputs`, `PriceGap`, `Comptroller`, `Critical`. `YM.Stationary.encamp`, `YM/Next/STATIONARY/Joint/Gauge.lean`, and `inheritJ fₛ V := fₛ (encamp F r (content V)).1`, `YM/TraceExtension/Perfect/Desktop.lean` (definitions read): a fine function composed with the stationary configuration in the forest chart.
   Established by these readings: the Lean operator `extracted S F W` is `W` plus a fine gradient, vanishes on the forest, satisfies the two stationarity identities with `probe`, and is the derivative at zero of the stationary germ in the forest chart; Scott states the same for `U_stat` (tree representative of `W_0`). Inferred, by agreement of formulas and not from a Lean statement: that the Lean matrix `W` of `Inputs` is v3's `W_s`; that `extracted S F W_s` is v3's `W_F` (both are `W_s` plus a fine gradient, vanish on tree links, and have site potential `−R W_s` at the block roots: Lean lemma `centers`, v3 5:1118 with `E h(Ly) = h(y)`; the Lean structure `Forest` was not read); that Scott's "axial"/"tree" is v3's "forest"; and that `inheritJ` formalises the `𝓘` of 17t:31.
*Across chapters:* the symbols are used consistently in chapters 5, 7 and 17 (`W_s` "the operator `W` built with the linear averaging operator `M`", 5:1094; `W_a`, 5:1118; `W_F` "the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge", 5:1161, 7:583); the phrase is now the same everywhere: the linearization `W` of the critical configuration, with its two representatives named (7:583; 17m:263; 17c:8, 49–54; 11:642). 5:1246 states the relation: "`W_a` is the smooth representative of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration, whereas `W_F` is its representative in the block axial gauge". Three operators are to be kept apart; they differ pairwise by fine gradients and have the same curl: `W_s` (straight average; satisfies the identities with `M`), `W_a` (smooth; satisfies them with `𝒬 = M + d_{0,c}R`), `W_F` (zero on tree links; satisfies them with `𝒬`; the derivative of the critical configuration). `W_F` is called "the forest representative" at 17c:50 and "the representative in the block axial gauge" at 5:1161, 1246; 6:954; 7:583; 9s:194; 11:642. `blueprint/notation.md` line 242 ("the actual forest-coordinate response `W_a`") is wrong against 5:1161–1162, 9s:194–196 and the Lean definition: the forest-coordinate operator is `W_F`. The text of 17c:49–54 states the relation that Scott `B-section.tex:473` states: the derivative is the forest representative `W_F`, `W_F − W_a` is a fine gradient, and the computation uses `W = W_a`.
*See also:* actual; block bridge; bridge legs; stationary tangent; `𝒰_F`.

#### adjacent pair
*Now:* replaced by *two consecutive scales* (sense 1); *stage pair* (sense 2, defined at 10:30); the old word remains at 11:663 and 11R:252 ("adjacent pair"), 11R:40 ("adjacent stage pair"), 11:642–643 ("the adjacent Gaussian identities"), 11:737 ("adjacent quadratic identities") and 17c:239 ("adjacent-stage cases"), outside the chapters revised for this entry.
*Variants:* adjacent stage pair (11R:40); adjacent-stage cases (17c:239); no longer in the text: adjacent pair of scales; adjacent pair of stages (5:689); adjacent quadratic pair (6:953; 9:914); permitted adjacent pairs (10:30, 126).
1. **The two levels of one step.** The fine and the coarse scale of one renormalisation step, with the data attached to them: "Fix two consecutive scales, with fine scale `m+1` and coarse scale `m`" (9:15); "We work at two consecutive scales, the fine scale `m+1` and the coarse scale `m`" (6:13). The former "adjacent quadratic pair" (6:953; 9:914) is the pair of free quadratic forms of these two levels (the fine and coarse curvature metrics with their kinetic forms), related by the transport identities of chapter 5: "Use the quadratic forms of the two consecutive scales as in (ch06:flat-identities)" (6:953–954), where "For the selected quadratic data these identities follow from the transport and positive-defect identities of Chapter 5"; "the compatible untruncated quadratic identities of the two consecutive scales" (6:1560–1561); "Fix the free quadratic forms of two consecutive scales, with the positive metrics, exact transport identities and the gauge-covariant averaging operation of Chapter 5" (9:914–916).
   *Basis:* R (9:15); R (6:953–954, 1560–1561; 9:914–916) for the quadratic forms. *Where:* "two consecutive scales" at 6:13, 953, 1561; 7:589, 838; 9:15, 914; "pair of consecutive scales" at 9:964. *Adopted:* *two consecutive scales* (*fine scale `m+1`, coarse scale `m`*); *the free quadratic forms of two consecutive scales*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/C-section.tex:83` "Lemma B2 gives the exact adjacent free relation and the row factor `ρ_{N,m}`".
2. **The stages of the two levels of one step.** The pair `(J(m+1), J(m))` of the stage of the fine level and the stage of the coarse level. Since the stage is constant on plateaus and increases by one at a transition, a step involving stage `j` has one of finitely many stage pairs (`(j,j)`, or `j` together with a neighbouring stage): "At a fixed stage there are only finitely many permitted *stage pairs* (the stages of the two scales of one step). Choose constants for all these pairs simultaneously" (10:29–31); "the largest smoothing order used in stage `j` or a permitted stage pair" (10:125–126); "For each pair of stages of one step (Section (ch10:choices)) choose the coarse modification large enough for its finitely many incoming possibilities" (5:689–690).
   *Basis:* D (10:30); R (5:689–690). *Where:* 5:689 ("pair of stages of one step"); 10:28–31, 126 ("stage pair"); 13ba:264 ("permitted stage pairs"); the chapter 17 uses of "adjacent-stage cases" are listed under *stage*. *Adopted:* *the pair of stages `(J(m+1), J(m))` of a step* (*stage pair*).
   *Source:* Martin `existence/restarted-rank-history.tex:464–466` "Consider the step from the fine level `m+1` to the coarse level `m` … with stage pair `(J(m+1), J(m))`"; `:497–500` "each for its own stage pair, which is one of `(r,r)`, `(r,r−1)` and `(r−1,r−1)`"; `:734` "For the three possible adjacent stage pairs"; `existence/common-scale-selection.tex:65–66` "For each fixed stage `j > j_*` there are only finitely many entry and comparison bounds". Scott `part2/E-section.tex:142` "Include both adjacent stages at a transition."
*Across chapters:* the word paired the two levels of one step throughout; in chapters 5 and 10 what is paired is their stages. 9:15 names the two scales in passing and is not a definition. "Adjacent stage pair" and "adjacent-stage cases" are compounds of *stage*. Whether "permitted" at 10:30 restricts the stage pairs further (for instance to those that occur in the schedule of 10:118–135) is not said in v3 or in the sources read.
*See also:* stage; step.

#### admissible
*Now:* partly replaced by *majorant admitted in the infimum* (sense 6, 12:80) and by the stated condition (sense 9, 14lc:23, see *admissible comparison depth*); deleted in sense 5 (10:215, "The coupling band at scale `m`") and sense 7 (13sb:27, 36); remains, as proposed, in senses 1–4 and 8 and at 17m:72.
*Variants:* admitted; permitted; allowed (chapters 3–6 use the four words interchangeably: 3:1020, 1081; 5:281, 693, 1051, 1144, 1339, 1398; 6:633, 1102, 1114, 1425).
1. **Comparison coefficient / coefficient family (ch. 11, 13).** "A comparison coefficient is admissible when its inverse coordinates under `𝖹_{N,p,d}` have a uniform subpower bound" (11:887–889); "Call a coefficient family `z_i` admissible here if `‖X_i^{-1}z_i‖_1` is bounded by a sequence subpower in `a_N^{-1}`" (11:1106–1107), uniformly in `p`. The "admissible reference labels of the trials" of 13:396 belong to this sense: 11:1079–1080 gives "the reference label `v_{N,p}` of the trial, with subpower cutoff-scale coordinates", and 13:241 says "The backward comparison yields admissible coefficients".
   *Basis:* D (11:887–889, where "cutoff-scale coordinates" is now defined; 11:1106–1107); R for 13:396 (11:1079–1080 with 13:241). *Where:* 11:887–889, 1106–1110, 2258, 2316–2329; 13:217, 221, 241, 396. *Adopted:* keep, define once (*family whose inverse terminal coordinates grow subpolynomially in `a_N^{-1}`*).
2. **Graph (ch. 12).** A linear map `G : V_d → 𝓡_m` with `‖Gx‖ ≤ s_m‖x‖_1` (12:82–83); "admissible remainder graph" is used at 12:37, 45 lines before the definition.
   *Basis:* D (12:82–83). *Where:* 12:37, 82, 89, 97 (twice), 140. *Proposed:* keep, define before first use (12:37 still precedes the definition).
3. **Separated test function at volume `p`.** "Admissible at volume `p` if its support is contained in `((−R_p/2, R_p/2)^4)^n`" (1:359–361); "admissible period cell" (12:377) refers to this.
   *Basis:* D (1:359–361). *Where:* 1:359–361; 12:377. *Adopted:* keep.
4. **Curvature coordinate, for a link `e`.** Neither its plaquette nor its path uses `e`.
   *Basis:* D (2e:62–67). *Where:* 2e:66–67, 71, 104. *Adopted:* keep.
5. **Inverse coupling band.** Formerly "The admissible inverse coupling band at level `m` is `[β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`"; now "The coupling band at scale `m` is …" (10:215).
   *Basis:* D (10:215; the band is already at 4:462–463). *Where:* 10:215 ("coupling band"). *Adopted:* *the coupling band `𝔅_m`*.
6. **Majorant of a remainder array (12:80).** A family of bounds for the entries of a remainder array (derivative bounds for the regular entries, supremum bounds for the large-field entries) with finite weighted sum, that is, one of the families over which the infimum defining the seminorm of `𝓡_m` is taken (12:71–73: "Its seminorm is the infimum of the sum of the regular derivative majorants and the large-field value majorants multiplied by `κ_m^{-1}`"). "This follows first for any majorant admitted in the infimum and then by taking the infimum" (12:79–80) says: prove the bound on the evaluation maps with one such family within `ε` of the infimum and let `ε ↓ 0`.
   *Basis:* R (12:71–73, 79–80); S for the argument. *Where:* 12:80 ("majorant admitted in the infimum"). *Adopted:* *any majorant admitted in the infimum*.
   *Source:* Martin existence/fixed-rung-convergence.tex:11–14, 27–29: "Let `E_m` be its vector space of admissible remainder arrays, with the seminorm obtained by minimizing their total regular mass plus `κ_m^{-1}` times their forced mass"; "To justify the last inequalities when the infimum defines the norm, first use any admissible majorant within `ε` of the infimum and let `ε ↓ 0`". Lean `YM.MergeProof.Matric.ticket`, YM/FullVolume/Mark/Purse.lean (definition read: `ticket f = sInf {v | Pay F Y S f v}`), `YM.MergeProof.Matric.fortune` and `Coin` (definitions read: the seminorm `ticket` on the space of arrays having some finite bound); `posture` (statement read: the infimum is attained). `Pay` itself was not opened; its content (regular bounds with sum `a`, large-field bounds with sum `κ·b`, `a + b ≤ v`) is read off the proof of `posture`.
7. **Representation of the density, and its bounds (13sb:27, 36).** The former "admissible path-action representation" (13sb:27, now "the path-action representation of the density") is the representation of the level-`i` density of the trajectory by path action, regular activities and large-field activities, belonging to the class to which the one-step theorem applies (conditions of Section (ch04:admissibility), 4:665–693, with the path bounds); the former "have their admissible bounds" (13sb:36, now "satisfy the bounds (ch04:activity-bounds)") referred to the bounds that every member of that class satisfies (cf. "It has the admissible activity bounds", 10:240; 9:940–943).
   *Basis:* I from the v3 text (10:240; 9:940–943); S for the class. *Where:* 13sb:27 ("path-action representation of the density"), 36 ("the bounds (ch04:activity-bounds)"). *Adopted:* *the representation of the density of the trajectory at scale `i`*; *the bounds (ch04:activity-bounds)*.
   *Source:* Scott part2/E-section.tex:25–27: "For an admissible unmarked representation `ρ_m` on `V` sites write `Φ_m = v_{sc,m}V − P_{N,m} − Σ_i 1_{X_i healthy}E_i^reg` and `K_{m,Y}` for its forced activities"; the lemma "Normalization cost" that follows is the estimate of 13sb:27–39. Scott part1/05-renormalization.tex:191: "The *admissible classes* consist of everything reachable from it [the Wilson initialization] … Every member satisfies … the path bounds … and (eq:I12-activity-caps)".
8. **Request (18lp:103).** A numerical requirement on the schedule of the kind permitted at 10:66–70 ("Future applications may prescribe countably many finite numerical requests, provided their analytic estimates have already been established for a fixed stage"), met by raising the coupling threshold of the stage: "Impose `(σ_{l+1}+1)h_l = o(τ_l)` by choosing the lower bounds on the reference coupling at each stage … so this is a finite admissible request" (18lp:101–103); a requirement of the same kind, but on the minimum starting scale `b_q` (10:122–127), is called "a permitted finite requirement on the starting scale" at 13ba:262 ("coupling-threshold requirement" until 25 November 2026). 10:66–67 now reads "countably many finite numerical requirements on the schedule".
   *Basis:* R (10:66–70; 13ba:262). *Where:* 18lp:103. *Proposed:* *a requirement of the kind allowed in Section (ch10:schedule)*.
9. **With a separate entry:** comparison depth (formerly 14lc:23; see *admissible comparison depth*), conditional integral with insertions (17m:72; see *admissible marked conditional integral*), path action, periods.
   *Basis:* see those entries (17m:72 remains I). *Where:* as listed. *Proposed:* see those entries.
*Literature:* **admissible** (sequence of domains, domains, sets): B88b p. 257 "admissible sequences of domains"; p. 248 "resummed over all admissible `P_0, P_1, Q_1`"; B89b p. 390 "admissible domains, i.e., domains with nonzero expressions"; B85e p. 258, (8), "`1 = Σ_{admissible Ω_1} ζ_{Ω_1^c} χ_{Ω_1}`"; B85b p. 99 "an admissible family of subsets"; also "admissible contours" (B84b p. 231). The same use of the word as the "admissible" of v3's sources for the families allowed in the exact-cover sum (the "eligible family" of 8:292–296). The other senses of the dictionary entry (comparison coefficients, periods) have no counterpart. Suggested: "admissible" is the literature word for the allowed index families.
*Across chapters:* the word is attached to at least eleven nouns; no two definitions coincide. Senses 1–4 are defined in v3; sense 8 is settled by the context and needs one clause at the place of use; senses 5–7 no longer use the word. Chapters 12–16 have 12 occurrences, 6 of them with "graph" (12:37, 82, 89, 97 twice, 140, 375; 13:217, 221, 241, 396; 18lp:103). Martin's text has a further defined use that v3 did not keep under this name: "a coefficient family is *admissible* at `m`" (existence/selected-centered-service.tex:2052–2069), a list of eight conditions of which `c(v) ≤ s_m‖core x(v)‖_1` is the bound of sense 2.

#### admissible comparison depth
*Now:* replaced by *comparison scale whose comparison window lies in a single stage* ("At a comparison scale `k` whose comparison window lies in a single stage put `H_k = exp((log log β̂_k)²)`", 14lc:23–24); the condition itself is still not stated.
*Also in the text for:* the former *admissible* (see those entries).
- **Meaning.** A level `k > 0` whose comparison window lies in a single stage of the schedule. With `H_k = exp((log log β̂_k)²)`, `L` the block ratio of the stage of `k`, `h_k(α) = ⌈(α+2) log H_k / log L⌉` and `v_k = ⌈10 log B_k / log L⌉` (`B_k = ⌈log² β̂_k⌉` in the formalisation), the condition is `h_k(α) + v_k ≤ k` together with: the stage index is constant on the levels `k − h_k(α) − v_k ≤ m ≤ k`. On such a window the block ratio and the stage constants do not change. There are arbitrarily large such `k`, for finitely many exponents `α` simultaneously (in 14lc: `α_0, α_1, α_2`). "At a comparison scale `k` whose comparison window lies in a single stage put `H_k = exp((log log β̂_k)²)`" (14lc:23–24) is the only place; v3 does not state the condition. "Comparison depth" is now "comparison scale" also at 11:1154, 1349, 1367, 2069 and 13:165–166; 11:887 defines an admissible comparison *coefficient*, not a scale.
  *Basis:* S (the v3 text names but does not state the condition, 14lc:23); I that the three exponents of 14lc are handled by one common `k`. *Where:* 14lc:23. *Proposed:* *a scale `k` whose comparison window lies in a single stage*, with the condition stated once, in a lemma that can be cited.
  *Source:* Lean `YM.Next.Rank.Station.Allowed`, YM/Next/RANK/Station.lean (definition read: `0 < k`; `height A b k + surplus A k ≤ k`; `∀ m, width A b k ≤ m → m ≤ k → J m = J k`; with `height = ⌈log(P^b·P²)/log L⌉`, `P = exp((log log β̂_k)²)` (`YM.Vac.Numbers.P`, YM/Vac/Treasury.lean, definition read), `surplus = ⌈log(⌈log² β̂_k⌉^{10})/log L⌉`, `middle = k − height`, `width = middle − surplus`, `L` the block factor of the stage `J k`, all definitions read; file docstring "An `Allowed` station knows its stretch fits inside a plateau"); `gap A b k = a_k · H_k^b` and `gap_rate` (statement read: `gap → 0`), the `r_k` of 14lc:26. Scott part2/E-section.tex:48–53 (eq. `eq:E-window`: `h_t(b) = ⌈(b+2) log 𝔐_t / log L⌉`, `v_t = ⌈10 log B_t / log L⌉`, `k_t = t − h_t(b) − v_t`) and :119 (Lemma `lem:E1.1`): "For every finite set of exponents `b ≥ 1` and finite comparison requests, arbitrarily late terminal levels `t` meet the comparison requirements simultaneously on their windows, with `k_t → ∞` and `J_i = J_t` throughout each window." Martin existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:244–246: "On the admissible comparison levels the calendar is constant in stage throughout `[ℓ(k), k]`." Lean and Martin index the window by its top `k`, as 14lc does; Scott writes `t` for the top and `k_t` for the bottom. No Lean statement that infinitely many levels are `Allowed` for several exponents at once was found; that part rests on Scott's lemma.
*Across chapters:* single place. v3 should restore the condition, for instance from Scott part2/E-section.tex:119 quoted above with the window of `eq:E-window`.
*See also:* admissible; comparison depth; comparison window.

#### admissible conditional integral with insertions
*Formerly:* *admissible marked conditional integral*.
*In the text:* (17m:72: "an admissible conditional integral with the differentiated kernel inserted"); "admissible" is kept without definition, and the proposal was not applied.
- **Meaning.** A conditional integral `∫ (extra factor) · k(U,V) f(U) dU` whose integrand, after the change of variables of chapter 6 (6.protected-change), satisfies the pointwise derivative hypothesis (6.pointwise-jets), so that the bound (6.actual-jet-integral) applies and the connected expansion of chapter 11 can be rooted at the extra factor. This is what the following sentences use: "Its extra factor is a finite sum of smooth local kernel scores times `Y` or its derivative. On a protected dependence set the incoming measurable product remains fixed under the change of variables in Chapter 6 … The bounded pointwise-jet estimate (6.actual-jet-integral) therefore applies … Rooting the connected expansion at this extra factor gives the same expansion with insertions as in Chapter 11" (17m:72–81). "Admissible" is not a defined class here.
  *Basis:* I (17m:72–81 with 6:1043–1057). *Where:* 17m:72. *Proposed:* *a marked conditional integral satisfying the hypotheses of (6.actual-jet-integral)*.
*Across chapters:* single occurrence. The passage 17m:1–133 has no counterpart in the source manuscripts (`audit/ch17-marked-rates.md`), so the reading rests on the v3 context alone. A reading "admissible in the sense of chapters 9 or 11" is not supported: chapter 11 defines "admissible" only for coefficient families.
*See also:* admissible; marked; protected (sense 1).

#### admissible path action
*Now:* not applied; the phrase stands at 5:1398 and 17t:87, "admissible action" at 17c:12.
*Variants:* admissible action (17c:12); no longer in the text: admissible path-action representation (13sb:27, now "the path-action representation of the density").
- **Meaning.** An action `Σ_γ c_γ ×` (local analytic term in the holonomies along the paths `γ`) satisfying the two conditions named at 5:1390–1399: the summability hypothesis `sup_z Σ |c_γ| e^{σℓ(γ)} ≤ P` of 5:1253–1264 (label `ch05:path-budget`) and "the quadratic hypothesis leading to (ch05:actual-hessian)" (5:1394–1395); "These conditions will be imposed on the admissible path action" (5:1398). The hypothesis at 5:1253–1264 is stated without a name; that "admissible" means "satisfying these conditions" is inferred from 5:1398.
  *Basis:* R (5:1253–1264, the hypothesis) / I (5:1398, the name). *Where:* 5:1253–1264, 1398; 13sb:27 (without the adjective); 17t:87; 17c:12. *Proposed:* *action with exponentially summable path coefficients* (state the second condition with it).
*Across chapters:* one object. Chapters 17 point to chapter 7 ("the same admissible path action used in Chapter 7", 17t:87), but the word "admissible" does not occur in chapter 7; the pointer resolves only through 5:1390–1399.
*See also:* admissible; path budget.

#### admissible periods
*Now:* partly applied: on 25 November 2026 (decision 36) "admissible physical periods" at MT:14–15 became "admissible periods in continuum units", the wording of 19:20–21 ("admissible periods `R_p` in continuum units"); "admissible" is kept, and "admissible period" stands at MT:19.
*Variants:* admissible periods in continuum units (MT:14–15; 19:20–21); admissible period (MT:19); no longer in the text: admissible physical periods (MT:14).
1. **The selected sequence of periods (MT:14–15; 19:20–21).** The periods `R_p = 4(M+p+1)`, `p ≥ 0` (10:200), where the integer `M` is chosen "large enough that the lattice side `R_p/a_m` meets the required lower bound at every step of [the first] plateau for all `p ≥ 0`" (10:196–198). The phrase is tied to this sequence by 19:20–21 ("admissible periods `R_p` in continuum units"). "Admissible" means: a member of this sequence, that is, a multiple of four, at least the required minimum physical period, and such that the lattice side `R_p/a_m` is at least the stage requirement at every level (the volume requirement, `100(B_m+1)` for the covering radius `B_m`, cf. 9:934–936, and `100(`patch radius`+1)` for the block-average patch on the finer side). Chapter 10 does not use the word for periods, and 1:202–203 asks only for "strictly increasing periods `R_p` (the side lengths of the tori in continuum units), each an integer multiple of four".
   *Basis:* R (19:20–21 for "the periods are the `R_p`"; 10:200 for the formula); S for the content of "admissible". *Where:* MT:14–15; 19:20–21. *Adopted:* *admissible periods in continuum units* (MT:14–15, decision 36). *Proposed:* state the conditions on `M` of 10:196–198 where `R_p = 4(M+p+1)` is chosen, or cite them from MT (not applied; "admissible" is still not defined for periods).
   *Source:* Martin `existence/common-scale-selection.tex:116–126`: "Choose an integer `M` at least their finitely many values `V_{j_*}(s_m)` and at least the required minimum physical period. Use periods `P_p = 4(M+p+1)` … The three summands of `V_j` pay respectively the specified volume, coarse-cover and fine-patch requirements." Lean `YM.RG.Supply.Program.page`, `YM.RG.Supply.Program.book` (`YM/Price/Waits.lean:87–104`; definitions read): `page M = 4*(M+1)`, `period i := page (M+i)`, with `period_strict`, `period_four`; `YM.RG.Supply.Wait.engine` and `YM.RG.Supply.AsDivisors` (`YM/PhysicalNext/RG_NEXT_COMPLETE_REPEATABLE_NONLINEAR_STEP/Pane/Divisors.lean:21–75`; statement and the choice of `M` in the proof read): `M := B.minLength + sup_{i≤n} Y.bill p.first (s i)`, and every positive integer divides arbitrarily late periods; `YM.RG.Calendar.Fits`, fields `sizeT : 100*(coverSize m + 1) ≤ side m p` and `fitsPatch : 100*(patch.radius + 1) ≤ side (m+1) p` (`YM/RG/History.lean:97–110`; definition read). The public structure `YangMills.WilsonFamily` (`PublicWilson.lean:35–46`; definition read) asks of the periods only `periodStrict` (strictly increasing positive integers).
2. **Period admissible for a test function (MT:19, "at each fixed admissible period").** A period `R_p` whose box contains the support of the test function: "It is admissible at volume `p` if its support is contained in `((−R_p/2, R_p/2)^4)^n`" (1:359–361; sense 3 of *admissible*). Convergence along the lattice spacings is asserted at every such period.
   *Basis:* D (1:359–361) for the notion; S for reading MT:19 in this sense (the main theorem does not mention the test function there). *Where:* MT:19. *Proposed:* *at each fixed period (for test functions supported in the corresponding box)*.
   *Source:* Scott `part1/02-definitions.tex:90–96`: a separated test "is *`p`-admissible*, or supported inside volume `p`, if its support lies in `((−L_p/2, L_p/2)^4)^n`"; ordered convergence holds "at every admissible `p`". Lean `YangMills.WilsonFamily.suitable`, `YangMills.WilsonFamily.Converges` (`PublicWilson.lean:75–91`; definitions read): the mesh limit is required at every `p` with `suitable p t`.
*Across chapters:* the front matter merges two notions under one adjective: a property of the sequence of periods (sense 1) and a relation between a period and a test function (sense 2). Only the second is defined in v3 (1:359–361).
*See also:* admissible (sense 3); period.

#### affine
*Now:* not applied; "normalized affine directions" stands at 9:35, 504. At 9s:303, where it had replaced "reflected seminorm directions" on 25 November 2026, it is replaced on 26 November 2026 (definitions from the sources; Scott `part2/D-section.tex:417–425`): "Original small-field logarithmic coordinates and the directions admitted by the activity seminorm (ch04:local-seminorm), restricted to the cube `N_{w̄}` about the localization site and carried to the reflected periodic extension (… the cube `N_r(x)` is used there without a definition), are bounded by a polynomial in `B` times `t_m`" (9s:303–305); a margin note says that all directions of the seminorm are meant, not only the affine ones, and that Scott leaves the chart requirement on the reflected torus "under verification" (grep).
*Variants:* normalized affine directions (9:35, 504); no longer in the text: normalized affine directions at 9s:303.
- **Meaning.** An *affine direction* is a tangent link field that is an affine function of position, `A_μ(y) = u_μ + Σ_ν y^ν v_{μν}` with `u_μ, v_{μν} ∈ 𝔤` (9:460–461), the fields of the affine Hessian condition (4:670–684). The "normalized affine directions" of 9:35 and 9:504 are the particular fields `A^{q,T_*}_c(y) = 1_{c=b} ξ_o(y)^a T_*`, `q = (a,b)`, of 9:465–467 (links in direction `b` with value `(y−o)^a T_*`; constant curl `T_*` in the plane `q`) and their half-sums, multiplied by the threshold `t`: these are admitted directions of the activity seminorm (4:622–624), which is what "belong to the activity seminorm" (9:35–36) says, and evaluating the Hessian of `f` on them gives `t²|q_f(q,q)| ≤ a_f` and, by polarization, `t²|q_f(q,r)| ≤ 3a_f` (9:504–505).
  *Basis:* R (9:460–469, 504–505) for "affine"; R (4:622–624) for the normalisation; S for the statement that the directions are `tA^{q,T_*}` and their half-sums. *Where:* 9:35, 504 (9s:303 until 26 November 2026). *Proposed:* *the fields `tA^{q,T_*}` and their half-sums*; in general *affine link fields scaled by the threshold `t_m`*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:22` "the Hessian of `A ↦ E_i(exp A)` at zero vanishes on every pair of affine directions `A_{(y,a)} = u_a + Σ_c ξ_{o_i}(y)^c v_{ac}`, `u_a, v_{ac} ∈ 𝔤`"; `:516` "If `a_f` majorizes `f`, the diagonal tests `tA^{q,T_*}` and their half-sum are permitted directions in Definition D05a. They give `t²|q_f(q,q)| ≤ a_f`, `t²|q_f(q,r)| ≤ 3a_f`. Indeed four times the half-sum's diagonal Hessian is `t²(q_f(q,q) + q_f(r,r) + 2q_f(q,r))`." Martin `existence/physical-reset-reorganization.tex:104–107` "let `W_a(v)` be the affine field whose links in direction `j` have the value `(x−o)_i v` and whose other links vanish. Its curl is `v` in the plane `a`".
*Across chapters:* chapter 9; from 25 to 26 November 2026 also 9s:303, where the phrase stood for Scott's "direction of that definition" (Definition D05a, D:425), that is, any admitted direction of the activity seminorm, not only the affine fields `tA^{q,T_*}` of 9:504; on 26 November 2026 9s:303 was rewritten to "the directions admitted by the activity seminorm (ch04:local-seminorm)", so "affine" there was not right. v3 should restore from Scott D:516 the sentence saying which directions are used ("the diagonal tests `tA^{q,T_*}` and their half-sum").
*See also:* affine Hessian; affine stack; normalized directions; reflected normalized directions.

#### affine Hessian
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* affine-Hessian cancellation; affine Hessian condition.
- **Meaning.** The Hessian at zero of `A ↦ E(exp A)` restricted to pairs of affine link fields `A_{(y,μ)} = u_μ + Σ_ν ξ(y)^ν v_{μν}`; the condition requires it to vanish. "The meaning of the affine Hessian condition is fixed in the chosen local coordinates" (4:683–684).
  *Basis:* R (4:670–684). *Where:* 4:670–684; 9:208, 214, 460–482, 499, 566. *Adopted:* keep, define once (it is defined in chapter 4; refer to 4:670–684 at 9:208).
*Literature:* **`E^{(j)}(1) = 0`**; "no relevant variables"; **irrelevant** terms, after subtraction of the `β_j A` term (B85e p. 264: "by the assumption that g is semi-simple, the only element invariant is 0 … In the renormalization group language it is the statement that there are no relevant variables in the effective action"; B87 p. 258: "E^{(j)}(1) = 0"; p. 259: "Terms satisfying the inequality (0.29) are called irrelevant"); in D1 the corresponding conditions define a **normalized** functional (see *remainder*). An analogue of the normalisation of regular activities (`E_i^reg(1) = 0`, vanishing linear term, Hessian vanishing on affine fields, 4:669–684). The argument for the linear term is the same (v3 4:679–682; B85e (31)–(32)); but Bałaban imposes no condition term by term: he resums over `X` and subtracts `β_j A`. The "normalization conditions" of B87 pp. 294–295 concern a Laurent decomposition in the analysis of `Π` and are unrelated. Suggested: *conditions making the term irrelevant (no constant, linear or marginal quadratic part)*; cite B85e (32) for the linear term.
*Across chapters:* one sense; defined in chapter 4, used in chapter 9.

#### alias
*Now:* unchanged; its compounds are replaced: *zero alias* for "principal alias" (remains at 11:1742), *nonzero alias* for "nonprincipal alias". On 25 November 2026 the alias argument of the proof of preservation of the order of vanishing (17c:56–69, 77–88) and of the stress jets (17c:324–331) was removed, with "Fourier coefficient at the alias `l`" (formerly "alias amplitude", 17c:62), the "transverse coefficient" and the "projected coefficients" (17c:81–86; 17m:233): the proof now tests Hessians on polynomial fields (see *polynomial field*). In chapter 17 the word remains only in the disclaimer "No alias decomposition of the linearization … is used" (17c:68), in "no inverse of a kinetic symbol at a nonzero alias" (17c:69), in the remark on the double zero of `K_0` "at every nonzero alias" (17c:74–75), followed by "The argument above does not use this double zero" (17c:77), at 17c:335–336 and at 17m:215–232.
*Variants:* zero alias; nonzero alias; scalar zero alias (7:711); alias formula (11:1736; 17c:335); principal alias (11:1742); no longer in the text: nonprincipal alias; scalar principal alias; alias amplitude; two-leg alias term (17c:77).
- **Meaning.** One of the fine momenta `k_l(p) = (p + 2πl)/L` lying over a coarse momentum `p` (7:1148). The zero alias is `l = 0`, the nonzero ones `l ≠ 0`; the "columns" of 5:581–600 and 17m:204, 232 ("the column at the zero alias has value `I`", 17m:232) are the alias components `𝒜_l`, `𝒯_l`.
  *Basis:* R (7:1148); R / I for "columns" (5:581–600). *Where:* 5:166, 351–353, 402, 581–600; 7:496, 594, 604, 608, 710–732, 822–826, 1148–1161; 11:1736–1745; 17c:68–69, 74–77, 335–336; 17m:215–232. *Adopted:* keep *alias*; *zero alias*, *nonzero aliases*. *Proposed:* define once at 5:351 (the text there has "At the zero alias with real momentum", 5:352, without definition); *alias components*.
*Literature:* no name; the decomposition "`p ∈ T̃_η` is represented as a sum `p = p' + l`, `p' ∈ T̃_1^{(k)}` and `l_μ = 2πm_μ`" (B84a p. 23). The same object, in Bałaban's rescaled units and for `k` steps at once. Suggested: keep *alias* (a signal-processing word); the literature offers no noun.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 5, 7, 11 and 17. The word is not new in chapters 17–19: it is the chapter 5 term in the same sense. The formula `k_l(p)` was first written at 17c:57 until 25 November 2026; it now stands at 7:1148 ("For aliases `k_l(p)=(p+2πl)/L`"), in the alias argument of chapter 7 (7:1148–1161), which is independent of chapter 17 and was not changed, as is that of 7:822–826.
*See also:* box-filter identity; principal; amplitude.

#### allocation
*Now:* replaced by *partition of unity* (sense 1, 6:67); *assignment* (sense 2, 6:1333, 1467); at 9:81–82 by "retain all the weights defining the sectors". 17c:120 ("either allocation of four differences") and 9:437 ("Allocate distinct positive fractions of the exponent") are unrelated ordinary uses.
*Variants:* no longer in the text: sector allocation weights; sector allocation indicators.
1. **Partition of unity over the large-field sets:** the weights `ϑ_f`, `ϑ_n`, `1 − ϑ` that distribute a configuration over the large-field index sets.
   *Basis:* R (6:67–79); R for 9:81–82 ("retain all the weights defining the sectors", with 6:85). *Where:* 6:67 ("partition of unity"), 68–79, 85 ("this decomposition"); 9:81–82 ("the weights defining the sectors", which also include the probability weights of the auxiliary index and the condition on `A_c`). *Proposed:* *partition of unity*; *partition-of-unity weights* (applied in chapter 6; 9:81–82 names the larger family of weights).
2. **Assignment of the terms of the action to the core or the annulus** of a large-field component.
   *Basis:* R (6:1333). *Where:* 6:1333, 1467 ("assignment"). *Adopted:* *assignment*.
*Literature:* **decomposition of unity** (B85e p. 257: "We introduce the decomposition of unity 1 = Σ_P ∏_{p∈P} χ({|U(∂p) − 1| ≥ ε_1}) ∏_{p∈P^c} χ({|U(∂p) − 1| < ε_1}), where the sum is over sets P of plaquettes"; B88b p. 246: "Now we introduce the decomposition of unity"; B89a p. 181: "the decomposition of unity `1 = χ + (1 − χ)`"); the identity `1 = Π_□(ζ(□) + χ(□)) = Σ_P ζ(P)χ(P^c)` (D2 p. 092301-31, (233); p. 092301-42, (324); p. 092301-2). An analogue of sense 1 (the weights `ϑ_f`, `ϑ_n`, `1−ϑ`, 6:67–79): in the literature the decomposition is sharp (characteristic functions), so the set is determined by the field; v3's is smooth with overlapping thresholds `t_f/4`, `t_f/2`, so several selections have nonzero weight. It is not the spatial "partition of unity 1 = Σ ζ_□" of B87 p. 270 or the `{h_□}` of the random walk expansions. Sense 2 (core/annulus allocation) has no counterpart. Suggested: *decomposition (partition) of unity over large-field sets*, with "smooth" stated explicitly: "smooth version of B85e (7) and of Dimock's `1 = Π(ζ + χ)`".
*Across chapters:* formerly two senses inside chapter 6, now named apart; chapter 9 no longer uses the word.
*See also:* allocation sector; assigned; sector.

#### alphabet
*Now:* removed; 11:1916 now reads "Consequently, for each term of the original expansion with insertions".
*Variants:* no longer in the text: original marked alphabet; letters (the remaining "alphabet" at 3:15 and "letter" at 16:296 are unrelated).
- **Meaning.** The index family of the factors of the connected expansion of one step, each index carrying its support and its prescribed set of large-field sites; the individual factors are the "letters". The "original marked alphabet" is the full family of factors, with and without insertions, of the original (not restarted) history, so the former "term by term on the original marked alphabet" (11:1916) meant: for each factor of that expansion separately, which is what the text now says.
  *Basis:* S (11:1916 did not explain the word). *Where:* 11:1916 ("for each term of the original expansion with insertions"). *Adopted:* *for each term of the original marked expansion*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/actual-corrected-body-compiler.tex:4–9 ("The marked expansion needs one unmarked alphabet chosen before the number and locations of the insertions"); existence/actual-mixed-marked-compiler.tex:314–322 ("allows that alphabet to embed into the full marked alphabet, with the same full supports and inventories"). No Lean declaration located; the module comment of `YM/Source/Insertion.lean` ("Pad alphabet with unused addresses as needed") uses the word the same way (comment read, not a definition).
*Across chapters:* single occurrence. That "original" means the non-restarted history is read from the context of 11:1916 and of the source passage; the source has no one-sentence definition of "alphabet".

*Now:* partly replaced by *Fourier coefficient* (sense 2); *source weight* (sense 4); remains in senses 1 and 3 (6:1082, 1179, 1214, 1458, 1479, 1488, 1568; 7:1186, 1209; 9s:23; 11:257, 277, 281–282, 340, 1605).

#### anchor
*Now:* replaced by *base point* (sense 1); *site attached to a coordinate* (sense 2); *real point*, *base point* (sense 3); *insertion point* (sense 4). The noun no longer occurs in prose; the participle survives in *anchored* (see that entry).
*Variants:* anchored (see *anchored*); no longer in the text: source anchors (10:181); insertion anchor (11:163); output anchors (6:93; see *output anchors*); common anchor (7:157); fine anchor (17t).
1. **Distinguished site of a support or of a local function:** "A *localized term* of the regular part of the action consists of a *localization domain* `X_i`, a base point `o_i ∈ X_i`, and …" (4:479); the site at which an activity, a term or a local function is counted. In chapter 6 the base points are the addresses of the six local energy terms `E_f, E_n, E_c, E_N, E_L, E_D` ("the sum of the six terms at base points in `A^{[2B]}`", 6:216–217; "Its assigned action terms have base points within `200B` of `O`", 6:1335–1336); base points of fine terms are counted at their coarse projection. The former "output anchors" of 6:93 are now "the coarse plaquettes based at distance at most `4B/5` from `D`".
   *Basis:* D (4:479); R (6:215–217) for the base points of the energy terms; S for "output" = coarse level. *Where:* "base point" at 4:479, 550, 615; 6:195 ff., 211, 1330; 2e:39, 83, 126; 7:157, 628, 922, 1132; 8:76; 9:235, 464; 17t:30; 17c:13, 72; "based" at 6:93; "anchored" at 9:515 and 18:177 (see *anchored*). *Adopted:* *base point*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:915`: "Its *local energy* `𝓔_A` sums the six local energy terms over anchors in `A^{[2B]}`, fine anchors being projected to coarse sites"; `:918`: "let Aff be the set of output anchors within `4B/5` of `D`, the *affected* anchors"; "output" is the coarse level throughout that section (`:913` "an output plaquette with `chord(V_p) > t_c`", `:945` "output plaquette, `r^c_p > δ`").
2. **Site `a_i` attached to a coordinate.**
   *Basis:* R (5:1216). *Where:* 5:1216 ("has a site `a_i` attached to it"). *Adopted:* *site of the coordinate*.
3. **Real base point of a holomorphic weight or of an analytic continuation.**
   *Basis:* R (5:905). *Where:* 5:905 ("at every real point `x`"); 7:743 ("at each real base point"). *Adopted:* *real point `x`*; *real base point*.
4. **Position of an insertion** (to be placed in a cell).
   *Basis:* R (13:85–91). *Where:* "insertion point" at 10:181; 11:163; 13:85, 88, 91; 13sb:86, 158, 160; 12:22, 209. *Adopted:* *insertion point* (also for "origin", 12:22, 209).
*Literature:* no name; the point `z` of `E^{(j)}(X; U, z)` (B88b pp. 259–260, (2.26)–(2.27), text layer only: "the sum over all `X ∈ D_j` containing the point `z`"), which comes from a partition of unity `h_z` (B88b p. 275). An analogue of the anchor `o_i`. No anchored norm is stated in the literature: Bałaban states pointwise bounds per term and Dimock's sums are over polymers containing a cube (D1 p. 1330010-20), so for "anchored" as a kind of sum nothing was found in D1–D3; see *containing-site bound*. Suggested: the proposal stands; no literature name for the norm.
*Across chapters:* senses 1–3 in chapters 4–9; sense 4 from chapter 10 on; chapters 17–19 return to sense 1. Sense 4 is kept separate because the insertion point is not the base point of a polymer. Not *base point* for "root": the root of a spanning tree (5:920; 6:86) is standard and is a different role; the two coincide only at 5:1254–1258 and 6:1469.
*See also:* anchored; anchor average; base; root; origins.

- **Meaning.** Summed or bounded over the supports whose anchor is a given site, as opposed to over all supports containing the site: `sup_x Σ_{γ: anchor(γ) = x} e^{α c(X_γ)} b_γ`, each term counted at one designated site of its support. "It counts every polymer at each site in its support. A norm which counts a polymer only at a chosen base point, an *anchored* norm, is different" (8:75–76). The passage from one to the other costs one unit of support decay ("turn an anchored bound into a site bound", 11R:142; 9:515; 11:267–273). The anchored form is the one used for the localized terms; the remainder norm of 11:362–366 is its version with a single anchor (all supports contain the insertion site and the sum runs over all terms).
  *Basis:* D (4:646; 8:76); R (11R:142). *Where:* 4:646–648; 8:76; 9:515; 11:267–273, 362–364; 11R:142, 200, 210, 341, 376. *Adopted:* *sum over supports with base point `x`* (*anchored norm*), against *sum over supports containing `x`* (*containing-site norm*).
  *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.Activities.EBound` (YM/RG/Activities.lean:98–100; definition read: for every site `x`, the sum over `i` of `mass (reg i).support (b i)` restricted to `(reg i).site = x`, with `b i` a derivative bound of the `i`-th regular activity), against `YM.RG.Activities.KBound` (same file:102–104; definition read: restricted to `x ∈ (forced i).support`); `YM.Source.Coefficient.remBound` with `Format.origin` (YM/Source/Insertion.lean:52, 63–68; read) for the remainder norm.
*Literature:* see *anchor* and *containing-site bound*.
*Across chapters:* one sense; defined at 4:646 and 8:76. The Lean definitions confirm the division of chapter 4: anchored for regular, containing-site for large-field activities.
*See also:* anchor; anchored correction; containing-site bound; site conversion.

#### anchored marked support bound
*Now:* replaced on 26 November 2026 (decision of that day, by content): 18:177 reads "the estimate (ch18:signed-transport), the bound (ch11:higher-induction) for the terms of source degree at least two, and the graded quotient comparison"; the phrase stands only in the margin note there ("Formerly 'the stronger anchored marked support bound', identified by its content. v2 (E-several-mark) asks for an anchored majorant and says it is 'not yet established'; v3 states (ch11:higher-induction) with an incidence bound. Whether that suffices here is not checked") (grep).
- **Meaning.** A nickname, cited at 18:177 with the estimate (ch18:signed-transport) (formerly "the signed local transport") and (18:178) "the graded quotient comparison". It refers to the bound, proved by induction over the levels, for the sum, taken over supports with base point at the insertions (*anchored*), of all coefficients of the marked expansion that contain two or more insertions, in a norm with a larger support exponent than the norm for one insertion. In v3 this is §11 "Propagating the already formed terms of source degree at least two" (`ch11:higher-modes`, 11:479–530): the cover inequality `B r ≤ 64 c_B(X)` (11.separated-cover) for `r ≥ 2` insertions pairwise at distance at least `B²`, and the induction `H_c ≤ C_e{e^{−B/64} H_f + ζ}` (11.higher-induction) for "that stronger incoming incidence bound" `H_f`, with two cover units retained (11:495) and the input specified at exponent `σ_f − 4` (11:528). The same words recur at 18:129–131 ("Its stronger support norm absorbs the factor lost when several insertions are attributed to the same coarse region"). The nickname names the chapter 11 estimate itself; 18lp, "Grouping insertion points and retaining their supports" (18lp:67–136), is the place where it is used ("It applies in the submultiplicative norm in the source variables to a whole incoming joint factor", 18lp:125–127), not a second candidate for the bound: the three items of 18:177–178 are the three inputs of the replacement estimate, and the source of that sentence names the middle one as part of the propagation lemma of the chapter on insertions.
  *Basis:* ? (18:177) for the v3 text until 26 November 2026; S for the meaning of "stronger anchored … bound" and for its location in the chapter on insertions; I for the identification with (11.higher-induction), which rests on matching content and not on a label (adopted by the decision of 26 November 2026). *Where:* 18:177. *Adopted:* *the bound (ch11:higher-induction) for the terms of source degree at least two* (decision of 26 November 2026). Not verifiable from the text, per the reviewer: whether chapter 18 needs more than (ch11:higher-induction).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:19`: "The lattice replacement and its continuum consequences below use the full marked-source propagation of Lemma `lem:E-source-attachments`, including the stronger anchored higher-mode estimate and the stopping-level restart at support exponent 98 not yet established there" (the estimate belongs to the lemma of Scott's section E, v3 chapter 11, and section J, v3 chapter 18, uses it); Scott `part2/E-several-mark.tex:176–181`: "one must propagate a stronger anchored majorant for the already-formed higher modes and the new joins, at a fine support exponent that retains the output reserve after reweighting. The singleton estimate above does not by itself establish that propagation"; Scott `part2/E-section.tex:233`: "The marked regular norm below is anchored at the insertion site … it is not anchored separately at each support". Lean `YM.Bid.I01` (`YM/Bid/Fuels.lean:124–126`; statement read), proved as `YM.Work.I01.answer` (`YM/Work/I01.lean:19`): for `B ≥ 8` and at least two points pairwise at distance at least `B²` in a support `H`, `B·(number of points) ≤ 64·coverNumber B H`; `YM.Multi.radius_change` (`YM/Next/MULTISOURCE/Swarm.lean:94–97`; statement read): for a mode with at least two sites, `B ≥ 8`, insertions `Spaced` at `B` and `0 ≤ r ≤ exp(B/64)`, `r^{|sites|} · fare P 2 X ≤ fare P 1 X`. The induction (11.higher-induction) itself was not located in Lean.
*Across chapters:* single occurrence, now replaced. Scott's draft states that this estimate was "not yet established" there (J:19) and that later applications are "conditional on this remaining estimate" (E-several-mark:182); v3 gives the induction at 11:505–524. The margin note at 18:177 records this.
*See also:* anchored; marked; signed local transport; graded quotient comparison.

#### angular boundary
*Now:* partly replaced by *boundary term at infinity* (section title 14:417, "Joint spectral measures and the boundary term at infinity"); remains as "angular flux at infinity" in the subsection title 14:715.
*Variants:* flux at infinity; angular flux at infinity (14:715); no longer in the text: angular boundary.
- **Meaning.** The boundary term at infinity in the rotational Ward identity. For `K ∈ so(4)` and a list of insertions `A_i(x_i)`, the *angular sum* is `Ang_K = Σ_i { S(…, Y(K)A_i, …) + Σ_b (Kx_i)_b S(…, p_bA_i, …) }`, the left side of (ch14:line-ward) (14:804–806). By conservation and the shell identities it equals `−∫ Σ_{μ,c} ∂_μV_c(y) S(J_{μc}(y), A) dy` for any compactly supported vector field `V` equal to `Ky` near all insertions (14:783–784); the integrand lives where `V` departs from `Ky`, a region that moves to infinity as the box on which `V = Ky` grows. The titles "… the boundary term at infinity" and "Vanishing angular flux at infinity" (14:417, 715) refer to this: the integral tends to zero as `λ → ∞` for the anisotropic fields `V` of 14:775–780, while it does not depend on `λ`; hence `Ang_K = 0` for configurations on a coordinate line (14:804–808). The text now calls the sum "the angular Ward sum, the left side of (ch14:line-ward) below" (14:783–784) and "the angular Ward sum" (14:803), formerly "the total raw angular response" and "the total shell response"; "Ward sum" is defined at 3:915.
  *Basis:* R for the integral (14:783–784, 803–808); S for the names. *Where:* 14:417 (section title, "boundary term at infinity"), 708 (subsection title), 776–777, 796. *Proposed:* *the boundary term at infinity of the rotational Ward identity*; for the title at 14:715, *Vanishing of the angular sum on coordinate lines*.
  *Source:* Scott part2/G-section.tex:656–663: "define the angular sum `Ang_K[Y,p](q;x) = Σ_i [S(…, Y_KA_i, …; x) + Σ_b (Kx_i)_b S(…, p_bA_i, …; x)]`. It is the total angular flux of the raw charges of Lemma G2.3"; "The next lemma removes the angular boundary at infinity before continuous rotations are known. Its mechanism is as follows. The shell identities and conservation write the angular sum as the integral of the conserved tensor against the derivative of a vector field equal to `Ky` on a large box; the sum does not depend on the box, so it suffices that this integral tends to zero"; :679 "`Ang_K = −∫ Σ_{μ,c} ∂_μV_c S(J_{μc}(y), q) dy`"; :7 "Coordinate reflection positivity controls the angular flux at infinity for configurations on coordinate axes through the origin". Martin existence/physical-ward-propagation.tex:23–34: "Define the angular Ward expression by `𝒜_K(q;x) = Σ_i (S(q[i ↦ (d_i, 𝒴_{d_i}(K)v_i)]; x) + Σ_b (Kx_i)_b S(q[i ↦ (d_i+1, 𝒫_{d_i,b}v_i)]; x))` … The condition *collinear* means this identity [`𝒜_K = 0`] holds whenever the points lie on one coordinate axis". Lean `YM.Ward.angular`, YM/Ward/Sum.lean (definition read: `Σ_i (disc(q[i ↦ turns T K (q i)]) x + Σ_b M4.move K (x i) b • disc(q[i ↦ rise W b (q i)]) x)`; `M4.move` not opened, taken to be `(Kx_i)_b`), `YM.Ward.Collinear`, same file (definition read: `angular W T q K x = 0` for every separated `x` on a coordinate axis).
*Across chapters:* chapter 14 only. The two titles still lack the sentence that explains them; v3 should restore, after 14:784, Scott's "the sum does not depend on the box, so it suffices that this integral tends to zero" (14:802–803 says only that every term tends to zero "whereas the angular Ward sum is independent of `λ`"). The words "flux" and "boundary term" name the same integral here: Scott calls `Ang_K` "the total angular flux of the raw charges"; v3 now says "the angular Ward sum".
*See also:* response (sense 10); shell factor; total response; flux.
