#### annular estimates
*Now:* not applied; 14:978 reads "Under the comparison with insertions and the annular estimates used above"; 19:51, 96 unchanged.
- **Meaning.** A nickname for the estimate (14.annular-input), 14:339–350: for `A ∈ F_d`, `ϰ = 0` for a constant and `ϰ = 1` for a linear Killing field, `D = d+1−ϰ`, finitely many spectator functionals `ℓ_i` on `F_D` and coefficients `g_i` with `Σ_i g_i ℓ_i = 0`, there are `ρ_m ↓ 0` with `sup_{1/4 ≤ |z| ≤ 2} |Σ_i g_i ρ_m^{3+ϰ} S(J_{μν}(x_0 + ρ_m z), A(x_0), B_i)| → 0`. In words: on the annulus `ρ/4 ≤ |x − x_0| ≤ 2ρ` the product of the stress tensor at `x` and the field `A` at `x_0`, multiplied by `ρ^{3+ϰ}`, is a field of degree `D` up to an error that tends to zero with `ρ`, with the same field for all spectators of the finite family. In v3 it is derived from Proposition (18.mixed-bound) (14:356–377).
  *Basis:* I (19:51–52, 96–97 name Chapter 14; 14:339–377 is the estimate on an annulus there); S for the identification. *Where:* 14:978; 19:51, 96. *Proposed:* *the estimate (14.annular-input) on shrinking annuli*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/G-section.tex:316–321`, Lemma "Annular annihilator estimate" (`lem:G-annular`), with the same display (`eq:G-annular-input`): "For every finite list of grid tests and coefficients `g_i ∈ ℂ` with `Σ_i g_i r_i = 0` on `F_D`, there are `ρ_l ↓ 0` such that `sup_{1/4≤|z|≤2} |Σ_i g_i ρ_l^{3+ϰ} h_i(ρ_l z)| → 0`". Lean `YM.Next.UVStress.annulus`, `YM.Next.UVStress.NodeBound`, `YM.Next.UVStress.ShellBound`, `YM.Next.UVStress.Probed` (`YM/Next/UV_STRESS/Annulus.lean:26–54`; definitions read): `annulus e = {x | e/4 < ‖x‖ < 2e}`; `Probed` asks `ShellBound (d+1) 3` (translations) and `ShellBound d 4` (rotations); `YM.Next.UVStress.annular_field` (`YM/Next/UV_STRESS/Shell.lean:161–168`; statement read): `ShellBound F D (3+p) v J` for a Killing field homogeneous of degree `p` gives a field `B ∈ F_D` whose correlations equal the flux.
*Across chapters:* used in chapters 14 and 19 for one estimate of chapter 14. "Annular correction `C_{m,ρ}`" (14:465) is a different object.
*See also:* annular correction; bounded approximations.

#### attachment
*Now:* partly replaced by *site norm* (sense 2, 9:699, 796; 10:778–779) and by *merge* for "join" (11:150–151, 510); remains in senses 1 and 3 and at 9:689 (sense 2), kept as proposed but still not defined in one sentence.
*Variants:* attach; source / terminal / local / joint attachment (bound, estimate); attachment of the large-field part (11:944); attachment bound `u_i`; number of attachments; attachment reserves (10:763); no longer in the text: join (in this sense); complementary attachment; attachment reserve `u_N` (11:940, now "the strict margin for attachments at the ultraviolet cutoff"); attachment norm; strict attachment margin (10:778, now "a strict margin in the site-norm bound").
1. **Merging the large-field part of an insertion with existing large-field supports.** "Merge the link support of each large-field part with every selected large-field support it meets, and merge intersecting …" (11:150–151); "Attach the latter to the original selected large-field factors" (11:925–926). The margin `u_N > 0` (11:940, "the strict margin for attachments at the ultraviolet cutoff") is the part of the decay kept for this step; the "attachment bound" `u_i = ¼ β̂_i^{-1/2}` of 13ba:61–62, 77 is that reserve.
   *Basis:* R (11:150–151, 925–926). *Where:* 10:763; 11:150–151, 171, 217, 253, 502, 510, 925, 940, 944; 11E:57, 80, 92–103; 13sb:64, 70, 74; 13ba:58, 62, 77, 78, 99, 123, 145; 18lp:148. *Proposed:* keep, define once (*merging of the large-field part of an insertion with the selected large-field supports it meets*).
   *Source:* Scott `part2/E-section.tex:73–76`: "This bound controls attachments of other marked factors to a distinguished mark. … let `η^att_i > 0` be the attachment threshold in Lemma D-connected for the step at level `i`", with the requirement (E-attachment-allowance) `2A_{j,d}(2B_i+1)^4(1+B_i)^4 β̂_i^{q_d} ζ_{d,i} ≤ η^att_i/4`. That v3's reserve `u_N` (which enters as `ζ_{e,N} u_N^{-1}`, 11:936) is this threshold up to the constants is inferred from the form of the two conditions, not stated.
2. **A further support meeting one already present, in a tree sum; the norm that controls how many there can be.** In the rooted tree sums of chapters 8–9 each child support is attached to its parent by meeting it. Since "a support has at most `(2B+1)^4 c(Z)` sites" (9:689–690), a bound on the sum of the weights of the supports through one site becomes, after multiplication by `(2B+1)^4` and at the price of one unit of the support exponent, a bound on the weights of the supports that can be attached to a given support: "One additional unit of the support exponent bounds the number of attachments" (9:689). The former "attachment norm" (9:699, now "majorants small in the site norm") is the norm of 9:661, `sup_x Σ_{a: x ∈ Z_a} e^{(σ+1)c(Z_a)} v_a`, the site norm of 8:69 at exponent `σ+1` applied to majorants; the former "strict attachment margin" (9:796, now "the strict margin in the site-norm bound"; 10:778–779, now "a strict margin in the site-norm bound", the same margin of the exact regrouping) is the slack in `(2B+1)^4 γ ≤ 1/2` (9:703–704).
   *Basis:* I (9:689, 699); S for the statement. *Where:* 9:689 ("attachments"), 697, 794 ("site norm"); 10:778–779 ("site-norm bound"). *Adopted:* *the site norm (9:661)*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:109` "A support covered by `n` radius-`B` balls has at most `(2B+1)^4 n` sites; this converts a site bound into an attachment bound"; `:111–116` (Lemma "Rooted polymer bound"): if `(2B+1)^4 sup_x Σ_{a: x∈Z_a} v_a e^{η cov_B(Z_a)} ≤ η`, the sum over rooted trees "in which every child support meets its parent's" is at most `v_⋆ e^{η cov_B(Z_⋆)}`; `:214` calls `(2B+1)^4 sup_x Σ_{a: x∈Z_a} v_a` "the attachment parameter".
3. **Assigning a condition to a set of links.** "Attach this condition to its dependence set" (17m:125): the failed chart condition is counted with the set of links on which it depends.
   *Basis:* I (17m:125). *Where:* 17m:125. *Proposed:* *assign the condition to the set of links it depends on*.
*Literature:* no name; for sense 1 (joining stencils or logarithmic corrections to large-field supports, 11:150) the nearest named operation is the **resummation** of D3 App. B (p. 2173) and D2 pp. 092301-71/72; in B89b the nearest statements are about "exponential factors connecting" localization domains (p. 376). A weak analogue, found in D2, D3 only; B88b–B89b have no name and nothing corresponds to the number of attachments or the attachment reserve. Suggested: see *fusion*; keep "attachment" defined once.
*Across chapters:* never defined in one sentence. The statement of sense 1 is read at 11:150–151 and 11:925–926. A wider reading ("joining an insertion stencil or a complementary part … and the sum over the places where this can happen") is not adopted: the "sum over places" belongs to 9:689 and is a separate use (sense 2). Both senses come from one picture in the source: a support attached to another by meeting it.
*See also:* complementary; reserve; site norm; anchored.

#### available weight
*Now:* replaced by *product of the remaining source weights* (18lp:128, 168; "this product of weights", 18lp:175).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: available (product) weight `ω`; available mark weights.
- **Meaning.** Not defined in chapters 12–16. One of the positive numbers (`w_i`, `ω`) by which the source variables are scaled in the marked norm, so that the coefficient of `z_S` is bounded by `1/∏ w_i` (12:244–245; display 11:810–813). The weights are defined at 11:43–49. In 18lp, `ω` is the product of the weights of the source variables of one group that are still positive, that is, what remains of `∏ w_i` after the reductions for support enlargement and the per-step losses. It is bounded below by (ch18:group-weight): "With `g` groups left, the product of their remaining source weights is consequently at least `(a_j/a_l)^{4n}(α_j/8)^{n(n−g)}∏w_i`" (18lp:128–131); `ω` at 18lp:168 is this product for the single remaining group ("Suppose the cluster has become one group at scale `m+1`, with product `ω` of its remaining source weights", 18lp:167–168; "by this product of weights", 18lp:175).
  *Basis:* R (12:244–245; 11:43–49) for the weights; D (18lp:128–131, 167–168) for `ω`. *Where:* the object `ω`: 18lp:128, 168, 175. The whole group of weight words: 12:248, 282, 283; 13sb:73–76; 13ba:44, 124; 14lc:60, 63; 18lp:73, 84, 105, 128, 138, 168, 188 (about 25). *Adopted:* *the product of the remaining source weights* (the product of the weights of its source variables after the reductions); for the group of words, *source weight*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:224`: "To each marker `ι` attach a commuting variable `z_ι` with `z_ι² = 0` and a mark weight `w_ι > 0`"; `J-section.tex:236`: "A grouped coefficient carries the product of its live mark weights, denoted by `ω`"; `J-section.tex:280`: "Divide a grouped coefficient by its available weight `ω`"; Scott `part2/G-section.tex:334`: "Let `u_{m,1}, u_{m,2}` be the available mark weights of the degree-`d` and rescaled degree-four marks at level `j(m)`".
*Across chapters:* one object in chapters 12–18, now called *source weight* throughout (12:248, 283; 13sb:73; 14lc:60, 63; 18lp:128, 168); "residual" survives in the symbol `ω_i^res` (13ba:124). The sentence of Scott J:236, which says what `ω` is, is now in substance at 18lp:167–168.
*See also:* amplitude (sense 4); source weight; live group.

#### average over the forests
*Now:* new in chapter 11 on 25 November 2026 (decision 27, issue 2 of the fork); the subsection `chapters/09-forest-average.tex` ("Lattice symmetries and the average over forests", label `ch09:forest-average`) defines it.
*Variants:* average over forests (9:149, 332, 928, 956); averaged over the forests (11:19, 336; 11R:193, 248); averaged activities `E_F a_M^F`, `ā_M` (11:336; `chapters/09-forest-average.tex`:374–399).
- **Meaning.** The expansion of a step is carried out with one forest `F` (one rooted spanning tree in every block); its activities `a_M^F` depend on `F`, the block integral does not. The forests in different blocks are chosen independently and the activities are averaged: under parts (a)–(b) of Assumption `ch09:forest-assumption` ("Fixed-forest expansion", `chapters/09-forest-average.tex`:221–300) the normalization constant `𝒩_F` does not depend on `F` and `𝒵_blk = 𝒩 e^{−𝒮} Σ_𝒜 ∏ ā_M` with `ā_M` the average of `a_M^F` over the trees `F(y)`, `y ∈ X_M` (Proposition `ch09:forest-average-prop`(i)–(ii), `chapters/09-forest-average.tex`:374–399); under part (d) the averaged activities are equivariant (part (iii)). Chapter 11 now states that its local representations are those of chapter 9, "whose activities are averaged over the forests" (11:19), and that the density with insertions is averaged by the same average (11:336), under Hypothesis (H).
  *Basis:* D (`chapters/09-forest-average.tex`:374–399). *Where:* `chapters/09-forest-average.tex` passim; 9:149, 332, 928, 956; 11:19, 294, 336, 679, 726, 1054; 11R:193, 248. *Proposed:* keep.
  *Source:* report `audit/decisions-2026-11-25/ch11-forest-adaptation.md`: Martin `marked-block-integral.tex:140–156` (the activities with insertions read the forest only in the blocks of their support; "`a_C = E_F a_C^F`"); Lean `YM.PhysicalNext.InteractingRank.glance` (`Layout.lean:124`), the average over one independent tree tag per coarse site, applied also to the integrands with insertions (`Display.pages`, `Display.tucked`, `Curated.lean:34, 66`); source read by the adapting and reviewing agents, not traced to the final theorem.
*Across chapters:* chapters 9 and 11 (11R). Neither Assumption `ch09:forest-assumption` nor Hypothesis (H) is proved in the monograph (`chapters/09-forest-average.tex`:923–925; 11:19, 336). The status paragraph of `chapters/09-forest-average.tex`:963–967 still says that chapter 11 is "Not yet adapted"; the reviewer's replacement was not applied (`ch11-forest-review.md`). Chapter 6 does not say that its forest is averaged afterwards, and 17:164–165 uses one translated forest (`chapters/09-forest-average.tex`:969–973).
*See also:* forest; Hypothesis (H).

#### background insertion
*Now:* replaced by *background derivative* ("`b(p;k)` its first derivative in the background field, for short its first *background derivative*, and `c(p,p′;k)` its second background derivative", 7:339–340).
*Variants:* first background derivative, second background derivative; background derivatives `b`, `c` (17t:99); no longer in the text: first insertion, second insertion; background insertions `b`, `c`.
- **Meaning.** The first and second derivatives of an operator with respect to the background field: "`b(p;k)` its first derivative in the background field, for short its first *background derivative*, and `c(p,p′;k)` its second background derivative. These are exact derivatives of the same operator" (7:338–340).
  *Basis:* D (7:339–340). *Where:* 7:339–340, 387–398, 423–425, 612–621 and passim; 17t:99, 105. The former "infinitesimal gauge insertion `d`" at 17:236–237 and 17t:88 is now "infinitesimal gauge action `d`", a different object. *Adopted:* *first and second derivative in the background field* (*background derivative*).
*Literature:* no name for the derivatives of an operator in the background field; functional derivatives `δ/δB` are written out. Only the second derivative of the new term of the effective action has a name, the **vacuum polarization tensor** `Π^{ab}_{j+1,μν}(g_j,x,x′)` (B87 p. 264, (1.20): the second derivative `δ²/δB δB` of `E^{(j+1)}(g_j, U_{j+1}(exp iB))` at `0`, "This is the vacuum polarization tensor of the theory defined by the j-th fluctuation field integral"; p. 291: "The function Π is called the vacuum polarization tensor"). An analogue of the second background insertion and of the quadratic Taylor symbol of the Gaussian contribution (7:236–238, 338–340): Bałaban's `Π` is the second derivative of the whole new term `E^{(j+1)}`, not of the determinant alone. The first insertion has no counterpart. Suggested: use *vacuum polarization tensor* for the second background derivative of the one-step effective action; keep "insertion" for the operator derivatives, defined once.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 7 and 17; one name now.
*See also:* insertion; denominator.

#### backward comparison
*Now:* unchanged; its former synonyms are replaced by it ("trial descent" at 13:241; 17m:458, 466; "descending graph" at 17m:441; "bulk descent bound" at 11E:124; "Descent" at 11:948).
*Also in the text for:* the former *descent*; *trial descent* (see those entries).
*Variants:* backward comparison of a local trial (title, 11:893); no longer in the text: descent; trial descent; bulk descent bound (the remaining "descent" is in labels such as `ch11:trial-descent`, and 7:1200 "a quantitative descent" is unrelated).
- **Meaning.** The transfer of the trial at the ultraviolet cutoff (a local function at the fine end, compared with a normalized local insertion) down the block steps, which gives the decay `c_i + |x_i| ≤ 4(1 + C_N) w e^{−(τ_N − τ_i)/8}` (11:916–918). It is not a downward induction: the induction on the cone condition "starts at the coarsest scale with zero coefficient" (11:912) and runs upward (`A_{i+1}|x_{i+1}| ≤ c_{i+1}`, 11:911).
  *Basis:* R (11:893–920). *Where:* 11:27, 893, 948; 11E:120, 124; 13:241; 13ba:170 ("Transfer this whole polynomial down to `m`"); 17m:441, 458, 466, 467; 18lp:34. *Adopted:* keep *backward comparison* as the name of the argument. *Proposed:* define it once as *transfer of the trial at the ultraviolet cutoff down the block steps*; cite it by section number in chapters 13 and 17.
*Across chapters:* one sense and one name; chapters 13, 17 and 18lp say "the backward comparison". 11:893–920 describes the operation explicitly; "graph" is kept ("the graph of the backward comparison", 17m:441).
*See also:* descent; trial; bottom.

#### `Bad_m(U)`
*Now:* unchanged (a symbol); 4:469 now names it "the *large-field set* of `U`", and 4:470–472 states the regularity condition on its complement.
*Variants:* `Bad_m`.
- **Meaning.** The set of sites incident to a plaquette with `χ > t_m`; it is determined by the configuration `U`.
  *Basis:* D (4:469). *Where:* 4:469; 9:647, 884. *Adopted:* *large-field set of `U`*.
*Literature:* **large field region** (B85e p. 257, (7): the set `P` of plaquettes with `|U(∂p) − 1| ≥ ε_1`; p. 273: "small factors connected with large fields regions P"; B88b p. 244: "Consider a large plaquette variable in the first step"; p. 246, (1.1): the cubes where `sup_{p ⊂ □~} |U(∂p) − 1| ≥ ε_0`; D2 p. 092301-2: "ζ(Ω_1^c, …) is the characteristic function of fields which violate at least one of these inequalities at some point in each cube", regions `Λ_k^c`, `Ω_k^c`); **large field domain** (B95 p. 109; B88b p. 252). Its complement, v3's small-field condition `X ∩ Bad_m(U) = ∅` (`h_X`, 4:468–472), is the **small field region** or **small field domain** (B87 p. 254: "functions restricted to small field regions, which in this case means that … are restricted to regular configurations U, i.e. configurations satisfying bounds |U(∂p) − 1| < ε_0"; B85e p. 266; D1 p. 1330010-17: "Our small field assumption is chosen so that when it is violated either … is tiny"; D2 p. 092301-23: "a definition of local small field region"), and in B85a, B85b the **regularity condition** on plaquette variables, never "small field" (B85a p. 26, (52): "we have to assume that `|U(∂p) − 1| < α_0η²`, η = L^{-k}"; B85b p. 75: "The regularity conditions (0.1) are the most fundamental conditions we impose on gauge field configurations. They are invariant with respect to gauge transformations"). The small-field condition is the same object in form, a gauge-invariant bound on plaquette variables in units of the current lattice; `Bad_m(U)` itself is an analogue: Bałaban's set is a set of plaquettes or of cubes of side `LM_2R`, tested from the second step on on the local minimiser `U_{k,□}(V_k)` and not on the field (B88b (1.4), (2.17)), and Dimock's region is a union of `M`-cubes enlarged by `5[r_k]` layers and summed over; v3's is a set of sites determined by `U`, neither enlarged nor summed over. In the literature the large field region also contains the places where a fluctuation-field bound fails (see *cutoff failure*); `Bad_m(U)` does not. Bałaban's spaces of regular configurations `𝔘_k({Ω_j}, α_0)` (B85b p. 77) carry a nested sequence of domains with scale-dependent bounds and a second condition (1.9) on `D*∂U`; v3's small-field set is one scale, one condition. Adopted (23 November 2026): *large-field set of `U`* (it agrees with usage; add "not enlarged or summed over"); for its complement, *regularity condition* (on plaquette variables), Bałaban's word, in place of "small-field condition", and *small-field region* where the region is meant; a configuration satisfying the condition is a "regular configuration" in Bałaban. v3's condition is at one scale and is a single inequality: to be stated once.
*Across chapters:* one sense. To be kept distinct from the large-field index triple `A` of chapter 6 (a selection) and from the large fluctuation-field events (formerly cutoff-failure events).
*See also:* defect (sense 1); actual (sense 7).

#### barycenter identity
*Now:* replaced by *the identity (ch15:mixture)* ("The same uniqueness argument continues the identity (ch15:mixture) from imaginary times", 16:122).
- **Meaning.** The integral representation of the undecomposed correlations over the phases, `S(w) = ∫_Ξ S^ξ(w) dν(ξ)` for every word `w` at distinct points; this is (ch15:mixture), 15:152–154. At 16:122 "The same uniqueness argument continues the identity (ch15:mixture) from imaginary times" extends it to the analytic continuations and, by (ch16:taylor-boundary), to the boundary distributions: `W_n^mix(A)(f) = ∫ W_n^ξ(A)(f) dν(ξ)`, the "`ν`-average" of 16:92.
  *Basis:* S for the former name; R for the statement (15:152–154; 16:91–92). *Where:* 16:122. *Adopted:* *the integral representation (ch15:mixture)*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/phase-selection.tex:68–72: "Equations (ex-spectral-state) and (ex-compression-values) give the barycenter identity `S(w) = ∫_Ξ S_χ(w) dμ(χ)`"; existence/assembly.tex:85–96 (Proposition "Boundary barycenter"): "the map `χ ↦ W_n^χ(v)(f)` is continuous and `W_n^mix(v)(f) = ∫_X W_n^χ(v)(f) dν(χ)`". Lean `YM.OS.Spread.Resolution.barycenter`, YM/Phase/Mixture.lean (statement read: `∫ (T i).expect q dμ(i) = S.expect q` for every word `q` at distinct points, under `Out`, which contains commutativity of the algebra, a probability measure of full support and `∫ character x p dμ = ⟨ω_0, p ω_0⟩`, and under `receives`, which says `(T i).expect w = character i (slot w)`); `YM.EveryPhase.barycenter`, YM/EveryPhase/Barycenter.lean (statement read: `∫ W^i_n(v, f) dμ(i) = W^B_n(v, f)` for joint Schwartz tests `f`).
*Across chapters:* single place; 16:122 now cites (ch15:mixture).
*See also:* mixed; phase.

"Block averages" stood in the subsection title "Difference-preserving block averages" (17t:12), for the linear averages `M_a` of 17t:22–29, until 26 November 2026; the title is now "Base-point averages and fine and coarse differences" (decision on titles).
*Variants:* `Q_e(U)`, `Q_e^pred`; derivative of the averaging operation (7:483); (in labels and in the superscript only) predictor; block averages (title, 17t:12); no longer in the text: gauge-covariant block average; block average derivative; block average discrepancy; straight average (the phrase "straight length-`L` average" remains at 5:1003 as a gloss, and "the straight length-`L` link sums" at 6:379).
1. **Gauge-covariant block average.** The group-valued average `Q_e(U)` of the fine links attached to a coarse edge, constructed in chapter 4 (`Q_e^pred`, 4:214–223: on one branch the unique minimiser, "The value of the averaging operation is then unique, independently of the number of transporters or the weights", 4:218–219; otherwise a transporter `Y_{e,z}`, the index taking the value `z`), and used as "the value `Q(U)` of the averaging operation of Chapter 4" (6:43). Its linearisation is `𝒬a = Ma + d_{0,c}Ra` (5:996–1000). It is nonlinear and gauge covariant; objects built with it are now said to be "built with the averaging operation" (formerly "actual", that word's sense 3).
   *Basis:* R (4:214–223; 6:43; 5:996–1000). *Where:* "averaging operation" at 4:218, 271, 323, 327, 430–435; 5:857, 915, 996, 1316; 6:43, 166, 366, 485, 497, 1561; 7:483, 509–512, 532–533, 585; 9:915; 17c:162, 361–362; 17t:160–161, and the other lines formerly listed (5:934, 1010, 1088, 1128, 1246, 1301, 1323, 1333; 6:170, 450, 508; 9s:196; 11R:248; 13ba; 17m), where the sentence now names the averaging operation, its linearization `𝒬`, the block axial chart or gauge, or the critical configuration. *Adopted:* *averaging operation*, with its symbol `Q_e(U)`; *its linearization* for `𝒬`. *Proposed:* say once that it is an analogue of Bałaban's averaging operation `Ū`, not the same map (the nearest group point to a weighted mean, where Bałaban takes the exponential of a mean of logarithms); rename the superscript `pred`.
2. **Straight (linear) average.** The linear average `M` without the gradient correction: "Here `M` is exactly the linear averaging operator, the straight length-`L` average with the averaging weights used in (ch05:alias-recursion)" (5:1003–1004).
   *Basis:* D (5:1003). *Where:* 5:535 ("`Q` is the linear averaging operator of this construction"), 859, 993, 1084 ("built with the linear averaging operator `M`"); 7:645–649, 679, 702, 718–722, 1125, 1167; 17c:278, 281; 17m:221, 274. *Adopted:* *linear averaging operator `M`*.
*Literature:* **averaging operation** `Ū` (B85a p. 19: "The most important part of the above definition is an averaging operation Ū. It transforms a configuration U defined on Ω^(j) into a configuration Ū defined on Ω^(j+1)"; **one-step averaging operation**, B85a p. 23, (15) = (42), `Ū_c = exp[i Σ_{x∈B(c_-)} L^{-d} (1/i) log U(Γ_{c,x})U(c)^{-1}] U(c)`; B87 p. 252: "Renormalization transformations are defined by averaging operations", (0.4), (0.12); B85c p. 392: "They are compositions of `j` one-step averaging operations"); **averaging operator** `Q`, `Q_k` for the linear map (B84a p. 19, (1.11): "We may define the averaging operation as given by `Q` directly"; B84b p. 223; D1 p. 1330010-4: "First we define averaging operators", §2.1 "Block averaging"; BIJ85 pp. 302–304: "The average (2.10) is highly nonlinear"); **linear averaging operation** `Ā_c` with **main term** `Q_0A` (B85a p. 19, (14); p. 36, (125)). Sense 1 (the group-valued `Q_e(U)`, `Q_e^pred`) is an analogue: the same role and the same two requirements (gauge covariance, B85a (11); linearisation equal to the linear average), but a different definition: Bałaban takes the exponential of the uniform block mean of the logarithms of `U(Γ_{c,x})U(c)^{-1}`, times `U(c)`, with one fixed contour system, uniform weight `L^{-d}` on one corner-based block, and a single deterministic formula ("we may use many other definitions", B87 p. 254); v3 takes the nearest group point to a weighted Euclidean mean, with a `j`-fold convolution weight on centred blocks, frames, and a second (random) branch. The linearisation `𝒬a = Ma + d_{0,c}Ra` is an analogue of the first form of the averaging operation, B84a pp. 18–19, (1.8), and of `Q_j(U)`, "a linear part of the function (3.13)" (B85c pp. 392–393), with fixed axial contours in place of v3's frames. Sense 2 (the straight average `M`) is the same object for smoothing order `j = 1`, up to the factor `L^{-1}` (B84a (1.11) averages along the line with weight `L^{-(d+1)}`, v3 sums, 5:157) and up to cornered against centred blocks; for `j > 1` it is an analogue. The identification of `M` with the main term (125) of B85a is an inference and was not computed. Calling `Q^pred` "Bałaban's averaging operation" without qualification would be wrong; "a gauge-covariant averaging operation in the sense of B85a (11)" is right. "Predictor" has no precedent. Adopted (23 November 2026): *averaging operation* for the nonlinear gauge-covariant `Q_e(U)`, said once to be an analogue of Bałaban's `Ū` (B85a (15), B87 (0.4), (0.12)): nearest-point projection of a weighted mean against the exponential of a mean of logarithms; *linear averaging operator* for the linear one (`M`; `Q` at 5:535), with "for `j = 1` it is `L` times Bałaban's `Q` of B84a (1.11)". The decision does not name the linearisation `𝒬`; the suggestion for it was *linearised (gauge-covariant) averaging operator*.
*Across chapters:* the two averages are now kept apart by the nouns: *averaging operation* (nonlinear) and *linear averaging operator* (`M`). The letters are not stable: `Q` is an abstract block map at 5:87 ("a linear averaging operator", 5:88), "the linear averaging operator of this construction" at 5:535 (which is `M` at 5:156 and 5:1003) and the value of the nonlinear averaging operation at 6:43; `𝒜` is used at 6:375–379; `H` is "the derivative of the averaging operation" at 7:483. "Predictor" occurs in the chapters only in label names (`ch04:predictor-*`) and in the superscript of `Q^pred`. Of the former noun piles, 17c:162 and 17t:160–161 now read normally; 17c:361–362 reads "within the patches of the averaging operation and of the base-point average", naming the patches of the two kernels `M_{ef}` and `K_0` of the bound above it. Text read at 4:212–223, 5:996–1004, 6:41–47.
*See also:* `Q^pred`; straight; actual; block-average patch; connector; mismatch; discrepancy; stationary tangent; contact term.

#### block bridge
*Now:* replaced by *linearization of the critical configuration* ("One must use the same linearization of the critical configuration, clipping data and critical-configuration map", 10:924–925).
- **Meaning.** The linear coarse-to-fine map `W` of one block step, i.e. the solution of the two matching equations `K_f W = 𝒬^* K_c`, `𝒬 W = I − b^{-1} K_c` (v3 5:1094–1102 for `W_s` with the straight average `M`; `W_a = W_s − d_{0,f} E R W_s`, 5:1117–1120, for the block mean `𝒬 = M + d_{0,c}R`), with the bound `L^{-1-r}` on `r` fine differences, (ch05:actual-bridge) (5:1138–1143). At 10:924 the text now says "One must use the same linearization of the critical configuration, clipping data and critical-configuration map": the auxiliary zero-array histories use this same map. The word survives in prose only in "Background smooth bridge legs" (7:606, formerly "External …") and in the label `ch05:actual-bridge`.
  *Basis:* S; I for the representative `W_a` rather than `W_s` (it follows from the block mean used in the step and from the label of the bound, not from a sentence; 10:924 does not name the representative). *Where:* 10:924. *Adopted:* the book-wide *linearization `W` of the critical configuration*. *Proposed:* name the representative `W_a` at 10:924.
  *Source:* Martin existence/selected-history-limits.tex:378–383 ("the auxiliary torus …, carrying the same block bridge, the same two paths and clips") and :447–449; existence/quadratic-pole-transport.tex:21, 33–37 ("the installed linear bridge `W`"; "The bridge `Φ` is holomorphic and periodic on the strip … and is the common Fourier representation of the installed matrices `W_i`, which satisfy both matching equations … with block mean `Q_i` and penalty coefficient `κ`"); existence/inherited-loop-transport.tex:162–165 (`K_{f,i}W_i = Q_i^T K_{c,i}`, `Q_iW_i = I − κ^{-1}K_{c,i}`); existence/classical-stationary-vertices.tex:37–42 (`sup_z|∇^jΦ(p)e_a(z)| ≤ Dμ^{1+j}`). Lean `YM.Stationary.Bridge` (YM/Next/STATIONARY/Shape/Shim.lean:27; definition read: a matrix-valued function of the momentum), `YM.Stationary.Cruise` (YM/Next/STATIONARY/Shape/Vertex.lean:83; definition read: `‖∇^l K(p)e_i‖ ≤ L^{-(1+|l|)}C` for `|l| ≤ n` on the strip), `YM.Stationary.primalV`, `YM.Stationary.secondV` (YM/Next/STATIONARY/Loops/HessianMatch.lean:300–301; definitions read: the two matching equations in momentum space), `YM.Stationary.actor_duo` (same file; statement read), `YM.Stationary.Premise` (YM/Next/STATIONARY/Films/Routing.lean:449; definition read, its constituent `Jaunt` not unfolded).
*Across chapters:* one reading. The correspondence of the source "bridge" with v3's `W` rests on the matching equations and on the shared bound; it is not the forest representative `W_F`.
*See also:* bridge legs; actual stationary tangent.

#### block-completed form
*Now:* replaced by *the kinetic form with the penalty term added* ("The kinetic form with the penalty term added, the form `𝒢` below, needs a quotient estimate", 7:696–697); "the blocked completed matrix `C_0`" remains at 7:783.
*Variants:* blocked completed matrix `C_0` (7:783); no longer in the text: block-completed form `𝒢`.
- **Meaning.** The kinetic form completed by the penalty term, `𝒢(u,r) = ⟨u, K_f u⟩ + b|Mu − d_{0,c} r|²`. It is still gauge-degenerate ("The kinetic form with the penalty term added, the form `𝒢` below, needs a quotient estimate", 7:696–697); the gauge term is added afterwards ("a positive weighted lower bound for `𝒢 + F*F`", 7:738–739). The matrix `C_0` of 7:783 appears to contain both completions (inferred).
  *Basis:* D (7:696–700); I (7:783). *Where:* 7:696–700, 738–739, 783. *Adopted:* *the form `⟨u, K_f u⟩ + b|Mu − d_{0,c} r|²`* (kinetic form plus penalty term); not "gauge-fixed operator", and the penalty term is not a "gauge-fixing term".
*Literature:* the operator **`Δ_a`** and its inverse **`G`, `G_k`** ("Operators `G`"), the **propagators**; without the gauge term `Δ + aQ*Q`, with inverse `G_0` (B84a pp. 29–30, Sect. E, (1.68)–(1.69); p. 17: "they define propagators, i.e. covariances of the Gaussian measure defined by these terms"; p. 39: "`G_0 = (Δ + aQ*Q)^{-1}`"). An analogue of `𝒢` and of the matrix `A = K_f + bQ*Q` (5:89–91): the formulas are identical, but in v3 `A^{-1}` is the fluctuation covariance (5:99–106), while in Bałaban `G` is an auxiliary Green's function and the fluctuation covariance is the constrained one, the **unit lattice propagator** (see *window*). In D1 the composite operator `a_kG_kQ_k^T` contains the same `G_k`. Suggested: *the form `⟨u,K_fu⟩ + b|Mu − d r|²`* stands; add "the soft-constraint counterpart of Bałaban's `Δ_a`; its inverse corresponds to his `G_k`".
*Across chapters:* chapter 7 only.
*See also:* block penalty; completed.

#### block length
*Now:* not applied.
*Variants:* length (11E:31–32).
- **Meaning.** The block ratio `L`: "These quantities are fixed before the block length" (11E:20); "then the length, then the lower bound on the reference coupling" (11E:31–32); "The choices of Chapter 10 select all block lengths, derivative orders" (19:18–19). At 11:1878 ("Choose the block length after `A_{2D}` and then `v`") the same reading is probable: the product error "over `m` steps" is `m H^{−v} A_{2D}^m`, the number of steps is `m = ⌈(b+2) log H / log L⌉` (11:1765, 1958), and a large `L` makes `A_{2D}^m` a small power of `H`; the alternative reading, the number of steps `m`, is not excluded by the sentence itself.
  *Basis:* I (11E:20, 31–32; 11:1878). *Where:* 11E:20, 31–32, 112; 11:1878; 17w:42 ("the logarithmic block length", `log L_i`); 19:19. *Proposed:* *block ratio `L`*.
*Across chapters:* one sense; the reading at 11:1878 is an inference.
*See also:* block floor.

#### block penalty
*Now:* replaced by *penalty parameter* (sense 1, defined at 4:239); *penalty term* (sense 2).
*Variants:* penalty parameter (MT:12; 1:409, 420; 4:239; 5:88, 102; 6:21; 7:583; 19:17); penalty term; penalty (5:103, "has penalty `bβ`"); no longer in the text: block penalty; block parameter; soft-block penalty `b`; soft constraint, soft constraint coefficient.
1. **The constant `b > 0`** of the block kernel `q_{bβ}` (4:239, 271), which in the normalised Gaussian form of chapter 5 is the weight `exp(−(b/2)‖Qa − v‖²)` (5:87–103): "Fix the *penalty parameter* `b > 0` of the block kernel" (4:239); "`b > 0` the penalty parameter" (5:88); "Thus the penalty parameter remains `b` after normalization, although the original block kernel has penalty `bβ`" (5:102–103); "the penalty parameter `b > 0`" (6:21).
   *Basis:* D (4:239). *Where:* 1:409, 420; 4:239; 5:88, 102–103, 312; 6:21; 7:583; 10:408; MT:12; 19:17, 147 (6:128 now says "the penalty term"). *Adopted:* *the penalty parameter `b`* (the phrase of the main theorem, MT:12), one phrase in every chapter.
2. **The penalty term itself,** the function `(b/2)‖Qa − v‖²` in the exponent of the block kernel: "the fine action at the critical configuration together with its penalty term is exactly the coarse quadratic action" (5:145–146); "Let `r(x)` be the derivative of the penalty term with respect to that increment of the averaging operation" (7:532–533); the joint action "contains the fine kinetic action and the penalty term built with the averaging operation" (7:883–884); "In the penalty term, simultaneous left multiplication … leaves the penalty term unchanged" (17c:289–291). Its Hessian is the matrix `B` ("`B` for the Hessian of its penalty term", 7:483, entering as `H*BH`).
   *Basis:* R (7:532–533, 883–885). *Where:* 1:409; 5:146; 6:128; 7:483, 532, 884, 1061; 9s:39 ("the penalty term of the block kernel"); 17c:289–291; "penalty gradient" (7:547) and "penalty vertices" (7:923). *Adopted:* *penalty term of the block kernel* (a different object from the penalty parameter `b`).
*Literature:* see *penalty parameter*.
*Across chapters:* the two objects now have two names throughout: *penalty parameter* for the constant (chapters 1, 4–7, 10, 19 and the main theorem), *penalty term* for the function (5:146, chapters 7 and 9s, 17c:289–291). 4:239 adds that Bałaban's transformations have a delta function in place of the densities `q_{bβ}`.
*See also:* block-completed form; soft constraint.

#### `B_n`
*Now:* unchanged.
- **Meaning.** One letter for two radii in chapter 17. At 17m:429–435 (and `B_k` at 17m:332, 413) it is the support radius `B_m = ⌈(log β̂_m)²⌉` of the original representation (4:457): "`B_n = O((log β̂_n)²)`" (17m:435). At 17w:33 it is "the radius of the restarted representation", `B_i = b(x_i)²` with `b(x) = ⌈(log x)²⌉` (11R:15–18). Chapter 11 warns that these differ: "The original insertion norm uses radius `M`, whereas the restarted representation uses radius `B`. These are different radii" (11:1157–1162).
  *Basis:* R (4:457; 17m:435; 17w:33; 11R:18). *Where:* 17m:332, 413, 429–435; 17w:33–34. *Proposed:* two symbols.

Lean `YM.Pressure.radiusB x := ⌈(log x)²⌉`, `YM/Pressure/Seeds.lean` (definition read). The arithmetic `L_*⁴ B_n⁸ q_n = O((log β̂_n)²²)` at 17m:433 requires `B_n = O((log β̂_n)²)`.
*Across chapters:* two radii under one letter: 17m:435 is the chapter 4 radius and 17w:33 names the restarted radius.
*See also:* restart.

#### bottom
*Now:* replaced by *coarsest scale* ("the residual coefficient at the coarsest scale", 11:899; "The induction starts at the coarsest scale", 11:912; "the stage of the coarsest scale of the interval of scales", 17w:97) and *coarse endpoint* (10:853).

- **Meaning.** The lowest (coarsest) level of the range of scales considered: "common coarse endpoint" (10:853), "the residual coefficient at the coarsest scale" (11:899), "The induction starts at the coarsest scale" (11:912). At 17w:97–98 ("The lower bound on the partition function is imposed at the stage of the coarsest scale of the interval of scales, with its constant at most `I`; it is not multiplied once per step") the estimate is the lower bound on the partition function (the positive-density ratio bound), applied once, at the coarsest level `k` of the window, with the constant of the stage `J_k` to which that level belongs. #### bounded approximations
*Now:* partly replaced by citation of *Proposition (13.bounded-singleton) and Corollary (13.bounded-word)* (19:50); "the real approximation" remains at 19:100, "the bounded-real approximation" at 13ba:308, "bounded real approximation" at 15:188 and in the section title "Bounded real approximations for separated words" (13ba:2).
*Variants:* real approximation (19:100); bounded-real approximation (13ba:308).
- **Meaning.** Real lattice observables `𝓑_{N,p}(c,y)`, bounded uniformly in the cutoff `N`, the period index `p` and the position `y`, that approximate a normalized local insertion `O_{N,p}(d,c;y)` to within `δ` in the chessboard seminorm of a fixed cell tiling, on the ordered cutoff and volume tails: Proposition "Coarse bounded approximation" (13.bounded-singleton), 13ba:201–213. "The real approximation" (19:100) is its consequence for differences of words, Corollary "Real word differences" (13.bounded-word), 13ba:306–311 ("the bounded-real approximation used for phase reflection in Section `ch15:phase-symmetry`").
  *Basis:* R (19:50 cites the proposition and corollary; 13ba:201–213); I for 19:100 (13ba:306–311). *Where:* 19:50 (by number), 99. *Adopted:* *Proposition (13.bounded-singleton) and Corollary (13.bounded-word)*, cited by number (at 19:50, not at 19:100).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/E-bounded-real.tex:4–10`, Lemma "Bounded coarse approximations" (`lem:E-coarse-bounded`): "For every `d`, `k ≥ …`, real `c ∈ V_d` and `δ > 0`, there are measurable real observables `𝓑_{N,p}(c,y)` and `M_bnd < ∞`, independent of `N,p,y`, with `|𝓑_{N,p}(c,y)| ≤ M_bnd` and `‖𝓑_{N,p}(c,y) − O^{(d)}_{N,p}(c,y)‖_{𝒞^tile_k(y)} ≤ δ` eventually in the ordered limits." No Lean declaration was identified.
*Across chapters:* chapter 19 only as a nickname, now only at 19:100; the results are in `13ba`.
*See also:* annular estimates; trial.

*Now:* partly replaced by *critical configuration* / *critical-configuration map* (sense 2, at all its places); "fallback branch" is now "alternative branch" (4:434); sense 1 keeps "branch" (proposal *case* not applied), sense 3 unchanged.

Adopted (23 November 2026): keep v3's defined sense (13:337); never gloss *halo* as "buffer".

#### centered
*Now:* partly replaced by *zero-mean* (sense 1, at its places in chapters 3, 5, 6, 9, 14, 17 and 19) and by explicit differences in sense 6 (5:1351; 9s:291–292; and, since 26 November 2026, 9:295: "The resulting bound, for the left side of (ch09:pure-decomposition) in Section (ch09:stationary-remainder) below minus its value at the flat configuration"); remains in sense 1 for Gaussians at 10:733 ("a centered Gaussian variable") and 11:550 ("a centered joint Gaussian array") and at 19:119 ("be the centered trace", the trace minus its expectation), in senses 2–5, and at 9:127 (sense 6) (grep).
*Variants:* center (13 occurrences); recentering (7:515, 590, 652; 9:351; 18lp:42); no longer in the text: centred; center, centers as verbs at 14:286, 288 (now "subtract expectations").
1. **Zero-mean.** "Zero-mean means that each component has zero expectation" (14:268–269); of Gaussians and of tensors, e.g. "zero-mean degree-four symmetric … tensors" (17:163).
   *Basis:* D (14:268; also 3:580–585). *Where:* "zero-mean" or "zero mean" at 3:580–584; 5:127; 6:857; 9:776; 14:266, 268, 307, 1011, 1026; 17:23, 44, 163, 292, 353, 392, 404, 411; 19:126; "centered" for a Gaussian still at 10:733; 11:550. *Adopted:* *zero-mean*; *with zero expectation*.
2. **Placed about a point, or symmetric about the origin or the block centre** (the ordinary geometric sense). About `x₀` (3:699) or the anchor `o_i` (4:671); symmetric blocks and kernels ("Odd block ratios give centered blocks", 1:217; "centered level-`(m+1)` block", 18lp:224).
   *Basis:* R (1:217). *Where:* 1:183, 217; 2:188, 285; 3:699; 4:671; 5:202, 307, 341, 919; 7:414, 712; 18lp:224. *Proposed:* *centered at `x₀`*; *symmetric*.
3. **Normalised representative.** At 4:141 the text now says what was meant by "Center two minimizers": "Multiply two minimizers `h,k` on the left in this way, so that `1` is nearest to each centroid" (4:129–130, 141). In chapter 7 "centered coordinates" are `r = r_root − Ru`, the frame normalised in the mean by `Σ_x ω(x) Π F_x = Π 1`, as opposed to the rooted coordinates `Q = M + d_{0,c}R` with scalar `r_root`; "recentering" is the passage to them.
   *Basis:* R (4:129–141; 7:664–665, 702–704). *Where:* 7:513–709, 893, 924 (4:141 no longer has the word); recentering 7:515, 590, 652. *Proposed:* *normalized*; *frame normalized in the mean*.
4. **Lying well inside a cell of the tiling.** "Centered cell / scale / seminorm / tiling / chessboard estimate": the bound holds when the insertion lies in a cell at distance at least the margin `3a_k` from its boundary ("if the centered local bounds apply at scale `k` with margin `3a_k`", 13:89–90). Never defined as a term, here or in chapters 1 and 11.
   *Basis:* I (13:89–90). *Where:* 13:89, 100, 303, 316, 348, 363, 374, 384, 397; 13sb:103, 122, 160; 13ba:30, 127, 204, 316 (16 uses). *Proposed:* *seminorm for an insertion at distance at least `3a_k` from the cell boundary*; define once.
5. **Centred difference** (standard).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 12:391; 14:439; 17t:17; 17c:30. *Proposed:* keep.
6. **With the value at the flat (zero) configuration subtracted.** Three uses, all of this kind.
   (a) The former "centered log determinant" (5:1350, now "the log determinant of its vertical Hessian, with its value at `v = 0` subtracted", 5:1350–1351): `log det A(x) − log det A(0)` for the vertical Hessian `A(x) = D_y²φ(x, ρ(x))`; see *centered log determinant*.
   (b) "Centered determinant variation" (9:127, a row of the table of local factors): the determinant factor with its flat value subtracted, and also the quadratic term that has already been assigned to `α𝒬`.
   (c) The former "centered auxiliary bound" (9:295, since 26 November 2026 "for the left side of (ch09:pure-decomposition) … minus its value at the flat configuration") and the former "centered expression in (ch09:pure-decomposition)" (9s:291, now "the left side of (ch09:pure-decomposition) minus its value at zero", 9s:291–292): the corrected logarithm `G = log 𝒵 + β′a_c + d_c` with its value at zero subtracted, `G − G(0)`; the bound `P_j(𝔟){𝔟^{-1}h + 𝔟h⁵ + h³}` of 9:295–298 is the bound (ch09:pure-small-bound) for `G − G(0)` on the ball of radius `h`.
   *Basis:* S; R from the v3 text for (a) (5:1351), 9s:291–292 and, since 26 November 2026, 9:295; I for (b). *Where:* 5:1351; 9:127, 295; 9s:241 (title "Centering the full logarithm"), 283–284. *Proposed:* write the difference explicitly (applied at 5:1351, 9s:291–292 and 9:295, the last by the decision of 26 November 2026; not at 9:127).
   *Source:* (a) Martin `existence/uniform-stationary-chart.tex:193–198` "`D log det M[h] = tr(M^{-1}DM[h])` … polynomial bounds for every positive derivative of `log det M` through order `N−2`. Its centered value is bounded by integrating the first derivative"; `existence/truncated-stationary-log.tex:23, 40–41` ("the relative log determinant"; "Put `s(x) = ½ log det M(x)` and `A(b,x,z) = s(x) − s(0) + …`"). (b) Scott `part2/D-section.tex:153` (row "centered determinant remainder") and `:162` "For the determinant, subtract its flat value and the quadratic term already assigned to `α_{N,m}𝒬_m`. The inverse identity bounds the remaining variation by `P_j(t_{m+1}+g)`." (c) Martin `existence/pure-action-small-field.tex:187–197`: "the centered stationary logarithm has bound `ah` at scale `h^{-1}`, by integrating its first derivative … The centered error has bound `2v`. … `G − G(0) ∈ 𝓑_j(ah + 2v + βK_C h⁵ + K_W h³ + 3{(a+v)h + qh²}, h^{-1})`" (pure-remainder-budget).
*Across chapters:* sense 1 is now *zero-mean* except for the two Gaussians at 10:733 and 11:550 and "the centered trace" at 19:119; "centered" keeps senses 2–3 in chapters 1–7, sense 4 in chapter 13, sense 5 in chapters 12, 14, 17, and sense 6 at 9:127 and in the title 9s:241. "Recentering" has two further uses outside these senses: translation of the reflection cube (9:351) and subtraction of the output column (18lp:42). 9s:291–292 now writes the difference ("minus its value at zero").
*See also:* cell; centered log determinant; corrected logarithm; conserved line; rooted coordinates.

#### centered log determinant
*Now:* replaced by the formula in words: "the log determinant of its vertical Hessian, with its value at `v = 0` subtracted" (5:1350–1351).
*Variants:* centered determinant variation (9:127); relative log determinant (source).
- **Meaning.** The logarithm of the determinant of the vertical Hessian of the stationary graph, `A(x) = D_y²φ(x, ρ(x))`, with its value at the base point subtracted: `log det A(x) − log det A(0)`, which is twice the `s(x) − s(0)`, `s = ½ log det A`, of 9s:51, 64. Its derivatives through order `N − 2` are bounded by polynomials in the coordinate number (5:1349–1352); the derivatives of positive order are those of `log det A`, and the value of the difference is bounded by integrating the first derivative.
  *Basis:* D (5:1350–1351, "the log determinant of its vertical Hessian, with its value at `v = 0` subtracted"); R for `s(x) − s(0)` (9s:51, 64). *Where:* 5:1350–1351; 9:127; 9s:51, 64. Does not occur in chapters 10–19. *Adopted:* *`log det A(x) − log det A(0)`*, said in words at 5:1351.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/uniform-stationary-chart.tex:193–199`: "`D log det M[h] = tr(M^{-1}DM[h])`. Repeated product differentiation and `|tr A| ≤ W‖A‖` give polynomial bounds for every positive derivative of `log det M` through order `N−2`. Its centered value is bounded by integrating the first derivative. Its uncentered value is bounded too"; `:231` "through order `n+1` for the relative log determinant"; `existence/truncated-stationary-log.tex:40–42` "Put `s(x) = ½ log det M(x)` and `A(b,x,z) = s(x) − s(0) + V(0,0,z) − V(b,x,z) + …`". Martin's `M(x) = D_y²φ(x, ρ(x))` is v3's `A(x)`.
*Literature:* **`log Z^{(j)}(U_k) − log Z^{(j)}(1)`** (B87 p. 260, (1.3)–(1.4): "the factor Z^{(j)}(U_k) is given by the Gaussian integral normalizing the Gaussian measure for a fluctuation field in j-th step integration"; B85e p. 265: "we normalize log Z^{(0)}(Ω_1,U_1) subtracting and adding the term log Z^{(0)}(Ω_1,1)"). An analogue: the same subtraction at the trivial background, for a different matrix (Bałaban's is the gauge-fixed fluctuation covariance on the constraint surface). Suggested: *normalized fluctuation determinant `log Z(U) − log Z(1)`* next to the formula.
*Across chapters:* chapters 5, 9 and 9s only; no occurrence in chapters 12–16. Not `log det H(v) − log det H(0)`: 5:1350–1351 names the vertical Hessian, so the matrix is `A`, not the two-form operator `H` (text read). The "centered determinant variation" of 9:127 is a different subtraction (flat value and the quadratic term assigned to `α𝒬`); see *centered* (sense 6).
*See also:* centered (sense 6).

#### chart
*Now:* unchanged; of its compounds, "forest chart" and "tree chart" are replaced by *block axial chart* (5:934, defined there), "stationary chart" by *chart for the critical configuration* (5:1333; 7:877), "ordinary chart" by *small-field chart* (10:97; 13ba:37).
*Variants:* block axial chart; logarithmic chart; exponential chart; protected chart; local chart; small-field chart; common chart; safe chart; chart cutoff; chart indicators; chart condition; chart velocity; no longer in the text: forest chart; tree chart; ordinary chart; stationary chart.
- **Meaning.** The standard sense: local coordinates on a set of gauge configurations, together with the set on which they are valid. The word is not house vocabulary; what varies is which chart is meant, and this is seldom said. The charts that occur are: (a) the block axial chart `U(v,ψ)_e = exp((ι_Fψ)_e)(rep exp v)_e`, "the chart of the block axial gauge (the gauge in which the links of the chosen spanning tree of each block equal the identity)", "a chart on this gauge slice, not a choice of independent variables on tree edges" (5:934–941; "the same block axial chart", 6:1519; "block axial charts", 11R:248); (b) the logarithmic (exponential) chart, the Lie-algebra coordinates of the links near a base field ("Within a protected logarithmic chart define `u_V(e) = log(…)`", 6:701–702; "supported strictly inside the logarithmic chart, equal to one on the smaller chart used for Taylor extraction", 17m:41–42; the moving left-exponential charts of 17t:182–254), with its smooth "chart cutoff" (6:1024, 1357) and its "chart indicators" (6:677; 11R:284); (c) the chart for the critical configuration ("Uniform chart for the critical configuration", 5:1333), the product neighbourhood on which the critical-configuration map exists (5:1333–1347); (d) the "safe chart" of 9s:144–146: the set of fine configurations `U = 𝒟_x(y)`, `𝒟_x(y)_i = exp(y_i) V(x)^rep_i`, whose coarse and fine coordinates satisfy `max(‖x‖_∞, ‖y‖_∞) ≤ r_s` for a fixed radius `r_s` (the "safe coordinate radius"); it is chart (a) restricted to a closed coordinate ball, and "the common chart" of 9s:226 is this set, the same for all coarse configurations `x` and all values of the auxiliary index; it is now named at 9s:145 ("a fixed closed coordinate ball of the chart, the *safe chart*"); (e) the "small-field chart" on which the small-field cutoff equals one ("On that chart the indicator of the relaxed regularity condition is one", 10:97–98; also 10:753; 13ba:37; 17m:89, 173).
  *Basis:* D for (a) (5:934–941); R for (b) (6:701–702; 17m:41–42) and (c) (5:1333–1347); D for the name in (d) (9s:145), S for "the common chart"; R for (e) (10:97–98), which is not otherwise defined. *Where:* 5:934–962, 1071, 1088, 1333, 1346; 6:363, 677–679, 701, 1024, 1285, 1298, 1357, 1519–1530; 7:241, 877, 1216; 9s:43, 131, 145–153, 218–226, 237; 10:97–98, 716, 740, 746, 753, 769; 11R:44, 248, 284, 310; 13ba:37; 17m:41–45, 89, 124–125, 173; 17t:182–254, 333, 353. *Adopted:* keep (standard); *block axial chart* for the forest chart. *Proposed:* name the chart at each use (*logarithmic chart at `V_0`*, …).
  *Source:* for (d): Martin `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:14–23` ("`𝒟_x(y)_i = exp(y_i) V(x)^rep_i` … The combined chart norm is `max(‖x‖_∞, ‖y‖_∞)`"), `:81` ("On the common safe chart assume the fine Hessian satisfies `D_y²φ ≥ (γ/2)I`"), `:88–91` ("Here the safe chart is the inverse image of the closed combined coordinate supremum ball … Both endpoints lie in that chart, and its convexity contains their entire joining segment"), `:111–118` ("For a prescribed safe coordinate radius `r_s > 0`, choose `δ ≤ …`. Taking the logarithm of each relative free bond now yields `U = 𝒟_x(y)` with `‖y‖_∞ ≤ r_s`"). For the former "the common chart and tag-coincidence radius" (9s:226–227, now "The common chart and the ball on which the actions for all values of the auxiliary index with positive probability weight coincide"): `:259–262` ("The same conditions place the entire region inside the Haar chart and inside the region where all tag actions coincide") and `:282–283` ("eventually smaller than the fixed safe radii, the action-coincidence radius and one"). No Lean declaration was read for this.
*Literature:* **local coordinates** (B87 p. 258: "we introduce the local coordinates constructed in Sect. F [15] for the configurations U_k on □̃. This means that U_k = exp iηH modulo a gauge transformation"). The same object (standard) for the logarithmic small-field chart `U = exp(A)` (6:701–702). No change suggested.
*Across chapters:* one meaning, several charts. Whether (e) is the domain of (b) or a smaller set is not said (17m:41–42 distinguishes "the logarithmic chart" from "the smaller chart used for Taylor extraction"); the source manuscripts call (e) a "healthy chart" (Scott `part2/D-section.tex:208`, "On a healthy chart the link logarithm is `m_Y + gz`") without defining its domain either, so this point stays open. In "The common chart and the ball on which the actions for all values of the auxiliary index with positive probability weight coincide contain these regions" (9s:226–227) the chart is the safe chart (d), in Martin's sentence the "Haar chart" (the domain of the exponential coordinates) together with the "fixed safe radii". A chart is the domain with its coordinates, not the map defined on it: the former "stationary chart" was not a name of the critical-configuration map. The old note has no row for the bare word; this entry collects its rows for the compounds. Text read at 5:932–941, 6:700–703, 1023–1025, 9s:225–227, 10:752–754, 11R:283–285, 17m:39–43, 88–90.
*See also:* forest; safe chart; stationary chart; chart recognition; chart velocity; protected; ordinary; tag-coincidence radius; tree slice.

#### chart for the critical configuration
*Formerly:* *stationary chart*.
*In the text:* (title of 5:1333; 7:877, 1217).
- **Meaning.** The product neighbourhood, with its coordinates, on which the critical-configuration map `ρ` exists and is unique (Proposition "Uniform chart for the critical configuration", 5:1333–1347: radii `r_V, r_ψ` "such that its unique critical-configuration map `ρ` satisfies …"); "The fixed-`L` chart for the critical configuration of Chapter 5 provides existence and differentiation" (7:877–878).
  *Basis:* R (5:1333–1347). *Where:* 5:1333–1347; 7:877, 1217. *Adopted:* keep *chart* for the neighborhood; do not use it for the map.
*Literature:* no name; the counterpart is **Theorem 1** of B85d (p. 277, abstract; pp. 278–279): a unique critical orbit in "the space `𝔘_k({Ω_j},ε_0) ∩ 𝔅_k(𝔅_k,V)`" of "regular gauge field configurations with fixed averages". An analogue (existence and uniqueness of the critical point on a neighbourhood). Suggested: keep *chart*; cite B85d Theorem 1 as the counterpart.
*Across chapters:* chapters 5 and 7. Not a name of the critical-configuration map: the chart is the domain, the graph the map (5:1333–1347; 7:877–879).
*See also:* stationary graph; safe chart.

#### class modulo the tiling
*Formerly:* *residue patterns*.
*In the text:* ("the main points lie in at most `2n` classes modulo the side-`a_m` tiling", 13:368–369; "the classes modulo the tiling", 15sp:13).
- **Meaning.** The classes of the main insertion points modulo `a_mℤ⁴`, that is, their positions relative to the cells of the tiling of side `a_m`. Since the copies of the word are translates by multiples of `s`, and `s` is a multiple of `a_m`, only the `2n` classes of the points of `w` and of its reflection `θw` occur, whatever the number `j` of copies: "Since `s` is a multiple of `a_m`, the main points lie in at most `2n` classes modulo the side-`a_m` tiling, independently of `j`" (13:368–370); "The cell scales are chosen from the classes modulo the tiling and the separations of one fixed word, not from the total number of copies" (15sp:12–14). The count is used to place the cell boundaries away from all main points ("strip count").
  *Basis:* I from the v3 text (13:367–370); S, confirming the reading. *Where:* 13:369; 15sp:13. *Adopted:* *classes modulo `a_mℤ⁴`*; *positions modulo the tiling of side `a_m`* (as "classes modulo the side-`a_m` tiling").
  *Source:* Scott part2/F-infinite-volume.tex:213: "Translations by multiples of `s` preserve residues modulo `a_mℤ⁴`, so the main anchors have at most `2n` residue patterns, those of `w` and `θw`, for every `j`"; :215: "The strip count for the `2n` main residues modulo `a_m` with strip width `5a_{k_w}`". Martin existence/actual-slab-copy-bounds.tex:103–128: "Suppose the main points have only `N_0` residue patterns modulo `a_mℤ⁴` … In each coordinate, the `N_0` patterns forbid at most `N_0(10a_k)` of the possible coarse offsets when a margin of `5a_k` is required … Congruent unperturbed main patterns have identical coarse residues." No Lean declaration was traced for this term.
*Across chapters:* chapters 13 and 15sp; used with "cell" and "strip count". v3 dropped "those of `w` and `θw`" from the sentence at 13:369; it should be restored.
*See also:* cell; reflected replica cell.

#### coarse forecast
*Now:* replaced by *linear prediction of the fine curvature from the coarse field* ("One joint Gaussian sample and one linear prediction of the fine curvature from the coarse field are used for all subsets", 11:725–726).
*Variants:* parent forecast (source); no longer in the text: forecast.
- **Meaning.** The deterministic vector, indexed by the fine curvature coordinates that are read, obtained by applying a fixed linear matrix (the curvature transport of the step, i.e. the map induced on curvatures by the linear coarse-to-fine map) to the plaquette curvature of the coarse field `V` and dividing by the coupling `g`. Each normalised fine curvature coordinate is compared with (forecast) + (linear image of the joint Gaussian vector), up to a small error. "One joint Gaussian sample and one linear prediction of the fine curvature from the coarse field are used for all subsets" (11:725–726) says that this vector and the Gaussian sample are the same for every subset of insertions.
  *Basis:* S (11:725–726 names but does not give the formula). *Where:* 11:725–726. *Adopted:* *the linear prediction of the fine curvature from the coarse field*. *Proposed:* define it once by its formula, in the notation of the curvature response of 11:646–648.
  *Source:* Martin existence/actual-reader-guarded-curvature.tex:5–8 ("All comparisons use one coarse field, one gauge based at one site, one parent forecast, and one joint Gaussian sample"), :44–48 ("The parent forecast is the fixed real row `𝒫_{o,V,g'}(u,a) = (1/g') Σ_q K_{u,a;q} 𝒞_o(V)_q`"), :288 (lemma "Read error against the common parent forecast"). Lean `YM.PhysicalNext.PhysicalGuard7f546.Curved.forecast`, `.sampled`, `.wind` (YM/PhysicalNext/PHYSICAL_GUARD_7F546/Continuation/Sights.lean:31–38; definitions read), `.flow`, `.look` (…/Continuation/Psi.lean:56–63; definitions read: `flow` applies the matrix `psi` colourwise, `look` is the plaquette curvature), `.flow_spins` (Psi.lean:66; statement read: `d(low v) = flow(d v)`); the comparison `sampled − (forecast + wind)` is at …/Continuation/Measure.lean:173–176 (read). The matrix `psi` was not unfolded.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. It is a linear prediction (the mean of the Gaussian approximation), not an exact conditional expectation; the earlier guess "conditional mean" holds only to linear order. The identification of the source row `K` with the Lean matrix `psi` is by matching formulas.
*See also:* common Gaussian; response (sense 6).

#### coefficient functional
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* coefficient functionals `𝗾`, `𝗹`, `𝗵`, `𝖼`; cubic momentum (coefficient) functional.
- **Meaning.** The explicit Taylor-coefficient functionals of chapter 17: `𝗹(F)`, `𝗾(F)`, `𝗵(F)` are real parts of sums of Taylor coefficients ("including reciprocal factorials") of the Fourier transform of the second derivative of a vector `F_b` or a scalar action `F` (17:215–225), `𝖼(F)` is the correction term of `𝗵` (17t:398), and `𝔥(Y) = 𝗵(div_Haar Y)` (17:226–227). The "cubic momentum functional" of 17m:351, 356 is read as `𝔥`: it "takes values `−24, −96, 0`, while `ρ` takes values `−2, −8, 0`", after "the remaining coefficient" is identified as `𝔥(Y)/12`.
  *Basis:* D (17:215–227); I for the cubic momentum functional (17m:353–357). *Where:* 17:215–227; 17t:398; 17m:351, 356. *Proposed:* keep the symbols.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17 only. Not the "fixed common coefficient functionals" of chapter 10.
*See also:* Haar coefficient.

#### coefficient graph

The phrase is the source's: "A coefficient graph at level `m` is a linear choice `x ↦ g_m(x) = (R(x), Q(x))` of such remainders, with the supports fixed and `‖g_m(x)‖_rem ≤ C^col_{J_m}|x°|_1`" (Scott part2/E-section.tex:242). In v3 the notation is introduced only at 11:379–380 (R; "As in the graph transform for invariant manifolds, the step with insertions maps coefficient graphs at the fine scale to graphs at the coarse scale"); lines 11:347, 379, 447, 454, 468, 889, 895, 902, 914. *Graph* is kept, with *graph transform* for `G ↦ G'` (the source's own comparison, same line).   *Basis:* R (11:381–382; 12:90–92). *Where:* 11:381–382, 445–447; 12:90–92. *Proposed:* keep *coefficient map*; one symbol for `M_G` and `I_G`.
*Across chapters:* one sense; the symbol changes from `M_G` (chapter 11) to `I_G` (chapter 12). That the two are the same map is inferred from the parallel formulas `G' = R_G M_G⁻¹` and `ΦG = J_G I_G⁻¹`.

*Now:* not applied in senses 1 and 2 (the word stands at their places; at 11:1243 "normalized target columns" was replaced on 25 November 2026 by "the solutions `u=u_{j,N,p}` of the lift equations"); sense 4 is gone (11:1349 read "the one-step coefficient bounds in the direction of the transfer" from 25 November 2026, and since 26 November 2026 "the one-step bounds for the coefficient of one transferred insertion (… with the stage column bound `C_j` of Section ch10:choices)", with `D_k` stated at 11:1350); in sense 3 the alias columns of 5:581–600 are now "columns at the zero alias", "columns at each nonzero alias".

A "column bound" or "column constant" is a bound, in the `ℓ¹` norm, on this map or its inverse: "`|x| ≤ s_f |M_G x|` after fixing a suitable stage column constant `s_f`. Thus `M_G` is invertible" (11:445–446).
   *Basis:* R (18lp:26; 11:445–446); I that the bound is always an `ℓ¹` operator-norm bound. *Where:* 10:83; 11:446, 1062, 1108, 1149, 1206, 1310, 1346; 11E:19; 13sb:15, 49, 76, 93; 13ba:13, 14, 109; 18gq:26, 93; 18lp:26, 40, 46, 48, 56, 64, 213, 305; 17w:12 (17m:425 now says "coefficient-map factors"). *Proposed:* *coefficient vector*; *coefficient map*; *bound on the inverse coefficient map*.
2. **Image of a basis vector** under a section or coefficient map, as a column of its matrix: "basis column" `P_d^loc[b_{d,i}]` (chapter 2); "the reference insertion with coefficient `c` is a linear combination of the trial columns" (13ba:279–282); "bounded label columns" (13:166), a finite list of labels.
   *Basis:* I (2:200, 260); R (13ba:279–282). *Where:* 2:200, 260, 374, 390; 11:2038; 13:166; 13ba:280, 282 (11:1243 until 25 November 2026). *Proposed:* *image of the basis element*; *the vectors `J_h e_i`*.
3. **Literal column** of a matrix, kernel, table or figure: column sums (17c:333, 337, 338); column vectors ("gradient columns", 17m:204, 232); the alias components `𝒜_l`, `𝒯_l` ("columns at the zero alias", "columns at each nonzero alias", 5:581–600); the columns of the localized approximate inverse (6:523–580, e.g. "The column `Pe_i` solves", 6:569); a column of a figure (13:51) or of the table of exponents (14:802).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* as listed. *Proposed:* keep.
4. **"Front-column"** in the former "At a fixed comparison scale the front-column bounds give `‖u‖_1 ≤ D_k ‖Au‖_1`" (11:1349; since 25 November 2026 "the one-step coefficient bounds in the direction of the transfer", since 26 November 2026 "the one-step bounds for the coefficient of one transferred insertion", with the inequality and `D_k` stated at 11:1349–1350): the bound for one block step on the coefficient of one transferred insertion, `‖x_m‖_1 ≤ C_{J(m+1)} L_m^d ‖x_{m+1}‖_1` (`x_m` the coefficient at scale `m`, `C_j` the stage column bound of Section ch10:choices, sense 1). Applied from the reference scale `r(d)` to `k` it gives `D_k = a_k^d ∏_{m=r(d)}^{k−1} C_{J(m+1)} L_m^d` (11:1349–1350; the source has the product from 0 and writes `C_{m+1}`), the factor `a_k^d` undoing the `a_k^{-d}` contained in `A`. It is the bound in the direction of the transfer; the bound of sense 1, `|x| ≤ s_f |M_G x|` (11:445–446), is the one in the opposite direction, which is why the former word "inverse" at 11:1349 was misplaced; it has been removed. "Front" is a name from the formal source without mathematical content. See *front-column*.
   *Basis:* S; R since 26 November 2026 for the statement (11:1349–1350). *Where:* 11:1349–1350 (the word itself formerly at 11:1349). *Adopted:* *the one-step bounds for the coefficient of one transferred insertion*, with the inequality (26 November 2026; see *front-column*).
   *Source:* Martin existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:176–188 ("Explicitly one may take `D_k = a_k^d ∏_{u=0}^{k-1} C_{u+1}L_u^d`, where `C_{u+1} ≥ 1` is the purchased front-column bound. This follows by applying that bound successively from the normalized reference level to `k` … The factor `a_k^d` undoes the normalization in `A_{k,N,p}`"). Lean `YM.Source.TransferData.Based` (YM/Source/Insertion.lean:89–99; fields read: `front : coeffSize x_m ≤ columns_{m+1} · L_m^d · coeffSize x_{m+1}` and `back : coeffSize x_{m+1} ≤ columns_{m+1} · coeffSize x_m`, for `r ≤ m < N`), `YM.Next.Rank.Price.outward` (YM/Next/RANK/Matrices.lean:38; definition read: `∏_{i<k} columns_{i+1} · L_i^d`), `.at_current`, `.reference_size` (:42–60; statements read: `coeffSize v ≤ outward d k · a_k^d · coeffSize (awake … v)` for `ref d ≤ k ≤ N`, proved by one use of `front` per level).
*Across chapters:* two readings, "image of a basis vector of `V_d`" and "coefficient vector, and the linear map on it". Text read (11:443–446; 18lp:25–27; 13ba:278–282): both uses occur and neither is tied to a chapter group, so they are recorded as senses 1 and 2; this is not a change of meaning between chapters. The use at 17w:12 (and the former one at 17m:425, now "coefficient-map factors") refer to the chapter 11 coefficient maps and are not determined inside chapter 17. About 22 occurrences in chapters 12–16. The two one-step bounds of chapter 11 are the two fields `back` (sense 1, 11:445–446: the inverse-column bound, with the stage column constant) and `front` (sense 4) of one structure of the formalisation, with the same constant. The former "normalized target columns" of 11:1243 (replaced on 25 November 2026 by "the solutions `u=u_{j,N,p}` of the lift equations") were the vectors `Au_j` for the solutions `u_j` of the lift equations (ch11:simultaneous-detector-lifts); their bound is stated as `H^{bd+c_d}` at 11:1244 and 11:1369, the one in the source and in the formalisation (see *target*, sense 3 and *Across chapters*).
*See also:* coefficient map; graph; row.

#### comparison
*Now:* not applied.
*Variants:* equation comparison; Gaussian / covariance comparison; local-trial comparison; adjacent comparison; interior-cell comparison; smooth comparison; backward comparison; comparison maps `U_{k,d}`; comparison cells, labels, matrix, sequence.
- **Meaning.** Not one object: the word is attached to at least six different constructions in chapters 12–16 alone (47 occurrences), among them the comparison of the interacting with the free (Gaussian) theory at a level `k`, the maps `U_{k,d}` between free and interacting fields (14:234–307, 953), the comparison of two local sections, and the cells of the reflected tiling ("comparison cell", chapter 11). Of these, the *comparison maps* are a definite object: linear maps `U_{k,d} : F_d^0 → F_d` from the free to the interacting field space of degree `d`, eventually isomorphisms, with scales `r_k ↓ 0`, such that the correlations of the images at the rescaled points converge to the free correlations uniformly over test functions of supremum norm at most one on a compact separated window (ch14:uniform-tests, 14:206–209), compatible with the inclusions, the unit and the real and hypercubic structures (14:215–227).
  *Basis:* I for the word; R for the comparison maps (14:206–227). *Where:* ch. 11 passim; ch. 12–16 (47); 17w, 17m. *Proposed:* name the two objects compared each time; keep only the defined compounds.
  *Source:* for the comparison maps, Lean `YM.Climb.Scaling`, YM/Climb/Cells.lean (structure read: `U k d : (comparator L).Field d ≃ₗ[ℂ] S.Field d`, `r k > 0` strictly decreasing to 0, and positive numbers `xi k`); `YM.Next.UVStress.Stable`, YM/Next/UV_STRESS/Invert.lean (structure read: eventually in `k`, `U k d` commutes with the real structure, with the inclusions and maps unit to unit); `YM.Next.UVStress.tested`, YM/Next/UV_STRESS/Station.lean (definition read: the correlation of the images under `U` at the points `r • x`). Martin existence/actual-stress-normalization.tex:153–161 uses the same `U_{k,4}`, `U_{k,5}`.
*Across chapters:* a generic word, never defined by itself; the compounds with a fixed meaning have their own entries.
*See also:* comparison level; comparison term; comparison window; cell.

*Now:* replaced by *comparison scale* (sense 1, at all its places, and 17m:136; "deep comparison scale" at 11:2037, 2040; "comparison scale `k` whose comparison window lies in a single stage" at 14lc:23); sense 2's proposal *insertion scale `k_i`* is not applied at 17m:136.
*Variants:* comparison scale `k`; deep comparison scale; no longer in the text: comparison depth; comparison level / depth `k`; deep comparison level; admissible comparison depth (14lc:23).
1. **The level `k` below which the history is restarted and at which the comparison with the free (Gaussian) theory is made**; the top of the three levels `k > ℓ > w` of chapter 11 ("the comparison scale `k`", 11:2090; "finest scale `k`", 11R:219; `m = k − ℓ`, 11:1759). At that level `H_k = exp((log log β̂_k)²)` (14lc:23–24).
   *Basis:* I (11:734–737; 11:1758–1759, 2090–2093; 11R:218–219; 14lc:23–24); the three levels are never defined together. *Where:* 11:734–737, 1154, 1349, 1367, 1407, 2037, 2040, 2069, 2184–2185; 11R:7, 71; 13:165–167; 14:231–232; 14lc:23; 15:255 (all "comparison scale"). *Adopted:* *comparison scale `k`*. *Proposed:* named once together with `ℓ` and `w`; afterwards only the symbols.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/E-Gaussian-sources.tex:77–81`: "A comparison window is a triple of levels `k < l < t`", with (Win1) `log(a_l/a_t) ≥ (b+2) log 𝓜`, `log(a_k/a_l) ≥ 10 log B_t`; Scott's top level `t`, middle level `l` and bottom level `k` are v3's `k`, `ℓ`, `w`.
2. **In 17m: the insertion level.** "At the comparison scale `k`" (17m:136) is the fixed level at which the transferred current and its degree-five coefficient are computed; at the end of the argument it is taken to be the insertion level `k_i` (17m:386). In 17w the comparison window runs backwards from the radius level `n` (17w:31–33, 100–103), so there the level in the role of sense 1 is `n`, not `k_i`.
   *Basis:* S; I from the v3 text alone (17m:136, 386). *Where:* 17m:136. *Proposed:* *insertion scale `k_i`*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:213` (Lemma "Regulated Ward coefficient"): "Fix a level `k` … let `N_ν > k` and let `(J, Y, 𝓔, q, t)^{(ν)}` be translation-invariant local data on the level-`k` torus of period `n_ν → ∞`"; `I-section.tex:331`: "The choices are made in this order: the block ratios and entry couplings of the stages … at a fixed level `k`, the transfer depth and the period; then the ordered limit at that `k`; and finally `k = k_i` along the radii."
*Across chapters:* the former "level" and "depth" were the same index, now one word, "scale". Chapters 11–15 use sense 1; chapter 17 attaches the word to different levels in 17w (the radius level `n`, top of the window) and 17m (the insertion level `k_i`). "Admissible comparison depth" (14lc:23) is a comparison level whose window lies in a single stage of the schedule; see *admissible comparison depth* (basis S). In chapter 17 the word stands beside "radius scale `n_i`", "output scale" and "middle and output stopping scales" (17:85, 86, 120; 17w:41, 102; 17t:408; 17c:242, 393; 17m:136, 331, 416; not split by term; "level" became "scale" in all these compounds); the output scale of 17t and 17c is the level `k` of sense 2, not the `w` of chapter 11 (see *output level*).
*See also:* admissible comparison depth; comparison window; output level; level.

#### compensation
*Now:* replaced by *compensating rescaling* (sense 1, 10:532–533) and *the change of variables `T_V`* (sense 2, 6:1547).
*Variants:* compensating rescaling (10:532–533); compensated change of variables (source); no longer in the text: compensation; compensating map (6:1547).
1. **Rescaling of the Gaussian variable when the coupling varies (chapter 10).** A change of variables that leaves the fine field unchanged: "A compensating rescaling keeps each fine field read fixed: the Gaussian coordinate is rescaled by `ℓ(t)` while its fluctuation coefficient is divided by `ℓ(t)`" (10:532–535). The fine field is `m + g z` with `g = β^{-1/2}`; when `β` is replaced by `β_0 ℓ(t)^2`, `g` is divided by `ℓ(t)` and `z` is multiplied by `ℓ(t)`, so the fluctuation field `gz` (6:914) is unchanged.
   *Basis:* R (10:532–535). *Where:* 10:532–535, cf. 678. *Adopted:* *compensating rescaling* (of the Gaussian coordinate `z`; the fluctuation field `gz` is kept fixed).
   *Source:* Martin `existence/local-parameter-comparison.tex:51–55`: "Put `λ = g(β)/g(β')`. The identity `g(β')λ = g(β)` implies that the fine field at `(R', λz)` is precisely the fine field at `(R, z)`. It also gives `βλ² = β'` and makes the compensated noise course for `R'` equal to `λ` times the course for `R`."
2. **The compensating map of chapter 6: the protected change of variables when the coarse field varies.** "The estimate above for the change of variables `T_V` supplies bounds on `T_V` and its density scores" (6:1547–1548). The map is `T_V z = g^{-1}{F_{M(V)}(m_Y(V_0) + g z) − m_Y(V)}` with `M_e(V) = (rep V_0)_e (rep V)_e^{-1}` (6:732–735), the globally defined extension of (ch06:protected-change), 6:701–706: it changes the Gaussian coordinate `z` as the coarse field `V` moves away from `V_0` so that every protected fine link `U_e = exp(u_e)(rep V)_e` keeps its value. Its "density scores" are the logarithmic derivatives in `V` of the Gaussian density and of the Jacobian after this change. The rescaling of sense 1 is not this map; both apply the same device (move the integration variable so that the fine field read by a merely measurable factor is not differentiated) to two different parameters.
   *Basis:* R (6:701–706, 732–735, 1547). *Where:* 6:1547. *Adopted:* *the change of variables `T_V` of (ch06:protected-change)*.
   *Source:* Martin `existence/compensated-variation.tex:3–9`: "Differentiating a packet directly in its coarse field would also change the fine configuration represented by its fluctuation variable. … We instead make the actual compensated change of variables. It is a global bijection on the fluctuation space near the chosen coarse configuration, and agrees with the required logarithmic adjustment where the protected integrand can be nonzero"; `:130–134` (`eq:compensator-course`): `M_i(V) = V̄_{0,i} V̄_i^{-1}`, `u_i(V) = F_{M_i(V)}(u_{0,i})`, `z_i(V) = g_β^{-1}{u_i(V) − ν_i(V)}`; `:147–150` (`eq:compensator-held-fine`): `exp(u_i(V)) V̄_i = exp(u_{0,i}) V̄_{0,i}`. The formulas coincide with 6:701–735.
*Across chapters:* chapters 6 and 10, two changes of variables under one word. Text read at 6:1539–1548 and 6:697–735: "the estimate above" is the estimate for `T_V` ("holding its physical fine links fixed with the change of variables (ch06:protected-change)", 6:1541–1542); 6:1547 now names the map.
*See also:* protected; physical.
