#### complement of the large fluctuation-field event
*Formerly:* *small-coordinate event*.
*In the text:* (6:903).
- **Meaning.** The complement of the large fluctuation-field event `ℰ_w = {∃i: d(i,w) ≤ 2B, |z_i| ≥ T}`, `T = ξ t_f/(2g)` (6:843–849): "On the complement of the large fluctuation-field event, `v = m_Y + gz` has size `O(t_f)`" (6:903). The large fluctuation-field event is the event outside which a cutoff remainder vanishes ("Its smallness comes from a large fluctuation-field event", 6:840–841).
  *Basis:* R (6:843–849, 903). *Where:* 6:903. *Adopted:* *the complement of the large fluctuation-field event `{|z_i| ≥ T for some i near w}`*; `ℰ_w` is not called "large-field event" without "fluctuation".
*Literature:* see *cutoff failure* (sense 1); the complement is the small fluctuation field condition, `χ_k`, `χ^w_k`.
*Across chapters:* chapter 6 only. These Gaussian-tail events are distinct from the large-field selection `A` and from `Bad_m(U)`.
*See also:* cutoff remainder; large-coordinate event; selected.

#### complementary
*Now:* partly replaced by *large-field part* (sense 1, at all its places); remains in sense 2 (11:1619, "absorbs the complementary …"), in sense 3 (17m:122, 128, 131, 321, 322, where it was replaced for a time and is now restored; also in the margin note at 17m:330) and as ordinary adjective (5:518; RG:25). At 10:629 "the complementary one" (new on 25 November 2026) was removed on 26 November 2026 with the split into principal and complementary regular bounds; the word stands there only in the margin note that records the removal (grep). At 10:99 "Its complementary global value" was replaced on 25 November 2026 by "The value of the trial outside that chart".
*Variants:* complementary cutoff (11:1619); complementary sum, terms, part, large-field estimate (17m:122, 128, 131, 321); no longer in the text: complementary stencil / insertion factor / attachment; complementary part (in sense 1); complementary profile; complementary marked sum.
1. **The large-field part of an insertion**: the part multiplied by one minus the small-field indicator. The formula is not at the first use (11:149–153); it is explicit at 11:1322–1327 (`f − χF`, which "vanishes wherever `χ = 1` and is assigned to the original prescribed large-field set") and 11:1496–1500 ("Expand it as a product of factors `1 − (1−χ) R z_I`").
   *Basis:* R / I (11:149–153; 11:1322–1327, 1496–1500). *Where:* "large-field part" at 11:141, 149–153, 924–925, 944, 1642; 11E:80, 100, 118; 13ba:18, 68, 165; 10:99 had "complementary global value" until 25 November 2026 (now "The value of the trial outside that chart", 10:98–99). *Adopted:* *large-field part of the insertion*.
2. **The factor `(1−γ)W` left by a smooth local cutoff `γ`** ("the complementary principal cutoff", after the split `(1 + γWz_S)(1 + (1−γ)Wz_S)`).
   *Basis:* R (11:315–320, 1619). *Where:* 11:1619. *Proposed:* *the factor `(1−γ)W`*.
3. **The terms with a large fluctuation-field event somewhere in the connected component of the inserted factor**: "Every term with a large fluctuation-field event anywhere in the connected component of the differentiated kernel, including a distant such event joined to the score, is kept in the complementary sum" (17m:121–123; "failure" until 25 November 2026); "The absolute score bound is used only for these complementary terms" (17m:128); "the complementary large-field estimate" (17m:131); "applies to the complementary part" (17m:321).
   *Basis:* R (17m:121–131). *Where:* 17m:122, 128, 131, 321, 322. *Proposed:* *complementary terms*, kept. Not *large-field terms*: "large-field" names the large-field set proper (6:7–11). The author decided on 25 November 2026 (decision 50) that the former "failures" are large fluctuation-field events, as the text now says; the incoming prescribed large-field sets are "retained" separately (17m:127).
*Across chapters:* senses 1 and 3 have the same role (what is left when a small-field condition fails) for different objects (one insertion; a sum of terms); sense 2 is a smooth cutoff, not an indicator. In chapter 17 the opposites are `ordinary` (the whole small-field part) and `regular` (one term of it). The former "complementary profile" (13ba:165) is now "large-field part" ("has no large-field part"), as at 13ba:18.
*See also:* complete; cutoff failure; large-field profile.

#### completion
*Now:* partly replaced by *gauge-fixing term* and *gauge-fixed* (sense 1: 7:234, 378, 887, 945, 1038; 17t:89; 17c:145, 171, 177, 301) and by *the kinetic form with the penalty term added* (sense 2, 7:696–697); remains at 7:783 ("blocked completed matrix `C_0`", sense 3) and 11:1696 ("the completed inverse"). The "completed fine kinetic matrix" of 17c:65 was removed with the alias argument on 25 November 2026.
*Also in the text for:* the former *completed* (see those entries).
*Variants:* completed; blocked completed matrix `C_0`; quotient calculation; no longer in the text: completed fine kinetic matrix (17c:65); gauge completion; block-completed form `𝒢`; completed vector operator.
1. **Gauge completion**: adding `F*F` (or `d_U d_U*`, `dd*`) to a gauge-degenerate Hessian. "Given a gauge condition `F` with invertible `G = Fℛ`, put `C = 𝖩 + F*F`" (7:256–257), `𝖩` being the joint Hessian of 7:247; the section is now titled "Haar measure and the gauge-fixing term" (7:234). In chapter 17: "At the zero field the gauge-fixed vector operator is `H + dd* = |k|²I + O(|k|³)`" (17t:89–90). The "completed fine kinetic matrix" of 17c:65 (removed on 25 November 2026) was of this kind: the fine kinetic symbol `K_f(k)`, which vanishes on the gradient direction, with the gauge term added, so that it is invertible at a nonzero alias `k_l(0)`; the sentence before it projected `N_l` off the fine gradient direction (former 17c:64), and the parallel argument at 7:822–824 uses "the positive transverse fine inverse".
   *Basis:* R (7:256–257; 17t:89–90); I for the former 17c:65 (7:822–824). *Where:* 7:234, 256–257, 320, 378, 889, 945, 1038; 17t:89; 17c:145, 171, 177, 301. *Adopted:* *gauge-fixing term* for what is added; *gauge-fixed operator* for the result. The proposal for 17c:65 lapsed with the sentence; 17c:69 now says only "no inverse of a kinetic symbol at a nonzero alias, is needed".
   *Source:* for 17c:65 (the sentence was removed on 25 November 2026), Scott `part2/C-section.tex:241` "the fine curl form has a positive floor on the transverse subspace at each nonzero alias, [so] the transverse part of `N_z(ξ)` is `O(|ξ|²)` there"; Martin `existence/stationary-determinant-prices.tex:174, 185` ("the gauge-completed fine matrix" is `K + dd* + Σ_a s_a^*Cs_a`). The source passage from which the sentence 17c:65 itself was written was not found.
2. **Block completion**: the kinetic form completed by the penalty term, `𝒢(u,r) = ⟨u, K_f u⟩ + b|Mu − d_{0,c} r|²`, which is still gauge-degenerate ("The kinetic form with the penalty term added, the form `𝒢` below, needs a quotient estimate", 7:696–697); the gauge term is added afterwards (7:738–739).
   *Basis:* D (7:696–700). *Where:* 7:696–700. *Adopted:* *kinetic form plus penalty term*. Not *gauge-fixed operator*, and the penalty term is not a *gauge-fixing term*.
3. **Both together: the "blocked completed matrix `C_0`"** (7:783). The matrix, at zero background and on the joint space of fine one-forms and coarse scalar coordinates, of the fine kinetic form plus the block penalty (with the contact term of the averaging operation removed, that is, with the penalty Hessian replaced by its constraint pullback) plus the gauge term `F*F`: the matrix of `𝒢 + F*F` of 7:738–739. It is compared with `Ã_μ = diag(A_μ, I)`, the gauge-completed auxiliary fine matrix extended by the identity on the coarse scalar part; "This proves uniform holomorphic inverse bounds for both matrices" (7:749).
   *Basis:* I (7:738–739, 749, 782–784); S for the formula. *Where:* 7:783, 811–813. *Proposed:* *the matrix of `𝒢 + F*F`* (kinetic form, block penalty and gauge term), written as a formula where `C_0` is introduced.
   *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-determinant-prices.tex:171–178`: "The three matrix triples to be compared are `M_act = b*Kb + B + F*F`, `M_core = b*Kb + Q*HQ + F*F`, `M_rank = b*(K + dd* + Σ_a s_a^*Cs_a)b + e*e`. The first uses the full penalty Hessian; the second retains its constraint pullback"; `:183–186` "the zero-background penalty Hessian equals its constraint pullback, and the gauge-completed fine matrix is precisely the auxiliary matrix treated there." v3's `C_0` is `M_core` and `Ã_μ` is `M_rank`; this correspondence is by agreement of the roles in the comparison (difference of trace class, 7:786–787; Martin `:189–193`), not by a shared symbol.
*Literature:* see *gauge completion* (sense 1) and *block-completed form* (senses 2–3).
*Across chapters:* chapters 7 and 17 use sense 1 for the same kind of operation but for different operators: the "gauge-fixed inverse" of chapter 7 (formerly "completed inverse") is `𝒞⁻¹ = (ℋ + F*F)⁻¹` (7:887–889), not the inverse of the `H + dd*` of 17t:89. Text read at 17t:88–91 and, before 25 November 2026, 17c:64–66. Further unrelated uses: the "positive completion" of the two-form operator (5:456), the completion of squares (6:101, 127, 672), the completion of normed spaces (10:393, 796, 862; 14:33; 16:356); the former "covariant (path) completion" of a jet (17m:28–34) is now "gauge-covariant extension". v3 never displays `C_0`; it should restore the formula.
*See also:* curvature metric; contact.

*Now:* unchanged; "ground algebra" (15:157) is now "compression algebra", as proposed.
*Variants:* compression `M(w)`; compression algebra `𝔄`; compressed operators, errors, limit, exterior words; compressed whole words (15:11); compresses (19:99); no longer in the text: compressed product moments.
- **Meaning.** `M(w) = P_0 B_h(w)|_{H_0}`: the compression to the zero-energy subspace of the operator of a whole separated word `w` ("the compression of a whole separated word", 18:20). The `M(w)` generate the commutative compression algebra `𝔄`, whose characters are the phases.
  *Basis:* D (15:57, 94). *Where:* 15:11, 51–60, 92–94, 124, 157–158, 215, 269; 15sp:17; 18:19, 20, 189; 18r:14, 37; 19:99. *Adopted:* keep (compression of an operator to a subspace is standard operator theory; the text also uses the noun for the resulting element); *compression algebra* for `𝔄`, also at 15:157 ("characters of the compression algebra").

#### compression algebra
*Formerly:* *ground algebra*.
*In the text:* (15:157–158).
- **Meaning.** The compression algebra `𝔄`: the norm-closed unital `*`-algebra of operators on the zero-energy subspace `𝓗_0 = ker H` generated by the compressions `M(w) = P_0 B_h(w)|_{𝓗_0}`; "ground algebra" was "algebra on the ground space". "This is a representation of the undecomposed correlations by characters of the compression algebra", said of `S^ξ(w) = ξ(M(w))` (15:152–158).
  *Basis:* I from the v3 text (15:152–158); S, confirming the reading; the algebra `𝔄` itself is defined in Proposition "The compression algebra" (15:92–94). *Where:* 15:92, 157; 18:19, 189. *Adopted:* *compression algebra* for `𝔄`, also for "ground algebra" (15:157).
  *Source:* Martin existence/phases.tex:229–231: "The norm-closed unital star algebra `𝒜 ⊂ B(ℋ_0)` generated by the `M(w)` is commutative"; existence/phase-selection.tex:4: "a commutative algebra on the whole ground space. Its characters provide a useful way of separating the vacuum state into components." Scott part2/H-section.tex:41: "compression by the ground projection `P_0` gives `M^0(w)`, and these operators generate the commutative algebra `𝔄_0`. A phase is a character `ξ` of `𝔄_0`." Lean `YM.OS.Spread.algebra := (StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ P.generators).topologicalClosure`, with `generators = {atom w d | Slab timeAxis d w}` and `atom w d` the composition of the orthogonal projection onto `D`, the operator `P.place d w`, and the inclusion of `D`, YM/Phase/Mixture.lean (definitions read; `P.place` not opened); `YM.OS.Chamber.D := C.flow.ground`, same file, and `ground := ⨅ t, ker (E t − id)`, YM/OS/Core.lean (definition read: the vectors fixed by every `E t`).
*Across chapters:* the former "ground algebra" had one occurrence (15:157; text read at 15:152–158); "compression algebra" stands at 15:92, 157 and 18:19, 189.
*See also:* compression; zero-energy subspace.

#### compulsory
*Now:* replaced by *required large-field factor* (sense 1, 10:657) and *cutoff factor kept inside the component* (sense 2, 6:1468); at 6:1025 "the compulsory component region" was replaced on 25 November 2026 by "within distance `300B` of its component of the index triple `A`", and on 26 November 2026 (definitions from the sources) by the convention "By convention, a cutoff factor other than a chart cutoff whose location (the projected corners of its plaquette, the endpoints of its edge, or its site) meets `A^{[300B]}`, and a chart cutoff on a link whose projected endpoints meet `A^{[304B]}`, is not written as one plus a cutoff remainder: it is kept whole as a factor of the sector, and its cutoff remainder is set to zero" (6:1025), with a margin note citing Lean and Martin. The word no longer occurs in the chapter files (grep).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: compulsory component region (6:1025); compulsory large-field factor; compulsory cutoff factor.
1. **Chapter 10: the large-field factor that a constrained array necessarily contains.** "Arrays with a prescribed large-field set retain one required large-field factor throughout the exact regrouping" (10:657–658), "with the hard factor retained once" (10:669).
   *Basis:* R (10:657). *Where:* 10:657. *Adopted:* *the large-field factor required by the prescribed sites* ("required large-field factor").
2. **Chapter 6: kept as a factor of the component, not expanded.** The *compulsory component region* of a selected component is the set of test positions (fine plaquettes, coarse bonds, coarse sites) whose coarse location meets the neighbourhood of fixed radius of the selection; the radius is `300B` in the formalisation, which agrees with "the retained `300B` region" of 6:1348–1357. At such a position the allocation weight or tag weight `a_p` stays a factor of the component itself; it is not written `1 + w_p`, and its cutoff remainder `w_p` is set to zero: "A cutoff remainder assigned within distance `300B` of its component of the index triple `A` is zero by definition" (6:1025, 25 November 2026; formerly "within the compulsory component region"); since 26 November 2026 the convention at 6:1025 reads "… whose location … meets `A^{[300B]}`, and a chart cutoff on a link whose projected endpoints meet `A^{[304B]}`, is not written as one plus a cutoff remainder: it is kept whole as a factor of the sector, and its cutoff remainder is set to zero" (the radius `304B` for chart cutoffs was found by the reviewer). The former *compulsory cutoff factor* is such a retained factor `a_p`; the component factor contains the product of all of them, hence "where a cutoff factor kept inside the component vanishes, the full component factor is zero" (6:1468).
   *Basis:* S; since 25 November 2026 R at 6:1025, which states the radius `300B`; since 26 November 2026 D (6:1025, the convention). *Where:* 6:1025 (now without the word), 1461. *Adopted:* *a cutoff factor … whose location meets `A^{[300B]}` … is kept whole as a factor of the sector, and its cutoff remainder is set to zero* (6:1025, decision of 26 November 2026); *a cutoff factor kept inside the component* (6:1468). Not checked (merge-2026-11-26.md): that Lean's factor types are v3's cutoff factors.
   *Source:* Martin `existence/gaussian-warnings.tex:206–208`: "A warning factor is either a bounded cutoff times one of these factors minus one, or a bond cutoff minus one. Factors inside their compulsory seed region are defined to be zero"; `:225` "the compulsory seed region has radius `R_c ≥ R_p + B`"; `:281–282` "inside the compulsory region the warning is zero by definition". Martin `existence/gaussian-reassembly.tex:187–192`: "Write `a_p` for a compulsory test and `w_p` for its optional warning. At a compulsory position `w_p = 0` and its packet supplies `a_p`; at every other position the optional factor is `1 + w_p = a_p` on the smaller full mask. … If it vanishes, the entire product on both sides is zero." Lean `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Coat.mandatory`, `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Coat.mayor`, `YM/AnalyticNext/CONNECTED_ACTIVITY_JETS_E6/Alert.lean` (definitions read): `mandatory A B p` says that the location of `p` meets `A.dome (300·B)`; `mayor` is `0` there and a cutoff times (factor − 1) elsewhere. The retained products are `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Mask.profiles`, `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Mask.tickets`, `YM/AnalyticNext/CONNECTED_ACTIVITY_JETS_E6/Mask.lean` (definitions read). `enforce` and `Contract.charges` were not read.

#### connected covering number
*Now:* unchanged; now defined under this name at 4:630, and "connected cover number" and "fine cover number" are replaced by it (11:1374; 6:1302; 18lp:78).
*Also in the text for:* the former *cover* (see those entries).
*Variants:* `cov_B(X)`; `c_B(S)`; `c_B`; `c(X)`; covering number; cover units; no longer in the text: connected cover number; fine cover number.
- **Meaning.** The minimum number of radius-`B` periodic balls whose union is connected in the nearest-neighbour graph and covers `X`. Activities are weighted by `e^{α c_B(X)}`; a "cover unit" or "unit of support exponent" is one unit of the exponent multiplying `c_B(X)`.
  *Basis:* D (4:630–632). *Where:* 4:630–632; 6:1178, 1302–1303; 9:220, 421, 513; 10:619; 11:269, 396, 495, 502, 528, 533, 942, 1167–1168, 1374, 1452; 12:230, 270, 275–281; 13ba:132–137; 18lp:78–82; 17m:331–332, 412–413. *Adopted:* keep, with one name: *connected covering number*. *Proposed:* one notation `c_B(X)`.
*Literature:* **linear size** `d_j(X)`, `𝓛(X)`; **tree size**; `d_M(X)`; **relative linear size** `d_{k,Z}(Y)` (B87 p. 257: "Consider a class of tree graphs contained in X and intersecting all the cubes in X. A length of a shortest graph in this class, divided by M, is the linear size of X, and is denoted by d_j(X)"; B85e p. 262: "Following [19] we define a linear size 𝓛(X) of a localization X as the length of a shortest tree graph connecting the centers of big blocks in X"; B95 p. 117: "a function d_j(X) which measures a tree size of X"; D1 p. 1330010-19, (118): "`M d_M(X)` = the length of shortest tree in X joining the M-cubes in X", with `d_M ≤ |X|_M ≤ 3^d(1 + d_M)`; B89b p. 376; p. 380: "`d'_j` is the linear size defined in terms of `MR_j`-cubes instead of `M`-cubes"). An analogue: the tree length of a connected polymer in block units, against the covering number of an arbitrary set; both give `exp(−κ d)` decay and are comparable (B88a (2.30) bounds `d_k(Y)` above and below by multiples of `M^{−4}|Y|`). The block scale `B_m = ⌈(log β̂_m)²⌉` corresponds to the cube side `MR_j`, `R_j ≥ (log g_j^{-2})^r` (B88b p. 255, (2.5)). Suggested: keep *connected covering number*; add "(plays the role of the *linear size* `d_j(X)` of Bałaban)".
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout, under two notations: `cov_B` (chapters 4, 9, 12) and `c_B` (chapters 6, 11, 13, 18lp), with "boxes" at 12:230–231 against "balls" elsewhere. Chapter 11 uses it with a one-line reminder (11:1374 "Here `c_B(X)` is the connected covering number at radius `B`"); 12:229–231 and 18lp:78 recall the definition in words ("counts a connected covering of `X` by radius-`B_m` boxes"; "counts the radius-`B` balls in a smallest connected covering of `X`"). The symbol is at 6:1303; 6:1302 has "fine connected covering number".
*See also:* containing-site bound; cover.

#### connector
*Now:* replaced by *transporter* (defined at 4:186 as *gauge-transformed parallel transporter*, for short the *transporter*).
- **Meaning.** `Y_{e,z}`: the frame-conjugated product of `L` fine links along a straight path.
  *Basis:* D (4:186–196). *Where:* 4:186–196; 5:996; 6:373; 7:645, 649, 679, 718–722; 13ba:250 ("transporter" on each line). *Adopted:* *gauge-transformed parallel transporter*.
*Literature:* no noun; the object is the **contour** `Γ_{c,x} = Γ_{c_-,x} ∪ [x,x(c)] ∪ Γ_{x(c),c_+}` and its group element `U(Γ_{c,x})` (B85a p. 19: "is an oriented contour with `c_-` as an initial point and `c_+` as a final point. We denote it by `Γ_{c,x}`"; B84a p. 19, (1.8); B87 p. 252: "For a bond c and a point x ∈ B(c_−), let [x, x′] denote a contour which is obtained by a parallel transport of c to the point x"). An analogue in general; the same object when the v3 frame is the axial frame based at the coarse site with one coordinate order fixed, in which case `Y_{e,z} = U(Γ_{c,x})` (this identification is an inference). Bałaban closes the contour with `−c` and takes a logarithm (B87 (0.4)); v3 conjugates by frames that may be minimising or random. Suggested: *holonomy of the contour from one coarse site to the next through the fine site `x`* (the parallel translate of the coarse bond, Bałaban's `[x,x′]`, closed by the frame contours); there is no literature noun.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 4, 5, 6, 7, 13ba. 13ba:248–249 restates the radius without the word "macro-box" of chapter 4: "the local gauge transformation at each endpoint reads a box of fine-lattice radius `(j_i+3)L_i`". At 7:702 the operator `M`, formerly "the straight averaged connector", is now "the linear averaging operator".

#### conserved line
*Now:* replaced by *one-dimensionality of the space of conserved tensors* (the statement, 3:591, 17:343); *line of conserved stress tensors* (the line, 14:263), *line of zero-mean conserved tensors* (14:1026).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: conserved stress line; conserved tensor line; centered conserved line.
- **Meaning.** The statement that the conserved (divergence-free) centred tensors of degree four form a line, and that line. For the free fields: `{J ∈ 𝒯_{≤4} : div J = 0} = ℝ T^Max` (Proposition "One-dimensionality of the space of conserved tensors", 3:591–596). For the interacting fields the section "The line of conserved stress tensors" (14:263–313) proves two things. (i) Let `𝒦` be the real space of centred (each component has zero expectation), real, symmetric, hypercubic-covariant degree-four tensor arrays in the interacting ("undecomposed") field space, and `𝒱` the space of degree-five covariant vector arrays. Then the divergence `div : 𝒦 → 𝒱` is onto and `dim ker(div|_𝒦) = 1` (ch14:conserved-line, 14:297–299). Proof: the free divergence `𝒦^0 → 𝒱^0` is onto with kernel `ℝT^0` (14:271–284, from the rank computation of chapter 3); the centred comparison map `C_k : 𝒦^0 → 𝒦` and the vector map `V_k` are isomorphisms with `V_k^{-1} r_k div C_k → div^0` (14:286–293); composing with a right inverse of `div^0` gives a map tending to the identity, so `div` is onto for large `k`, and rank–nullity gives the dimension. (ii) A generator `J` can be chosen, with positive numbers `c_k`, such that `U_{k,4}^{-1}(c_k^{-1} r_k^4 J) → T^0` (ch14:balanced-stress, 14:301–310); this fixes the sign of `J` but not its normalisation, and no lower bound on `c_k` is asserted (14:311–313). The normalised stress tensor `T` of 14:1012–1028 "belongs to the same line of zero-mean conserved tensors as `J`", and `J = c_*T`. At 17:343, "The one-dimensionality of the space of conserved tensors, (ch14:conserved-line), gives `Z_i = ν_i T`": `Z_i = β_iB_i^L + c_{i,0}B_i^X + c_{i,1}B_i^D` is a combination of the centred transferred tensors (17:292) with zero divergence (17:330), hence an element of `ker(div|_𝒦)`, hence a real multiple of `T` by (i).
  *Basis:* R (3:590–596 for the free statement; 14:263–313 for the interacting one; 17:292, 330, 343 for the use). *Where:* 3:591–596, 654; 14:263, 298–299, 304, 313, 1026; 17:173, 343. *Adopted:* *the line `ker(div|_𝒦)`*; *one-dimensionality of the space of conserved tensors*, cited as (ch14:conserved-line).
  *Source:* Martin existence/actual-stress-normalization.tex:138–180 (subsubsection "The physical conserved line"): "Let `K^0` and `K^1` be the real spaces of centered, symmetric, real, signed-covariant grade-four stress arrays in the reference and physical tables. Centering means that every entry has expectation zero … Assume the fixed reference tensor `J^0` belongs to `K^0`, is nonzero and conserved, and that `D^0` is onto with `ker D^0 = ℝJ^0` … Therefore `B_k` is onto … shows that `D^1` is onto. The two pairs of spaces have equal dimensions, so rank–nullity gives `dim_ℝ ker D^1 = 1`." Lean `YM.Next.UVStress.KernelSpace`, YM/Next/UV_STRESS/Tensor.lean (definition read: tensors `B : Axis → Axis → Field 4` that are symmetric, fixed by the conjugation, covariant under the signed permutations, with `expectation (B i j) = 0`), `Vectors` and `currentDiv` (definitions read: `(div B)_i = Σ_j ∂_j B_{ji}` as an `ℝ`-linear map `KernelSpace → Vectors`); `YM.Next.UVStress.differential_rank`, YM/Next/UV_STRESS/Dimension.lean (statement read: under `FreeDiv` (the free divergence is onto with one-dimensional kernel containing the nonzero conserved free tensor) and the convergence and compatibility hypotheses on the comparison maps, `currentDiv` is surjective and `finrank_ℝ (ker currentDiv) = 1`; docstring "Actual physical full rank (onto) and one-dimensional stress line"); `produce_current`, YM/Next/UV_STRESS/Limit.lean (statement read: statement (ii)).
*Across chapters:* the object changes from the free line (chapter 3) to the interacting one (chapters 14, 17). The interacting statement is conditional on the comparison maps of Section (ch14:comparison) and on the free rank computation; in the source and in the formal statement these are explicit hypotheses. In chapter 14 "line" also names a coordinate line `ℝe_l` carrying the spectators (14:504, 718, 730–731, 738, 760–763, 809, 816), a different object. The source's "physical line" ("of the interacting theory"; source: "the reference and physical tables") is now "the line" (14:313: "This fixes the sign of the chosen tensor on the line"), and "physical divergence" is "the interacting divergence" (14:296).
*See also:* centered (sense 1); orientation of the line; physical line.

#### contact
*Now:* partly replaced by *coincident points* (sense 1: "Positivity at coincident points", 19:156; "specified extensions to coincident points", RG:64); remains on 30 lines in chapters 3, 7, 14, 17t, 18, 19 ("contact term", "contact extension", "contact Ward identities"; in sense 2 now defined at 7:538; sense 3 kept as proposed, since 26 November 2026 as "contact identity in group coordinates", 17t:178, 499) (grep, labels excluded).
*Variants:* contact term; contact correction; contact identity; contact Ward identities; no longer in the text: contact assertion; contacts.
1. **Coincident-point term** (chapters 18–19): "Positivity at coincident points, contact Ward identities, compatibility with removal of an identity field, and uniqueness of contact terms" (19:156–158).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 18:2, 22, 331, 431–433; 19:111, 154, 156–157 (10 uses). *Proposed:* *coincident points*; *contact term* is standard for a term supported at coincident points.
2. **The contact term of the averaging operation in chapter 7**: the second-order difference `D²(log det M_act − log det M_core)(0)`, due to the second derivative of the nonlinear averaging operation. The text now names both pieces: "we call `Z` the *contact term* of the averaging operation, and the difference in (ch07:contact-exact) below the *contact correction*" (7:538); `Z(x) = S_x(r(x))` in `M_act = A + Z` (7:534–538) is the first derivative `r` of the block penalty paired with the second derivative `D_v² w_x(0)` of the averaging operation, and the contact correction is the second-order difference. This is the source's assignment of the name. Not a coincident-point term.
   *Basis:* D (7:538); R (7:538–554). *Where:* 7:509, 512, 538, 577, 774, 783, 817. *Proposed:* *second-order correction to the determinant from the averaging operation* (no standard name known); the text has *contact correction* instead.
   *Source:* Martin `existence/thermal-contact-cancellation.tex:1` (title "The thermal determinant and its contact term"), `:126–141` ("The finite-volume contact identity … The Hessian chain rule for the penalty says exactly `M_act(x) = A(x) + Z(x)`. It separates the pullback of the penalty Hessian from the gradient of the penalty paired with the second derivative of its constraint").
3. **The contact identity in group coordinates of chapter 17** (until 26 November 2026 "group-coordinate contact identity"): the algebraic identity (17.contact) of the proposition at 17t:232–240. It has the structure of sense 2: its `DS[Z]` term and the matrix `C_{ij} = DS[D_z² 𝒴_U(0)[e_i, e_j]]` (17t:249–250) are the first derivative of the action paired with the second derivative of a nonlinear coordinate map. No source says why this kind of term is called "contact".
   *Basis:* D for the object (17t:232–240); S for the correspondence with sense 2; ? for the reason for the word. *Where:* 17t:178, 232, 336, 417, 427, 499, 503. *Proposed:* keep, cited by proposition number, with a remark that it is not a coincident-point term.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:228` (the identity, labelled `eq:I-contact`, inside the proof of Lemma `lem:I-regulator`; Scott's prose does not use the word); Martin as under sense 2.
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes: chapter 7, chapter 17 and chapters 18–19 use the word for three things, and only the last is the standard one. Senses 2 and 3 are the same usage: in both the name is attached to the term of a Hessian chain rule in which a gradient is paired with the second derivative of a nonlinear map (the block average in chapter 7, the chart velocity `𝒴_U` in chapter 17). This is read off 7:538 (and Martin's sentence) for chapter 7 and the formulas of 17t; 7:538 names the term but does not say why the word is used.
*See also:* collision; contact projection; group-coordinate contact identity.

#### contact projection
*Now:* glossed at 18:407 on 25 November 2026 (sentence repair, decision 11/12/34): "If the contact projection of degree `q`, which reads a cluster of fields near a point through its correlations with finitely many fixed separated probe words, extracts a degree-`q` field from that cluster, one subtracts the normal Taylor jet of the test function through order `L_h − 1 − q`" (18:407–409). The gloss is the applying agent's condensation of Scott `def:D36`–`def:D37` (`repairs-apply.md`), judged "a fair condensation of Scott `J-section.tex:591–612`" by the review; the formula `P_{=q}(o)` is not given.
*Variants:* child / parent operators (the same tree vocabulary).
- **Meaning.** A linear map that assigns to a cluster of fields near a centre `o` a single field at `o` of a prescribed degree `q`, defined through finitely many separated correlations. In the source: at each degree `q` fix finitely many probe words whose correlations distinguish the fields of `F_q`, and a left inverse (the "contact decoder") of the resulting injective map `F_q → ℂ^{𝒫_q}`; a word all of whose positions lie in a ball `B(0, ρ_q)` clear of the probes is sent to the field with the same probe correlations, averaged over rotations and made real; the maps `P_{≤q}(o)` are made compatible across degrees by the recursion `P_0 = B_0`, `P_{q+1} = ȷP_q + (1 − ȷT_q)B_{q+1}`, `T_q = P_q I_{q+1}`, and `P_{=q}(o) = (1 − ȷT_{q−1})B_q(τ_{−o} ·)` is its part of exact degree `q`. In 18:407–409, "If the contact projection of degree `q`, which reads a cluster of fields near a point through its correlations with finitely many fixed separated probe words, extracts a degree-`q` field from that cluster, one subtracts the normal Taylor jet of the test function through order `L_h − 1 − q`" (18:407–409) refers to `P_{=q}` at the centroid of the collision subset `h` (now "every subset `h` of coincident points", 18:402). The "child" and "parent" operators of 18:417–419 are the normal Taylor operators `Tay^⊥_{b,k_b}`, `Tay^⊥_{h,k_h}` of nested collision subsets `b ⊊ h`: the operator of the larger subset acts on the test function first.
  *Basis:* S; R in outline from the gloss at 18:407 (the coherence across degrees and the formula are not in v3). *Where:* 18:407–421 (the term itself only at 18:407; 18:260 has the operators that the descendants apply to the test function, without the term). *Adopted in part:* the gloss at 18:407. *Proposed:* *projection `P_{=q}(o)` onto the degree-`q` fields at the center, defined by separated correlations*; state it by its formula; *Taylor operators of the nested subsets* for the child and parent operators.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:591–597` (Definition "Contact projection", `def:D36`: "fix at each degree `q` a finite family of separated mixed correlation probe words whose responses distinguish the fields in `F_q` … fix a linear left inverse, the contact decoder … This extracts contact fields on a fixed region clear of its probes"), `:602–609` (Definition "Coherent contact projections", `def:D37`), `:611–619` (`def:D38`, `P_{=q}^ct(o)`), `:673` ("In a nested term, the parent Taylor operator acts first on the test and the child operators act afterwards: if `b ⊊ h` are a child and its parent, with Taylor orders `k_b, k_h` …"). Lean: `YM.Contacts.Normal.System` (`YM/Contacts/Score/Formula.lean:31–34`; definition read) has a field `reader (g) (w) : E → A →ₗ[ℂ] A`, used in `subtractAt` in the place of Scott's `R_{h,q}`; it is instantiated in `waySystem` (`YM/Contacts/Harvest/Yield.lean:39–40`; definition read) by `M.insertRow (centroid i (P x + o)) w`, where `insertRow x w = (insertField D x w).comp (M.row x w)` (`YM/Contacts/Coherent.lean:117`; definition read). The map `M.row`, which should be the degree-`w` projection, was not opened, so the identification of `insertRow` with `P_{=q}` is inferred from its place in the recursion.
*Across chapters:* chapter 18 only; "contact" here is sense 1 of *contact*. v3 uses the term with the gloss of 18:407 but without Scott's definitions `def:D36`–`def:D38`; the paragraph 18:401–424 describes a prescription that "is formalized but not used in the main result" (18:422). The contact projections of the source are chosen separately from the probe coordinates of the operator product expansion ("no cross-grade biorthogonality is required", J:592), so they are not the `H_d` of 18:69–72.

#### containing-site bound
*Now:* unchanged. The review of the merge of 26 November 2026 notes an inconsistency inside upstream's own text, left for the author: 6:1249 uses "containing-site bound" after upstream deleted its definition there, and the same quantity is `M_n` in `17-trace-law.tex` and `H_n` in `17-variable-windows.tex` (merge-2026-11-26.md; the line is 6:1249 by grep, the record says 6:1251).
*Variants:* containing-site sum; containing-site norm; site norm `‖z‖_α`; support norm; site bound; site sum.
- **Meaning.** The bound `sup_x Σ_{λ: x ∈ S_λ} e^{α c_B(S_λ)} a_λ ≤ ε` (6:1178–1185), and the norm it defines, `‖z‖_α = sup_x Σ_{γ: x ∈ X_γ} |z_γ| e^{α c(X_γ)}` (8:69–74): every activity is counted at each site of its support, as opposed to an anchored sum, which counts it at one chosen anchor ("It counts every polymer at each site in its support. A norm which counts a polymer only at a chosen base point, an *anchored* norm, is different", 8:75–76). Chapter 4 has both kinds side by side: of the two sums of (ch04:weighted-sums) the first, for regular activities (localized terms), is anchored and the second, for large-field activities, is of the containing-site kind, and "Replacing an anchored sum by a sum over the terms whose localization domain contains `x`, a *containing-site* sum like the second, requires a bound for the number of possible base points; it is not a harmless notational change" (4:646–650). "The support norm" (8:197; 11:219; 11R:7) has no formula; at 8:197 it stands directly after the site norm and is read as that norm, while at 11:219 ("the stronger support norm") and 11R:7 ("All support norms in this subsection use connected covers and include full dependence regions") it is generic: any of the support-weighted norms, with the emphasis on the exponent or on the choice of cover and support.
  *Basis:* D (4:646–650; 6:1178–1185; 8:69–74); I for "support norm". *Where:* 4:648; 6:1181, 1233, 1249, 1322; 8:69–79, 144, 197; 9:515–520, 609, 699, 896; 11:174, 219, 256, 258, 267, 302, 337, 790, 1479, 1486, 1521, 1526, 1535, 1583, 1950; 11R:7, 75, 126, 143, 171, 182, 315, 320, 323, 331; 13sb:36. *Proposed:* *site norm `‖z‖_α`* (*containing-site norm*), kept and defined once, against *anchored norm* and against the *incidence* sum over the terms containing a given insertion; always with the exponent and the cover function stated. "Weighted polymer-activity norm" alone would cover all three and drop the distinction the text insists on (4:646–649; 8:75–78).
  *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.Activities.KBound` (YM/RG/Activities.lean:102–104; definition read: for every site `x`, `Σ_i [x ∈ (forced i).support] · mass (forced i).support (b i) ≤ budget`, with `‖K_i‖ ≤ b_i`), `YM.RG.BudgetPoint.mass` (YM/RG/Masks.lean:144; definition read: `exp(supportExponent · coverNumber B X) · c`), `YM.Lattice.coverNumber` (YM/Lattice/Support.lean:70–71; definition read: least number of balls with connected union covering `X`). The anchored counterpart is `YM.RG.Activities.EBound` (YM/RG/Activities.lean:98–100; definition read: for every site `x`, the sum of `mass (reg i).support (b i)` over the regular activities with `(reg i).site = x` is at most `budget`; see *anchored*).
*Literature:* no named norm in Bałaban: a sup bound per domain together with the sum over domains containing a fixed cube (B88a p. 8, (1.26): `Σ_{X∈D_j, X⊃□′} exp(−κ d_j(X)) ≤ O(1)`, "This inequality was used many times in convergence proofs for cluster expansions"; B88b p. 260); in D1 the norm `‖E‖_{k,κ} = sup_X ‖E(X)‖_k e^{κ d_M(X)}`, used with the "standard bound" `Σ_{X⊃□} e^{−κ_0 d_M(X)} ≤ K_0` (D1 p. 1330010-19, (119); p. 1330010-20; D2 App. D "Connected polymer sums"). An analogue: the literature takes a supremum over polymers and gives up part of the decay rate to sum; v3 puts the sum in the norm. Suggested: keep, defined once; state that it is the summed form of Dimock's `‖·‖_{k,κ}`.
*Across chapters:* one notion in chapters 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, under the names "containing-site sum / bound" (chapters 4, 6), "site norm" (chapter 8; 9:609, 699), "containing-site norm" (9:520), "site bound / site sum" (chapters 6, 11, 11R). The support-weighted norms of the book are three normalisations and not one norm: (a) this one; (b) the anchored norm, one designated site per term (regular activities; remainder norm of 11:362–366); (c) the sum over the terms containing a given insertion, with the source weight `ω^{|I|}` (the incidence bound, also at 11:1443–1446: "its incidence bound at `(ω, e)`"). The "site norm" of 9:699 refers to the hypothesis 9:661, which is of form (a) at exponent `σ+1` (read from the v3 text; inferred). The sum of 12:179–180 ("Summing the norms of (ch04:weighted-sums) over the finitely many sites") is not (c): the density there carries no insertions. It is (b) for the regular activities and (a) for the large-field activities, the two norms of the activity arrays; summing either over the finitely many sites of the torus bounds the unweighted total, which is all that 12:179–181 uses. The source has the same argument: "To pass from a rooted weighted sum to its unweighted sum on a fixed torus, sum the rooted inequality over all its sites. Every nonzero factor has nonempty assigned support and is counted at least once; all removed support and extra-cost weights are at least one" (Martin existence/parameter-comparison-suppliers.tex:31–35); that 12:179 was written from this passage is inferred from the identical argument. 9:515–520 distinguishes (b) from (a), and 11:267–273 converts one into the other.
*See also:* anchored; incidence; connected covering number; site conversion; support-weight reserve.

#### contraction estimate of the graph transform
*Formerly:* *rebasing contraction*.
- **Meaning.** "They are the input for the contraction estimate of the graph transform on the coefficient graphs" (11:467–468). The contraction property of the map `G ↦ G' = R_G M_G^{-1}` (11:447) on the ball of coefficient graphs: outgoing graphs differ by at most half the (normalized) difference of the incoming ones. "Rebasing" is the passage from the incoming coefficient `x` to the outgoing coefficient `M_G x` as the variable in which the remainder is written, by the inverse bound `|x| ≤ s_f|M_G x|` (11:445–446). The difference of two outgoing graphs then has two parts, the changed remainder at fixed input, bounded by (ch11:graph-difference), and the changed input coordinate; the condition `4δ s_f ≤ 1` (11:464) makes each at most a quarter.
  *Basis:* S; I from the v3 text (11:447, 454–468). *Where:* 11:467. *Adopted:* *contraction of the map `G ↦ G'`* (*the graph contraction*), as "the contraction estimate of the graph transform".

This is the graph contraction used in Lemma E-fixed-level"). No Lean declaration was sought.

#### coordinate hybrids
*Now:* removed (14lc:97–98 now reads "Include a strip for each configuration taking every coordinate from the point or from its rounding (finitely many)").
- **Meaning.** For two configurations `x, y ∈ (ℝ⁴)^n` (at 14lc:97 a configuration and its rounding to the grid), a coordinate hybrid is any configuration each of whose `4n` coordinates is taken either from `x` or from `y`; there are finitely many (at most `2^{4n}`). They are the intermediate configurations met when `x` is moved to `y` one coordinate at a time, and the displacement estimate needs each of them to have separated coordinates; hence "Include a strip for each configuration taking every coordinate from the point or from its rounding (finitely many); the total volume of the strips is still `O(δ_k)`" (14lc:97–98). "Hybrid" occurs nowhere in the chapter files.
  *Basis:* S (14lc:97–98 now states which configurations, but not why they are needed). *Where:* 14lc:97–98 (described, not named). *Adopted:* the second option, *the intermediate configurations obtained by replacing the coordinates of a point by those of its rounding*, in the form quoted above.
  *Source:* Scott part2/E-section.tex:583: "A coordinate hybrid of `x, y` chooses each coordinate from either configuration."; :590 (Lemma `lem:E-displacement`): "If `|x−y| ≤ r` and every coordinate hybrid has coordinate separation at least `4r`, then …"; :614: "Replace the `4n` coordinates one at a time. Each starting configuration is a coordinate hybrid and hence has the required separation."; part2/I-section.tex:105: "include a strip for each coordinate hybrid, a finite union of volume `O(δ_n)`". No Lean declaration was looked for.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. 14lc:97–98 now states the content of the defining sentence of Scott part2/E-section.tex:583, without the word; it does not say that the configurations arise when the coordinates are replaced one at a time.

#### coordinatewise splice
*Now:* removed (7:646 now reads "the link read at a fixed position sits at a translate of a point having some coordinates of each endpoint").
- **Meaning.** For two endpoints `x, y` of a coordinate path and a set `s` of coordinate axes, the point whose coordinates on the axes in `s` are those of `y` and whose other coordinates are those of `x`. A coordinate path from `x` to `y` has four straight pieces, one per axis; after the axes in `s` have been traversed it is at this point, so the link read at a fixed position of the next piece sits at a translate of it: "For the coordinate contours of the transporters, the link read at a fixed position sits at a translate of a point having some coordinates of each endpoint" (7:645–646). The map `(x,y) ↦ (splice_s(x,y), splice_s(y,x))` is an involution of the space of endpoint pairs and preserves the uniform measure; this is the "measure-preserving coordinate permutation" of 7:647–648.
  *Basis:* S. *Where:* 7:646. *Adopted:* "the link read at a fixed position sits at a translate of the point `(y_i)_{i∈s}, (x_i)_{i∉s}`".
  *Source:* Martin `existence/weighted-frame-penalty.tex:78–83`: "For pairs of endpoints, a coordinate path has four straight pieces, each of length at most `2(J+3)L`. At a fixed position along one piece, the link read is a translate of the coordinatewise splice of the two endpoints. Swapping the corresponding endpoint coordinates is a bijection of `𝓑×𝓑` and preserves its uniform measure." Lean `YM.Stationary.panelSwap`, `YM.Stationary.swapPanel`, `YM/Next/STATIONARY/FrameEst/Averages.lean` (definitions read): `panelSwap v s = fun i => if i ∈ s then v.2 i else v.1 i`; `swapPanel s` is the equivalence `x ↦ (panelSwap x s, panelSwap x.swap s)`; lemma `stopPanel` (statement read): the endpoint of the route through the axes in `s` is `panelSwap p s`.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. The text now says that the link "sits at a translate of" the point, as the source and the adopted wording do (the intermediate "is a translate of" made the link itself a translate of a point); the sentence about four straight pieces is still missing, and the name "coordinatewise splice" is not used.
*See also:* connector; fixed-position read.

#### corrected
*Now:* partly replaced by *inclusions of the (interacting) field spaces* (sense 2, 18gq:8, 115); remains in sense 1 (kept, as proposed), now glossed as Wick products with respect to the free field (11:2071; 14lc:53; decision 5 of 25 November 2026), and in "corrected projection" (sense 2, 18gq:111, not applied).
*Variants:* corrected coefficients `R_I`; Wick products of the `F_i` (11:2071) or of the insertions (14lc:53) with respect to the free field; corrected source `Jq_N`; corrected word; corrected moment estimates; corrected pair bound; corrected projection; no longer in the text: corrected-source estimate (14lc:45, now "the estimate for the corrected coefficients"); corrected (physical) inclusions.
1. **With the free moments subtracted on every subset.** `R_∅ = 1`, `R_I = ∏_{i∈I} I_i − Σ_{∅≠J⊆I} G_J R_{I∖J}`, with `G_J` the free moments: "These are the Wick products of the insertions with respect to the free field (the moments `G_J` are those of the free field, not of the lattice measure), and precisely the coefficients of the squarefree source polynomial divided by the free moment polynomial … For the limiting Gaussian variables every nonempty coefficient has expectation zero" (14lc:53–59); "Define the corrected coefficients, the Wick products of the `F_i` with respect to the free field, by the recursion" (11:2071); "Equivalently subtract its finite connected logarithm" (11:2104). Explicitly `R_{i} = I_i − G_{i}` and `R_{12} = (I_1 − G_1)(I_2 − G_2) − (G_{12} − G_1G_2)`: `R_I` is not the product of the centred insertions. The inverse relation is `∏_{i∈I} I_i = Σ_{J⊆I} G_{I∖J} R_J`. Three points fix the object. (a) The `I_i` are the lattice insertions, functions of the lattice field; `R_I` is a function of the lattice field. (b) The numbers `G_J` are the correlations of the *free* (Maxwell) fields with the chosen labels at the rescaled points, not the lattice expectations of `∏_{i∈J} I_i`; hence the lattice expectation of `R_I` is not zero, and its smallness is the estimate (ch11:n-mark-root), `‖R_I‖_root ≤ H^{−1/(16n)}`. (c) In the algebra generated by commuting variables `z_i` with `z_i² = 0`, `Σ_I R_I z_I = ∏_i (1 + z_i I_i) · (Σ_J G_J z_J)^{-1}`, and `Σ_J G_J z_J = exp(C^ref)` with `C^ref` the polynomial of free connected correlations; so the "corrected source" `Jq_N`, `J = exp(−C^ref)` (11:766–771), is the same operation applied to the density.
   *Basis:* D (11:2069–2075; 14lc:47–53); S for the explicit cases and the inverse relation. *Where:* 11:769–771, 1841, 2069–2075, 2101–2104; 14lc:45–59; 15:18, 255, 260; 17w:87 (since 25 November 2026 "the polynomial `Σ_IG_Iz_I` of free moments", not the corrected polynomial). *Adopted:* keep *corrected*, defined by the recursion (11:2071–2075; 14lc:47–51, "define by recursion"), and call `R_I` the *Wick products* of the insertions *with respect to the free field* (11:2071; 14lc:53), by the author's decision 5 of 25 November 2026. Never *Wick-ordered insertions*: the sources and v3 use "Wick ordering" for the removal of the internal contractions of a single insertion. Not *truncated* or *connected*.
   *Source:* Lean `YM.Extra.WeakScaling.corrected`, YM/Extra/WEAK_SCALING_ACTLAW/Rooted.lean (definition read: for a finite set `I` of slots and a lattice configuration `U`, `corrected I U = insertions I U − expected v x I − Σ_{∅≠t⊊I} expected v x (I∖t) · corrected t U`, by recursion on the cardinality of `I`; `insertions I U = ∏_{i∈I}` (lattice insertion `i` at its cell location)`(U)`; `expected v x s = disc (within v s) x`, the correlation of the free table at the rescaled points `x` with the labels of `v` in the slots of `s` and the identity field in the others; the value on `∅` is not used; module docstring: "Product corrections defined recursively by triangular free moment subtraction (i.e. the coefficients after formally dividing the source by the free moment series in commuting square-zero variables). In particular not the simple product of centered variables."); `multiply_back` (statement read: `insertions I U = expected I + corrected I U + Σ_{∅≠t⊊I} expected (I∖t) · corrected t U`, the inverse relation); `finite_comparison` (statement read: `‖⟨∏_{i∈I} I_i⟩ − G_I‖ ≤ (1 + #{∅≠t⊊I}·B)η` from chessboard bounds `η` on every `corrected s`, `s ⊆ I` nonempty, and `|G_s| ≤ B`); two-slot case `YM.Push.FiniteDetection.corrected p q a b c = (p−a)(q−b) − (c−ab)`, YM/Push/FINITE_DETECTION/Roots.lean (definition read). Scott part2/E-section.tex:506–521: "Let `𝒢_J^ν` be the Maxwell moment of the labels `(𝔪_{j_h})_{h∈J}` at `(y_h^{ν,i})_{h∈J}`, with `𝒢_∅^ν = 1`. Define the relative errors by `R_∅ = 1`, `R_I = ∏_{h∈I} F_h^tst − Σ_{∅≠J⊆I} 𝒢_J^ν R_{I∖J}`", with the singleton and pair cases displayed and "Thus the pair error subtracts the connected free two-point value from the product of the centered insertions"; part2/G-section.tex:279–285: "This subtracts the full continuum Gaussian moment on every subset of slots; for exact continuum Gaussian variables its nonempty coefficients have expectation zero, by induction on `|I|`". Martin existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:152–154, 281: "The propagation keeps their invoice, meaning the original marked density after subtraction of its prescribed free connected coefficients", "every nonempty corrected coefficient has the root bound"; existence/allarity-cumulant-comparison.tex:163–176, 216–218: "Taking the finite logarithm … the cumulant polynomial is uniquely determined by the moment polynomial"; "its sum with the compensating negative free cumulant is bounded by `H^{−31/32}`". "Wick" in the three texts: Scott part2/E-Gaussian-sources.tex:108, 113: "Gaussian contraction and Wick ordering are the mutually inverse operators `e^{Δ_C/2}π`, `:π:_C = e^{−Δ_C/2}π` … We Wick-order each insertion with respect to its internal contractions; contractions between distinct insertions remain"; Scott part2/E-section.tex:521: "A lift is the reference coefficient whose Wick-ordered leading polynomial at scale `r_ν` is the specified basis element"; Martin existence/allarity-cumulant-comparison.tex:17–22: "Let `𝒲_{Q,μ}` be the Wick evaluation with symmetric covariance `Q` and mean `μ`", defined by the Gaussian recurrence, that is, the Gaussian expectation of a polynomial; v3 3:101–103: "We write `:P(x):` for the Wick-ordered insertion `(P,x)`".
2. **Relative to the naive inclusion of polynomials**: the former "corrected (physical) inclusions", now "the inclusions of the interacting field spaces" (18gq:8) and "the inclusions of field spaces" (18gq:115), are the maps `ι_{d,e}: F_d → F_e` of 13:265–266 ("It remains to identify this low plane of the cutoff scale with interacting lower degrees; it is not the naive inclusion of unnormalized polynomials", 18gq:95–96); the "corrected projection" (18gq:110–111) is identified with `Π_u x_u` of the normalized-null argument (13:197–205) by matching "division by one plus the norm of their corrected projection" with `1 + ‖Π_u x_u‖` (13:202).
   *Basis:* R for the inclusions (18gq:95–96); I for the projection. *Where:* 13:197–205, 222, 265–266; 18gq:8, 95–96, 115 ("inclusions"); 18gq:111 ("corrected projection"). *Proposed:* *the inclusions `ι_{d,e}`* (adopted, as "the inclusions of field spaces"); *the projection `Π`* (not applied).
*Across chapters:* two unrelated senses, chapters 11, 14lc, 15, 17w against 18gq. Sense 1 is not the truncated (connected) coefficient. Neither source manuscript, and nothing in the formal source, calls `R_I` a Wick product; they use "Wick ordering" only for one insertion with respect to its own (internal) contractions, and "Wick evaluation / Wick's rule" for Gaussian expectations. Since 25 November 2026 v3 does call `R_I` the Wick products with respect to the free field (11:2071; 14lc:53), by the author's decision, and states the first qualification below at 14lc:53 ("the moments `G_J` are those of the free field, not of the lattice measure"); the recursion is kept as the definition. What is established is the formula: `Σ_I R_I z_I = ∏_i(1 + z_i I_i) / Σ_J G_J z_J` in the squarefree algebra, with `G` the free moments. Whether to call this a Wick product is a question of convention for a mathematician: the relation is the generating-function definition of the multilinear Wick (Appell) polynomials, `:exp(Σ z_iX_i): = exp(Σ z_iX_i) / E exp(Σ z_iX_i)`, restricted to squarefree monomials (general knowledge, not from a source), with two qualifications that a reader must be told: the reference moments `G_J` are those of the limiting free field and not those of the measure under which the `I_i` are integrated, so `R_I` is not centred on the lattice; and it is not the Wick ordering of each insertion separately (not stated in the text; 3:101–103 still uses "Wick-ordered insertion" for that other operation). v3 should restore the two explicit cases and the sentence of Scott part2/E-section.tex:521, "Thus the pair error subtracts the connected free two-point value from the product of the centered insertions", after 14lc:52. In sense 2 the text does not say why the projection is "corrected".
*See also:* corrected body product estimate; corrected free-subset polynomial; corrected logarithm.

#### corrected body product estimate
*Now:* replaced by *inflated product bound (ch11:integrated-component) for the factors without insertions* (11:1668–1669).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: body product estimate; inflated product estimate (source only).
- **Meaning.** The product-integral bound for the factors without insertions of one step of the restarted history: for every finite collection `I` of such factors, `(∏_{a∈I} μ_a) ∫ ∏_{a∈I} |X_a| dν ≤ ∏_{a∈I} z_a`, where `ν` is the probability law of the step, `μ_a = m` for a factor with a nonempty prescribed set of large-field sites and `μ_a = l` for the others. "Body" is the source's word for the factors without insertions ("body letters"); "corrected" refers to the family of these factors built from the representation with the additive remainder removed. In v3 this is the common local integral bound with inflation factors `m, l` of 11:275–293, (ch11:integrated-component), verified for the restarted representation at 11R:287–335 ("This proves the inflated product bound", 11R:334). The v3 form has one factor `t_C` per compatible connected collection `C` (`m` if some factor prescribes large-field sites, `l` if none does and some factor is nonprincipal, `1` if purely principal) and bounds `t_C |∫∏_{j∈C} F_j dν| ≤ ∏_{j∈C} b_j` (11:283–292), not a product of individual inflations.
  *Basis:* S for the former wording; R now, since 11:1668–1669 cites (ch11:integrated-component): "This calculation requires the decay kept aside and the inflated product bound (ch11:integrated-component) for the factors without insertions of the restarted representation". *Where:* 11:1668–1669. *Adopted:* *the inflated product bound for the unmarked factors, (ch11:integrated-component)*, with "factors without insertions".
  *Source:* Martin existence/actual-mixed-marked-compiler.tex:102–112 ("The body-letter product estimate on the actual sector measure supplies …: if `I` is a collection of body letters and `X_I` is the product of their nonnegative absolute weights, then `M_I ∫ X_I dν ≤ ∏_{a∈I} z_a`. Here `M_I` is the product of their individual inflations: a letter with nonempty forced inventory contributes `m`, and any remaining body letter contributes `l`"); existence/actual-corrected-body-compiler.tex:1–9 ("The corrected unmarked alphabet on the actual block … also use the representation with the additive remainder removed"); existence/restarted-rank-history.tex:640–662, 698 ("the inflated body-product premise"; "the inflated product estimate itself"). No Lean declaration located.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. 11:1668–1669 now cites (ch11:integrated-component); the identification with 11R:287–335 is still by the matching inflation factors `m`, `l`, not by a cross-reference.
*See also:* alphabet; inflation factors.

#### corrected free-subset polynomial
*Now:* replaced by *the polynomial `Σ_IG_Iz_I` of free moments* (17w:87, on 25 November 2026, the dictionary's proposal): "The quadratic covariance and the polynomial `Σ_IG_Iz_I` of free moments are common to all subsets" (17w:86–87). The phrase no longer occurs.
- **Meaning.** The polynomial `Σ_I G_I z_I` in the nilpotent source variables whose coefficients are the free moments `G_I` of the chosen labels on the subsets `I` of insertions (`G_∅ = 1`), used through its inverse: the corrected coefficients `R_I = ∏_{i∈I} F_i − Σ_{∅≠J⊆I} G_J R_{I∖J}` of 11:2069–2076 are the coefficients of the source multiplied by that inverse ("The polynomial `Σ_I G_I z_I` has constant coefficient one, so its inverse exists there. Multiplying the density with insertions by this inverse gives exactly the displayed recursion", 11:2101–2103). The former "The quadratic covariance and corrected free-subset polynomial are common to all subsets" (17w:86–87) said that one covariance and one such polynomial serve every subset `I`, as at 11:2098 ("There is no new normalization for individual spectator subsets").
  *Basis:* I (17w:86–87 with 11:2069–2076, 2101–2104); the phrase occurs once and 17w does not point to chapter 11 at this place. *Where:* formerly 17w:87. *Adopted:* *the polynomial `Σ_I G_I z_I` of free moments* (the identification is the applying agent's, from 11:2068–2103, with no source sentence; `repairs-apply.md`).
  *Source:* for the wording only: Martin `existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:300–302` ("The factor `P_n` is the finite polynomial in the absolute free subset moments appearing when the connected subtractions are undone") and `existence/fullmesh-fixedbounds-producer.tex:411–413` ("undoing the finitely many connected subtractions costs the free-subset moment polynomial `P_k`"); Scott `part2/I-section.tex:105` ("use the corrected Gaussian source of Lemma `lem:E-Gaussian-sources` on every subset of the `n_ar` slots"). These show that "free-subset" means "of the free moments of the subsets" and "corrected" means "after the connected subtraction"; none of them is the source of the sentence 17w:86–87.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence; sense 1 of *corrected*. It remained possible that the author meant the corrected source `Σ_I R_I z_I` and not the correcting polynomial `Σ_I G_I z_I`; the two determine each other, and "common to all subsets" fits the second, which the text now names.

Further variants in chapters 10–11: "narrow band" (10:408, 433, 494), "reserved band" (10:532, 679), "comparison band" (11:1881), "reference band" (10:793). *Proposed:* *the interval `[β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`*; or keep, defined once.
*Literature:* no name for the band. The two-sided logarithmic bound of B87 Theorem 2, p. 259, (0.31): `1/g² + β log(L^kε)^{−1} ≤ 1/g_k² ≤ 1/g² + β′ log(L^kε)^{−1}`, "there exist constants β, β′, 0 < β ≤ β′", under the hypothesis "contained in an interval ]0,γ]"; a close analogue of the inner barriers, `ℓ_m ≤ β_m ≤ u_m`, with `g^{−2} = β̄` and `log(L^kε)^{−1} = τ_m`. The coefficient itself is the **effective coupling constant** `g_k` (`β = 1/g_k²`), "running coupling constants", against the **bare coupling constant** `g_0` (B87 pp. 250, 255, 259); the same object. For the pair reference coupling `β̂_m` against actual coupling: **ideal flow** against **actual flow** (B95 p. 112: "As the actual flow differs from such an ideal flow due to renormalization operations performed at each step, we interpret the equalities (2.9), (2.11) as definitions of this ideal flow"); in D3 "running coupling constants" `λ_k, μ̄_k` (pure scaling) against "dynamical coupling constants" `ε_k, μ_k` (p. 2135), with the allowed region `|μ_k| ≤ λ_k^{1/2}`, `‖E_k‖ ≤ 1`; an analogue. In B88b the effective coupling is a function `g_k(x)` on the lattice near large-field regions (p. 253: "functions on the lattice `T` instead of the constants"); v3 has one number `β`. Suggested: *a priori interval for the effective coupling (cf. B87 (0.31))*, "band" kept as a defined word; *reference (ideal) coupling `β̂_m`* and *actual coupling*, citing B95; *effective (running) inverse coupling* for `β`, *bare coupling* for `β_{N,p,N}`.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout. The set `𝔅_m` is defined at 4:462–463 without the name; the name "coupling band" is first given at 10:215–216 (text read), so chapters 6 and 9 use the name before it is introduced, for the set of chapter 4.
*See also:* coupling threshold.

#### coupling constant renormalization
*Formerly:* *residual scalar inverse coupling correction `q_m`*.
*Also in the text for:* the former *reset*; *scalar*; *scalar correction* (see those entries).
*In the text:* ("`q_m` is the coefficient `Δ` of the coupling constant renormalization of the step", 10:424–425; "Their coefficients `q_m` of the coupling constant renormalization converge as well", 10:819; both since 25 November 2026, decision 52).
*Variants:* coefficient `Δ` (9:725, 750; 10:424); coefficients `q_m` of the coupling constant renormalization (10:819); no longer in the text: coupling constant renormalizations `q_m` (10:819); scalar correction (in this sense; "The scalar correction" of 17m:208 is another object); coupling correction (in this sense; the draft `09-forest-average.tex:21` still has "the inverse coupling correction in Section ch09:subtraction").
- **Meaning.** The operation that fixes the output inverse coupling, `β = β′ + α + Δ` (9:719–725), and its coefficient `q_m = β_m − β_{m+1} − α_{N,m}`; "`q_m` is the coefficient `Δ` of the coupling constant renormalization of the step. It is not the vacuum energy renormalization" (10:419–425), that is, not the additive normalization constant (10:268–269; "additive vacuum normalizations", 10:821–822). It is the `Δ` of equation `ch09:reset` (`β = β' + α + Δ`, 9:721, with output coupling `β = β_m`, input `β' = β_{m+1}` and `α = α_{N,m}`, "the coefficient `α_{N,m}` fixed by the matching", 10:425–426); the bounds agree (`|Δ| ≤ C_j H_pre / t_m²`, 9:735, against `f_m = C ε x^{−11/10} / t(x)²`, 10:651).
  *Basis:* D (9:719–725; 10:419–425); R for the identification with `Δ` (10:422 against 9:721, 725), now stated at 10:424. *Where:* 9:719; 10:424–425, 449, 654, 775, 819, 845–846, 905; 13sb:26. *Adopted:* *coupling constant renormalization* for the operation and *the coefficient `Δ` (`q_m`) of the coupling constant renormalization* for the number (decision 52 of 25 November 2026; applied at 10:424, 819).
*Literature:* see *reset*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 9 uses the name for the whole operation `β = β′ + α + Δ` (9:719–725: "the increment of the inverse coupling is the coefficient `α` fixed by the matching plus the coefficient `Δ`") and calls `Δ` alone "the coefficient `Δ`" (9:750). The author decided on 25 November 2026 (decision 52) that the name is the operation's and `q_m` its coefficient `Δ`; 10:424 and 10:819 now say so. 10:449, 654, 775, 845–846, 905 and 13sb:26, which still used the name for the number `q_m`, were brought into line on 26 November 2026 ("the coefficient of the coupling constant renormalization"). The letter `q` is reused for the per-site vacuum bound (`q_k`, `q^site`) in chapters 11–13 and for `q_i` in chapter 17.
*See also:* reset; rates `e_i`, `q_i`.

#### coupling threshold
*Now:* replaced by *lower bound on the reference coupling* (*lower bound on `z`* in 9s, where `z = β̂_{m+1}`); the compound "coupling-threshold" at 13ba:262, 265 ("coupling-threshold requirement", "coupling-threshold conditions"), which named a condition on the minimum starting scale, was replaced on 25 November 2026 (decision 48) by "requirement on the starting scale" and "conditions on the starting scales". The word no longer occurs in the chapter files (grep); the variant "stage threshold(s)" remains at 11:523 ("Choose the stage threshold so `C_e e^{−B/64} ≤ 1/2`") and 11:1909 ("The stage thresholds can impose"), not converted (whether these are lower bounds on `β̂` was not determined).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: coupling-threshold requirement / conditions (13ba:262, 265; a different object, see *Across chapters*); coupling thresholds; inverse coupling threshold (chapters 10–11); stage threshold `d_j` (10:158–159; but see 11:523, 1909 under *Now*); coupling entry threshold (7:1203); coupling-threshold-controlled (17w:76); "the threshold" unqualified (9:203; 9s:224).
- **Meaning.** A lower bound imposed on the reference coupling `β̂` (at a stage, after the block ratio `L` has been chosen) above which the estimates hold: "choose `L` so that `CL^{-2} ≤ 1/4`, then the lower bound on the reference coupling" (7:1202–1203); "Only afterwards choose the lower bounds on the reference coupling and minimum auxiliary periods. Enlarging such a lower bound does not change the block ratio" (10:38–39); "Every subsequent such lower bound `d_j` is satisfied by increasing its starting scale until `β̂_m ≥ d_j`" (10:158–160); "sufficiently large lower bounds on the reference coupling" (13sb:41).
  *Basis:* R (7:1202–1203; 10:38–39, 158–159; 11:443–444). *Where (now "lower bound on the reference coupling", or "on `z`" in 9s):* 6:327, 437; 7:1203; 9:146, 203, 432, 711; 9s:212, 224; 10:38, 39, 110, 158–159, 630, 646; 11:279, 443, 711; 11E:32; 11R:10; 13:239; 13sb:16, 41, 45; 13ba:39, 50, 83, 101; 14lc:71; 18lp:101, 148; 17:134; 17w:24, 43, 74, 76, 95; 17c:142, 235, 237, 386, 388; 17m:142–143, 174, 185, 315, 346–347, 365, 427; 19:20. The former "coupling-threshold" at 13ba:262, 265 named a condition on the starting scale (see *Across chapters*). *Adopted:* *lower bound on `β̂`* (depending on the stage `j` and on `L`); in running text *for `β̂` sufficiently large*; the text writes "lower bound on the reference coupling".
*Literature:* see *threshold* for the small-field threshold `t_m`; the lower bounds on `β̂` have no named counterpart.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout, now with one wording. The former "coupling-threshold requirement" and "coupling-threshold conditions" of 13ba:262, 265 were not this sense: the condition imposed there, `b_q log 3 ≥ 2 log(ȷ_q+7)`, is on `b_q`, "the minimum starting scale" of the stage (10:122–127: "Let `b_j, c_j` be nonnegative integers specifying respectively the minimum starting scale and a requested number of consecutive scales at stage `j` … include `b_j log 3 ≥ 2 log(ȷ_j+7)`" (upstream's wording since the merge of 26 November 2026; before, "a requested length for a stage plateau")), not a lower bound `d_j` on `β̂` (10:158–160). Adopted for 13ba:262, 265 on 25 November 2026 (decision 48): "a permitted finite requirement on the starting scale" and "among the conditions on the starting scales of Section (ch10:schedule)" (the dictionary had proposed "lower bound(s) on the starting scale(s)", as at 10:63, 609, 695; 12:124); not *lower bound on the reference coupling*. "Threshold" alone is not safe: it is also the small-field threshold `t` (an upper bound on the field; 2:326; 9:19; 17c:317; 17m:304) and the restarted large-field threshold `ϑ` (11:749). The other former thresholds are now written as lower bounds: "lower bound on the period" (2e:210), "lower bound on `N`" (12:266; 13:27, 390; 11:1124, 1820, the former mesh threshold), "lower bound(s) on the starting scale(s)" (10:63, 609, 695; 12:124).
*See also:* coupling band.

*Now:* partly replaced by *infinite lattice `ℤ⁴`* (sense 1) and *connected covering number* (sense 2); remains at 10:81 ("fixed cover paths"), 11:495 ("cover units"), and in "lift" (1:181; 11:399–400, 414); in sense 2 "cover" also remains in "cover cost" (11:244), "coarse cover" (11:396), "(change of) cover radius" (11:515, 528; 11R:189, 282, 322; 18lp:112), "connected (`B`-)cover" (11:489, 1426, 1433, 1438; 11R:177), "bounded-cover" (11:1411), "cover bound" (11R:139, 350) and "support cover" (6:1228) (grep).

1. **The infinite lattice `ℤ⁴` as universal cover of the tori**; the former "cover coefficients" and "cover row" are the kernel on `ℤ⁴`, as opposed to its periodisation, now "the coefficients on the infinite lattice `ℤ⁴`" (5:735) and "the infinite-lattice kernel" (5:849).
   *Basis:* R (4:18; 5:735, 751). *Where:* 1:181 ("lifts"); 2:291, 295, 366, 381; 2e:210; 4:18; 5:735, 751, 806, 820, 828, 849 ("infinite lattice" or "`ℤ⁴`" on each line); 10:81 ("cover paths"); 11:399–400, 414 ("lift"). *Adopted:* *the infinite lattice `ℤ⁴`*; *infinite-volume kernel* (as "infinite-lattice kernel").
2. **A connected cover of a set by balls of radius `B`**, in "connected covering number" (formerly "connected cover number", 11:1374), "fine connected covering number" (formerly "fine cover number", 6:1302), "cover units": see *connected covering number*.

#### cross-modes
*Now:* not applied (17m:401 still reads "pushed spectator cross-modes").
*Variants:* pushed spectator cross-modes.
- **Meaning.** The coefficients of the joint marked expansion that are indexed by sets of marks containing the score source together with one or more spectator marks, the spectators having been integrated down ("pushed") to the current level. "The same differentiated kernel is used for every `A`, so the joint rooted expansion retains all pushed spectator cross-modes and this exact zero-moment statement" (17m:400–402); the "differentiated kernel" `𝒟_Y k` (17m:396) was formerly called the "score source". A "mode" is the coefficient of `z_I` for a subset `I` of marks.
  *Basis:* S for "mode"; I for "cross" and "pushed" (17m:393–402). *Where:* 17m:401. *Proposed:* *all mixed source–spectator coefficients*.
  *Source:* the coefficients are those of the monomials `z_I`, `I` a set of marks: Scott `part2/E-several-mark.tex:22` "Rescaling mark `h` by `𝗐_h > 0`, its mark weight, multiplies the coefficient of `z_I` by `∏_{h∈I} 𝗐_h`"; `part2/E-Gaussian-sources.tex:159` "to any mode in one cell" (the word "mode" for such a coefficient). `audit/ch17-score-independent-review.md:8, 45`: "All generated joint modes must remain …"; "retaining all original fine spectator modes". No Scott sentence has "cross-modes".

#### curl-division
*Now:* partly replaced by *the choice of coordinate contours* (for "path-placement operations", 10:317); "curl division", now unhyphenated, remains at 10:317 and 17c:348 (kept, as proposed).
*Variants:* curl division (10:317; 17c:348); two-leg division (7:1175); no longer in the text: path-placement operations (10:317–318).
- **Meaning.** The division by the lattice curl of chapter 7 (section "Division by the lattice curl", 7:68 ff.), built from the elementary division `D_a f(p) = (f(p) − f(p|_{p_a=0}))/(e^{ip_a} − 1)` (7:90–92). Chapter 10 fixes these linear operations once in order to make the representation by transported curvature terms unique (10:316–319). The former "path-placement operations" fixed in the same sentence, now "the choice of coordinate contours" ("For comparisons we fix the linear curl division and the choice of coordinate contours of Chapter 7 once on the common index sets of the coefficients", 10:317–319), are the second half of the same construction: after the division, the Fourier coefficients `g(z)` of the curvature kernel are turned into transported curvature terms by choosing, once and for all, coordinate contours from the origin to the displacements `z_1, …, z_{n−1}` and putting the `j`-th curvature factor at the end of its path, `F_{γ,ab}(U,x)` of (ch07:slot) (7:149–155). Division and placement are both linear in the input kernel, which is what 10:316–319 uses.
  *Basis:* R (7:68, 90–92; 10:316–319) for the division; R (7:149–164) for the placement on contours, now also R (10:317–318) for its identification with the choice of coordinate contours of chapter 7. *Where:* 10:317; 17c:348 ("Two-leg curl division leaves one extra difference"); 7:1175 ("the two-leg division"). *Proposed:* *division by the lattice curl (Section 7.…)*; *the choice of coordinate contours (ch07:slot)* (adopted at 10:317, citing the chapter and not the equation); keep, cite chapter 7.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/C-section.tex:139`: "Fix the order of axes, the shears, the coordinate paths and the strip losses in this construction once and for all. The restrictions, divisions and corrections in the proof are linear in the input kernel. Fourier inversion and the placement on paths are linear too. In the normalized Taylor tensor, average over leg permutations … before placing paths." Martin `existence/multileg-curvature-lift.tex:306–309` "For each tuple `(𝐚, z)` of oriented coordinate plaquettes and displacements, put the zeroth plaquette at the origin and plaquette `j` at `z_j ∈ ℤ⁴`".
*Across chapters:* defined in chapter 7, used in chapters 10 and 17c (text read at 10:316–319 and 7:68, 89–92, 149–164). "Placement" at 7:763 is a different use (see *placement*, sense 3).
*See also:* placement.

1. **The ultraviolet cutoff `N`** (the finest level). "Outer cutoff" is `N` (13ba:53, 224); the former "cutoff threshold", the `N_0` beyond which a bound holds, is now "the lower bound on `N`" (12:266; 13:27, 390); the former "cutoff tail", all sufficiently large `N`, is now written so (12:191, 250; 13sb:85).
   *Basis:* R (5:705–706). *Where:* 1:15, 209, 387; 5:705; 9:949 ("ultraviolet cutoff" on each line); ch. 10 passim; most of the 66 uses in ch. 12–16. *Adopted:* *ultraviolet cutoff `N`*; *for all sufficiently large `N`*.
2. **A smooth cutoff function** (`χ` in chapters 3, 14, 16; `γ` in chapter 11).
   *Basis:* R (3:758; 11:544–557). *Where:* 3:758; 9:478; 14:257, 331, 335, 354, 403, 621, 627, 632, 743; 16:209, 237, 240, 288, 465, 545 ("cutoff function" on each line); 11:315, 544–557, 708 ("cutoff"). 13ba:36, 165 do not belong here: the former "smooth cutoff" there is an indicator, as the text now says ("small-field indicator"; the factor `𝟙_{small-field stencil}` of 13ba:218–220; 10:98). 13ba:68 no longer has the word ("its large-field part"). *Adopted:* *cutoff function* (outside chapter 11).
3. **A threshold on the field, or the indicator of the condition it defines**: `ε_pred`, `t_m` (4:215, 224, 406: "the threshold"); the former "level-`m` cutoff", now "the regularity condition at scale `m`" (12:188); the former "pass the cutoff", now "satisfy the regularity condition `χ(U_p) ≤ t_f`" (9s:131–132); the former "cutoff-to-noise ratio", now "the ratio of the threshold to the fluctuation scale" (11R:62–63).
   *Basis:* R (4:215, 450). *Where:* 4:215, 224, 450; 9s:132; 11R:62; 12:188 (with the new words); 9s:10 ("cutoff"). At 7:25 the text now has "the small-field region", at 9:112 "event labels", at 9:842 "relaxed regularity condition". *Adopted:* *threshold*; *regularity condition* where the threshold is the plaquette threshold `t_m`; at 11R:62 *ratio of the threshold to the fluctuation scale `g`*.
4. **Truncation of the path length at `R_*`**.
   *Basis:* R (6:23). *Where:* 6:23, 911; 11:672 ("path-length truncation"). *Adopted:* *path-length truncation*.
*Across chapters:* senses 1, 2 and the compound "cutoff condition" run through the book; sense 4 no longer uses the word, and sense 3 keeps it only for the integration cutoff of 9s:2, 10, 113 and in the compounds with "cutoff factor" listed under *Now*. At 14:331 "independent of the cutoff function" refers to the function `χ`, not to `N`. The compounds "cutoff failure", "failed cutoff condition" have their own entry; they are *large fluctuation-field events*, not events of the large-field set. The former "cutoff tail" (12:191, 250; 13sb:85) is not the *ordered tail*.
*See also:* cutoff amplitude; cutoff failure; cutoff remainder.
