#### cutoff failure
*Now:* replaced by *large fluctuation-field event* (sense 1) and *failure of the regularity condition* (sense 2); "failed-cutoff factor" stands again at 11:1482, 1493, 1506, 1529 and "failed cutoff" at 11:1937 (sense 2), after a period as "large-field factor"; since 25 November 2026 it is defined at 11:1482 (decision 47): "*failed-cutoff factors* (the terms `−(1−χ)Rz_I` of the factors `1−(1−χ)Rz_I` in the proof below, which vanish where the cutoff `χ` equals one)" (11:1482).
*Variants:* failures of smooth local cutoffs (6:9, now in apposition); failed-cutoff factor (11:1482, 1493, 1506, 1529); failed cutoff (11:1937); no longer in the text: failed cutoff condition; failed remote cutoff (9:281); cutoff-failure indicator (6:1025, now "cutoff remainder"), label (now "event label"), probability, catalogue.
1. **The event that a Gaussian coordinate is large where the field is small**, so that a smooth local cutoff differs from one: "Large fluctuation-field events, the failures of smooth local cutoffs in the remaining coordinates, are controlled by simultaneous Gaussian tail estimates" (6:9–10); the event is `ℰ_w = {∃ i : d(i,w) ≤ 2B, |z_i| ≥ T}`, `T = ξ t_f/(2g)` (6:843–849). In chapter 9: "Distinct event labels" (9:112); "large fluctuation-field event at a distinct event label" (9:134); "a large fluctuation-field event far from the index triple has the joint Gaussian-tail bound of Chapter 6" (9:281–282).
   *Basis:* R (6:7–11, 843–849). *Where:* 6:9; 9:134, 281; 10:535, 598–600, 730; 11:1619; 11R:284, 312 ("large fluctuation-field event" on each line); 9:112 ("event labels"); 6:1025 ("cutoff remainder"); 11R:285 ("event-indicator factors"). *Adopted:* *large fluctuation-field event* (defined once), the region where it occurs being a *large fluctuation-field region*; *the event `{|z_i| ≥ T for some i near w}`*. The large-field set proper (`Bad_m(U)`, the selection `A`) keeps "large-field"; the event is not called "large-field event" without "fluctuation".
   *Source:* for the catalogue and for the word "warning": Martin existence/gaussian-warnings.tex:4–7 ("A warning factor, for example, need not be small on a configuration with a large fluctuation. What is small is the probability that all warnings in a given term are present"); existence/parameter-comparison-suppliers.tex:30 ("The warning catalogue is finite on the fixed torus and its finite jet bounds can also be summed"); existence/selected-history-limits.tex:454–457 ("deterministic statements about the fixed sector, warning catalogue and thresholds … They do not involve the activity array"); existence/local-parameter-comparison.tex:303–304 ("Packets and warnings have finite catalogues"). No Lean declaration was sought for the catalogue.
2. **Failure of the small-field indicator, that is, presence of a large-field site**: "The covering condition of the disjoint covering families ensures that the link support of a large-field part containing a failure of the regularity condition meets at least one selected support" (11:152–153); the "failed-cutoff factor", defined since 25 November 2026 as the term `−(1−χ) R z_I` of the factor `1 − (1−χ) R z_I` (11:1482), `χ` the restarted small-field indicator (11:1315), whose "support contains a large-field indicator covered by an original prescribed large-field set" (11:1493–1503); "Every nonzero failed cutoff and every old large-field activity meets a new large-field site. Its selected site factor has size at most `e^{−2u}`" (11:1937–1939). These factors are suppressed by the large-field site factor, not by a joint Gaussian tail, so they are not large fluctuation-field events (sense 1).
   *Basis:* R (11:152–153, 1493–1503, 1937–1940). *Where:* 11:152–153; 11R:379 ("failure of the regularity condition", "the regularity condition fails"); 11:1482, 1493, 1506, 1529 ("failed-cutoff factor"), 1932 ("failed cutoff"); 11:1568 ("large-field part"). *Adopted:* *failure of the regularity condition*; *large-field site*. *Adopted:* *failed-cutoff factor*, kept by the author and defined at 11:1482 (decision 47 of 25 November 2026); not *large-field factor* (which names the incoming factors carrying a prescribed large-field set, 11:247–926; 10:657) nor *large fluctuation-field event*. The definition names the term `−(1−χ)Rz_I`, whereas 11:1493 ("A failed-cutoff factor of nonconstant source monomial `I` occurs in the exact …") and 11:1937 ("Every nonzero failed cutoff") may be read of either; not checked further.
*Literature:* **large fluctuation field** characteristic function, the set **`R_j`**, "new large fields" (B88b p. 252, (1.23): `χ({sup |A'(b)| ≥ g_0^{-1} δ_0})`; p. 255: "a large fluctuation field characteristic function associated with the set `R_j`"; B89a p. 188, (1.55): "`χ'^{(j)} = χ({|B_j(b)| < δ'_j …})`. We exclude from `Z` the components with the large field function `1 − χ'^{(j)}`"; p. 181: "In components with the function `1 − χ` we have introduced new large fields"; B88a p. 12: the event `{|B(b)| ≥ ε_1/g_k}`; B87 p. 256: "χ_k restricts the integral to small fluctuation fields"); violation of `|W_k(x)| ≤ p_{0,k}`, `ζ^w_k(□) = 1 − χ^w_k(□)`, the region `R_{k+1}` (D2 p. 092301-43: "Anticipating that the factor exp(−½‖W_k‖²) suppresses large W_k we define χ^w_k(□, W_k) = Π χ(|W_k(x)| ≤ p_{0,k})" and "The new large field regions Q_{k+1}, R_{k+1}"). Sense 1, the event `ℰ_w = {∃ i : |z_i| ≥ T}`, `T = ξ t_f/(2g)`, is the same object in role, with the same form of threshold (`g^{-1}δ = A_1 p_0(g)` against `ξ t_f/2g`); it was classified "analogue" against B88a and B88b–B89b and "same object (role)" against D2, without disagreement on the content. The naming is opposite: Bałaban and Dimock call this a large (fluctuation) field event and add its location to the large field region; v3 does not, because a cutoff failure does not enlarge `Bad_m(U)` and is bounded by a joint Gaussian tail estimate. Adopted (23 November 2026): *large fluctuation-field event*, on a *large fluctuation-field region*, which is Bałaban's and Dimock's name (the set `R_{k+1}`); the earlier *cutoff-failure event* and the rule "never large-field event" are withdrawn. The difference is stated at first use: Bałaban and Dimock add the location of the event to the large field region; v3 does not, and bounds it by a joint Gaussian tail estimate. The entries *large-coordinate event*, *tail events* and *warning* say the same.
*Across chapters:* Sense 1 is a *large fluctuation-field event*, not an event of the large-field set: chapter 6 separates the two mechanisms (6:7–11), as Bałaban separates large plaquette or background fields from large fluctuation fields. Text read (6:1021–1025; 10:533–536; 11:149–154, 1492–1498, 1617–1620, 1936–1939): chapters 6, 9, 10 and part of chapter 11 have sense 1, and chapter 11 also has sense 2. The former "failures" of 17m:121–129 are of sense 1: the text now calls them large fluctuation-field events (17m:121, 122, 127, 129; decision 50 of 25 November 2026; see *failure*). The former "cutoff-failure catalogue" (10:730), now "the list of large fluctuation-field events", is the finite list of the cutoff-failure factors of a step on the fixed torus, the source's "warning catalogue"; it is part of the combinatorial data fixed at each level independently of `N` and of the activity array (S); with the clipping data, *the fixed data: prescribed large-field sets, list of cutoff events, clip parameters*. 10:396 ("event indicators") and 10:924 ("clipping data") name the same fixed data. The former "tail events" (11R:44–46, 284–285) are now "large fluctuation-field events" (11R:44, 284) and "event-indicator factors" (11R:285), the events of sense 1, those of (ch06:tail-event). The source's "warnings" at 6:1483 and 11:320 are now "cutoff remainders" (see *warning*). 6:11 now states the comparison with Bałaban in the text: "Bałaban makes the same split, into large plaquette fields and large fluctuation fields; he adds the location of a large fluctuation field to the large-field region, whereas here the large-field set is not enlarged and these events are bounded by a joint Gaussian tail estimate".
*See also:* complementary; cutoff-failure label; cutoff remainder.

#### cutoff remainder
*Now:* unchanged (now defined at 6:840, as proposed); since 26 November 2026 6:1025 also states the convention for the zero remainders: "a cutoff factor other than a chart cutoff whose location … meets `A^{[300B]}`, and a chart cutoff on a link whose projected endpoints meet `A^{[304B]}`, is not written as one plus a cutoff remainder: it is kept whole as a factor of the sector, and its cutoff remainder is set to zero" (from Lean `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Coat.mandatory`, `Coat.mayor`, `Coat.aura` and Martin `gaussian-warnings.tex:206–208`; margin note).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: warning (6:1483; 11:320); cutoff-failure indicator (6:1025); both lines now say "cutoff remainder(s)".
- **Meaning.** One factor of the local expansion of chapter 6: the difference `W_w = F_w − 1`, where `F_w` is one of the cutoff factors attached to an address `w`. The cutoff factors are the fine-plaquette and block-average-discrepancy cutoffs (the allocation weights of 6:68–76), the normalised weights of the frame tags and of the block-average tags, the inventory tests, and the chart cutoffs on active fine links; the addresses are, respectively, fine plaquettes, coarse edges, coarse sites and coarse edges, fine sites, fine edges (the inventory tests are those called contraction factors under *warning*). Near a large-field component the difference is part of the component factor. "A cutoff remainder, a cutoff factor minus one, is bounded but need not be pointwise small. Its smallness comes from a large fluctuation-field event" (6:840–841): it vanishes, with all its derivatives, unless some Gaussian coordinate within `2B` of the address is at least `ξ t_f/(2g)` (the event `ℰ_w`, 6:843–849), and its amplitude is bounded by the fixed constant `M_w` (6:1111–1113).
  *Basis:* D (6:840) in the short form "a cutoff factor minus one"; S for which cutoff factors are meant; R (6:840–849) for its properties. *Where:* 6:745 ("Cutoff remainders (defined in the next section)"), 834–843, 892–898, 1018, 1025, 1040, 1046, 1476, 1483; 11:320. *Adopted:* keep *cutoff remainder*, defined once as "a cutoff factor minus one".
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:1173`: "Cutoff remainders are the departures from one of the fine-plaquette and mismatch cutoffs, the frame and predictor tag likelihoods, the inventory tests, or the active chart cutoffs. The addresses are fine plaquettes for fine cutoffs, coarse edges for mismatches and predictor tags, coarse sites for frame tags, fine sites for inventory tests, and fine edges for chart cutoffs. … Near a large-field component the corresponding departure is included in its component factor"; Scott `part2/D-section.tex:96`: "(v) the cutoff remainders of Lemma B-D2, that is, the failures of the fluctuation, chart, tag and inventory tests. Put `W_a = F_a − 1`"; Martin `existence/gaussian-warnings.tex:206–207`: "A warning factor is either a bounded cutoff times one of these factors minus one, or a bond cutoff minus one." Lean declarations: see *warning*.
*Literature:* the **complementary characteristic function** `ζ(□) = 1 − χ(□)` (D2 p. 092301-31: "with ζ^q_k(□) = 1 − χ^q_k(□)"; p. 092301-42); the **large field function** `1 − χ` (B89a p. 181); the factor `χ^c_{k,P} = ∏_{b∈P} χ({|B(b)| ≥ ε_1/g_k})` with sign `(−1)^{|P|}` in the "decomposition of the characteristic functions `χ_k`" (B88a p. 12, (2.3): "χ_k = χ_{k,Y_0} χ_{k,Y_0^c} = Σ_{P⊂Y_0^{c*}} (−1)^{|P|} χ_{k,Y_0} χ^c_{k,P}"). An analogue of `W_w = F_w − 1`: Bałaban expands the sharp small-fluctuation indicator as `∏(1 − χ^c)`, each `−χ^c` being "cutoff minus one" with a Gaussian tail factor per bond of `P` (B88a (2.31)); in B88b the sharp `1 − χ'` is a term of a decomposition of unity whose cubes `R_{k+1}` become part of `Λ_{k+1}^c` (pp. 268–269), with smallness "by the same positivity bound for the quadratic form" (B89b p. 380). v3's cutoffs are smooth and of five kinds (plaquette, mismatch, tag weights, inventory tests, chart), and its remainders form a polymer instead of enlarging a region. "Warning" has no source. Suggested: *cutoff remainder* = "the factor `cutoff − 1` of the expansion of the small-fluctuation cutoff (B88a (2.3)); complementary cutoff factor".
*Across chapters:* chapters 6 and 11 (11:320: "the joint tail bound for cutoff remainders"), now under this one name at 6:1025, 1483 and 11:320, which had "cutoff-failure indicator" and "warning(s)". These Gaussian-tail objects are distinct from the large-field selection `A` and from `Bad_m(U)`, which the chapter treats by a separate mechanism (6:7–11); Scott `part2/D-section.tex:107`: "A cutoff remainder and an output flag are different objects." 6:840 now gives the short definition; the list of cutoff factors of Scott `B-section.tex:1173` is still not stated there.
*See also:* cutoff failure; warning; likelihood; compulsory.

#### cutoff-scale coordinates
*Formerly:* *inverse terminal coordinates*.
*Also in the text for:* the former *terminal map* (see those entries).
*In the text:* (11:888, 949–950, 961, 1080; 13:161, 219).
*Variants:* subpower cutoff-scale coordinates; no longer in the text: subpower inverse terminal coordinates.
- **Meaning.** For a coefficient `z` at the reference scale, the vector `𝖹_{N,p,d}^{-1}z`: its coordinates at the cutoff scale, obtained by inverting the terminal map `𝖹_{N,p,d}`, the composition of the single-insertion coefficient maps from the cutoff `N` to the reference scale (11:1052–1054). "Recall that `𝖹_{N,p,d}` transfers a cutoff coefficient to its fixed reference scale. A comparison coefficient is admissible when its inverse coordinates under `𝖹_{N,p,d}`, its *cutoff-scale coordinates*, have a uniform subpower bound" (11:886–889); "It bounds cutoff-scale coordinates, not the raw reference labels" (11:961). "Subpower" means bounded by a sequence subpower in `a_N^{-1}`, independently of the period; this is the definition of an admissible coefficient family, "`‖X_i^{-1}z_i‖_1` is bounded by a sequence subpower in `a_N^{-1}`" (11:1106–1107), where `X_i = 𝖹_{N,p,e}` by 11:1094. Chapter 13 says "subpower cutoff-scale coordinates" without naming the variable.
  *Basis:* D (11:888); R (11:1094 with 1101–1102). *Where:* 11:888, 949–950, 961, 1080; 13:161, 219. *Adopted:* *coefficients at the cutoff scale, `𝖹^{-1}z`*, in the form *cutoff-scale coordinates*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/actual-insertion-derivative-relay.tex:38–40 ("Write `ξ_{N,p} = X_{N,p}^{-1}x_{N,p}` for the actual inverse terminal coordinates of a label row. If this row is subpower in those coordinates, its insertion has protected local bounds at weight `d`").
*Across chapters:* one sense, defined in chapter 11 (11:888) and used in chapter 13. The two readings formerly kept apart, `𝖹^{-1}c` and `‖X_i^{-1}z_i‖_1`, are the same: 11:1094 sets `X_i = 𝖹_{N,p,e}` (text read), and the source defines the phrase by `ξ = X^{-1}x`; v3 now names the coordinates at 11:888, before their use at 11:949.
*See also:* terminal map; microscopic; level.

#### defect
*Now:* not applied (the senses keep the word; "signed defects" at 6:218 was removed, the sentence now reading "The two terms `E_L, E_D`, which are not of definite sign, must therefore be estimated locally", 6:217–218).
*Variants:* defects; quadratic defect; defect Ward identity; no longer in the text: signed defects.
1. **Place where the small-curvature condition fails.** "Connected sets of defects are summed" (1:457).
   *Basis:* I (1:457). *Where:* 1:457. *Proposed:* *large-field regions* (or *large-field sites*).
2. **Curvature defect** `Z₀ = B_c − T*B_fT − b⁻¹d₁d₁*`; the former "two signed defects" of 6:218, `E_L`, `E_D`, are no longer called defects.
   *Basis:* R (5:638–641). *Where:* 5:638–641; 6:139 (only in the label of (ch05:positive-defect)). *Proposed:* as for *curvature defect*; write the symbols.
3. **Current defect** `𝓔_b = Σ_a ∇_a J_ab − D𝖲[Y_b]`: the failure of the lattice Ward identity, that is, of current conservation up to the equation-of-motion term. The sentence "The removed gradient is annihilated by the defect Ward identity" (17c:67, removed on 25 November 2026) referred to the Ward identity of the Hessian symbol `E_b(p,q)` of the defect in each of its two field arguments: `𝓔_b` is gauge invariant, so its Hessian at zero vanishes when either argument is a gradient ("Gauge invariance gives a Ward identity on each leg", 17c:16; "The Ward identity on each leg, `B(d_{0,f}φ,a′)=B(a′,d_{0,f}φ)=0`, holds for finitely supported `φ`", 17c:57; "Since `W_F − W_a` is a fine gradient, the Ward identities of `E_b` allow us to compute with the smooth representative `W = W_a`", 17c:53–54; quotation updated: before 24 November 2026 the text had "Fine gauge changes of `W` have no effect on this quadratic calculation by the Ward identities of `E_b`"). It is not the Ward identity whose failure the defect measures.
   *Basis:* D (17:196–197); R (17c:16, 53–54, 57) for the Ward identity of the defect. *Where:* 17:196, 246; 17t:160, 411, 419; 17c:6, 13, 17 and more; 17m:154, 234 ("the current defect"). Counts not redone after 25 November 2026. *Proposed:* *defect of the lattice Ward identity*. The proposal for 17c:67 lapsed: the sentence was removed and 17c:57 now writes the identity as a formula.
4. **Internal defect** `[L(K), L(M)] − L([K, M])`, the failure of the rotation generators to represent the Lie bracket.
   *Basis:* R (14:938–940). *Where:* 3:910; 14:939–944. *Proposed:* as for *internal rotation defect*.
*Across chapters:* four objects under one word: sense 1 once, in the introduction; sense 2 in chapters 5–6; sense 4 in chapters 3 and 14; sense 3 in chapter 17, where it is new relative to the curvature defect.
*See also:* `Bad_m(U)`; curvature defect; current defect; defect space; internal defect.

#### definition by derivatives in left increments
*Formerly:* *split-field definition*.
*In the text:* ("the left-coordinate response, whose definition by derivatives in left increments was used above", 7:633).
- **Meaning.** The definition of the Hessian by splitting the field into two factors: it is "obtained from `S(log(e^{x_+}e^{x_-}))` by two `x_+` derivatives" (7:369–370). The increments act by left multiplication, as in the left derivative `D_A^L F(U) = d/dε F(exp(εA_e)U_e)` of 2:318–321.
  *Basis:* R (7:369–370). *Where:* 7:369–370 (the definition); 7:633 ("whose definition by derivatives in left increments was used above"). *Proposed:* *second derivative in left-multiplication increments* (no fixed standard phrase). Not *left-invariant coordinates*: left multiplication is generated by right-invariant vector fields.
*Across chapters:* chapter 7 only.
*See also:* left increment.

#### delay
*Now:* replaced by *lower bound on the starting scale (of the stage)*; *increase of the starting scale* (11:1220, 1273, 1276, 1769, 1949); *starting scales* (11:2090, 2116).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: stage delay; finite delays; uniform delay; terminal delays (10:107–112).
- **Meaning.** The requirement that a stage, or the cutoff level, start at a sufficiently large level `m`, so that a fixed constant is dominated by a slowly growing quantity or a lower bound on the reference coupling is met: "Every subsequent such lower bound `d_j` is satisfied by increasing its starting scale until `β̂_m ≥ d_j`" (10:158–160); "A lower bound on the starting scale of the stage can impose `C_k ≤ H^γ`" (11:1198); "The stage choices of sufficiently large starting scales impose a common bound `H^{ε_j}` … This uniform lower bound on the starting scale" (11:1403–1408). The conditions of 10:107–112 are the same kind of condition at the cutoff level `N`: "absorbed by choosing sufficiently large lower bounds on the reference coupling", "Those lower bounds on the starting scales also impose `β̂_N ≥ a_{d,J(N)}`", which 11E:29–30 places "in the adjacent stage conditions on the starting scale".
  *Basis:* R (10:158–160; 11:1403–1408; 10:107–112). *Where:* 10:107, 111; 11:1198, 1205, 1220, 1273, 1276, 1408, 1769, 1949, 2027, 2090, 2116, 2151 ("starting scale(s)" on each line). *Adopted:* *lower bound on the starting scale of the stage*; state the inequality imposed (`β̂_m ≥ d_j`, `β̂_N ≥ a_{d,J(N)}`), which the text does at 10:112 and 10:159–160.
*Across chapters:* chapters 10–11 only; one kind of condition, the former terminal delays of 10:107–112 included. The condition is now written "lower bound on the starting scale", "increase of the starting scale", "condition on the starting scale".
*See also:* stage; coupling threshold; block floor.

#### density coordinates
*Now:* replaced by *representation data* (4:592, 609, 668, 699, 713–719; 9:7); *representation of the (effective) density* (4:8, 447, 574).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: coordinate tuple; "the coordinates of Chapter 4" (9:6–7).
- **Meaning.** The data `(β, v_sc, localized terms, large-field activities)` that represent a density. The data satisfying the norm bounds form a "much larger set" than the reachable outputs (4:717–720), and "Representation data satisfying the definitions alone need not give a positive density" (4:609); the text says nothing on injectivity. That these are therefore not coordinates in the usual sense is an inference.
  *Basis:* D (4:592). *Where:* 4:8, 447, 513, 574, 592, 699–719; 9:6–7, 401, 719–722, 906. *Adopted:* *representation of the density* (*representation data `(β, v_sc, activities)`*).
*Literature:* "inductive description of the effective actions"; "inductive assumption on the form of approximate effective actions" (B87 p. 260, title of Sect. 1; formula (1.3): `−(1/g_k²)A(U_k) + Σ_j {−β_{j+1}(g_j)A(U_k) + [log Z^{(j)}(U_k) − log Z^{(j)}(1)] + [E^{(j+1)}(g_j,U_k) − E^{(j+1)}(g_j,1)]}`; B85e p. 265, title of Sect. B, (41)). The represented object is the **density** `ρ_k`, the **effective density**, whose small-field logarithm is the **effective action** `A_k` (B85e p. 256: "This yields a sequence of densities ρ_k defined inductively by ρ_{k+1} = Tρ_k"; B87 p. 249; B95 p. 109: "the sequence of effective densities ρ_k"; D1 p. 1330010-6; BIJ85 p. 299: "the effective actions S^{(k)} obtained by k iterations"); the same object as v3's effective density, the iterate of the block transformation. The representation is an analogue: in Bałaban everything is a function of the background field `U_k(V)`, not of the coarse links directly, and B87, B88a represent only the small-field part ("under the simplifying assumption that integrals are restricted to small fields", B87 p. 250), so "effective action" is not v3's effective density off the small-field set. "Coordinates" has no precedent. Suggested: *inductive form (representation) of the effective density*; add a headword *effective density* = "Bałaban's density `ρ_k`", saying once that Bałaban's "effective action" is minus its logarithm on small fields.
*Across chapters:* one object; chapters 10–11 call it "local representation", and 11R "representation" (formerly "presentation"). Not *parametrisation*: nothing in the text makes the data a parametrisation. The phrase at 9:6–7 is now "in terms of the representation data of Chapter 4".
*See also:* presentation; scalar.

#### direction selectors
*Now:* replaced by *the four constant maps in the vector regulator that take a one-form to its components* (7:434), and on 25 November 2026 given their symbol and formula: "The four constant maps `J_a` in the vector regulator `M_μ=Σ_aJ_a^*m_μJ_a`, where `J_a` takes a one-form to its component in direction `a`, do not" (7:434).
- **Meaning.** The four linear maps `J_a` (`a = 1,…,4`) from one-forms (link fields) to site fields, `(J_a u)(x) = u(x,a)`. The vector regulator is `M_μ = Σ_a J_a^* m_μ J_a`, which is "`M_μ` applies `m_μ` to each one-form component" (7:281). They depend neither on the background field nor on the momentum, so they contribute nothing to the derivatives: "The four constant maps `J_a` in the vector regulator `M_μ=Σ_aJ_a^*m_μJ_a`, where `J_a` takes a one-form to its component in direction `a`, do not change these powers" (7:434–435).
  *Basis:* S; I from the v3 text (7:281, 434). *Where:* 7:434. *Adopted:* *the four constant maps `J_a` taking a one-form to its `a`-th component*, with the symbol and the formula `M_μ = Σ_a J_a^* m_μ J_a` (7:434, since 25 November 2026).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/C-section.tex:259`: "let `J_a` select direction `a` from fine links, so `M_μ = Σ_a J_a^* 𝔪_μ J_a`"; `:348` "The constant direction selectors in the vector regulator preserve these bounds." Martin `existence/annulus-same-data-binding.tex:367–368`: "The direction selectors are constant matrices, so their marked slots are zero." Lean `YM.Stationary.copiesV`, `YM.Stationary.brigadeM`, `YM.Stationary.rankAux`, `YM/Next/STATIONARY/Spectral/AuxReferences.lean` (definitions read): `copiesV a` is the component map (lemma `notes_u`, statement read), `brigadeM U = Σ_a (J_a)ᵀ U J_a`, and `rankAux` is a sum of three terms ending in `brigadeM (cannon μ U)`, the `A_μ = A + d_U d_U^* + M_μ` of 7:279 (the first two terms `flare`, `mail` were not read).
*Across chapters:* single occurrence. 7:434 now gives the formula `M_μ = Σ_a J_a^* m_μ J_a` (with `m_μ` of 7:275 and `M_μ` of 7:281, checked by the review); 7:281 itself is unchanged.
*See also:* selected.

#### discrepancy
*Now:* replaced by *the series of the indicator corrections `ζ_f`* (sense 1); *`f(d)`* (sense 2); *difference* (sense 3); *deviation `n_e`* (sense 4); *the normalized residual of (ch11:descent-error)* (sense 5). The word remains elsewhere in other uses (5:1017; 10:364, 725, 766, 869, 871; 11:958; 13ba:287, 290), not covered by this entry, and stands in upstream's new text of 26 November 2026 at 4:253 ("This penalizes the discrepancy in a gauge-invariant way") and 6:137 ("`Z^lin = √b(v − 𝒬a)` is their discrepancy") (grep).
*Variants:* mask discrepancy, supported discrepancy (sources only); no longer in the text: discrepancy series; scalar discrepancy; weighted input discrepancies; block average discrepancy; exterior discrepancy.
1. **Discrepancy series:** the family (and sum) of the functions `ζ_f = (1 − h_Z){f(1) + h_{{o}}Q_f − h_X f}` of 9:487–489, one for each preliminary regular function `f`. `ζ_f` is the difference, on configurations where `Z` is not small-field, between the two sides of the subtraction `h_X f = f(1) + h_{{o}}Q_f + h_Z R_f`, which holds without it when `Z` is small-field; it arises because the three terms carry different event indicators. "Consequently the series of the indicator corrections `ζ_f` has containing-site norm at exponent `σ+1` bounded by `C_j(1+B)^{d_j}H_pre`" (9:519–521).
   *Basis:* R (9:487–500, 519–521). *Where:* 9:519. *Adopted:* *the functions `ζ_f`* (*the indicator corrections `ζ_f`*).
   *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:491–495` "Define the regular remainder and the discrepancy of masks by `R_f = f − f(1) − Q_f`, `ζ_f = 1_{Z unhealthy}{f(1) + h_{{o}}Q_f − h_X f}`"; `:322` "The discrepancy of the health masks is supported near flags and will be included in the forced activities." Martin `existence/physical-reset-reorganization.tex:193–198` "Define the supported discrepancy `d_i = f_i(1) + χ_{{o_i}}P_i − χ_{X_i}f_i + χ_{Z_i}r_i`. It vanishes when `Z_i` is healthy", and `:213` `D = Σ_i d_i`.
2. **Scalar discrepancy:** the function `f(d) = (β′ + α + d)𝒦(U_*) + …` of the shift `d` of the inverse coupling ("vary only a shift `d` of the inverse coupling, and define `f(d) = …`", 9:758–761).
   *Basis:* R (9:758–761). *Where:* 9:759. *Adopted:* *the function `f(d)`*.
3. **Difference between the inputs at two parameter values** ("pass to a subsequence whose weighted input differences have sum at most `ε`", 9:793–794).
   *Basis:* R (9:793–794). *Where:* 9:793–794; 11:1876 ("difference at most `H^{−v}`"). *Adopted:* *difference*.
4. **Block average discrepancy:** the mismatch `n_e = χ(V_e Q_e(U)⁻¹)` between a coarse link and the block average, now defined as "the *deviation* of the coarse link `V_e` from its average `Q_e(U)`" (6:49).
   *Basis:* D (6:47–49). *Where:* 6:8 ("large deviations of coarse links from their averages"), 49, 1015, 1342 ("the deviation `n_e`"). *Adopted:* *deviation `n_e` of the coarse link from its average `Q_e(U)`* (the value of the averaging operation).
5. **Exterior discrepancy:** the residual of the backward matching (11.descent-error) for the source `Σ − βj`, whose exterior moments vanish, after replication and normalisation by (11.replicated-bound); see *exterior discrepancy*.
   *Basis:* R (17m:420–439) for the bound and the two chapter 11 equations used; S for the former name of the object. *Where:* 17m:439 ("Thus the normalized residual of (ch11:descent-error) is at most `e^{−T_n/100}`"). *Adopted:* *the normalized residual of (11.descent-error)*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:395` "Step 1: exterior moments vanish"; `:404` "Step 3: the matched residual is `e^{-H_n/100}`" (quoted under *exterior discrepancy*).
*Literature:* see *mismatch* for sense 4 (block average discrepancy); the other senses have no counterpart in the papers read.
*Across chapters:* five objects formerly under one word; all are differences between two quantities that are expected to agree, and none of the five is now called a discrepancy. The remaining uses (chapter 10; 11:958; 13ba:287–290) are differences of the same kind and were not part of this entry.
*See also:* mismatch; trial inverse coupling correction; exterior discrepancy.

#### distance from the identity
*Now:* partly replaced by the symbol (`χ(V_eQ_e(U)^{-1})`, 4:441); the phrase remains on 18 lines (1:90; 4:59, 373; 5:1016, 1036; 6:49, 245, 349, 426, 430, 1021, 1348, 1411, 1425; 9:754; 9s:221; 11:798, 800; grep).
*Variants:* squared distance from the identity (4:373; 6:1411); no longer in the text: mismatch distance(s) from the identity (4:441); squared group distance (6:1411).
- **Meaning.** `χ(u) = ‖u − 1‖_F / √n_G`, the normalised Hilbert–Schmidt distance of a group element from the identity, with `χ(u)² = 2w(u)` (1:90–95). The phrase is written out where the symbol would do: "adds a nonnegative squared distance from the identity which is zero at the minimizer" (4:373–374), "the nonnegative difference between the squared distance from the identity and the squared curvature representative" (6:1411–1412).
  *Basis:* D (1:90–95); 4:59 and 6:49 are reminders (R). *Where:* 1:90–95; 4:59, 373, 441 (now the symbol); 6:49, 1021, 1411; 9 + 2 + 13 lines in ch. 4, 5, 6 at the earlier count (18 occurrences of the phrase now). *Proposed:* write `χ(U_p)`, `χ(·)²`; the symbol is defined once, at 1:90 (applied at 4:441 only).
*Literature:* no name; `χ(u)` is `‖u − 1‖` in the **normalised Hilbert–Schmidt (`L²`) norm** `‖X‖² = tr X*X`, `tr X = N^{-1} Σ X_jj` (B85a pp. 20–21, (17)); the plaquette energy `w(u) = 1 − Re tr u/n_G` is `1 − Re tr U(∂p)` with the normalised trace (B85b p. 77, (1.10)). The same object as a function (the identification with the normalised trace is an inference). The papers differ on which norm the symbol `|X|` denotes, and two readings were reported: that `|U − 1|` in Bałaban is the normalised Hilbert–Schmidt norm (from B85c p. 389–390: "in this paper a norm `|X|` of a `N×N` matrix means the Hilbert–Schmidt norm: `|X|² = tr X*X`", and B85d p. 278), and that `|X|` is the operator norm and every regularity condition is stated in it (from B85a p. 21: "In estimates we will use much more frequently another norm for matrices. It is the operator norm", with `‖X‖ ≤ |X|`, `|X| ≤ √N ‖X‖`, and B85b). Both quotations were confirmed in the text layers; the convention changes from paper to paper (B85c says "in this paper"), so both are right for their papers: in B85a, B85b the conditions `|U(∂p) − 1| < …` use the operator norm, in B85c, B85d the Hilbert–Schmidt norm. Suggested: keep `χ`; add "the normalised Hilbert–Schmidt norm `‖u − 1‖` of B85a (17), which is the `|u − 1|` of B85c, B85d; the conditions of B85a, B85b use the operator norm, equivalent up to `√N`".
*Across chapters:* one sense; the definition is in chapter 1 (1:90–95), not at 4:59.
*See also:* mismatch; discrepancy.

#### dummy Gaussian coordinates
*Now:* replaced by *auxiliary standard Gaussian coordinates* (9:59); *auxiliary Gaussian integral* (9:72).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: dummy Gaussian integral.
- **Meaning.** The coordinates of the full real coordinate space, of dimension `D`, that are not Lie-algebra coordinates of active bonds: the tree coordinates and the coordinates of the inactive free bonds, `D − n_act q` in number. The sector precision and covariance act on all `D` coordinates, with an identity block on these; each of them is given an independent standard Gaussian variable, whose integral is one, so that the Gaussian reference measure lives on the whole space while the inactive bonds are still integrated in their original Haar variables. "let `D` be the dimension after auxiliary standard Gaussian coordinates have been added" (9:59–60); "The auxiliary Gaussian integral equals one after the inactive Haar variables have been frozen" (9:72–73). They account for the factor `(2π)^{-(D − n_act q)/2}` in the measure multiplier (9:66).
  *Basis:* R (9:59, 72–73) for their role; S for which coordinates they are. *Where:* 9:59, 72. *Adopted:* *auxiliary standard Gaussian variables on the inactive and tree coordinates* (the text does not say on which coordinates).
  *Source:* Martin `existence/gaussian-reassembly.tex:14–27` "All three [`A`, `A_0`, `C`] act on the full real coordinate space, of dimension `D` … `N` the number of free forest bonds, and `n` the number of active free bonds. The other `N−n` free bonds are integrated in their original Haar coordinates"; `:46–50` "Inactive coordinates are completed by independent standard Gaussians. Their energy is `𝒢(z) = ½ Σ_{i inactive} z_i²`. There are `D − nq` such coordinates, including the tree coordinates. Consequently the change of variables in the active Haar coordinates, with the dummy Gaussian integrals inserted, gives the multiplier …"; `:65–71` "The dummy insertion is exact even though the active integrand depends on the remaining Haar coordinates. Split the latter product measure into active and inactive free bonds and freeze the inactive variables. … In the orthogonal coordinate decomposition into active and dummy real variables, the dummy density integrates to one. Fubini therefore proves the identity for each fixed inactive configuration and then for its Haar integral."
*Across chapters:* chapter 9 only. v3 should still restore the sentence "Inactive coordinates are completed by independent standard Gaussians … There are `D − nq` such coordinates, including the tree coordinates."
*See also:* active coordinates; measure multiplier; missing-coordinate factor.

#### eligible
*Now:* partly replaced by *additional condition, an event `𝓔_i^extra`* (sense 2, 4:485–486, 494) and *allowed (covering families, supports)* (sense 3, 8:297, 333); "eligible" and "eligibility" remain on about 28 lines: sense 1 in chapter 4 (4:73, 80, 237, 349, 401, 403), sense 2 as "eligibility conditions / criteria / event" (chapters 4, 6, 9–13, 18), sense 3 at 11:127.
*Variants:* eligibility; eligibility criteria / conditions / event; eligibility condition (18:129); no longer in the text: eligibility test; eligibility indicators; eligible family.
1. **Pair satisfying the axial bound.** "If the loop condition fails, use axial gauge transformations. Fix `a_ax ≥ 16` and call a pair `(z,o)` eligible when" (4:72–73) `Σ_e χ(U_e^{z,o}) ≤ a_ax (2R+1) Σ_□ χ(U_□)`, the sums over links and plaquettes internal to the box.
   *Basis:* D (4:72–79). *Where:* 4:72–79, 237, 288, 349, 401–403. *Proposed:* *pair satisfying the axial bound* ("axial" refers to the patch frames of chapter 4, with base point `z` and coordinate order `o`; not to the block axial gauge of chapter 5).
2. **Additional condition attached to a large-field activity.** A large-field activity has an exclusion support `Y_i`, a nonempty prescribed large-field set `I_i^bad ⊂ Y_i` and "an additional Borel gauge-invariant condition, an event `𝓔_i^extra`" (4:484–486); the activity vanishes outside `{Bad_m(U) ∩ Y_i = I_i^bad} ∩ 𝓔_i^extra`. `𝓔_i^extra` is a set of configurations (an event). No rule defines it: it is a free datum of the activity, required only to be Borel, gauge invariant and determined by the links and large-field indicators in `Y_i` ("The additional condition reads the same links and large-field indicators", 4:494). The sources and the formalisation leave it equally free.
   *Basis:* D (4:484–494). *Where:* 4:484–494 ("additional condition"); 6:83; 9:94 ("eligibility conditions"), 902, 918; 10:672; 11:133, 155, 762, 791; 11R:81, 157, 167–169; 12:25, 183; 13sb:73; 13ba:253; 18:129. 8:333 now has "allowed supports" (sense 3). *Proposed:* *the additional gauge-invariant condition (event) `𝓔_i^extra` of the activity* for `𝓔_i^extra` alone (applied at 4:484–494); "eligibility conditions" or "eligibility criteria" for the whole event (ch04:eligibility), `{Bad_m(U) ∩ Y_i = I_i^bad} ∩ 𝓔_i^extra` (4:490–491). At 9:94 ("The large-field indicators in their eligibility conditions can read outside `Y_i`") the whole event is meant, since the large-field indicators sit mainly in its first factor; "additional conditions", which stood there for a time, narrowed it.
   *Source:* Scott part2/D-section.tex:34 ("A forced activity with address `(Y_i, I_i, 𝓔_i^extra)`, where `∅ ≠ I_i ⊂ Y_i`, … vanishes outside the eligibility event `𝓔_i^elig` … Its extra test is Borel, gauge invariant, and reads the same links and flags"); part1/05-renormalization.tex:62–65 (`𝓔_i^elig = {U : Y_i ∩ flags_m(U) = I_i} ∩ 𝓔_i^extra`). Lean `YM.RG.ForcedAddress` (YM/RG/Activities.lean:42–47; definition read: `support`, a nonempty `inventory ⊆ support`, and `extraTest : Config G n → Prop`, an arbitrary predicate), `YM.RG.ForcedAddress.eligible` (:54–55; definition read: `support ∩ flags t U = inventory ∧ extraTest U`), `YM.RG.Activities.ForcedFamily` (:77–84; definition read: the test is gauge invariant (`symtest`) and measurable (`meas_test`), satisfies the same locality condition as the activity (`reads_test`; the condition `UsesFinal` was not unfolded), and `K i U ≠ 0` implies `eligible` (`permit`)).
3. **Allowed covering family.** In the abstract polymer setting the same rule appears as a restriction on families: `𝔆(D)` consists of "the allowed finite families `B` of such labels with disjoint supports and `⋃ I_η = D`. The exact rules deciding which covering families are allowed are part of the definition of an effective density; they may exclude some otherwise possible covers" (8:292–298). The sum `Σ_{𝓕 eligible}` of chapter 11 runs over such families.
   *Basis:* R (8:292–298). *Where:* 8:292–298, 333 ("allowed"); 11:127 ("eligible"). *Proposed:* *allowed covering family* (applied in chapter 8, not at 11:127).
*Literature:* no name in either sense. Sense 1 (a pair `(z,o)` with `Σ_e χ(U_e^{z,o}) ≤ a_ax(2R+1) Σ_□ χ(U_□)`, 4:72–79): the underlying fact is the standard axial-gauge estimate, pointwise in B85a pp. 24–25 ("The conditions `V_0(Γ_{y,x}) = 1` imply `V_0(x,x+e_1) = 1`, `|V_0(x,x+e_2) − 1| < |x_1 − y_1| α_0`, …"; "for b ⊂ Δ(p′) we have `|V_{0,b} − 1| < |b_- − y| α_0 < dLα_0`") and for Lie-algebra fields in B84b p. 244, (2.123), `|B(x,x+e_2)|² ≤ |x_1−y_1| Σ |(∂_1B)(p(x'))|²`. An analogue, weak: the same telescoping fact, but Bałaban's bounds are in the sup norm (or pointwise `ℓ²`), with the root fixed at the block corner and under `sup|V(∂p) − 1| < α_0`; nothing corresponds to choosing a root for which a first-power bound holds on arbitrary configurations, and nothing corresponds to eligibility as a selection rule. Sense 2 (the extra gauge-invariant event `𝓔^extra` of a large-field activity, 4:484–494): the **characteristic functions** carried by `T_k`, `χ(Ω_j ∩ Λ_j^c, S_j)` and `ζ(Ω_j^c)` (B88b p. 255: "There is a characteristic function `χ(Ω_j ∩ Λ_j^c, S_j)` associated with these domains, which includes a large fluctuation field characteristic function associated with the set `R_j` … There is also a function `ζ(Ω_j^c)`, which includes summations over other large field characteristic functions"); an analogue: specific products of indicator functions in Bałaban, a free datum in v3. Nothing was found for sense 2 in B87, B88a, B85e or in D1–D3; the counterpart is in B88b only. For "eligible family" see *admissible*. Suggested: sense 1: *pair `(z,o)` satisfying the axial-gauge bound*, with the note that the bound is the summed form of the estimate of B85a pp. 24–25; sense 2: "the additional gauge-invariant condition" stands, with "(Bałaban: the characteristic functions `χ`, `ζ` carried by `T_k`)".
*Across chapters:* sense 1 is confined to chapter 4. Senses 2 and 3 are two forms of one rule (per activity in chapter 4, per family in chapter 8). The later uses are sense 2 (text read): 11:133 ("each large-field term retains its original eligibility and large-field conditions"), 11:155 ("original eligibility criteria" of the constituents), 11R:80–81 and 167–169 attach eligibility to terms and labels, so these are sense 2; 11:127 is sense 3.
*See also:* exclusion support; exact cover; event indicator.

Its integral is the partition function, which chapter 17 formerly called the denominator and now calls the partition function (17w:88).

#### endpoint
*Now:* partly replaced by *comparison scale* ("change of representation at the comparison scale", "density at the comparison scale"; sense 3), *the identity-field parts of the two endpoint values* (sense 6, 17m:471) and *integrated inequalities for the normalized products* (sense 6, 11:880); "endpoint" remains in senses 1, 2, 4, 5 and at 11:2292, 17m:466–471 (sense 6). In sense 1 it is now defined: "a prescribed value `β̄ > 0` of the coupling at unit scale, the *coarse endpoint*" (10:154).
*Variants:* coarse endpoint; endpoint estimate; endpoint comparison; endpoint constants; endpoint factors; no longer in the text: bottom endpoint; endpoint re-expression; unit endpoints.
1. **The level-0 coupling.** The value of the inverse coupling at the coarse end of the trajectory: "Choose a prescribed value `β̄ > 0` of the coupling at unit scale, the *coarse endpoint*" (10:154).
   *Basis:* D (10:154); R (10:212). *Where:* 1:465 ("its coarse endpoint has a prescribed coupling", before the definition); 10:18, 154, 212, 271–275, 281, 816, 853 ("common coarse endpoint", formerly "common bottom endpoint"); 19:21–23. *Proposed:* *value of the coupling at unit scale* (now the gloss at 10:154; the term is kept).
2. **End of an interval of levels.** The lower or upper end of a plateau or of another interval of levels.
   *Basis:* R (10:140–141). *Where:* 10:140–141, 250. *Proposed:* ordinary usage; keep.
3. **Top level `k` of the restart interval.** The level at which the density is re-expressed with new radius and threshold (formerly "exact endpoint re-expression", now "the exact change of representation at the comparison scale", 11:1935; Proposition "Change of representation at the comparison scale", 11R:69).
   *Basis:* R (11R:69–71). *Where:* 11:1935, 2097; 11R:69, 90, 385, 388 ("comparison scale" on each line; the word "endpoint" is gone). *Proposed:* *scale index `k`* (the text has *comparison scale `k`*).
4. **Last step of a range of steps.** The step at the cutoff `N` (11E:123); "the last-step endpoint estimate" and "the endpoint comparison" (13ba:20, 34) are the estimate at the last level of the interval.
   *Basis:* I. *Where:* 11E:123; 13ba:20, 34. *Proposed:* *estimate at the last step*.
5. **Constants entering a bounded number of times.** "Endpoint constants / factors": constants that enter at the ends of the comparison window and not once per step ("Only a bounded number of endpoint factors is multiplied").
   *Basis:* I (17w:24, 27). *Where:* 17w:24, 27. *Proposed:* *constants entering a bounded number of times*.
6. **End terms of a finite difference or of a telescoping sum.** Ends of a finite difference (11:2292); the former "unit endpoints" (17m:471), now "The identity-field parts of the two endpoint values are equal and cancel", the identity-field parts of the two end values of a telescoped average of forward differences (see *unit endpoints*); the former "normalized endpoint inequalities" (11:880), now "the integrated inequalities for the normalized products", the inequalities bounding the difference of the normalized product between the two ends `0` and `l` of the displacement, "a difference at most `A^q l/R`" (11:867–868), obtained by integrating Cauchy's estimate from `0` to `l`; "normalized" is "divided by the partition trace `Z`" (11:879–880).
   *Basis:* R (11:2292; 11:865–869 with 876–877); S for 17m:471 and for the origin of 11:880. *Where:* 11:880 (no longer "endpoint"), 2287; 17m:466–471. *Proposed:* *end terms*; at 11:880 *the inequalities for the differences between displacement `0` and displacement `l`* (the text has "integrated inequalities").
   *Source:* Scott part2/I-section.tex:451 ("the average of `m` consecutive forward differences telescopes to the difference of the two endpoint values divided by the window length `m a_k`. The unit parts of the two endpoints are equal and cancel, leaving at most twice the endpoint error"); Martin existence/centered-estimates.tex:438 ("Cauchy's estimate gives `|Φ_j'(t)| ≤ (∏_i f_{i,j}) Z_j^{1−qθ}/R`. Integrate from `0` to `l`. Taking `j → ∞` in the resulting endpoint inequality is justified by the cyclic quadrature convergence above").
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes with the object that has ends (trajectory, interval, restart window, finite difference). 11:880, formerly "normalized endpoint inequalities", is sense 6 (v3 text read at 11:863–881, with the source sentence it was written from). "Endpoint error" (17m:466–467) is the error of the backward comparison (formerly "trial descent") in each of the two end values of sense 6 ("leaving at most twice the endpoint error", Scott part2/I-section.tex:451; see *trial descent*). The initial vertex of a link is now called its "initial vertex" at 17c:260 (formerly "tail").
*See also:* fine end; re-expression of the endpoint.

#### equation calibration floor
*Now:* replaced by *the lower bound (ch11:calibration-floor) on the block ratio* (19:30); "block floor" at 11E:29 is now "the stage-`j` lower bound on the block ratio".
*Variants:* calibration floor (label `ch11:calibration-floor` only).
- **Meaning.** The lower bound `L^{1/8} ≥ max_{d≤j} 2(1+C_j) Q_{dj} δ_d^{-1}` on the block ratio `L` (label `ch11:calibration-floor`), where `Q_{dj} = 2 + e^{81σ_j}(a_{dj} + C_j + 2q_d)` and `δ_d = (2𝒪_d²)^{-1}` (11E:15–23). The text includes it "in the stage-`j` lower bound on the block ratio" (11E:23–29, formerly "block floor"): that lower bound is the whole collection of lower bounds on the block ratio at stage `j`, and this bound is one member of it. The same sentence adds a separate condition on the coupling, `β̂_N ≥ a_{d,J(N)}`, "in the adjacent stage conditions on the starting scale"; this second condition is not called a floor. 19:29–31 now reads "finite stage requirements, such as the lower bound (ch11:calibration-floor) on the block ratio, belong to these same choices", and so names only the first.
  *Basis:* R (11E:15–30). *Where:* 11E:23–30; 19:30. *Adopted:* *the lower bound (11.calibration-floor) on the block ratio `L`*; the accompanying condition on `β̂_N` is not mentioned at 19:30.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/marked-portfolio-calibration.tex:186–221`: "The sphere bound is `S_i(q_d,a) = 2 + e^{81α_i}(a + c_i + 2q_d)` … [the] sliver `δ_d = 1/(2𝒪_d²)` … Since the volume purse is `P(L) = L^{1/8} → ∞`, choose an integer `n_{di}` such that `2(1+c_i) S_i(q_d,a_{di}) ≤ P(L) δ_d` (`L ≥ n_{di}`)"; the threshold of stage `i` is the maximum of the `n_{di}`, `d ≤ i`, and of the `v_j`, `j ≤ i`, where `(1+2c_j) L^{−2/5} ≤ L^{−3/8}` for `L ≥ v_j`. Lean `YM.MergeProof.sphere` (`YM/MergeProof/Matter.lean:34`; definition read) `= 2 + exp(81·supportExponent)·(b + columns + 2p)`; `YM.MergeProof.sliver` (`YM/MergeProof/Marimba.lean:18`; definition read) `= (2·orbitCost²)⁻¹`; `YM.Bid.puffs` (`YM/Bid/Loan.lean:34`; definition read) `= L^{1/8}`; `YM.PhysicalNext.Repeat.Legato.paper` and `oyster` (`YM/MergeProof/Apres.lean:20–21`; definition and statement read): thresholds `l i` exist such that for all `d ≤ i` and `L ≥ l i`, `2(1+columns_i)·sphere ≤ puffs L · sliver`, together with a credit clause and `(1+2·columns_j)·rate L ≤ barunit L` for `j ≤ i` (`Bid.Credit` and `Doors.rate` were not opened).
*Across chapters:* one sense; used in chapter 19, stated in 11E (text read at 11E:13–31). In the sources the same threshold also contains the inequality `(1+2C_j) L^{−2/5} ≤ L^{−3/8}`, which v3 uses at 18lp:41–42 ("The lower bound on the block ratio makes this at most `L_l^{−3/8} q`") without a reference; v3 should state it with (11.calibration-floor).
*See also:* floor (sense 1); block floor.

#### equation space
*Now:* unchanged; the qualifiers "moving", "varying", "actual" and "microscopic" are now "cutoff-dependent" (11E:153; 11:1088, 2223, 2229) or "at the cutoff scale" (18gq:10), or dropped (11:1112).

- **Meaning.** The image at cutoff `(N,p)` of the equation ideal: `𝖤_{N,p,d} = 𝖹 P S_{t_N} R_d 𝓘_d` (11E:154–158), written `K_i = X_i P S_t R_e I_e` at 11:1094–1098; in chapter 13 it is `ker Π_{d,N,p}`, given by the same formula without a symbol (13:138–139). "Equation comparison" compares the two realisations of the equations of motion.
  *Basis:* D (11E:154–158; 11:1094–1098). *Where:* 11:969, 992, 1088, 1094–1098, 1112, 2223, 2229; 11E:43–46, 153–158; 13:14, 15–16, 138–139, 159, 222, 396; 18gq:10, 111. *Proposed:* *space of equation-of-motion labels at cutoff `(N,p)`*.
*Across chapters:* one object: `𝖤_{N,p,d}` in 11E, `K_i` in chapter 11 (11:1094–1098, 2223), `E_i` in the abstract lemma (11:968–970), and the formula without a symbol in chapter 13 (13:138–139). Not *cutoff-dependent subspace of field equations*: the elements are images of labels; the text now says "cutoff-dependent equation space", which states the dependence without that misreading.
*See also:* equation ideal; equation remainder.

#### `E_stat`, `E_tail`, `E_mark`
*Now:* not applied (the symbols stand, including `E_reg` for both objects at 17m:107 and 161; no defining sentence was added).
*Variants:* `E_reg` as an error coefficient (17m:161).
- **Meaning.** The four error coefficients of (17.finite-sigma), `Σ_k = 𝒫_{5,t}(div_Haar Y − D𝓛[Y]) + E_stat + E_tail + E_reg + E_mark` (17m:158–162). `E_stat` is the change in the degree-five coefficient caused by truncating the stationary kernels at radius `C_j(log β̂_k)²`; `E_tail` is the same for the loop paths of `𝓛` longer than that radius ("Here the kernels of the critical-configuration map and the loop kernels are truncated at `C_j(log β̂_k)²`. Their common exponential decay makes `E_stat` and `E_tail` at most `H^{-1}`", 17m:163–165; until 26 November 2026 "stationary and loop kernels"; the stationary kernels are defined at 17m:27 as "the kernels of the critical-configuration map (the coefficients of its Taylor expansion in the coarse field)", List 2, item 11). `E_mark` is "the remainder with insertions" (17m:176, formerly "the marked remainder"): what the marked step leaves after the radial Taylor coefficients through degree five are cancelled on nonwrapping supports, together with the large-field and wrapping contributions; it is bounded in (17.sigma-error) (17m:325). The fourth error, written `E_reg` at 17m:161, is the classical defect: the degree-five coefficient contributed by the regular term `E_reg` of `Z_ord = 𝒞 exp[−βS − 𝓛 − E_reg]` (17m:107), bounded by `t^{-2} ε_k^reg = β̂_k^{-1/10} H^{-2}` (17m:166–169). By 17m:104–111 and 168–171 ("A directional derivative along `Y` has the same bound") it is the extracted coefficient `𝒫_{5,t}(−D E_reg[Y])` of the directional derivative of the regular term.
  *Basis:* R (17m:163–169, 176) for the bounds; S for what each error is; I for the identification of the fourth error with `𝒫_{5,t}(−D E_reg[Y])`. *Where:* 17m:161–176; (17.sigma-error) 17m:325. *Proposed:* define each in a sentence after (17.finite-sigma); rename the fourth error, for example `E_cl := 𝒫_{5,t}(−D E_reg[Y])`, so that `E_reg` names only the regular term of 17m:107.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:358–362` (I-five-pieces) "`… + ε_stat + ε_tail + ε_cl + ε_mark` … The errors are stationary substitution, omitted loop paths, the classical defect and the marked remainder. Each has norm at most `e^{-h_k}`: truncate stationary kernels and loop paths at `C_j(log β̂_k)²` … The activity caps … bound `ε_cl` in the seminorm of Definition D05a"; `I-section.tex:366` "For `ε_mark`, Lemma E2.2a cancels the radial Taylor coefficients through degree five on nonwrapping supports". Scott names and bounds `ε_cl` and does not write it as a derivative of the regular term.
*Across chapters:* 17m only. One letter `E_reg` is used for the function at 17m:107 and for the coefficient of its derivative along `Y` at 17m:161. `E_tail` is not a Gaussian tail (see *tail*): it is the contribution of the omitted loop paths. v3 should restore, after (17.finite-sigma), the sentence of Scott I:362: "The errors are stationary substitution, omitted loop paths, the classical defect and the marked remainder."
*See also:* regular (sense 1); tail; mark; stationary substitution.

- **Meaning.** The indicator function of a Borel event of the configuration (small-field, large-field or cutoff condition) attached to a term; it is not smooth and is not differentiated: "this indicator may read additional adjacent plaquettes" (4:551); "Multiplication by the indicator of a fixed Borel event preserves uniform convergence; no continuity of this indicator as a function of `U` is required" (12:164–165).
  *Basis:* R (4:551; 12:164–165). *Where:* 4:551 ("indicator"), 532, 658; ch. 6 (7 uses; 6:852 now "the cutoff factors"); 9:19, 284, 349, 410, 496, 502, 543, 547, 549, 573, 577, 839, 841; ch. 10 (11 uses); ch. 11 (8); 11R (8); 17m:83; 12:25, 164–165 ("indicator(s) of … event(s)"). *Proposed:* *indicator of the event*; say which event (applied at 4:549–551 and in chapter 12).
*Literature:* see *test* (sense 3).
*Across chapters:* one sense. It formerly alternated with "test" in chapters 4 and 6; "test" is now nearly gone there (3 lines in chapter 4, 1 in chapter 6, mostly in labels), most uses having become "condition". In chapter 9 not every use is the small-field indicator `h_X` (9:19 is generic; 9:284 and 9:839 are not tied to `h_X`), so the phrase is not a synonym of *small-field indicator*.
*See also:* event label; health; eligible.

#### exact cover
*Now:* replaced by *disjoint covering family* (decision of 26 November 2026), defined at 4:589 ("We call them the *disjoint covering families* of the large-field sites (in combinatorics, exact covers)"); "exact-cover sum" and "exact-cover gas" by *sum over disjoint covering families*, "exact coverage" by *covering condition* or *disjoint covering*. The word remains only in that gloss (4:589) and in the figure label `ch08:fig-exact-cover` (8:299) and the file name `figures/exact-cover` (8:303) (grep).
*Variants:* disjoint covering family; sum over disjoint covering families; covering condition; disjoint covering; no longer in the text: exact coverage; exact-cover family; exact large-field indicator coverage.
- **Meaning.** A family of large-field activities with pairwise disjoint exclusion supports `Y_i` whose prescribed large-field sets have union `Bad_m(U)`; in chapter 8, `⋃ I_η = D`.
  *Basis:* D (4:583–589). *Where:* the new term at 4:506, 580 (title), 589, 606, 661; 6:1330; 8:349; 9:95, 152, 409, 595, 655, 674, 679, 804, 892, 950; 11:152, 249, 252; 11R:169, 184; 12:181, 189; 18lp:186; the families also at 8:292–300 (`𝔠(D)`, "covering families"). *Adopted:* *disjoint covering family* (the dictionary had proposed *compatible family covering the large-field set*).
*Literature:* the expansion of the density as a **sum over large field regions**, over **admissible sequences of domains** `{Ω_j}`, `{Λ_j}` (and `{S_j}`), produced by decompositions of unity, with the **factorization property** of `T_k` (B88b p. 257, (2.18): "`ρ_k(V_k) = Σ_{{Ω_j},{Λ_j}} χ_k(Ω_k) T_k({Ω_j},{Λ_j}) exp A_k(1/g_k², U_k)`, where the summation is over the admissible sequences of domains"; B89a p. 176, (0.2), text layer only: "`ρ(V) = Σ_Z ρ(Z,V)`, where the sum is over large field regions `Z`"; in D2, D3 the sum over nested sequences `Π`). An analogue: in Bałaban each term carries products of sharp characteristic functions, so the sum is a partition of unity over regions followed by resummations ("the factor `ζ(Ω_1^c)` is defined by all characteristic functions … resummed over all admissible `P_0, P_1, Q_1`", B88b p. 248); v3's condition `⋃ I_i = Bad_m(U)` plays the role of that product of characteristic functions, and v3 has no preferred partition into connected components (4:585–589). Nothing was found in B87, B88a (small field only), B85e (an inequality with the factors `ζ_{Λ_j}` left unexpanded) or, as a family of activities, in D1–D3; the counterpart is in B88b, B89a. "Gas" is not Bałaban's word here. Suggested: "**sum over large field regions** (B88b (2.18): sum over admissible sequences of domains); a family whose prescribed sets exactly cover `Bad_m(U)`".
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout.
*See also:* eligible; exclusion support; exact-cover gas.

#### exact-cover gas
*Now:* replaced by *sum over disjoint covering families* (decision of 26 November 2026) at 9:595; 12:181, 189; 18lp:186 ("never divides by the sum over disjoint covering families of the density without insertions") (grep: "exact-cover" no longer in the prose).
- **Meaning.** The large-field factor of the density: `𝒢(U) = Σ_b ∏_{i∈b} K_i(U)`, the sum over finite families `b` of large-field activities with pairwise disjoint supports whose prescribed large-field sets have union exactly the set of large-field sites of `U`; it equals 1 when `U` has no large-field site. The text calls it "a finite polynomial in the latter activities and the fixed indicators of the eligibility conditions" (12:181–183). It is a function of the configuration and only one factor of the density: `ρ̃ = e^{-s}ρ` is its product with the exponential of the regular action, and `Z⁰ = ∫ρ̃ dμ` (12:173–184). In chapter 9 the same phrase names `ℱ⁰` (9:595).
  *Basis:* R (12:181–184); S for the summation condition and the value 1. *Where:* 9:595; 12:181, 189; 18lp:186. *Adopted:* *sum over disjoint covering families* (decision of 26 November 2026; the dictionary had proposed *large-field polymer sum over exact covers*); not defined in words in v3.
  *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.Activities.gas`, YM/RG/Activities.lean (definition read: `gas U = Σ' b : Finset ℕ, gasOccurrence b U`, with `gasOccurrence b U = ∏_{i∈b} K_i(U)` if `admissible U b`, else 0); `Activities.admissible`, same file (definition read; docstring "Disjoint, exact coverage": supports of the members of `b` pairwise disjoint and `⋃_{i∈b} inventory_i = flags p.threshold U`); `YM.RG.flags`, YM/RG/Masks.lean (definition read: the sites touching a plaquette whose chord exceeds the threshold); `Activities.gas_one` (statement read: the gas is 1 if no site is flagged); `YM.RG.Rep.eval`, YM/RG/History.lean (definition read: `eval U = exp(exponent U) · gas U`, `exponent = v·|sites| − path action − sum of regular activities`). Martin existence/fixed-rung-convergence.tex:221–233: "Its gas is a finite sum over compatible subsets of these profiles, each multiplied by the fixed flag indicator … [the scalar-stripped density] is the product of the gas and the exponential of minus the path action and ordinary activity sum".
*Literature:* see *exact cover*.
*Across chapters:* one sense. In chapter 9 the identification with `ℱ⁰` is inferred. The former "unmarked gas" (18lp:186, once) became "the exact-cover gas of the density without insertions" and is now "the sum over disjoint covering families of the density without insertions" (see *unmarked gas*). Not *partition function* and not *density without insertions*: the gas is one factor of the density (12:173–184). Not *constrained sum `ℱ⁰`* as the book-wide name: it names the chapter 9 symbol only.
*See also:* gas; exact cover; unmarked gas.

#### exact reassembly
*Now:* replaced by *factorization identity* (8:282 section title "Large-field constraints and the factorization identity"; 8:358 "factorization identities (ch08:deletion-identity) and (ch08:reassembly)"); "reassembly" remains at 11R:377 ("The exact factorization and reassembly", where it is not settled whether "factorization" means this identity or the Gaussian factorization of the step), and, in another sense, at 9:57 and 09-forest-average.tex:312, 930.
- **Meaning.** The factorisation identity `Z_D = e^{𝓛} Σ_B Π K_η e^{−𝓛_{Y(B)}}` of the polymer expansion.
  *Basis:* R (8:313–319). *Where:* 8:282, 358 ("factorization identity"). *Adopted:* *factorization identity*.
*Literature:* no name and no identity; the add-and-subtract of the terms whose localization domains meet the large field region (B89b p. 377, text layer only: "Now we add all the missing terms with localization domains intersecting `Z`, more exactly we add these terms to complete the effective action, and we subtract them from the remaining expression"; B88b p. 253: "we separate the clusters with localization domains close to `Λ_1^c` … This is the boundary term"). An analogue of `Z_D = e^{𝓛} Σ_B ∏K_η e^{−𝓛_{Y(B)}}` (8:303–319): the same bookkeeping, restoring the regular terms removed near large-field supports. (One comparison paired "exact reassembly" with the regrouping of 9:653–668; the dictionary keeps that under *fusion*, where it is treated.) Suggested: *factorisation identity* stands; say "the subtracted terms are Bałaban's boundary terms".
*Across chapters:* one sense for the identity. The "reassembly" of 9:57 ("Here is the bookkeeping of the normalization constants in a form useful for checking reassembly") is not this identity: it is the recombination of the local factors and normalization constants into the block integral for one forest, "this reassembly" of 09-forest-average.tex:926–931 (also 09-forest-average.tex:312); the entry formerly listed 9:57 here, wrongly. The related identity of Proposition 9:653 ("exact regrouping", label "fusion") is a different statement; see *fusion*.

#### exact regrouping
*Formerly:* *fusion*.
*In the text:* the word survives only in the labels `ch09:fusion`, `ch09:before-fusion`, `ch09:fusion-prop`. Since 26 November 2026 the phrase carries a reference at 9f:919 ("exact regrouping (Proposition ch09:fusion-prop)").
*Variants:* no longer in the text: connected fusion estimate (now "the estimate of the exact regrouping", 10:669).
- **Meaning.** The exact regrouping of the preliminary large-field activities with the localized logarithmic corrections `ℓ_a` into connected components, each of which still contains a large-field activity: the proposition "Exact regrouping" of chapter 9 (9:653–668; labels `ch09:fusion`, `ch09:before-fusion`, `ch09:fusion-prop`). The word is the source's name for this proposition ("Forced fusion"); in v3 it survives only in the labels.
  *Basis:* S; in v3, R (10:658, 669 now name the proposition's operation "the exact regrouping"). *Where:* 9:630 ("the smallness needed for the exact regrouping"), 651 (title); 10:658, 669, 777, 917 (all "exact regrouping"; not cited by number); `09-forest-average.tex`:918. *Adopted:* *exact regrouping* (Proposition "Exact regrouping", ch09:fusion-prop, 9:653–669), cited by its number (the number is not cited at these lines).
  *Source:* Scott part2/D-section.tex:536 (subsection "Forced fusion, activity bounds and the reset"), :554–557 (Lemma "Forced fusion", `lem:D-fusion`: "Suppose `Σ_a sup_U |ℓ_a(U)| < ∞` … `|k_i| ≤ e^{−κ_fus} v_i`, `|e^{ℓ_a} − 1| ≤ v_a`, `sup_x Σ_{a: x ∈ Z_a} e^{(σ+1) cover_B(Z_a)} v_a ≤ γ`", the hypotheses of 9:655–662); Martin existence/soft-log-fusion.tex:1–6 (subsection "Absorbing localized logarithms into the forced gas": "an exact regrouping of the forced activities with localized logarithms"). No Lean declaration was sought.
*Literature:* no single word. Inside the R operation: the **Mayer expansion** of `exp Σ V(Y)`, then the **polymer expansion** with **activities** `F(X')` joining the `T'_k(X_j)` to the boundary terms `V(Y)` (B89b pp. 387–388, (1.90)–(1.91); p. 390: "admissible domains … contain at least one large field region connected with one of the `T'_k`-operations"); "resumming all terms with D and P determining a given domain Z_0" and factorisation `H(Z) = H(Z_1)⋯H(Z_n)` over connected components (B88a p. 12; p. 14, (2.10)); **resummation** onto the connected components of the large field region (D3 p. 2173, App. B "A Resummation Operation": "taking the union with any connected component of Λ^c connected to X"; D2 pp. 092301-71/72, "resum to polymers X ∈ D_{k+1}(mod Ω^c_{k+1})"). An analogue: the same algebra (expand `e^{ℓ} = 1 + (e^{ℓ} − 1)`, take connected components, each containing a large-field unit). Bałaban then exponentiates (B89b (1.98)), which is possible only because the R operation has divided by a normalising integral; v3 stops at the exact-cover sum and never takes its logarithm (9:653–668). In B88a the operation merges Mayer-expanded potentials with large-fluctuation bonds, not large-field activities with logarithms. No v3 term should be glossed as "the R operation": fusion corresponds only to the polymer-expansion step inside it. "Fusion" has no source. Adopted (24 November 2026): *exact regrouping*, the title of the proposition (9:653–669), cited by its number; "fusion", "resummation identity" and "regrouping identity" are not used. The earlier suggestion, "the **polymer expansion** of the large-field factors with the boundary terms (as in B89b (1.90)–(1.91)), without the subsequent exponentiation; resummation into connected localization domains", is withdrawn as a name.
*Across chapters:* chapter 9 (title 9:653, prose 9:630, labels), prose of chapter 10 (text read at 10:656–670) and the forest-average draft (918).
*See also:* hard; exact reassembly.

A compound of *unit*, sense 1.

*Across chapters:* chapter 11 only; "unit" is rendered *identity field* throughout.
*See also:* unit.

#### exceptional phases
*Now:* unchanged; now defined at 15:327 in the proposed words ("the exceptional phases, a null set on which uniqueness of the vacuum is not yet known"); "exceptional vacua" at 19:108 is replaced by "extend uniqueness of the vacuum to every phase".
*Variants:* the exceptional set; no longer in the text: exceptional vacua (19:108).
- **Meaning.** The `ν`-null set of phases outside which `ker H_ξ = ℂΩ_ξ` is proved (15:322–328: "we have not eliminated the exceptional phases, a null set on which uniqueness of the vacuum is not yet known"). The text never shows that uniqueness fails there; it is later obtained for every phase (16:385–387: "the zero-energy subspace is a line for almost every phase … To remove the exceptional set requires a bound uniform in `ξ`"). The former "exceptional vacua" (19:108, once) referred to this set, not to a kind of vector; the sentence now reads "the phase-uniform low-energy estimate extend uniqueness of the vacuum to every phase" (19:108).
  *Basis:* D (15:327); R (15:322–328; 16:385–387). *Where:* 15:327, 330, 341; 16:386; 19:108 (now without the word). *Adopted:* *the null set of phases on which uniqueness of the vacuum is not yet known*; for 19:106–108, *… extend uniqueness of the vacuum from almost every phase to every phase* (as "to every phase").
  *Source:* Scott `part2/H-section.tex:211`: "Vacuum uniqueness first holds only for `ν`-almost every phase (Lemma `lem:H1.3`). The low-energy estimate of Lemma `lem:H2.3` is uniform in the phase; with the continuity in `ξ` of the vacuum-subtracted heat pairings and the full support of `ν`, it removes the exceptional set." Lean not searched.
*Across chapters:* one sense. Not *non-uniqueness of the vacuum on the `ν`-null set of phases*: the text does not show that uniqueness fails there (text read at 15:326–330, 16:385–387, 19:106–109). Not *further invariant vectors*, for the same reason.

#### excess
*Now:* partly replaced by *large-field contribution `Δ_p`* (sense 1), *surplus* (sense 2), *loss (in the exponent)* (sense 3, 18lp:334; 15sp:7, 25); remains at 13sb:7, 165 (sense 3) and at 17:142, 17w:36 ("excess over the target", ordinary use).

1. **Large-field contribution `Δ_p`.** The term `Δ_p` in `r_p^c ≤ C_{j,L,W} t_f + Δ_p`, the contribution of the large variables; it is not small ("Separating the small-distance contribution from the large-field contribution `Δ_p` gives", 6:331).
   *Basis:* R (6:331–334). *Where:* 6:331 ("large-field contribution `Δ_p`"), 329 ("the constant `C` in the last bound"), 356 ("bound on `Δ_p` with a constant independent of `L`"), 517–518; 5:1031. *Adopted:* *large-field contribution `Δ_p`*.

   *Basis:* R (6:422). *Where:* 6:422. *Adopted:* *surplus*.
3. **The `ε` above the sum of degrees.** In the sharp bounds, the arbitrarily small loss in the exponent ("the loss … can be reduced to an arbitrarily small excess", 13sb:6–7).
   *Basis:* R (13sb:6–7). *Where:* 13sb:7, 165 ("excess"); 18lp:334 ("total loss one in the exponent"); 15sp:7 ("any positive loss in the exponent"), 24 ("arbitrarily small loss"). *Proposed:* *loss `ε` in the exponent* (applied except in 13sb).
*Across chapters:* three uses. Senses 1 and 3 are not slack in an estimate (6:331–334; 13sb:6–7): sense 1 is a contribution that is not small, sense 3 a loss. The word is therefore not a synonym of *reserve* or of the "strict margin" of 18lp:257, which is slack (16:205 now says "strict inequality").

#### exchange symmetry
*Now:* applied on 25 November 2026 (sentence repair): "exchange symmetry `f_{ab}^{uv}(p)=f_{ba}^{vu}(−p)` and signed-coordinate symmetry, has" (7:200).
- **Meaning.** The symmetry of a quadratic (two-leg) Taylor symbol under exchange of its two legs: `f_{ab}^{uv}(p) = f_{ba}^{vu}(−p)`, where `a, b` are the direction indices, `u, v` the Lie-algebra arguments, and the two legs carry momenta `(−p, p)`. It holds for the symbol of any second derivative. In the proof of the lemma it gives the symmetry of the colour form ("the symmetric diagonal forms on `𝔤`", 7:212).
  *Basis:* R since 25 November 2026 (7:200 gives the formula; index convention as at 7:185, 192, checked by the review); S before. *Where:* 7:200. *Adopted:* *exchange symmetry `f_{ab}^{uv}(p) = f_{ba}^{vu}(−p)`*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-output-construction.tex:192–199`: "Let `f_{ab}^{uv}(p)` be an analytic quadratic coefficient picture, where `a,b` are coordinate indices and `u,v` colour indices, with momenta `(−p,p)`. Suppose it comes from the common recording of analytic, gauge-invariant, signed-coordinate-invariant real functions as above. It then has the exchange symmetry `f_{ab}^{uv}(p) = f_{ba}^{vu}(−p)`"; `:228–230` "Reality follows from momentum reversal and even homogeneity; symmetry follows from the exchange identity."
*Across chapters:* one occurrence; unrelated to *exchange term*. In the source the symmetry is a consequence of the origin of the symbol, not a separate hypothesis; v3 lists it as a hypothesis; the formula has stood at 7:200 since 25 November 2026, but the text does not say that the symmetry follows from the origin of the symbol.

  *Basis:* R (7:949–956). *Where:* 7:945, 968, 1061, 1063; 10:340. *Proposed:* *the term `−Σ B 𝒞^{-1} B` of `D⁴E(0)`*; the word is physics usage (tree term with one propagator) and may stay if the formula is cited.
*Across chapters:* one sense. The use at 10:340 is the same term: 10:339–340 cites the chapter 7 formula by label (now as "the implicit-differentiation formula"), and 7:949–956 displays it (text read).

#### exclusion support
*Now:* unchanged (kept; now set in italics as a defined word at 4:484).
*Variants:* `Y_i`; `Y_η`.
- **Meaning.** The set `Y_i` attached to a large-field activity that enters the disjointness constraint of a family. The activity also depends on links outside `Y_i` (4:501–508), so it is not the dependence set.
  *Basis:* D (4:484, 499–508). *Where:* 4:484, 499–508; 8:339–350; 9:82–95, 409, 636–643, 892; 11:136–138, 152, 182, 248–252; 11R:8, 125, 158, 168–169. *Proposed:* keep, define once; or *the set `Y_i` of the disjointness constraint*. Not *polymer support*, which would suggest dependence only on `Y_i`.
*Literature:* **component of the large field region** `Z_k = Λ_k^c` (B88b p. 255, (2.3): "`Z_j = Λ_j^c`. These large field regions satisfy the following condition: if a component of `Z_j` is contained in a cube of the size `100MR_j` … then it is a rectangular parallelepiped"; p. 258: "If `Z_k` is represented as a union of disjoint regions, e.g. as a union of connected components"). An analogue: Bałaban's components are the connected components of one region, so disjointness is automatic and there is one decomposition per term; v3 allows any disjoint family. The name suggests more locality than `Y_i` has, because Bałaban enlarges the region until dependence is contained in it (see *full dependence region*). Nothing was found in B87, B88a, B85e or D1–D3 beyond the remark that the polymer activity "H(Z) is localized in the interior of Z with respect to the external gauge fields" (B88a p. 14), where the polymer is the dependence set. Suggested: the proposal stands; add "(Bałaban: a component of the large field region `Z_k`)"; the warning against "polymer support" stands.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout.
*See also:* full dependence region; exact cover.

#### exposure
*Now:* replaced on 25 November 2026 (sentence repair; "expanded in the fixed radial polynomial basis" added by the review): "Let `𝓔` send `v∈V_d` to its polynomial, of weighted degree at most `d`, in the fixed radial jet variables, expanded in the fixed radial polynomial basis. It is injective between finite-dimensional spaces, so one may choose `c_d≥1` with `‖v‖_1≤c_d‖𝓔v‖_coeff`" (11:1291–1293). The word no longer occurs.
*Variants:* `𝓔`; no longer in the text: exposure (11:1291).
- **Meaning.** The linear map `𝓔 : V_d → 𝒫_d` from the coefficient space of the labels of degree `d` to the space `𝒫_d` of polynomials of weighted degree at most `d` in the radial jet variables, sending a coefficient vector to the polynomial it represents (`𝓔v = Σ_i v_i b_i` in the fixed basis `b_i` of labels). It is injective between finite-dimensional spaces, which gives the constant `c_d ≥ 1` with `‖v‖_1 ≤ c_d ‖𝓔v‖_coeff`, the right side being the `ℓ¹` norm of the polynomial coefficients; `c_d` does not depend on the lattice volume. `Tu` is then defined by requiring `𝓔(Tu)` to be the truncated polynomial produced by the construction ("Define `Tu` to be precisely these basis coefficients", 11:1298–1299; formerly "frame coefficients").
  *Basis:* R since 25 November 2026 for domain, codomain and injectivity (11:1291–1292); I for the formula `Σ_i v_i b_i` (neither v3 nor the source displays it). *Where:* 11:1291–1299. *Adopted:* the map `𝓔` described in words, "exposure" dropped (the dictionary's proposal in substance; no formula).
  *Source:* Martin existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:545–555 ("The primary coefficient space and the polynomial jet space have different norms. Write `E : V_d → 𝒫_d` for exposure in the fixed radial jet frame, where `𝒫_d` is the space of polynomials of weighted grade at most `d` … Fix `c_d ≥ 1` such that `|v|_1 ≤ c_d|Ev|_1` … Such a constant exists because `E` is injective between fixed finite-dimensional spaces"). Lean constituents only: `YM.Labels.Pol`, `YM.Labels.limited`, `YM.Labels.Label` (YM/Labels/Polynomial.lean:29, 60, 112; definitions read), `YM.Labels.Frame.coords : Label G d ≃ₗ[ℂ] F.Coeff`, `YM.Labels.Frame.coeffSize` (YM/Labels/Reference.lean:20, 128; definitions read). No Lean declaration for `𝓔` or `c_d` was located.
*Across chapters:* chapter 11 only (text read at 11:1291–1299). The source sentence giving domain, codomain and the reason for `c_d` is now in the text in substance (11:1291–1292).
*See also:* frame; extraction.
