#### letter
*Now:* unchanged; 16:296 now also defines the word: "a word is a finite ordered list of letters".
*Variants:* field word (a finite sequence of letters; 16:10, 293).
- **Meaning.** "A letter is a pair `(A,f)` with `A ∈ F`, `f ∈ 𝒮(ℝ⁴)`; a word is a finite ordered list of letters. The star of a word reverses its order and replaces every letter by `(A^*, f̄)`. Let `𝒫` be their algebraic span, including the empty word `1`" (16:296–298). Concatenation is the product, so `𝒫` is the space of formal finite linear combinations of words: the free associative algebra with unit on the set of letters `F × 𝒮(ℝ⁴)`, with the star above. No linearity in `A` or `f` is imposed on `𝒫` itself; the functional `w_ξ` defined by the distributions `W_n^ξ` is multilinear in the labels and the test functions, and the fields `Φ_ξ(A,f)` act on the quotient `𝒫/𝒩_ξ` by the null space of the form `w_ξ(b^*c)` (16:319–324). No product of operators is formed before that quotient.
  *Basis:* D (16:296) for "letter" and "word"; S for the algebra. *Where:* 16:296–298, 328. *Adopted:* keep, defined. That the quotient of `𝒫` by the multilinearity relations is the tensor (Borchers–Uhlmann type) algebra over `F ⊗ 𝒮` is a remark from general knowledge, to be confirmed; the source attributes the construction to Wightman.
  *Source:* Martin existence/reconstruction.tex:4–5, 18–23, 37–38: "The construction by quotienting the positive form on field words goes back to Wightman [§6]"; "A letter is a pair `a = (v,f) ∈ E × 𝒮`, and a word is a finite ordered list of letters … The empty word is denoted by `1`. Concatenation is written without an intervening symbol"; "The functional `w` is multilinear separately in every label and every test function, and `w(1) = 1`".
*Across chapters:* chapter 16 only. The "word" of chapters 13–15 is a different object, a finite list of labels and positions (13:284).

#### level
*Now:* replaced by *scale* (and *scale index*): insertion scale `k_i`, radius scale `n_i` (17:85–86), comparison scale `k` (11:734–737; 17m:136), middle and output scale (11:1557, 2093), stopping scales (17w:102), reference scale, late scale, consecutive scales (9:263), cutoff scale; "coarse kernel level" became "coarse kernel order" and, on 25 November 2026, "coarse smoothing order" (11:352). "Level" survives only in ordinary uses ("level set", 10:232; "sliced-integrand level", 11R:359).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: insertion level `k_i`; radius level `n_i`; comparison level `k`; top, middle, output level; stopping levels; reference level; late level; adjacent levels; kernel level.
- **Meaning.** The scale index `m` of the sequence of lattices. Larger index is finer; blocking goes from `m+1` to `m` ("The scale `m` has spacing `a_m = D_m^{-1}`; blocking proceeds from `m+1` to `m`", 12:6–7). "Scale", "depth" and "step" were used for the same index; the text now says "scale" throughout. Named levels: the **radius level** `n_i` is the level whose spacing `a_n` fixes the radius `r = a_nM_n^u`, and the **insertion level** `k_i` is the finer level at which the insertion and its coupling are taken ("The inverse coupling at a finer insertion scale `k_i` is denoted by `β_i` … The radius scale `n_i` precedes `k_i`", 17:84–87; `k(n)` by the formula at 17:108). They are related by `k_i = k(n_i)`, which v3 does not write. The **output level** is, in chapter 11, the lowest of the three levels `k > ℓ > w` of the restart argument; at 17t:408, 17c:242, 393 it is the fixed level `k` at which the transferred current is evaluated, later the insertion level `k_i` (see *output level*). The **middle level** `ℓ` is the middle one of the three levels `k > ℓ > w` of chapter 11 (`m = k − ℓ`, 11:1759; `ℓ − w`, 11:1577). The "middle and output stopping levels" of 17w:101–102 are the two backward stops of 17w:31–33 (from `n`, the first scale `n'` with `log(a_{n'}/a_n) ≥ (b+2) log H_n`, then the first `n''` with `log(a_{n''}/a_{n'}) ≥ 10 log B_n`); they are the `ℓ` and `w` of chapter 11, with the radius level `n` in the place of `k` (compare 11:2090–2093, "Neither … depends on the choice of middle or output scale"). The **comparison level** is, in chapter 11, the level `k` below which the history is restarted (11:734–741, now "comparison scale"); in 17w the window runs backwards from the radius level `n`, and at 17m:136 "the comparison scale `k`" is the insertion level. "Sufficiently late scale" (17:120) is the ordinary phrase for a large index. The former "coarse kernel level" (11:352, now "coarse smoothing order") was not a level in this sense: it is the stage index of the block kernel at the coarse level (see *coarse kernel level*).
  *Basis:* R for the index and for the names `n_i`, `k_i` (17:84–87); R for `k_i = k(n_i)` since 25 November 2026 (17:140, "which gives `n_i`, `k_i=k(n_i)` and the maps `U_{i,d}`"; before, S, with I from 17:108, 139–142; 17m:386, 420 alone), for the stopping levels and for the chapter 17 output level; I for the middle level. *Where:* 4:15; 7:15; 9:263; ch. 10–11 passim; ch. 12–16 (77); 17:85, 86, 120; 17w:31–33, 41, 101–102; 17t:408; 17c:242, 393; 17m:136, 331, 416 (all now "scale" or "scale index"). *Adopted:* *scale index `m`* for the index (and *step* for the map between two scales); *scale index `n_i`*, *scale index `k_i = k(n_i)`* with a sentence saying what each indexes (the text has "radius scale", "insertion scale"); the three scales of the restart argument by their symbols `k`, `ℓ`, `w` only (not applied: the text says "comparison scale", "middle scale", "output scale").
  *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:109`: "Diagonal extraction over degrees, arities, compact sets and jet orders gives `n_i`, `k_i = k(n_i)` and frames"; `I-section.tex:91` (the two backward stops, quoted under *first crossing*); Scott `part2/E-Gaussian-sources.tex:77–81`: "A comparison window is a triple of levels `k < l < t` … (Win1) `log(a_l/a_t) ≥ (b+2) log 𝓜`, `log(a_k/a_l) ≥ 10 log B_t`" (top `t`, middle `l`, bottom `k`); `I-section.tex:213`, `331` for the output level (quoted under *output level*).
*Literature:* no fixed word: the index `k` of the "k-th renormalization transformation"; "scale" `η = L^{−k}`; "unit lattice", "unit scale" `K` (B87 p. 256: "We continue the calculation of the effective actions until we reach the unit lattice, or rather until we reach a scale which we define as the unit scale. Let us denote the corresponding index by K"); "step k", "level K", "truncated at the jth level" (D1 p. 1330010-42: "the total mass at level K"; D2 p. 092301-29); lattices `Ω^(j) = Ω ∩ L^jηℤ^d` (B85a p. 17, (1)). An analogue with the index reversed: Bałaban's and Dimock's `k = 0` is the finest (bare) lattice and `k` increases towards the unit lattice, with a fixed `L` and a rescaling after each step; v3's `m` increases towards the fine lattice, with level-dependent `L_m`. For fixed `L`, Bałaban's `k` is `N − m` (an inference). In B84a–B85d the objects `Q_k`, `H_k`, `G_k`, `U_k(V)` are `k`-step composites, so the subscript counts composed steps, not a level. "Scale" in these papers can also mean the lattice spacing `L^{-j}` of a region. Adopted: *scale* for the spacing, *scale index `m`* for the integer; note the reversal once.
*Across chapters:* the index has one meaning throughout, but "comparison scale" and "output scale" (formerly "level") are attached to different levels in chapter 11 and in chapter 17: the letter `k` is the top of the window in chapter 11 and the insertion level in 17t, 17c, 17m, while in 17w the top of the window is `n`. At 17t:408, 17c:242, 393 the former "fixed output level" is now simply "a fixed scale". The index is called *scale index*, following Bałaban ("a scale which we define as the unit scale. Let us denote the corresponding index by K", B87 p. 256); "level", formerly the text's most frequent word and Dimock's, is gone, and *stage `j`* is kept for the stages of 10:25 only. v3 should restore `k_i = k(n_i)` at 17:139–141.
*See also:* leading; middle level; microscopic; mesh threshold; output level; comparison level; smoothing order.

#### lift
*Now:* partly replaced by *preimage* (sense 1, chapter 5: 5:626–633, 746, 829) and *primitive* (sense 1, chapter 7: 7:134–138); by *linearization* / *representative* (sense 4, 9s:194–196); senses 2, 3 and 5 kept, as proposed for 2 and 3; "lift" remains in sense 5 (11:1312–2220; 14:176, 197, 215; 14lc:32–102; 15:258) and in the label `ch05:defect-lifts`.
*Variants:* periodic lift; coordinate lift; parent lift; lifted potential; coefficient lift `u_{k,N,p}`; simultaneous, normalized lift; lift equations; lifted vectors; bounded lifts; no longer in the text: left / right lift (now "left / right preimage"); zeroth-factor lift; first lift; scalar lift (now "primitive"); forest-coordinate lift `W_F`; actual lift `W_a`.
1. **Preimage under a differential.** In chapter 5 a solution of an equation such as `d_2^*W_0 = E` or `A = V d_{r+1}` ("first choose a left preimage `W_0`, that is, `d_2^*W_0 = E`", 5:626). In chapter 7 a preimage under the contraction `δ = ι_q`, solving `δ_0X = f` (7:122, 134–135: "zeroth-factor primitive", "first primitive", "scalar primitive"). The two are analogous; they are not the same operator. *Basis:* R (5:626–633; 7:134–138). *Where:* 5:626–633, 746; 7:134–138. *Adopted:* *preimage*; *primitive* (chapter 7).
2. **Lift to the covering lattice** of a point or box of the torus. *Basis:* R. *Where:* 1:181; 4:332, 671; 11:399–400, 414 ("centered nonwrapping lift"). *Proposed:* keep (standard).
3. **Parent lift** of a coarse gauge. *Basis:* I. *Where:* 6:361. *Proposed:* none proposed ("parent" is defined at 1:218–220).
4. **The operators `W`** from a coarse field to the stationary fine field: "Let `𝒰(x) = 𝒟_x(ρ(x))` be the critical configuration as a physical fine field. Its linearization is the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge of Chapter 5. Its curl agrees with that of the smooth representative `W_a`" (9s:193–196); "lifted potential" (9:209). Here the text itself says which operator is the derivative of the stationary field: `W_F`; `W_a` is its smooth representative (same curl). *Basis:* R (9s:193–196). *Where:* 9s:194–196; 9:209. *Adopted:* *the linearization `W_F` of the critical configuration* (9s:194) and *its smooth representative `W_a`* (9s:196); not *lift*, *transport* or *representative* as a name for this operator; no symbol is renamed, and the representative is written wherever `W` is unqualified: `W_s` at 5:527–535 (now 5:535 "`W` is the representative written `W_s`"), `W_F` in chapter 11 (11:642, now "taken in its representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge"), `W_a` in `17-current-contraction.tex` (not checked). "Lifted potential" (9:209) is kept.
   *Source:* agrees with Lean `YM.Precision.Guessed`, `YM/PCalc/Chart.lean` (definition read: the derivative at zero of the stationary germ is `extracted S B W` minus the linear copy) and `YM.Precision.extracted`, `YM/PREC/TreeMatch.lean` (definition read); see *actual stationary tangent* (sense 2) for what is established and what is inferred there.
5. **Coefficient lift.** The solution `u` of `S_{g/θ}Tu = W_ρ v` for a free representative `v` (11:1358; 14lc:32–34, with `W_{H_k^{α_0}}`); "bounded lifts of the separating family" (15:258) are such polynomial preimages of free fields. *Basis:* D (11:1358; 14lc:32–34). *Where:* 11:1312, 1332, 1347, 1357–1360, 1844–1847, 2064–2068, 2164–2167, 2202, 2213, 2220; 14:176, 197, 215; 14lc:32, 41, 102; 15:258. *Proposed:* *preimage `u` of `W_ρ v` under `S_{g/θ}T`*.
*Literature:* see *stationary tangent* for sense 4 (the former forest-coordinate lift `W_F` and actual lift `W_a`); the other senses have no counterpart in the papers read.
*Across chapters:* the meaning changed: senses 1–3 in chapters 1 and 4–7, sense 4 in chapter 9, sense 5 in chapters 11 and 14–15; senses 1 and 4 no longer use the word. The chapter 5 and chapter 7 uses of sense 1 are analogous but concern different operators. Sense 5 is not *preimage under the extraction map* alone: the equation `S_{g/θ}Tu = W_ρ v` is named. At 18:62 ("Lift a quotient basis through it") the verb is ordinary linear algebra.
*See also:* magnification; localization; stationary tangent.

#### likelihood
*Now:* replaced by *probability weight* (sense 1: 5:977; 6:64, 1113, 1352); *normalized weights of the auxiliary index* (sense 2: 6:926, 1023).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: likelihood tests; likelihood factors; positive likelihood; cutoff or branch likelihood amplitudes.
1. **Weight of a tag**: the probability weight `λ(U,α)` of the random index, in "The retained values of the auxiliary index for the local gauge transformations have positive probability weight" (6:1351–1352), parallel to "Every chosen value of the auxiliary index of Chapter 4 for a local gauge transformation must have positive probability weight" (6:63–64). It is a product over coarse sites of the weight of the frame tag and over coarse bonds of the weight of the block-average tag. *Basis:* I. *Where:* 5:977; 6:1113, 1351–1352. *Adopted:* *probability weight `λ(U,α)`*.
   *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.StepData.likelihood`, `YM/RG/Block.lean` (definition read): `∏_x frameMass · ∏_e predictorMass`, with docstring "Actual joint probability of physical site and bond tags"; the block kernel is `density = Σ_t likelihood · noise` (definition read).
2. **Former "likelihood tests", "likelihood factors"**: the tag weights of sense 1 taken one coarse site or one coarse bond at a time and multiplied by the number of tags, so that each equals 1 when the block average is in its minimising (small-field) branch, where the tag law is uniform; that is its plateau. They are not the allocation weights `ϑ_f`, `ϑ_n` of 6:68–76 (now called "partition-of-unity weights"). 6:925–926 now reads "The local factors of the two partition-of-unity weights and the normalized weights of the auxiliary index are then equal to one"; 6:1021–1023 "leave the fine plaquette distance from the identity below `t_f/4` and the deviation `n_e` below `W t_f`. The corresponding factors of the partition-of-unity weights and the normalized weights of the auxiliary index there are equal to one". The weights of 6:70–76 are products over all plaquettes or edges, so only their local factors equal one there. *Basis:* S. *Where:* 6:926, 1023. *Adopted:* *normalized tag weights*, as "normalized weights of the auxiliary index"; at 6:926 "the allocation weights and the normalised tag weights are equal to one".
   *Source:* Martin `existence/gaussian-warnings.tex:116–118`: "The five first types are fine plaquette masks, coarse bond masks, coarse bond likelihoods, coarse site likelihoods, and fine site contractions; the last type is a fine bond cutoff"; `:199–201`: "The corresponding fine and predictor masks therefore equal one; the local likelihood factors also equal one by the same local plateau estimates." Lean `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Tags.siteMass`, `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Tags.pinMass`, `YM/AnalyticNext/CONNECTED_ACTIVITY_JETS_E6/Sector.lean` (definitions read): number of tags times `frameMass`, resp. `predictorMass`; `YM.RG.Patch.frameMass`, `YM.RG.Patch.predictorMass`, `YM/RG/Patch.lean` (definitions read): the reciprocal of the number of tags on the minimising branch. The allocation weights are the separate factors `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Mask.fine`, `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Mask.noise`, `YM/AnalyticNext/CONNECTED_ACTIVITY_JETS_E6/Mask.lean` (definitions read).
*Across chapters:* chapter 6 only. The former ambiguity at 6:1021–1023 (thresholds `t_f/4`, `W t_f` read as if they belonged to the likelihood factors) is resolved: the text now names both kinds of weight and says that both equal one.
*See also:* mass; label; uniform mass.

#### linear graph
*Now:* unchanged; the explaining sentence proposed now stands at 11:380.
*Variants:* graph `G`; incoming / outgoing graph; coefficient graph (11:380, 468); graph norm; graph estimates; inhomogeneous graph estimate; graph of normalized local insertions.
- **Meaning.** A linear map from the coefficient vector `x ∈ V_d` of a label to families of regular and large-field remainders, with the supports of the remainders independent of `x`: "Let `G` be an incoming linear graph of regular vanishing-jet and large-field remainders, with norm at most `s_f` per coefficient. As in the graph transform for invariant manifolds, the step with insertions maps coefficient graphs at the fine scale to graphs at the coarse scale and halves the distance between two of them. The step with insertions gives a linear coefficient map `M_G` and a raw remainder map `R_G`" (11:379–382); one step maps `G` to `G' = R_G M_G^{-1}` (11:447). The density with one insertion at a level is described by the pairs (coefficient, remainders) `(x, Gx)`, i.e. by the graph of `G` over the coefficient space. The "graph norm" (11:889) is the norm of this map, with the remainder norm of 11:362–366 on the target (regular majorants plus `κ^{-1}` times large-field majorants); the "inhomogeneous graph estimate" (11:895: "controls local trials as well") is not glossed.
  *Basis:* R (11:379–382, 447), also for the reason of the name (11:380); S for the fixed supports. *Where:* 11:347, 379, 447, 454, 468, 889, 895, 902, 914. *Adopted:* keep *graph*, with the source's sentence "As in the graph transform for invariant manifolds, the marked step maps coefficient graphs at level `m+1` to graphs at level `m` and halves the distance between two of them" (now at 11:380, with "the step with insertions" and "fine scale", "coarse scale"); *graph transform* for `G ↦ G'` (11:468).
  *Source:* Scott part2/E-section.tex:242 ("A coefficient graph at level `m` is a linear choice `x ↦ g_m(x) = (R(x), Q(x))` of such remainders, with the supports fixed and `‖g_m(x)‖_rem ≤ C^col_{J_m}|x°|_1`. As in the graph transform for invariant manifolds, …"); Scott part2/E-one-mark.tex:100 ("Define the new graph by `g_m(u) = g̃_m(M_m^{-1}u)`"). Lean `YM.Source.TransferData.entries` (YM/Source/Insertion.lean:72; read), `YM.Source.TransferData.Based.linear`, `.cap` (Insertion.lean:91–93, 99–101; fields read: coefficient, regular and large-field parts linear in the coefficient vector, supports independent of it; remainder bound `columns_m · coeffSize(core x)` with `κ = sqrt(forcedAllowance m)`), `YM.Source.Coefficient.remBound` (Insertion.lean:63–68; definition read); for the map as an object of its own, `YM.MergeProof.Matric.Gram` (YM/FullVolume/Mark/Hinge.lean:12; structure read).
*Across chapters:* same object as the "admissible graph" `G : V_d → 𝓡_m` of chapter 12 (12:82–83). v3 now has the source's sentence at 11:380. Not *remainder map*: the text uses that phrase for `R_G` (11:381) and `J_G` (12:92).
*See also:* graph; incidence; lift.

#### linear in the plaquette sum
*Formerly:* *first-power*.
*In the text:* the word survives only in the label `ch04:frame-first-power`.
*Variants:* no longer in the text: first-power bound; first-power estimate.
- **Meaning.** A bound of a sum of distances from the identity by a constant times the first power of the sum of plaquette distances from the identity, `𝒫_y(U) = Σ_q m_y(q) χ(U_q)`, as in (ch04:macro-comparison), 4:335–341, and (ch04:axial-eligible), 4:74–79; as opposed to a bound by `𝒫_y^{1/2}`, which is what a comparison of quadratic energies gives ("linearity of this bound in the plaquette sum `𝒫_y(U)` is essential: a square-root consequence of a squared-energy comparison would not give the factor needed here", 4:343–345).
  *Basis:* R (4:335–345); S for the square-root alternative. *Where:* 4:327 ("A bound for the averaging operation, linear in the plaquette sum"), 308–312 (4:347 "Linear comparison for the averaging operation"); 5:1017 ("linear in the plaquette sum"); 6:319, 322 ("bound linear in the plaquette sum `𝒫_y(U)`", "The estimate for the averaging operation, linear in the plaquette sum"). *Adopted:* *bound linear in the plaquette sum `𝒫_y(U)`*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/seed-geometry.tex:4–7`: "The essential analytic point is a first-power estimate for the actual coarse predictor. It must hold on both branches of its definition and for every output with positive weight. Small-field uniqueness alone would not give the estimate needed here"; `:20–24` ("An axial gauge with a first-power bound"): `E_X(H·U) ≤ 16 q F_X(U)`, with `E_X`, `F_X` the sums of the normalised chords of the links and of the plaquettes in the box; `:89–91`: "Here are the details which improve the square-root estimate to this first-power bound. Comparison with the constant frame gives `𝓔(h) ≤ b`, since `r²/2 ≤ r`."
*Literature:* no name; **Proposition 1** and Proposition 2 of B85a (p. 26: "There exist positive constants `C_0`, `c_2′` such that for every configuration V satisfying (44) for p ⊂ Δ(p′) and for `α_0 ≤ c_2′` we have `|V̄(∂p′) − 1| < L²α_0 + C_0(L²α_0)²`"; "Each averaging operation rescales a bound on plaquette variables approximately by the factor L²"; quoted from the text layer with symbols restored). An analogue: Bałaban's bound is in the sup norm, requires `α_0` small and has a quadratic correction; v3's is a sum over the box (the factor `L^{-2}` on a sum of `O(L^4)` plaquettes is the same scaling `L²`; this is an inference), holds for all configurations, has no quadratic term, and carries the mismatch terms that the soft kernel makes necessary. Suggested: *bound of the coarse plaquette, linear in the fine plaquette sum (the analogue of B85a Proposition 1)*.
*Across chapters:* chapters 4–6. "First power" refers to the power of the plaquette sum on the right-hand side, not to a power of the coupling or of `L`.
*See also:* macro-box; `Q^pred`.

#### live tag actions
*Now:* replaced by *the actions for all values of the auxiliary index with positive probability weight* (9s:132); "tag-count factor" by "factor counting its values" (9s:139; 11R:359–360); "tag-coincidence radius" by "the ball on which the actions for all values of the auxiliary index with positive probability weight coincide" (9s:226).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: tag-count factor; tag-coincidence radius.
- **Meaning.** A *live tag* is a value `α` of the random index with `λ(U,α) > 0`; a *dead* tag has weight zero. Its *action* is the fine action plus the block-kernel penalty computed with the block average of that tag. Where the block average is in its minimising branch it does not depend on the tag, so all these actions equal the common function `φ` (fine classical action plus penalty): "all its fine plaquettes satisfy the regularity condition `χ(U_p) ≤ t_f`, and the actions for all values of the auxiliary index with positive probability weight coincide with `φ`" (9s:131–132).
  *Basis:* S; R from the v3 text (9s:132). *Where:* 9s:132, 139–140, 226. *Adopted:* *the actions for every `α` with `λ(U,α) > 0`*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:48–61`: the tagged integrand `Σ_k π_β λ_k(U) e^{−β[a(U) + n_k(U,V(x))] − ℓ(U)} 1{fine field healthy}`; "The nonnegative tag weights satisfy `Σ_k λ_k(U) = 1`; a dead tag has zero weight"; "all live tag actions there equal `φ`", where "`φ` is the fine classical action plus the smoothing penalty" (`:38–39`). Lean `YM.Push.SectorMeasure.Alive`, `YM/Push/SECTOR_MEASURE/Cells.lean` (definition read): `0 < S.likelihood U k`, with theorem `dead` (statement read); `YM.RG.StepData.density`, `YM/RG/Block.lean` (definition read): `Σ_t likelihood U t · noise β (prediction U t) V`; `YM.RG.Patch.frame`, `YM.RG.Patch.predict`, `YM/RG/Patch.lean` (definitions read): on the minimising branches the result is the minimiser and does not depend on the tag.
*Across chapters:* 9s only. In 11R:359–361 the former "tag-count factor", now "the finite factor counting the values of the auxiliary index", is the number of values of `α`.
*See also:* label; likelihood; live group; tag-coincidence radius.

#### localization
*Now:* unchanged, now qualified as proposed: *Taylor localization* and *one-step localization map* (11:372–373), *common localization map* (11:29, 1146, 1313, 1336, 1841, 2062; 14lc:30; 17w:100, 117); both maps are still written `T`. "Coefficient extraction" remains at 11:1294, 1341 in the form "extraction … of the coefficients of low scaling dimension"; 11:1332 now has "common localization map `T`" (formerly "coefficient extraction `T`"), and 11:2097 "localization map" (formerly "top map").
*Variants:* common localization map; localization map onto the polynomial label space `T`; coefficient extraction (11:1294, 1341); no longer in the text: low-weight coefficient extraction; common extraction (11:1336); extraction `T` (11:1332); top map (11:2097).
1. **One-step localization** `T`: "Taylor localization, the extraction of the local polynomial part by Taylor expansion of the fine local section on the free interpolated coarse jet, gives the one-step localization map `T`, a triangular change of basis" (11:372–373); "the leading map is `TS_L`". *Basis:* D (11:372–377). *Where:* 11:372, 438. *Adopted:* keep "localization", always qualified: *the localization operator* or *Taylor localization*; for this map, *one-step localization map*, with its own symbol (the symbol is not yet changed).
2. **Common localization map** at the comparison scale, also `T_{k,N,p,d}`: "Define `Tu` to be precisely these basis coefficients" (11:1298–1299); the `T` of 11:2090–2093 and 17w:100–102 ("The common localization map `T` depends only on the insertion"). *Basis:* D (11:1291–1311). *Where:* 11:29, 1146, 1294, 1298–1299, 1313, 1332, 1336, 2062, 2097. *Adopted:* *common localization map*, with its own symbol (the symbol is not yet changed).
3. **Localization by radial Taylor expansion** of the near sum: a third object, the `Au` compared with `Tu`. *Basis:* I. *Where:* 11:1186–1188, 1209. *Proposed:* name the map `A`.
*Literature:* name clash. In Bałaban and Dimock **localization (expansion)** is the writing of a functional as a sum over polymers of terms depending on the field in `X`, by weakening parameters `s_□` and a decoupling expansion (D1 p. 1330010-36: "We remedy this with the following localization expansion"; B95 p. 118: "The above expansion, called a localization expansion, plays a fundamental role"), with **localization domains** `X ∈ D_j` (B87 p. 257); also "the desired localization property" of characteristic functions (B88b p. 252). v3's localization (senses 1–2: Taylor expansion giving the map `T`, extraction of polynomial coefficients, 11:372–377) is what these papers call normalization or renormalization (conditions): see *extraction*. Adopted (23 November 2026): v3 keeps the word, always qualified: *the localization operator* or *Taylor localization* (*one-step localization map*, *common localization map*), and the two maps written `T` get different symbols. Reason recorded: v3's operation is the localization operator of perturbative and constructive renormalization, the extraction of the local part, the rest being an irrelevant remainder (Gallavotti's `L` with `R = 1 − L`; Brydges–Slade `Loc`); this identification is from the coordinating agent's general knowledge, and no source was consulted for it. Bałaban's sense appears only in his compounds *localized term* and *localization domain*, never as bare "localization". The text should say once, in chapter 11, that v3's localization is the extraction of the local polynomial part, which Bałaban calls imposing renormalization conditions (normalization); 11:372 now says the first half ("Taylor localization, the extraction of the local polynomial part"), without the comparison with Bałaban. "Extraction" stays as the manuscript's synonym and is not the proposed word.
*Across chapters:* chapter 11 (and 14lc, 17w for sense 2). Two different maps are both still written `T`; "localization" and "extraction" name the same operations.
*See also:* common localization; lift; local projection.

#### logarithm
*Now:* unchanged; at 6:448 the text now glosses it: "logarithms (Lie-algebra coordinates)".
*Variants:* logarithmic field; link logarithms; frozen logarithms; active logarithmic coordinate.
- **Meaning.** The Lie-algebra (exponential) coordinate of a link or of a link increment. For an active fine link of chapter 6 the coordinate is taken relative to the pull-back `rep V` of the coarse field: "Write an active physical link as `U_e = exp(u_e)(rep V)_e`" (6:700); these `u_e` are the "*Active* coordinates, the integration variables, … logarithms (Lie-algebra coordinates) of the remaining non-tree links" (6:448) and the Gaussian variable is `z = g^{-1}(u − m_Y)`. For a coarse field it is `h` with `V = exp h` ("a coarse logarithmic field `h`", 6:960–961); in the Gaussian problem of chapter 5 it is the unscaled field `A_f` ("unscaled link logarithms", 5:100). The "frozen logarithms" are the same coordinates of the frozen non-tree links, which are Haar variables and therefore not small: "No estimate below replaces an arbitrary frozen Haar logarithm by a small logarithm" (6:603–604). Glossed at 6:448, not otherwise defined.
  *Basis:* R (6:700; 6:447–449, with the gloss at 6:448); I elsewhere. *Where:* 5:100; 6:448, 604, 700–701, 960–961; about 28 occurrences in chapters 4–6, 25 of them in chapter 6; 9s:37, 180, 303. *Proposed:* *Lie-algebra (exponential) coordinate of the link*; acceptable if stated once.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:583`: "In exponential coordinates write this measure as `J_*^{n_e} ∏_e J(ψ_e) dψ`"; `:1171`: "On an active logarithmic coordinate put `χ_{a_*}(u_e) = χ(|u_e|/(a_* t_f))`"; `:1121`, `:1127`: "a bounded smooth extension of the frozen logarithms", "a specified frozen-log extension whose value and coarse-field jets are `O(t_f)` uniformly in the frozen Haar variables"; Martin `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:116–117`: "Taking the logarithm of each relative free bond now yields `U = 𝒟_x(y)` with `‖y‖_∞ ≤ r_s`."
*Literature:* no noun for the coordinate; **logarithmic function** `log` and **Lie algebra valued configuration** `A = (1/i) log U` (B85a p. 21: "The first is a logarithmic function. It is an inverse to the exponential function", (21)–(23); p. 19: "U = e^{iA} and A is a Lie algebra valued configuration"); on the scale `η`, `U = e^{iηA}`, `A = (1/(iη)) log U_1`, `B = (1/i) log V` (B85c p. 389; B85d pp. 281, 309; B85b p. 76, (0.3)); relative to a fixed configuration, the **new variables** `U′ = UU_0^{-1}`, `U′ = e^{iηA′}` (B85b p. 78: "We will choose gauge conditions relative to some fixed configuration `U_0`. This means that if we consider new variables U′ defined by `U = U′U_0` … then the conditions are imposed on the variables U′"), `U_0` being later "the background gauge field configuration" (B85b p. 82). The same object, with the fluctuation on the left as in v3; the convention differs by a factor `i` (hermitian `A`) and by the lattice spacing `η`. For the logarithm relative to the replicated coarse field (active coordinates, 6:700; forest chart) the fit is an analogue: the same left-multiplicative chart, but Bałaban's `U_0` is an arbitrary regular configuration and v3's is `rep V`. Suggested: *Lie-algebra-valued field `A = (1/i) log U`*; add "Bałaban's variables `U′ = UU_0^{-1}` relative to a background `U_0`"; "logarithm" and "exponential coordinate" are harmless.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 4–6 and 9s. "Local Haar logarithms" (6:1261) is not an example: it is the logarithm `log J(u)` of the Haar density in exponential coordinates, a factor of the local expansion ("The fourth line follows from `log J(u) = O(|u|²)` for the Haar density in exponential coordinates", 6:1296–1297; Martin `existence/actual-corrected-body-compiler.tex:162–163`: "The extended Haar logarithm satisfies `|log J_ext(u)| ≤ C min(‖u‖, 4 arc)²`"); see *Haar logarithm*. At 6:604 "frozen Haar logarithm" is, by contrast, a link coordinate (of a frozen link), not the logarithm of a density.
*See also:* logarithmic; logarithmic correction; Haar logarithm; free; safe chart.

#### logarithmic correction
*Now:* replaced by *large-field correction*, defined at 9:370 ("`L_x` is a *large-field correction*, a term of the exponent supported where its enlarged neighborhood contains a large-field site"); "logarithmic label" by *correction label* (9:640, 673, 679).
*Variants:* large-field correction `L_x`, `ℓ_a`; correction label; no longer in the text: logarithmic correction; logarithmic label, term, selection; logarithmic correction factor `e^{ℓ_a} − 1`.
- **Meaning.** Terms of the exponent that vanish on small-field supports ("Write the large-field corrections in (ch09:before-fusion) as `ℓ_a` on nonempty exclusion supports `Z_a`, with `ℓ_a = 0` when `Z_a` is small-field", 9:635–637). The "soft" bound of chapter 10 is the bound on the factors `e^{ℓ_a} − 1`.
  *Basis:* D (9:369–371); R (9:635–637). *Where:* 9:370, 434, 609, 632–640, 673, 679, 700; 10:659–669. *Adopted:* *large-field correction terms in the exponent*, in the form *large-field correction*.
*Literature:* **boundary terms** `B_k`, `B^{(j)}(X)`, localized at the large field regions (B88b p. 259: "The term `B_k` includes various expressions localized closely to large field regions"; p. 260: "It is a sum of small, or at least bounded, localized terms, with localizations close to large field regions"; p. 261, text layer only: sum "over domains `X ∈ D_j` such that `X ∩ Ω_j ≠ ∅`, and `X ∩ Z_j ≠ ∅`"; p. 253: "This is the boundary term … it is controlled by the large field estimates, and does not need to be renormalized"); in D2 the "active" and "inactive boundary terms". A close analogue of `ℓ_a` (terms of the exponent that vanish when their support is small-field): the same defining property, present only at large-field regions, bounded and not small, not renormalised; Bałaban leaves them in the exponent, v3 absorbs them into the activities (see *fusion*). The "soft" bound on `e^{ℓ_a} − 1` of chapter 10 has no literature word. Suggested: "**boundary terms** (Bałaban's `B_k`): terms of the exponent localized at the large-field regions".
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 9–10.
*See also:* logarithmic; label.

### M

#### `M_core`, `M_act`
*Now:* unchanged; traced on 25 November 2026 (decision 28; report `decisions-2026-11-25/contact-matrices-trace.md`, read-only, text not changed).
*Variants:* `A(x) = M_core(x)` (7:536); the completed matrix `C = 𝖩 + F*F` (7:256–257); "blocked completed matrix `C_0`" (7:783).
- **Meaning.** Two matrices on the full joint fluctuation space (the fine field and one local gauge transformation per block), both completed by `F*F` (7:530–540). `M_act(x)` is the full gauge-fixed Hessian of the path action plus the penalty term in the fluctuation coordinates at the critical configuration over `x`; `M_core(x)` is the same matrix with the Hessian of the penalty term replaced by its pullback through the derivative of the averaging operation. In rooted coordinates "The Hessian chain rule gives `M_act=A+Z`, with `r(0)=Z(0)=0`; we call `Z` the *contact term* of the averaging operation" (7:538), where `A(x)=M_core(x)`, `Z(x)=S_x(r(x))` and `r(x)` is the derivative of the penalty term with respect to the increment of the averaging operation (7:532–536). In v3's own notation `M_act` is the completed matrix `C = 𝖩 + F*F` of 7:256–257 (at zero background `𝒞 = ℋ + F*F`, 7:886–889), and `M_core` is the "blocked completed matrix `C_0`", taken "after removing the contact term of the averaging operation" (7:782–784); the second match is by role, not by a shared symbol. Neither matrix is a matrix of the block axial gauge: the forest enters only in the construction of the critical configuration, in the determinant factorization (7:246–264) and in the proof of the Ward identity (7:558–564).
  *Basis:* S (the v3 text uses the symbols at 7:536, 538 without defining them). *Where:* 7:536, 538, 551 (`D²(log det M_act − log det M_core)(0)`, the contact correction); `M(p)` at 7:571 is a different matrix, the mixed kernel of `DY`. *Proposed:* define both matrices at 7:532–533, as in the trace's proposed wording (not applied).
  *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-determinant-prices.tex:161–163, 172–173` ("`M_act = b*Kb + B + F*F`", "`M_core = b*Kb + Q*HQ + F*F`", with `K` the fine kinetic Hessian, `B` the actual penalty Hessian, `Q` the block constraint derivative, `H` its coarse penalty form, `F = X + T` the gauge-fixing map); `thermal-contact-cancellation.tex:130` ("Write `A(x) = M_core(x)` in rooted coordinates"), `:136–138`; Scott `B-section.tex:553–556, 618–633` (`C_μ = J + F_μ*F_μ`, :629), `:784` (`C^rem_μ` with the contact term removed). Lean (definitions read by the tracing agent): `YM.Stationary.Joint` (`YM/Next/STATIONARY/Joint/Chart.lean:229`), `YM.Stationary.medals` (`M_act`) and `YM.Stationary.legion` (`M_core`) (`Joint/Completion.lean:59, 61`), `YM.Stationary.Teller.contact` (`Completion.lean:116`, statement and proof read: `M_act = A + Z`), `YM.Stationary.lean_drift` (`Joint/Drift.lean:498`, statement read). Not checked: that `Lean/` is at the pinned revision; the proofs of `lean_drift`, `guard_y`, `y_stems`, `abides`, `fields`.
*Across chapters:* chapter 7 only. Symbol clashes found by the trace: `A` is the fine kinetic Hessian at 7:280 and `M_core` at 7:536; `Z` is the "coarse-frame projection" at 7:484 and the contact term at 7:536; `r_x` is the coarse scalar component at 7:514, `r` the scalar coordinate at 7:704 and `r(x)` the penalty gradient at 7:532 (Appendix C). The trace's inference, not stated in a source, is that the hypothesis "one reference tree translated over the blocks" is not needed for 7:530–577. Unrelated to `core` of chapter 6.
*See also:* rooted coordinates; centered coordinates; contact term; completion (sense 3).

#### macro-box
*Now:* not applied; the text keeps *macro-box* and now uses it for all the former variants ("macro-patch", "macro-frame"); "macro axial gauge" is now "axial gauge on the macro-box" (5:1015; 6:322, 349, 490).
*Variants:* lifted macro-box; axial gauge on the macro-box; no longer in the text: macro-patch; macro-frame; macro axial gauge.
- **Meaning.** The box of radius `(j+7)L` about `Ly` ("the lifted macro-box of radius `(j+7)L` centered at `Ly`", 4:332–333), that is, the block-average patch of radius `(j+3)L` enlarged by `4L`, and an axial gauge on it. "Lifted" means taken in the covering lattice `ℤ^4`, the periodic images being counted with their multiplicities `m_y(q)` (4:334–335).
  *Basis:* R (4:332–335). *Where:* 4:332, 407, 442; 5:1015–1042; 6:308–350, 483–501, 609. *Proposed:* *enlarged block*; *axial gauge on it* (the axial gauge of the patch frames of chapter 4, on the enlarged box; not the block axial gauge of chapter 5).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:991`: "Let `𝒫_y(U) = Σ_q m_y(q) chord(U_q)` be the fine plaquette sum in the lifted macro-patch centred at `ℓy`, with `m_y(q)` its actual multiplicity there. The macro radius is `(j+7)ℓ`". Lean `YM.Pressure.macroR`, `YM/Pressure/Cost.lean` (definition read): `macroR P = P.radius + 4·P.L`, with `YM.RG.Patch.radius = (P.J+3)·P.L`, `YM/RG/Patch.lean` (definition read).
*Literature:* no name. The neighbourhood **`Δ(p′) = B(y_0) ∪ B(y_1) ∪ B(y_2) ∪ B(y)`** of a coarse plaquette (B85a p. 24: "for x in some neighborhood of y containing 2^d blocks having the point y as one of the corners"; p. 25, (46): "it is a local result; the bound above depends on bounds for V(∂p) − 1 on Δ(p′)"); the **global axial gauge** on a cube (B85b p. 98: "satisfies the global axial gauge conditions on □^(k)"; B88b p. 283: "we introduce the axial gauge for the field `M^j(U_k)` on `□_0`, considering `□_0` as one block with center at `z`"; B89a p. 193 "a generalized axial gauge on the surface"); weakly, `□̃`, "the union of all M-cubes touching □" (D1 p. 1330010-13). An analogue: the same role, the region around a coarse plaquette on which a local axial gauge is used and on which the result depends. The word was not found in B87, B88a, B85e; the analogues are in B85a, B85b, B88b. Suggested: *enlarged box*, with "(the neighbourhood `Δ(p′)` of a coarse plaquette in B85a (46))"; "macro axial gauge" = *axial gauge on the enlarged box* (Bałaban: "global axial gauge" on a cube, against "axial gauge in blocks").
*Across chapters:* chapters 4–6 only; the word occurs in none of the files of chapters 12–16 (13ba:248–249 restates a radius `(j_i+3)L_i` without it). The "padded block" of chapter 7 was not this box: at 7:608 it is a box of radius `(j+5)L`, at 7:637 the patch of the averaging operation of radius `(j+3)L`; since 25 November 2026 the text gives both radii ("padded box of radius `(j+5)L`", 7:608; "the patch `Ly+𝔹_R`, `R=(j+3)L`", 7:637); see *padded block*.
*See also:* block-average patch; padded block; first-power.

#### margin
*Now:* unchanged. The proposal for sense 1 was applied only at 16:205 ("strict inequality"); elsewhere sense 1 stands, and the word now also names the slack in the support exponent and in the decay width (about 35 further lines in chapters 8–12, 17m, 18lp). In sense 2 "slab margins" (14:103) is replaced by *buffer*.
*Also in the text for:* the former *reserve* (see those entries).
*Variants:* strict margin; determinant margin; plateau margin; margin in the support exponent; width margin; margin `3t`; margin `3a_k`; interior margin; no longer in the text: strict attachment margin (9:796 now "the strict margin in the site-norm bound"); slab margins.
1. **Slack in a strict inequality**: the amount by which a bound is satisfied with room to spare, kept to absorb later errors. "a strict margin `(2B+1)^4γ ≤ 1/2`" (9:703–704); "The strict margin in the site-norm bound allows this addition" (9:796–797); "`Cξ` is less than one third of the margin" (6:924); "The margin between `−3/8` and `−1/4` absorbs the projection factors" (10:618). *Basis:* R (9:703–704; 10:618). *Where:* 5:1374; 6:743, 923–924, 1026, 1559; 9:703, 796; 9s:226; 10:618, 779, 918; 11R:262, 279, 307; 18lp:257 (16:205 now "strict inequality"). Also "margin in the support exponent": 8:151, 334, 365; 9:149, 268, 283, 440, 518, 921; 10:37, 510, 597, 606, 763, 916; 11:200, 227, 1049; 12:278; 17m:316; 18lp:177; "width margin", "margin in the decay width": 10:378, 445, 706, 715, 761; 11:471, 474, 1753; 12:62, 127; others 11:940; 11R:9, 275, 372; 12:283; 13ba:148. *Proposed:* *strict inequality with slack …*; print the inequality.
2. **Distance to a cell boundary**: a length. "if a margin `3t` is required" (11:2344); "with margin `3a_k`" (13:90); "the fixed interior margin of each reflected scale-`k` cell" (13ba:273–274). *Basis:* R (11:2342–2344; 13:89–90). *Where:* 11:2344, 2356; ch. 12–16 (11 of 16 lines), e.g. 13:89–90; 13ba:273–275; 14lc:95. The former "slab margins" of 14:103, the distance of the times from the two faces of the slab, together with the pairwise separation, is now the *buffer* `r` (14:103, defined at 13:337). *Proposed:* keep *margin* for this length, defined once.
*Across chapters:* both senses run through the book; in files 10 and 11R the word is the same as "reserve", in file 11 it is spatial. Not a synonym of "lower bound" (floor, gap): every use read is slack in an estimate (9:703, 796; 9s:226; formerly 9:951). "Margin" must not replace "buffer" (13:337), which also includes the pairwise separation. The former "numerical band margin" of 9:951 (removed on 25 November 2026) was sense 1: the slack `κ_G/4` in the condition `C_j^{drift}/log 𝓛_j ≤ min{κ_G/4, j^{−2}}` (10.drift-floor, 10:55–60) on the block ratios, which keeps the tuned inverse couplings between the inner barriers of 10:215–225 and hence in the band; see *numerical band margin*, where the sources are cited.
*See also:* loss; inner barriers; join; numerical band margin.

#### mark
*Now:* partly replaced by *with insertions* (senses 1 and 3); *insertion*, *insertion point* (sense 2); *nilpotent source variable*, *insertion*, *source weight* (sense 4); remains at 7:385 (sense 5); at 18:177 "the stronger anchored marked support bound" (sense 1) was replaced on 26 November 2026 by "the bound (ch11:higher-induction) for the terms of source degree at least two" and stands only in the margin note there (grep); otherwise only in math mode (`ρ_marked`, `E_mark`, `δ^mark`, and "unmarked exponent" inside the display at 11:1587–1588) and labels.
*Variants:* marked (18:177); symbols `δ^mark`, `E_mark`; "unmarked exponent" (inside the display 11:1588); no longer in the text in prose: unmarked; marker; marked point, site, ancestor; marked factor, term, component, activity; marked density, expansion, step, polynomial; two-mark; mark weights; marker weight, marker amplitude; nilpotent marker.
1. **Marked = carrying insertions tracked by nilpotent source variables.** The density without insertions is the coefficient of `z_∅`: "let `ρ_N ≥ 0` be the density without insertions" (11:72), `q_N = ρ_N∏(1 + z_iF_i)` (11:77); "the exact density with insertions" is a polynomial in the nilpotent `z_i` (12:201–207). Said of a single term, factor or component it means carrying a nonempty set of insertion labels; said of a whole object (density, expansion, step) it means "with insertions". *Basis:* R (11:72–77; 12:201–207). *Where:* now "with insertions" or "without insertions" (about 110 lines, chapters 9–19: e.g. 11:2, 140, 178, 220, 253, 381; 12 (17); 13sb:10, 26; 18gq:25; 18lp:26; 14:16, 172; 17:119, 132; 18:9, 121; 19:48); "marked" only at 18:177; earlier only at 5:861 ("They do not imply cutoff continuity of the localized terms and large-field activities of the nonlinear step, or of the integral maps of a step with insertions"), a forward reference: the maps are those of one block step applied to densities with insertions, whose dependence on the cutoff is the subject of 12:37 ("the cutoff-dependent step with insertions") and 12:90 (`I_G`, "the coefficient map of one step with insertions"); chapter 5 itself does not say so (I). *Adopted:* *with insertions*; *term carrying insertions*; *density with insertions*.
2. **Mark = one insertion**, its point, its lattice site or its index ("insertion points project to a coarse site", 11:261; "the insertion incidence sum at a fixed insertion point", 11:259; "several insertions", 18:130). The former "marked ancestors" of 13ba:131 are now "ancestors of insertion points". *Basis:* R. *Where:* now "insertion" or "insertion point": about 30 in chapter 11 (e.g. 11:186, 218, 259, 261, 269, 273, 496, 516); 13ba:131; 14:339; 15:254, 262; 18lp:67, 71, 72, 80, 86, 127, 183, 215; 17m:438; 18:130. *Adopted:* *insertion (point)*; *insertion index*.
3. **Marked with a factor that is not an observable**: in most of 17m the inserted factor is the differentiated block kernel `𝒟_Yk` ("an admissible conditional integral with the differentiated kernel inserted. Its extra factor is a finite sum of smooth local kernel scores", 17m:72–73). *Basis:* R (17m:72–73). *Where:* "with the differentiated kernel inserted" at 17m:72; "that conditional integral" at 17m:84; "the component of the differentiated kernel" at 17m:120, 122; the kernel score itself is "the full differentiated kernel" at 17m:68, 155, 440; still "with insertions" at 17t:148; 17m:81, 150, 176, 381, 393, 411 (17m:2 lost it with the title of 26 November 2026). *Adopted:* *with the differentiated kernel inserted* (17m:72); not applied at the other lines.
4. **Marker**: the nilpotent variable attached to an insertion (18:125, now "the nilpotent source variables"), or the insertion itself ("Insertions may merge", 18:126); the former "mark weights", "marker weight", "marker amplitude" (13sb:73; 14lc:60, 63) are now "source weights", "source weight". In the source a marker is one group of insertions not yet merged with another, with one nilpotent variable and one weight, which is why markers can merge. *Basis:* R / I; S for the marker as a group. *Where:* 18:125, 126; 13sb:73; 14lc:60, 63. *Adopted:* *nilpotent source variable*; *insertion*; *source weight*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:224`: "A marker is one group of insertions in the reflected cells not yet fused with another; it is live while its weight is positive. To each marker `ι` attach a commuting variable `z_ι` with `z_ι² = 0` and a mark weight `w_ι > 0`."
5. **External background leg**: "For a mark of direction `a` and Lie algebra direction `u`" (7:385), an external background leg with polarisation `e_a` and colour `u` in a first-order vertex. *Basis:* I (7:385–392). *Where:* 7:385. *Proposed:* *external leg with polarization `e_a` and color `u`*.
*Across chapters:* senses 1 and 2 are stable from chapter 11 to chapter 19; sense 3 is a new use in chapter 17, partly under the same words "with insertions" as sense 1 and partly under "differentiated kernel"; sense 5 an isolated one in chapter 7. `blueprint/notation.md` has mark = observable insertion. At 9:264 ("marking one changed factor") the word is ordinary. Where to draw the line between senses 1 and 3 in chapter 17 is a judgement.
*See also:* insertion; insertion label; incidence; label; nilpotent marker; group.

3. **Sum of the coefficients of a kernel**: "their coefficient sums are one except that no sum is prescribed for `K_a^t`" (17t:45–46); "row sum" (17c:337, 369); "`K_a` is a finite combination of fine translates with coefficient sum one" (17c:328; before 25 November 2026 "the base-point average with coefficient sum one", 17c:325); "Their normalization to total mass one" (11R:390) is the normalisation of the kernels. *Basis:* R (17t:44–46). *Where:* 11R:390 ("mass"); 17t:45, 46; 17c:110, 122, 328, 337, 369 ("coefficient sum", "row sum"). *Adopted:* *sum of the coefficients*; *row sum*; *with total sum one*.
4. **Measure of a set** (standard): "spectral mass near zero" (19:139); `N(0, A(x)^{-1}){|ξ| ≤ D}`, "the Gaussian measure of a ball" (9s:72–74). *Basis:* R. *Where:* 9s:74, 83 ("Gaussian measure of the ball"); 12:191; 14:429, 767, 771; 15:328; 16:393, 446; 17:70; 19:139. *Adopted:* keep (standard); *Gaussian measure of the ball* at 9s:74.
5. **Physical mass**: mass shell, mass gap (16:389), regulator mass `μ` (chapter 17). *Basis:* R. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes: sense 1 in chapters 4–6, sense 2 in chapters 11 and 18lp, sense 3 in 11R and chapter 17, senses 4–5 standard. Sense 2 is not the weight `λ(U,α)` of sense 1.

#### matching
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* classical matching; quadratic matching; quantum matching.
- **Meaning.** The conditions that make the coarse action agree with the fine one to a stated order. Classical matching: `E − J − S_3 − S_4 = O(v⁵)` with equal Hessians (7:1001–1011). Quadratic (determinant) matching: subtraction of `α b_H` from the determinant symbol (7:1172–1180). Later: "Matching replaces `S_stat` by an action with identical Taylor coefficients through field order four" (17c:302–304). "Quantum matching" (9:929; 9s:279) refers to the determinant matching; the phrase never occurs in chapter 7.
  *Basis:* R (7:1001–1011, 1172–1180). *Where:* 1:463; 4:515, 570; 6:174, 963; 7:1001–1011, 1172–1180; 9:929; 9s:278–279; 17c:302–304. *Proposed:* keep, define once (with the two conditions named *classical* and *determinant* matching).
*Literature:* **renormalization** of the localized terms, by expansion in the background field "up to the fifth order" (B87 p. 258: "we expand the last expression in H up to the fifth order. The fifth order term can be bounded by E_0 O((L^jη)^5) exp(−κd_j(X)). The sum of lower order terms is analyzed with a help of Ward-Takahashi identities"; p. 277: "This is the fundamental expansion for the analysis of renormalization"). An analogue of the quantum (determinant) matching: the same power counting, order at least five being irrelevant in `d = 4`. Classical matching (`E − J − S_3 − S_4 = O(v⁵)`, 7:1001–1011) has no counterpart: in Bałaban `A(U_k(V^{(k)})) = A(U_{k+1})` holds exactly (B87 (2.3), (2.6)), because the leading term is the Wilson action at the minimiser and not an explicit coarse action. Suggested: keep *matching*; say that Bałaban's name for the corresponding operation is "renormalization" and that classical matching is specific to an explicit coarse action.
*Across chapters:* one sense; chapters 4 and 6 use the word before chapter 7 states the conditions. The former "hypothesis matching" of 8:170 now reads "the verification of the hypotheses" of a cited theorem; it was unrelated.
*See also:* matched; inherited loop action.

#### measure multiplier
*Now:* replaced by *constant factor of the change of variables* (9:63).
- **Meaning.** The constant factor produced by the change of variables `a = μ + gz` on the active bonds together with the insertion of the dummy Gaussian integrals: `(2π)^{-(D − n_act q)/2} g^{n_act q} c_H^{n_act}` (9:63–66), the product of the normalisation `(2π)^{-1/2}` of one standard Gaussian for each of the `D − n_act q` dummy coordinates, the Jacobian `g^{n_act q}` of the affine substitution on the `n_act q` active coordinates, and the value `c_H` at zero of the Haar density for each active bond. "Before the Haar logarithm" means: without the field-dependent part of the Haar density, `exp(Σ_{e active} j_e)`, which stays among the local exponential factors (9:76–78), and without the Gaussian weight of the dummy variables. The display rewrites the constant as `(2π)^{-D/2} 𝔪^{N_free} e^{−(N_free − n_act) log 𝔪}`.
  *Basis:* R (9:63–71) for the formula; S for the origin of the three factors and for "before the Haar logarithm". *Where:* 9:63 ("the constant factor of the change of variables before the Haar logarithm"). *Adopted:* *the constant factor of the change of variables*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/gaussian-reassembly.tex:49–62`: "Consequently the change of variables in the active Haar coordinates, with the dummy Gaussian integrals inserted, gives the multiplier `b^{-(D−nq)} g^{nq} c_H^n exp(−𝒢(z) + Σ_{e active} j_e(u))` [`b = √(2π)`]. Here `j_e` is the localized logarithmic Haar correction … The constant in (reassembly-jacobian) is exactly `b^{-D} m^N exp(−(N−n) log m)`. Indeed the right side is `b^{-D}m^n = b^{-(D−nq)} g^{nq} c_H^n`"; `:68` "The active affine substitution has Jacobian `g^{nq}`."
*Across chapters:* single occurrence. The "bookkeeping of the normalization constants" of 9:56 is this computation.
*See also:* missing-coordinate factor; dummy Gaussian coordinates.

#### measurement
*Now:* partly replaced by *value of the functional* (11:2260 "the values of the averaged functionals on them"); remains at 2:220, 238, 362; 11:1811, 1925, 2182, 2253. At 18:74 upstream's merge of 26 November 2026 rewrote the sentence: "Each probe correlation is evaluated in the undecomposed hierarchy `S`" (upstream had "mixed hierarchy", changed to "undecomposed hierarchy" in the merge, to be confirmed); "measurement" is gone there (grep).
*Variants:* measurement matrix; measurement cell; curvature measurement; plaquette measurement (2:220 "linearized plaquette measurements"); no longer in the text: averaged measurements.
1. **Value of a correlation functional**: the value of the finite family of correlation functionals `L_i` on a coefficient, with `G` its free counterpart; "measurement matrix" is the matrix of these values. At 18:74 (formerly "The undecomposed correlations are always used for this measurement", since 26 November 2026 "Each probe correlation is evaluated in the undecomposed hierarchy `S`") it is the evaluation of `b_α(w)` in the undecomposed (formerly "mixed") correlations. *Basis:* I (chapter 11); R (18:74). *Where:* 11:986, 1811, 1925, 2182, 2238–2240, 2253, 2260, 2281, 2293, 2319, 2325 (at 2233–2235, 2255, 2276, 2288, 2320 now "values" of the functionals; 983 and 2314 now say "correlation pairings"); 18:74. *Proposed:* *value of the functional `L_i`*; *matrix of correlations*; *evaluation*.
2. **Curvature measurement**: the maps `J ↦ σ_{γ,□}(U(1,J))` and their linearisations. *Basis:* I. *Where:* 2:220, 238, 362. *Proposed:* *transported curvatures* (as functions of the jet).
3. **Measurement cell**: a cell of the reflected tiling, also "comparison cell", "reflected replica cell", "reflection cell"; none of these is defined. At 11:781 ("has `n` copies") `n` is the number of reflected cells (`V = n (a_m/a_k)^4`, from 11:811, 819–821). A "copy" is not a cell but the image of an insertion or of a slab in a cell ("copied product", 11:839; "reflected-copy bound for a slab", 11:849; "every other reflected copy", 11:1127). *Basis:* I. *Where:* 11:180, 196, 345, 781, 838–849, 1127–1131, 1474, 1925, 2078. *Proposed:* *cell of the tiling* (one word for the cells); *copy* for the image of an insertion in a cell, not for the cell.
*Across chapters:* senses 1 and 3 in chapter 11 (sense 1 also in chapter 18), sense 2 in chapter 2. Not *correlation functional* for the family "response, tested correlation, measurement, correlation pairing": a measurement is a number, the value of the functional. Neither *copies* nor *cell* alone for the family "copies, replica cells, reflected copies, repetitions": cell and copy are different things.
*See also:* magnification; mixed table.

#### mesh estimate
*Formerly:* *recording estimate*.
*Also in the text for:* the former *recording* (see those entries).
*Variants:* "this last mesh estimate" (7:468); "the Fourier mesh estimate" (7:772); no longer in the text: "this last recording estimate"; the paragraph title "Trace norms and recording" (now "Trace norms and finite-volume coefficients", 7:752).
- **Meaning.** The bound `C_μ e^{−c_μ n}` on the difference between the mesh mean and the integral of a periodic analytic function (7:464–467), called "this last mesh estimate" (7:468) and "The Fourier mesh estimate at the end of Proposition (ch07:integrand-input)" (7:772–773). "Recording" is a source term: a momentum-space coefficient function `P` *records* a function on a finite torus when the Taylor coefficients of that function on unit Fourier waves are `|Λ|·P` at momenta summing to zero, up to a stated error; "exact recording" is the case of zero error. The recording estimate bounds that error: the finite-torus coefficient is a mesh mean of an analytic periodic integrand, the infinite-volume coefficient is its integral.
  *Basis:* R for the object (7:464–468); S for the word. *Where:* 7:468, 752; 7:772–773. *Adopted:* *Fourier mesh estimate* (7:772; "mesh estimate" at 7:468).
  *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-output-construction.tex:14–27` (`eq:output-record`): "A common coefficient picture `P` for functions `F_k` on tori `Λ_k` means that `|C_n(F_k)[v_1,…,v_n] − 1_{Σp_j=0} |Λ_k| P(p_1,…,p_{n−1})| ≤ |Λ_k| ε_k` for every such tuple of unit waves … Exact recording is the case `ε_k = 0`"; Martin `existence/annulus-recording-yield.tex:1` ("Finite-volume recording and uniform drift") and `:65–70`: `|⟨f⟩_ℓ − c_0| ≤ 𝔯(σ,A) e^{−σℓ/4}`. Lean `YM.Stationary.Recorded`, `YM/Next/STATIONARY/Lift/Pathways.lean` (definition read): `‖noteAt f (t+1) (glyph p i b) − collected L p i b‖ ≤ A` for all `p, i, b`, with `collected` equal to the number of sites times `L` at momenta summing to zero and `0` otherwise; `noteAt` was not read, so that it is the Taylor coefficient on Fourier waves is taken from Martin.
*Across chapters:* one object (text read at 7:462–469 and 7:770–774). Not related to the *recording scale* of chapter 11R.
*See also:* radial bound; recording scale; Trace norms and recording.

#### mismatch
*Now:* partly replaced by *deviation* (sense 1, defined at 6:49); remains at 6:1386 ("each frozen mismatch") and 6:1417 (sense 2, "the two signed mismatch terms").
*Variants:* deviation `n_e`; signed mismatch terms; no longer in the text: mismatch edge; mismatch distance; mismatch test; block average discrepancy.
1. **Deviation from the block average**: `n_e = χ(V_eQ_e(U)^{-1})` (6:45–47), the distance from the identity of the coarse link times the inverse block average. The text now defines the name: "`n_e` is called the *deviation* of the coarse link `V_e` from its average `Q_e(U)`" (6:49); the former "block average discrepancy" (6:8, 1022, 1349) is now "large deviations of coarse links from their averages" (6:8) and "the deviation `n_e`" (6:1022, 1349), and 4:440–441 now reads "Replacing these four values by the links of `V` adds precisely the four distances `χ(V_eQ_e(U)^{-1})`, `e ∈ ∂p`". `χ` is the normalised Hilbert–Schmidt distance from the identity, `χ(u) = ‖u − 1‖_F / √n_G` (1:90–95). *Basis:* D (6:47–49; 1:90–95 for `χ`). *Where:* 4:441 (the formula); 6:8, 47–49, 258, 340, 352, 358, 1018, 1022, 1349, 1385 ("deviation"); 9s:146, 154, 168 ("deviation"). *Adopted:* *deviation `n_e` of the coarse link from its average `Q_e(U)`* (the value of the averaging operation), one name for the three; or write `χ(V_eQ_e(U)^{-1})`.
2. **"The two signed mismatch terms"** (6:1417): plausibly the terms `E_L`, `E_D` that 6:217–218 calls "The two terms `E_L, E_D`, which are not of definite sign". *Basis:* I. *Where:* 6:1417. *Proposed:* *the error terms `E_L`, `E_D`*.
*Literature:* no noun. With a Gaussian block kernel: the condition `|Φ_{k+1}(y) − (QΦ_k)(y)| ≤ p_k`, with characteristic function `χ^q_k` and `ζ^q_k = 1 − χ^q_k`, whose failure defines the region `P_{k+1}` (D2 p. 092301-31, (232)–(234): "Because of the factor exp(−½aL|Φ_{k+1} − QΦ_k|²) large Φ_{k+1} will also be suppressed in Λ_k. To take advantage of this feature …"). The same object in role (sense 1, `n_e = χ(V_eQ_e(U)^{-1})`), for a linear scalar average. In Bałaban's gauge-field papers the deviation is identically zero, because the new field equals the average exactly (`δ(B − QA)`, B84a; the fibres `Ū^j = V`, B85b (1.13)); the nearest quantities are the deviation of the prescribed `V` from the average of the background, `V′ = V(Ū_0^j)^{-1} = e^{iB}` with hypothesis (1.35), "`|\overline{(U′U_0)}^j − Ū_0^j| < α_1` on Λ_j" (B85b p. 82; a weak analogue: it compares with the average of the background, enters as a small datum and carries no energy), and the "approximate fluctuation field" `V_k (V^{(k)}_{□'})^{-1}` of the set `Q_{k+1}` (B88b p. 247). So "no counterpart" (B84a–B85d, B87, B88a, B85e, B88b–B89b) and "the same object in role" (D2) are both right, for the delta-function and the Gaussian kernel respectively. Bałaban's letter `B` must not be used for it. Suggested, in the vocabulary adopted on 23 November 2026: *deviation of the coarse field from its average* (the value of the averaging operation); no literature name.
*Across chapters:* sense 1 in chapters 4, 6 and 9s; sense 2 once.

#### missing-coordinate factor
*Now:* unchanged; since 25 November 2026 9:77 gives the formula: "logarithm, missing-coordinate factor `𝔪^{−(N_free−n_act)}` and residual of the mean equation".
- **Meaning.** The factor `e^{−(N_free − n_act) log 𝔪} = 𝔪^{−(N_free − n_act)}` of 9:68: one factor `𝔪^{-1}` for each free bond that is not active (left in Haar measure and not given Lie-algebra coordinates). It compensates the reference scalar `𝔪^{N_free}`, which is extracted once for all free bonds, and is assigned to the local exponentials of the components containing those bonds. The text named it without a formula until 25 November 2026; 9:77 now reads "logarithm, missing-coordinate factor `𝔪^{−(N_free−n_act)}` and residual of the mean equation".
  *Basis:* R (9:77, with 9:65–71); confirmed by S. *Where:* 9:77. *Adopted:* the formula at 9:77, which the review found equal to the factor at 9:68; the name is kept.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/gaussian-reassembly.tex:57–63` (`eq:reassembly-count`): "The constant in (reassembly-jacobian) is exactly `b^{-D} m^N exp(−(N−n) log m)`. … This uses `n + (N−n) = N`, not the number of active coordinates as a substitute for the number of free bonds"; `:105–109` (`eq:reassembly-packet-log`): the component exponent contains the term `−(N−n) log m`. No Lean declaration was identified.
*Across chapters:* single occurrence.
*See also:* active coordinates.

#### moment
*Now:* partly replaced by *lattice correlation at the cutoff* (sense 1 at 12:294); *vacuum expectations of products of compressions* (sense 3, 15:169, 215; 15sp:17); *polynomial factors in the support size* (sense 4 at 18lp:177); remains in sense 1 ("free moment", "cutoff moment", 11:82, 2070; 14lc:47, 55; 15:277), sense 2 (standard), sense 4 at 10:606 and sense 5.
*Variants:* cutoff moment (11:82); free moment; damped moment; support moments (10:606); marginal moments; low moments; moment norm; no longer in the text: free row moments; compressed product moments.
1. **Lattice correlation.** `M^lat_{N,p}(v;y) = ∫ ∏_{i=1}^n I_{N,p}(v_i, y_i; U) dμ_{N,p}(U)`, the expectation of a product of insertions at lattice sites `y` (1:341–343). The `M_{N,p}(v;x/a_N)` of 12:263, 381 and 13:256 is this function with the superscript dropped; "the lattice correlation at the cutoff" (12:294, formerly "the actual cutoff moment") is its value at cutoff `N`. "Free moments" `G_J` are the correlations of the free fields. *Basis:* D (1:341–343); S for the identification of `M_{N,p}` with `M^lat_{N,p}`. *Where:* 1:341–343; 12:263, 294 ("lattice correlation at the cutoff"), 379; 13:256; 14lc:47, 55; 14:905; 15:277 ("The free moments of each test"). *Proposed:* *lattice correlation `M^lat_{N,p}`*; write the superscript in chapters 12–13.
   *Source:* Scott part1/02-definitions.tex:66–74 (Definition "Lattice moments"): "The moment is the expectation of a product of insertions"; Scott part2/E-section.tex:672: "where `M_{N,p} = M_{N,p}(v; x/a_N)` is the cutoff moment and `C_{N,p,m} = C_{N,p,m}(v;x)` is its approximation computed at level `m`".
2. **Moment of a measure or of a profile** (standard). *Basis:* R. *Where:* 14:438–448, 462, 471, 496, 516, 574, 660–682; 7:1101–1103 ("zero zeroth and first moments"); 11:591. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
3. **Expectation in `Ω` of a product of compressed operators**: `⟨Ω, M(w_1)⋯M(w_k)Ω⟩`, the limit of the correlations of the translated words as their time gaps tend to infinity (ch15:cluster, 15:81–84), and in particular `⟨Ω, (A^*A)^jΩ⟩` (15:162–164). These are "the vacuum expectations of products of compressions" of 15:215 (formerly "compressed product moments"); they are not correlations of a word ("Compression is not multiplication of finite-separation words", 15:124). *Basis:* R (15:81–84, 162–164). *Where:* 15:162–171, 215; 15sp:17 (now "vacuum expectations"). *Adopted:* *expectation in `Ω` of the product*; not *correlation*.
   *Source:* Scott part2/H-section.tex:111–113: "Moment bounds in the vacuum state bound a compressed operator in every phase … Let `U ∈ 𝔄_0` and `B ≥ 0` satisfy `⟨Ω, (U^*U)^nΩ⟩ ≤ B^{2n}` for every `n`. Then `‖U‖ = sup_ξ |ξ(U)| ≤ B`."
4. **"Support moments".** Sums over supports (or polymers) weighted by a power of the size of the support: the polynomial factors `(1 + S)^k` in the size `S` of a support that derivative weights and Taylor remainders produce, summed against the exponentially weighted activity bounds. They are bounded by giving up a fixed part of the exponential support weight ("the polynomial factors in the support size with their positive margin in the exponent", 18lp:177; "Polynomial support moments are absorbed by another fixed margin in the support exponent", 10:606–607; "The additional incoming exponential support decay absorbs this polynomial", 11:420). *Basis:* I from the v3 text (10:606; 11:420); S for the estimate. *Where:* 10:606 ("support moments"); 18lp:177 ("polynomial factors in the support size"). *Proposed:* *polynomial factors in the size of the support*.
   *Source:* Martin existence/high-degree-cluster-prices.tex:123–151: for a connected set `P` of labels, `S(P) = Σ_{i∈P}(c(X_i) + e_i)` with `c` the connected cover number; "`(1+S)^k ≤ e^ε k! ε^{−k} e^{εS}` … The same `ε` therefore pays both the retained full-footprint exponential and the polynomial moment". That 10:606 and 18lp:177 were written from this passage is not established; the wording and the estimate agree. Scott part2/J-section.tex:280, the source of 18lp:170–180, has "The finite derivative sums, coefficient conversion and remainder constants are at most `Ξ_m`" and no "support moments".
5. **Vanishing-moment conditions of chapter 17** (see *low moments*). *Where:* 17; 17t; 17c; 17m; 19:161.
*Across chapters:* five senses; about 25 occurrences in chapters 12–16. Sense 1 must not be extended to 15:215.
*See also:* low moments; moment norm; mass.

#### moment norm
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* moment norm `M_q` of an evaluation; finite parameter evaluation.
- **Meaning.** For a finite linear combination `Σ a_iF(z + t_iv)` of values along a line (a "finite parameter evaluation"), its moment norm at radius `q` is `sup_{n≥0}|Σ a_i(t_i/q)^n|` (display 10:469–474; "Let a finite parameter evaluation have moment norm `M_q` at a fixed radius `q`", 10:633). The moment sequence `(Σ a_i(t_i/q)^n)_n` is an element of `c₀` (10:479–480); equivalently the quantity is the norm of the functional `f ↦ Σ a_i f(t_i)` on power series normed by `Σ|f_n| q^n`.
  *Basis:* R / I (10:471, 633–638). *Where:* 10:469–474, 479–480, 633, 636. *Proposed:* *sup norm of the moment sequence* `(Σ a_i(t_i/q)^n)_n`.
*Across chapters:* chapter 10 only. Not *norm of the functional on `c₀`* (wrong space: the sequence lies in `c₀`, the functional acts on power series).
*See also:* moment.

#### moving
*Now:* partly replaced by *cutoff-dependent*, *convergent sequence of free fields* (sense 1); *parameter-dependent* (sense 2 in chapter 10); remains at 7:267, 745 (sense 2, "the moving Haar Jacobian", "the moving weights") and 4:711 ("no moving large-field boundary"); ordinary uses at 14:909 ("the moving point"), 17t:253 ("moving charts").
*Variants:* moving weights; moving Haar Jacobian; no longer in the text: moving labels; moving free labels; moving field; moving test functions; moving equation space; varying equation space; moving equation kernel; moving complement; moving expression; moving threshold surface.
1. **Depending on the sequence index** (the cutoff `(N,p)`, or the level), usually while converging: "The cutoff-dependent equation space" (11:1088); "the cutoff-dependent test functions" (13:297, lattice-dependent); "also for convergent sequences of free fields", "Convergent sequences of free fields are handled by expansion in fixed finite bases" (14:243, 255); likewise 17:97; "a cutoff-dependent field has coefficient size `ε_m` at scale `m`" (18:178–179). *Basis:* R (11E:154–158 for the equation space; 14:243, 255). *Where:* 11:1088, 2223, 2229; 11E:153; 13:297; 18:178 ("cutoff-dependent"); 14:243, 255; 17:97, 372 ("convergent sequences of free fields"). *Adopted:* *cutoff-dependent*; *convergent sequence of labels (fields)*.
2. **Depending on the variable or parameter that is varied**, against "frozen": "these constant weights are uniformly comparable to the moving weights" (7:744–745); "the moving Haar Jacobian" (7:267–268); an expression that "would move with the mean or precision … no such parameter-dependent expression is compared here" (10:733–734). *Basis:* I (chapter 7); R (10:733–737). *Where:* 7:267–268, 744–745; 10:733–737 ("parameter-dependent"). *Proposed:* *parameter-dependent*; *variable* (against *frozen*).
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes: sense 2 in chapters 7 and 10, sense 1 from chapter 11 on. The "cutoff-dependent complement" (11:2229, formerly "moving complement") is the range of the bounded equivariant projection `Π_i` whose kernel is the equation space `K_i = 𝖹_{N,p,e}P_{N,p,e}S_{t_N}R_e𝓘_e`: a complement of `K_i` in `V_e`, depending on `i = (N,p)`, of dimension `r = dim(V_e/𝓘_e)` at every cutoff (11:1094–1104, 2223–2237; R, text read). The proposition bounds `‖Π_i v‖_1` for all `v ∈ V_e`, which is what "on the entire cutoff-dependent complement" says.
*See also:* moving comparison fields; label.

#### noise
*Now:* partly replaced by *fluctuation field*, *fluctuation variables*, *ratio of the threshold to the fluctuation scale* (sense 2); remains in sense 1 (chapter 5, 14 occurrences: 5:251, 280, 377–399, 418, 549, 775–782).
*Variants:* accumulated noise; no longer in the text: suffix noise; noise coordinates; cutoff-to-noise ratio.
1. **Gaussian term of the block kernel.** The independent Gaussian `b^{-1/2}ξ` in `v = Qa + b^{-1/2}ξ` (decomposition at 5:126–130, where the word is not yet used) and its propagated contribution: "The independent noise introduced at step `h` is propagated only through the subsequent, coarser steps `h+1, …, n`" (5:378–379).
   *Basis:* R (5:378–379). *Where:* 5:250–251, 377–378, 548–549 and about 10 further lines. *Proposed:* acceptable; or *the `b⁻¹` term*.
2. **Fluctuation variable of the local integral.** The former "noise coordinates" are the Gaussian fluctuation coordinates `g z_i` of the local integral, now "all components `gz_i` of the fluctuation field" (6:914); the former "cutoff-to-noise ratio" is now "the ratio of the threshold to the fluctuation scale" (11R:62–63).
   *Basis:* R (6:914). *Where:* 6:914 ("fluctuation field"), 1014 ("the bound on the fluctuation field"); 11:713 ("local fluctuation variables"); 11R:62. *Adopted:* *fluctuation field* for the Gaussian integration variables `g z_i` of the step; *fluctuation variables* for the unit-covariance coordinates `z_i`; for "cutoff-to-noise ratio", *ratio of the threshold to the fluctuation scale `g`*.
*Literature:* sense 2 (the Gaussian fluctuation coordinates `g z_i` of the local integral, 6:914): **fluctuation field** `U′`, `B′`, `A′` (B85e p. 259: "The new variables U′ are called fluctuation fields, and the minimal configuration U_1 is called a background field"; B87, title of Sect. 2: "Fluctuation Field Integral in k+1-st Renormalization Transformation"; B88b p. 248); **fluctuation variables** (B85d p. 305; B95 p. 120: "The functions χ^{(j)} give restrictions on fluctuation variables at corresponding steps"); in D1, D2 the fluctuation field `Z = Φ_k − Ψ_k` normalised to unit covariance, `Z = C_k^{1/2}W`, `W_k` (D1 p. 1330010-28: "the function χ^w_k enforces that the fluctuation field Φ_k − Ψ_k be small"). The same object: the integration variable of one step about the critical configuration; v3's `z_i` are the unit-covariance coordinates, Dimock's `W`. Sense 1 (the Gaussian term `b^{-1/2}ξ` in `v = Qa + b^{-1/2}ξ`, 5:126–130) has no name: it is the Gaussian weight of the transformation (B95 p. 107) and is absent in the gauge papers, where the kernel is a delta function. "Noise" is not from this literature. Adopted (23 November 2026), sense 2: *fluctuation field* (*fluctuation variables* for the normalised coordinates), replacing "noise coordinates". Sense 1 is not covered by the decision; the suggestion for it was *the Gaussian of the block kernel*.
*Across chapters:* two objects. Chapter 5 uses sense 1; chapter 6 and chapters 10–11 use sense 2 (11:713, 11R:62 have the chapter 6 sense).

#### normalized directions
*Now:* partly replaced by *directions of size `O(t_f)`* (6:644, 1288); remains in "normalized affine directions" (9:35, 504). At 9s:303 "the normalized affine directions of the activity seminorm" (25 November 2026, for "the reflected seminorm directions") is since 26 November 2026 "the directions admitted by the activity seminorm (ch04:local-seminorm), restricted to the cube `N_{w̄}` about the localization site" (from Scott `part2/D-section.tex:417–425`).

The "normalized affine directions" (9:35, 504) are the affine link fields `A^{q,T}` of 9:460–467 ("For an affine potential `A_μ(y) = u_μ + Σ_ν y^ν v_{μν}`"; `A^{q,T}_c(y) = 1_{c=b} ξ_o(y)^a T`), those of the affine Hessian condition (4:671–676), scaled by `t`: "The evaluations in normalized affine directions and polarization give `t²|q_f(q,r)| ≤ 3a_f`" (9:504–505). "Reflected" (formerly at 9s:303–304) meant restricted to the reflection cube and extended to the auxiliary torus by the coordinatewise fold of 9:323–331; since 25 November 2026 the text says this in words, since 26 November 2026 as "restricted to the cube `N_{w̄}` about the localization site and carried to the reflected periodic extension" (9s:304) (see *reflected seminorm directions*).

#### normalized local insertion
*Now:* unchanged; now also the name at the definition (11:1056); glossed at its first use since 26 November 2026, for the case at the ultraviolet cutoff only (narrowed after the review): "normalized local insertions (at the ultraviolet cutoff these are the observables `O_{N,p}(d,c;x)` of Section ch11:collected)" (11:353).

In the one-step statements (11:353–355, 438) it is the local section applied to the coefficient at that level, `P_d^loc[S_{1/t_m} x°]`, restricted to small fields on its stencil. It is what is subtracted from a trial ("Subtract one normalized local insertion density from the trial at the ultraviolet cutoff", 11:898; 13ba:119). The weight `ω_k = a_k^d β̂_k^{-w_d} E_k^{-1}` (13sb:59) is attached to it and is not part of it (13sb:66; 18lp:243).
