#### principal
*Now:* partly replaced by *zero alias*, *nonzero alias* (sense 1) and, at 5:541, by "the decomposition of `D` displayed below" (sense 5); remains at 7:713 and 11:1742 (sense 1, "principal real cube", "principal alias"), in senses 2–4 and at 6:1501, 11:1638 (sense 5). The "principal regular bound" of 10:629 (25 November 2026) was dropped on 26 November 2026; the word stands there only in the margin note that records it (grep).
*Also in the text for:* the former *leading*; *nonprincipal* (see those entries).
*Variants:* nonprincipal; purely principal; principal term, factor, component; principal norm, estimate; principal compression; principal covariance block; principal alias (11:1742); no longer in the text: principal / nonprincipal alias (elsewhere); principal / nonprincipal columns; principal covariance split.
1. **Zero alias.** The alias index `0` as opposed to the nonzero ones (the alias being `k_l(p) = (p + 2πl)/L`, 7:1148); "columns" are the alias components `𝒜_l`, `𝒯_l`, now "columns at the zero alias" (5:581, 599) and "columns at each nonzero alias" (5:582).
   *Basis:* R (5:351–353) for the alias; I for "columns". *Where:* now "zero / nonzero alias": 5:351–353, 402, 581–600; 7:496, 710–732, 822–826, 1148–1161; 17c:68–69, 74–77, 335–336 (the alias argument of 17c:57–88, 324–331 was removed on 25 November 2026); 17m:204, 215–232; still "principal": 7:713; 11:1742. *Adopted:* *zero alias*, *nonzero aliases*; *alias components*.
2. **Principal submatrix.** "Principal compression" (6:523–580; that the compression is the principal submatrix `A[Ω,Ω]` is inferred) and "principal covariance block `Γ_I`" (6:759): the diagonal block of a matrix on an index set, the standard sense.
   *Basis:* I (6:554, 759). *Where:* 6:523–580, 759. *Proposed:* *principal submatrix*.
3. **Linear inherited term.** "The inherited principal norm" and "the principal estimate" (9:236, 269): the contribution of the linear inherited term, before the comparison with the block integral.
   *Basis:* I (9:236, 269). *Where:* 9:236, 269. *Proposed:* keep *principal*, defined once (or *linear inherited term*).
4. **Main part of an insertion factor.** In chapter 11, the main part of a single-insertion factor on the small-field event, evaluated by the joint Gaussian comparison: "Purely principal connected components have the one-cell support bound proved earlier. Their integral is the joint moment … since it contains neither an insertion-free correction nor an incoming large-field factor" (11:330–333); in the split `(1 + γWz_S)(1 + (1−γ)Wz_S)` (11:315–320) the second term is "nonprincipal" (formerly "nonleading"). "Nonleading" and "nonprincipal" were synonyms (11:280, 289); only "nonprincipal" remains: the source calls the principal terms "leading pieces" and the others "nonleading". The principal terms are prescribed: for each cell `c` and each nonempty set `I` of its insertions there is one prescribed principal term `F_{c,I}` with a prescribed support `X_{c,I}`, the coefficient of the connected polynomial of the Gaussian history at the current level; the principal terms actually present are compared with it at each step.
   *Basis:* I (11:315–333) from the v3 text; S for the prescription `F_{c,I}`. *Where:* 11:181, 280, 289–290, 298, 315, 320, 322, 330, 340, 425, 608, 728, 1048, 1416–1419, 1557, 1612, 1620, 1631–1638, 1652, 1891, 2132, 2137 (principal 21; nonprincipal 6). *Proposed:* keep *principal* / *nonprincipal*, defined once.
   *Source:* Martin existence/allarity-marked-propagation.tex:5–6 ("At an intermediate level the marked expansion contains the desired principal insertion, a small regular remainder, and a forced remainder"), :54–56 ("Every principal piece has a nonempty marker subset `I ⊆ {1,…,n}` and a prescribed spatial support `X_{c,I}` in cell `c`"), :103–105 ("Write the current regular source as a sum of remainder pieces `H_a` and leading pieces `S_b`. Let `F_{c,I}` be the desired principal source at mode `(c,I)`, with support `X_{c,I}`"), :202–204 ("The principal sources are the connected polynomials of the same Gaussian history at the current level, with the same cell and marker labels"), :340–341 ("nonleading regular marker-root bound … leading marker-root (principal incidence) bound"). No Lean declaration located.
5. **Compounds placed by the text.** The former "principal covariance split" (5:541, now "the decomposition of `D` displayed below") is the decomposition `D = F_{1,0}D_0F_{1,0}^* + U` displayed at 5:543–547, the part carried by the zero alias plus a diagonal remainder (sense 1). "Principal resolvent identity" (6:1501) is read as the resolvent identity for the inverses of the window (principal-submatrix) precisions of sense 2. "Principal real cube" (7:713–714: "bounded away from zero after division by `μ²` on the principal real cube") is read as the real momentum cube of the zero alias (sense 1). "Reassigning a principal term to its prescribed enlarged support" (11:1638, formerly "a principal source term") concerns a prescribed principal term `F_{c,I}` of sense 4.
   *Basis:* R (5:543–547) for the split; I for the resolvent identity and the real cube; S for 11:1638 (see sense 4). *Where:* 5:541; 6:1501; 7:713–714; 11:1638. *Proposed:* at 5:541 *the decomposition of `D`* with the display cited (done); at 6:1501 *the resolvent identity for the window precisions*; at 11:1638 *a principal term* (done).
*Across chapters:* at least four senses. Not *leading part* or *leading term* (senses 3 and 4): chapter 11 uses "leading" for other things ("the leading rescaling", "the leading map", 11:370, 377). The former "principal column" (17m:204, 232) is the alias component of sense 1, now "the column at the zero alias" (17m:232). 11:1557, 1891 now say "the corrected principal coefficients at the middle scale" (formerly "leading"): the source calls the principal terms "leading" (see *leading*, sense 3). "Remainder" is not a synonym of "nonprincipal": it also covers the large-field remainders (11:379–380).
*See also:* alias; leading.

#### probe
*Now:* partly replaced by *jet functional* (sense 1, defined at 3:751) and *order of the coefficient evaluations* (sense 3, 17m:251); remains in sense 2 (chapters 14, 18gq, 18lp, 18, 18r).
*Variants:* probe word; probe family; probe coordinates; exterior probes; no longer in the text: jet probe; coefficient probe.
1. **Linear functional on jets.** In chapter 3, a linear functional on the space of order-`j` solution jets: "`U_j = (𝒮_j^sc)^*` for the scalar order-`j` jet functionals" (3:939); defined at 3:751: "every *jet functional*, that is, every linear functional on the jets of the curvature at `x_0`".
   *Basis:* D (3:751); R (3:939). *Where:* 3:751, 883, 939–985 (all now "jet functional"). *Adopted:* *linear functional on jets*.
2. **Fixed exterior word.** "A probe is a fixed word `v` at distinct nonzero positions. It defines `λ(A) = S(A(0)v)` on each field space on which `A` is defined" (18:38–39). The probe is the word; the functionals `λ` are the coordinate functionals on `F_D` it defines. Probes occupy cells ("fixed cells for exterior probes", 18lp:332) and are chosen before the spectator (14:361).
   *Basis:* D (18:38–39). *Where:* 14:361; 18gq:132; 18lp:269, 293, 321, 332; 18:38–78, 117, 171, 218, 225, 244, 407 (17; "finitely many fixed separated probe words" in the gloss of the contact projection, since 25 November 2026); 18r:38, 61, 63, 66 (5). *Proposed:* keep *probe* for the word `v`, defined once; *the functional `λ_v`* for the functional.
3. **Coefficient evaluation by derivatives along a test path (17m).** In "Choose `j` above the order of the coefficient evaluations" (17m:251, formerly "the fixed probe order") the probe is the evaluation of a Taylor coefficient of a local function: its derivative of a fixed total order `ℓ ≤ d` at zero along a polynomial test path of link fields; the "probe order" is the largest such order needed (here the tuples "whose summed scaling dimension is at most five", 17m:252–253), and `j`, the number of vanishing derivatives at the nonzero aliases (17m:231–232), is chosen larger.
   *Basis:* S; I for the attribution of 17m:251 to this source passage (the chapter note `audit/ch17-marked-rates.md:69` names it as the supplier of this part of 17m). *Where:* 17m:251. *Adopted:* *the order of the coefficient evaluation* ("Choose `j` larger than the order of the derivatives taken in the coefficient evaluations").
   *Source:* Martin `existence/trace-row-jet-estimates.tex:160–161` (Proposition "Local probe bound from a strip and a jet gap"), `:226–233` ("Let `γ : ℝ → 𝒳` be the actual `C^d` probe path in the tangent configuration space, with `γ(0) = 0` and `γ^{(k)}(0) = θ x_k` … Then the probe of total derivative order `ℓ ≤ d` obeys `|d^ℓ/ds^ℓ F(inc_1(γ(s)))|_{s=0}| ≤ …`"), `:282–285` ("In the selected construction the probe is the composition of the local observable with a routed test path: the logarithmic-link test curve of the coefficient probe is cropped to the chart of radius `m` and passed through the first-order row operator of the step").
*Across chapters:* three senses (text read at 3:937–941, 18:37–40, 17m:249–252). Sense 3 is close to sense 1 (both extract finitely many jet coefficients) but is not the chapter 3 object: it acts on local functions of the lattice field, not on solution jets of the Maxwell equations. A probe is not a "pairing with spectators" (it is the word, not a correlation functional). Not *test configuration* (not standard usage); senses 1 and 3 are now renamed, which removes the collision. The word does not occur in the prose of chapters 1–3, 7–11 and 17 (labels only in chapters 3, 10–11).
*See also:* word; spectator; separating family; contact projection.

#### protected
*Now:* unchanged in senses 1 and 3 (sense 1 now defined at 6:739; at 6:701 "a protected logarithmic chart" is since 26 November 2026 "the logarithmic chart of the active links, where these logarithms are defined"); in sense 2 "protected trial" is replaced at 11:2311 by "a trial … satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)" and remains at 11:1068 and 13:231.
*Variants:* protected change of variables; protected (logarithmic) chart; protected neighborhood; protected patch; protected dependence set; protecting cutoff; protected trial; protected local representative; protected local bounds (source); protected-path errors; no longer in the text: protected dependence region.
1. **Of the change of variables of chapter 6.** Carrying a smooth cutoff in the logarithmic coordinates of the finitely many active bonds it reads: a protected factor vanishes unless each of these coordinates is below a fixed multiple of the chart radius. The text now says so: "Call a factor *protected* when it is cut off inside this logarithmic chart" (6:739). "Within the logarithmic chart of the active links, where these logarithms are defined (its radius `d_*` is fixed below), define `u_V(e) = log(exp(u_e)(rep V₀)_e (rep V)_e^{-1})`" (6:701–706; until 26 November 2026 "Within a protected logarithmic chart", rewritten by the decision of that day, List 2, item 3); "both endpoints … carry the protecting cutoff" (6:812). The fixing of the incoming links is the consequence, not the meaning: on the support of the cutoff the globally defined change of variables coincides with the exact logarithmic one, so `exp(u_V(e))(rep V)_e = U_e` and the fine links read by the factor do not move when the coarse field is varied. Later chapters use this consequence: "Hold the physical links in the incoming localized term fixed by the protected coordinate change" (9:258–259); "The protected change of variables leaves measurable fine reads fixed" (10:723–724); "On a protected dependence set the incoming measurable product remains fixed under the change of variables" (17m:74–76).
   *Basis:* D (6:739); I (6:701–706, 812); S for the decision that the word refers to the cutoff. *Where:* 6:701–743, 812; 9:259; 10:508, 675, 723, 740, 901; 11:472, 1778; 17m:74. *Proposed:* *cut off inside the chart* (*the change of variables (ch06:protected-change)*, cited by number).
   *Source:* Martin `existence/compensated-variation.tex:6–9`: the compensated change of variables "is a global bijection on the fluctuation space near the chosen coarse configuration, and agrees with the required logarithmic adjustment where the protected integrand can be nonzero"; `:151–158`: "On the protected support all fine reads are consequently fixed, including their masks, likelihoods and selected branch tags. … A finite set of protected bonds has one common such neighbourhood. No condition is imposed on the unprotected Gaussian coordinates." Lean `YM.PhysicalNext.JointLoad.Psalm.Pitch.Protected`, `YM/PhysicalNext/V9_JOINT_ENDPOINT_LOAD/Psalm/Breaks.lean` (definition read): `∀ i ∈ s, ‖z i‖ < 4·d.radius`; lemma `protects` in the same file (statement read): a nonzero product `openedPatch` of the cutoffs (`YM/PhysicalNext/V9_JOINT_ENDPOINT_LOAD/Psalm/Factors.lean`, definition read) implies `Protected`. The Lean statement that the fine field is held fixed on the protected set was not located, so that part rests on Martin.
2. **Protected trial, protected local representative.** A trial satisfying two bounds that grow slower than every power of `a_N^{-1}`, one for its derivatives on small-field configurations and one for its supremum on all configurations; see *protected trial* for the full hypotheses. The finite difference written as an observable of higher degree ("A translated finite difference of degree `d` has a protected local representative at degree `d+1`: `a_N^{d+1} Δ_α O(x) = a_N^d O(x + a_N e_α) − a_N^d O(x)`", 11:1068–1073; "make this a trial at degree `e = d + |l|` satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)", 11:2310–2311) and the inclusion in a higher degree (13:231–234) are examples that satisfy these bounds; they are not the definition.
   *Basis:* S; I for the examples (11:1068–1073, 2310–2313). *Where:* 11:1068, 2311; 13:231. *Proposed:* *trial with subpower derivative and supremum bounds*; define once.
   *Source:* see *protected trial*.
3. **Protected-path errors.** The errors from discarding the response paths that leave the patch of radius `B`: "Retain only response paths lying in the protected patch and put the omitted paths in the regular remainder. The exponential response bound makes their absolute contribution at most `C B^a e^{−cB} g^{-1}`" (11:1778–1781). At 17w:72 ("Its stage-dependent constants, protected-path errors, ratio-dependent jet errors and finite incidence costs are made smaller than the requested powers of `H_n`", 17w:71–73) they are listed among the errors of the finite-cutoff covariance estimate (11.finite-covariance).
   *Basis:* R (11:1778–1781) for the errors; I for their being the ones meant at 17w:72 (the phrase "protected-path" occurs only there). *Where:* 17w:72. *Proposed:* *the error from response paths leaving the patch (11:1778–1781)*.
*Literature:* no name; the **change of variables** B88b (1.22) for each bond variable `A(b)`, built with a smooth cutoff so that the characteristic functions no longer depend on the new field in the small field domain (B88b p. 251: "The characteristic functions … depend on the new field `V` on the whole small field domain `Λ_1`. This is an undesirable situation for the next renormalization step, and now we will remove this dependence"; pp. 251–252: "Now we make a change of variables for each bond variable `A(b)` … Here `g` is a `C^∞`-function defined on the Lie algebra `g`, `0 ≤ g(A') ≤ 1`, `g(A') = 0` on `{|A'| ≤ 4/3 g_0^{-1} δ_0}`"; used again B89a p. 188). A close analogue of sense 1: the same purpose (decouple conditions from the coarse or background field) and the same device (a smooth cutoff inside the substitution), and it "produces new terms in the effective action" (Jacobians), as in v3. In B87 the changes of variables (translation to the critical point, p. 265; "a change of variables linearizing the function Q(B′)", p. 267; the scaling `B = g_k B′`) carry no cutoff, and nothing was found in D1–D3; the counterpart is in B88b only. Suggested: "the **localizing change of variables** with smooth cutoff (B88b (1.22))", cited by v3 equation number.
*Across chapters:* three uses. Sense 2 is not *with small-field cutoff* and not the change-of-variables sense: no cutoff appears at 11:1066–1073, 2308–2314 or 13:228–235 (text read). In sense 3 the "protected patch" is the patch of sense 1 in chapter 11 (11:1778). For sense 1, the source sentence "On the protected support all fine reads are consequently fixed, including their masks, likelihoods and selected branch tags" states the consequence that 6:739–743 gives in shorter form.
*See also:* protected trial; trial; physical (sense 4); normalization index.

#### protected trial
*Now:* partly replaced by *a trial satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)* (11:2311); remains at 11:1068 ("protected local representative") and 13:231 ("the protected trial construction").
*Variants:* protected local representative; protected trial construction; protected local bounds (source).
- **Meaning.** A trial of degree `e`, i.e. a family of local lattice functions `F_{N,p}` proposed as insertions at the cutoff level with `f = a_N^e F` ("a trial `f = a_N^eF` with fixed link support", 11:922), satisfying the following hypotheses: `f` lives on the translates of one fixed finite stencil containing the origin; it is local and gauge invariant and has the regularity and weighted derivative bounds of the top level; and there are two nonnegative bounds, uniform in the site and growing slower than every power of `a_N^{-1}`, namely `c_{N,p}` for its value and derivatives on small-field configurations and `b_{N,p}` for `|f|` on the whole configuration space. No vanishing of Taylor coefficients is required of the trial itself. These are the hypotheses under which the cost `E_{N,p}` of 11:927–946 is subpower and (ch11:trial-error) applies. A finite difference written at degree `d+1` (11:1068–1073), a difference word at degree `e = d + |l|` (11:2310–2313) and the inclusion of a degree-`d` insertion in degree `e ≥ d` (13:231–234) are examples.
  *Basis:* S for the hypotheses; I for the examples (11:1068–1073, 2310–2313); R (11:927–946) for the two bounds `c_{N,p}`, `b_{N,p}` and their use. *Where:* 11:1068, 2311 ("a trial … satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)"); 13:231. *Proposed:* *trial with subpower derivative and supremum bounds* (*a trial satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)*), the hypotheses stated once at 11:922; applied at 11:2311 only.
  *Source:* Martin existence/actual-insertion-derivative-relay.tex:24–35 ("We require a fixed finite stencil containing zero, the regularity and weighted left-derivative bounds of the actual top budget, and two nonnegative subpower bounds `c_{N,p}, b_{N,p}`. The first bounds those derivatives on the healthy region and includes the value bound there; the second bounds `|f_{N,p,o}|` on the whole configuration space. These bounds are uniform in `o`. … No vanishing Taylor condition is imposed on the trial itself … We call these the protected bounds"), :39–41 (a label row that is subpower in the inverse terminal coordinates "has protected local bounds at weight `d`"); existence/ope-filtration.tex:354 (proposition "Comparison of a protected local trial"); existence/fullmesh-fixedbounds-producer.tex:306 ("Every continuous protected trial whose two bounds are uniformly subpower …"). Lean `YM.Push.RelayDifference.RawProtected`, `.clothed`, `.unpriced` (YM/Push/RELAY_DIFFERENCE/RawTop.lean:25–37; definitions read: a finite stencil `X ∋ 0` and functions `c, b` of the cutoffs, both `Slow`, with `a_N^e F` regular on the translated stencil, bounded by `c` in the derivative bounds and by `b` in supremum); `YM.Push.RelayDifference.Slow` (YM/Push/RELAY_DIFFERENCE/Rates.lean:58–59; definition read: for every `ε > 0`, eventually `‖w(N,p)‖ ≤ exp(ε · scale N)`, with `flight` of :40), which is "subpower in `a_N^{-1}`" provided `scale N` is the logarithmic scale `log a_N^{-1}` (the field `scale` of the schedule was not unfolded); `YM.Extraction.Lease.Trial C` (YM/Lane/Lease.lean:17; definition read: a function assigning to each cutoff `N`, period `p` and site of the torus a complex function of the gauge configuration on that torus).
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 11 and 13. It is not *trial with small-field cutoff* and not the "protected change of variables" of chapter 6. v3 never states the hypotheses under this name; it should restore the source's sentence defining the "protected local bounds" where the trial is introduced (11:922–927). Why the source says "protected" is not stated (the Lean docstring of `RawProtected` says only "Raw protection of origin and same literally translated entries on ordered tails"); the bound `b_{N,p}` on all configurations is what controls the trial off the small-field region.
*See also:* protected (sense 2); trial; trial descent.

#### pulled back
*Now:* partly replaced by *composition with the critical configuration* (17t:31, 160; 17c:63, 73) and *pullback by the nonlinear critical-configuration map* (7:1163); remains at 7:1098, 1133, 1164; 17c:52, 66, 82, 92, 209, 305; 7:1096 now defines it.
*Variants:* pullback; linear pullback; exact pulled-back defect; no longer in the text: stationary pullback.
- **Meaning.** Composition of the inherited loop action, or of a function or defect, with the stationary map: "``pulled back'' means composed with the critical-configuration map" (7:1096); "the pullback by the nonlinear critical-configuration map has the same Hessian as this linear pullback" (7:1163–1164). In the display (ch07:inherited) the object is written in words, "`𝓛_{m+1}` pulled back". Chapter 17 gives the operation a symbol, `𝓘F = F(U_stat(V))`, introduced as "composition with the critical configuration" (17t:31). 1:290 and 9:329 use "pullback" in the ordinary sense.
  *Basis:* D (7:1096); R (7:1163–1164; 17t:31). *Where:* 7:1096, 1098, 1133, 1163–1164; 17t:160 ("composition … with the critical configuration"); 17c:52, 66, 82, 92, 209, 305; at 17t:162 the word is dropped ("its order-two term"). *Adopted:* *composition with the critical configuration* (as a function of the coarse field); give the object a symbol; reserve *pull-back* for `𝓘`.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 7 and 17. "Pull-back" also names, in chapters 5–6, the coarse field lifted to the fine lattice, `rep V` ("the pull-back under the parent map", 5:924; 6:185, 450, 496), a different object. In chapter 17 the word also overlaps the words for moving an object through the block steps (transport, transfer, propagation, update, push, descent), for which the one word is *transfer*.
*See also:* stationary substitution; transfer.

#### push
*Now:* partly replaced by *transfer* (11:97, 99, 1677, 1955; 13ba:124, 158, 188) and *image under the block maps* (11:773); remains at 17m:401 ("pushed spectator cross-modes") and, since upstream's merge of 26 November 2026, at 13ba:173 ("Let `𝖯_{h,N}` push densities from scale `N` to scale `h` by successive applications of (ch04:block-operator)") (grep).
*Variants:* pushed (17m:401); push (13ba:173); no longer in the text: pushed polynomial, density; exact push.
- **Meaning.** To apply the block maps coefficientwise: `q_m = 𝓑_m q_{m+1}`; the pushed object is the image ("Transfer the full polynomial `q_k` through them", 11:97; "its exact image under the block maps is `Jq_k`", 11:773).
  *Basis:* R (11:78, 97). *Where:* 11:97, 99, 773, 1677, 1955; 13ba:124, 158, 188; 17m:401. *Adopted:* *image under the block maps*; as a verb, *transfer*.
*Across chapters:* one sense. It was one of seven words for moving an object through the block steps (transport, transfer, pullback, propagation, update, push, descent); the single word is *transfer* ("parallel transport" along a path is a different notion and stays). "Pushed spectator cross-modes" (17m:401) are the coefficients of the joint expansion indexed by sets of insertions that contain the score insertion together with spectators, the spectators having been transferred to the current level; see *cross-modes* (S for "mode", I for the rest).
*See also:* transfer; pulled back.

### Q

#### `Q^pred`
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* `ε_pred`; `r_pred`.
- **Meaning.** The gauge-covariant block average `Q_e^pred(U)` of a coarse edge `e`, with its threshold `ε_pred`: the group element about which the coarse link `V_e` is distributed in the block kernel (`V_e = R_e Q_e^pred`, 4:323–323). The text calls the map `U ↦ Q_e^pred` "the averaging operation" (4:226) and `Q_e^pred` "the value of the averaging operation" (4:218). The superscript abbreviates "predictor", the name of this object in the manuscripts v3 was written from: it is the value that the fine field predicts for the coarse link. In the chapters "predictor" survives only in label names (`ch04:predictor-*`) and in `D_e^pred` (6:508); `notation.md` glosses `Q_e^pred` as "gauge-covariant block average" (source label `eq:I12-predictor`). `r_pred` (6:467, its only occurrence) is the largest coarse distance from a coarse edge to a fine link read by its block average, so that `R_* + 5 + r_pred` bounds the coarse radius of the stencil of a row; since 25 November 2026 the text defines it: "path; here `r_pred` is the largest coarse distance at which the averaging operation reads a link. Its coarse radius is at most `R_*+5+r_pred≤B/50`" (6:467).
  *Basis:* R (4:214–223) for the object; S for the superscript; D for `r_pred` (6:467, since 25 November 2026; before, S). *Where:* 4:214–223, 271, 323, 430–435; 6:467, 508. *Proposed:* *averaging operation*; rename the superscript (e.g. `Q_e^av`, `r_av`), or say once that "pred" stands for "predictor".
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:3`: "The predictor in that kernel averages fine parallel transports in local frames"; `:68` (caption): "the predictor is its nearest point of `G`, and the coarse link `V_e` fluctuates about it with weight `e^{−𝔟β w(V_e Q_e^{-1})}`"; `:100`: "If the minimum in (I12-predictor) is below `ε_pred`, then `Q_e^pred` is the minimizer there … Otherwise a tag `z` selects `Q_e^pred = Y_{e,z}`, with mass `w_z^av`"; `:1051`: "`r_pred` is the maximum coarse distance read by a patch predictor." Lean `YM.RG.Patch.predictorMass`, `YM/RG/Patch.lean` (definition read): the weight of a block-average tag, `1/|𝔹_R|` on the minimising branch and `w^av_r` otherwise; the Lean definition of the predictor itself and of a radius corresponding to `r_pred` were not read.
*Literature:* see *block average*.
*Across chapters:* chapters 4 and 6 only.
*See also:* block average; block-average patch; uniform mass.

#### read-count polynomials
*Now:* replaced on 25 November 2026 by "The polynomial factors `(1+s_M)^{d_j}` in the number of blocks read are absorbed by" (9:148); the phrase no longer occurs.
- **Meaning.** The factors `(1 + s_M)^{d_j}` of 9:100, where `s_M` is the number of blocks of radius `B` needed to cover everything the product reads (its complete dependence supports, retained path lengths included). They are absorbed by exponential decay in the support: `(1 + s_M)^{d_j} ≤ C_{j,η} e^{η s_M}`.
  *Basis:* R (9:148 with 9:100, 108); confirmed by S. *Where:* 9:148. *Adopted:* *the polynomial factors `(1 + s_M)^{d_j}`*. The bound `C_{j,η} e^{η s_M}` was not added, because `C_{j,η}` and `η` are not defined in chapter 9 (`repairs-apply.md`).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:105`: "The integer `s_M` is the sum of the numbers of radius-`B` blocks covering the complete read supports, including retained path lengths in the same units"; `:148` "read-count powers remain in `(1+s_M)^{d_j}`"; `:212` "The read-count polynomial obeys `(1+s_M)^{d_j} ≤ C_{j,η} e^{η s_M}` and is absorbed by a unit of support exponent that the output norm does not use." Martin `existence/high-degree-cluster-prices.tex:98–99`: "The read-count bound is `|I| ≤ (1+S(P)) b_B d_L`". No Lean declaration was sought.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. `s_M` is defined at 9:108: it "counts the full dependence set in radius-`B` blocks"; Scott D:105 also counts retained path lengths.
*See also:* read.

#### reconstruction
*Now:* partly replaced by *Fourier inversion* (sense 3); senses 1, 2 and 4 remain.
*Variants:* field reconstruction; unsymmetrized / symmetric reconstruction; fixed-probe reconstruction; reconstruction identity; reconstruction comparison (all sense 2); relativistic reconstruction; word reconstruction; reconstruction theorem (sense 1); no longer in the text: Fourier reconstruction (sense 3).
1. **Reconstruction of the relativistic theory** from the Euclidean correlation functions.
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 1:415–418, 495–499; 12:406; 14:9, 37; 15:341; 16:2, 22, 83, 319; 17:16, 20; 18:32; 19:94, 106, 132, 166; RG:62. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
2. **Field reconstruction `H_d`; fixed-probe reconstruction `𝒫_D`.** The map that assigns to a word (a cluster of nearby insertions) the field of `F_D` with the same fixed probe coordinates: "For a cluster word `w`, define the unsymmetrized field reconstruction `H_d(w) = Σ_{|α|≤d} b_α(w) u_α`, where `b_α(w)` means replacing the distinguished field in its probe correlations by the entire cluster" (18:69–74); "the degree-`D` reconstruction of a field in `F_t`, `t > D`, is exactly its low-degree component in this fixed biorthogonal system" (18lp:276–278); "Denote the resulting reconstruction of a word by `𝒫_D w`" (18lp:278–279). Chapter 18 distinguishes the unsymmetrized reconstruction `H_d` from the symmetric ones `A_d w = ∫_{O(4)} R_d(K) H_d(K^{-1}w) dK`, `B_d w = ½{A_d w + conj(A_d w̄)}` (18:83–86; "the unsymmetrized and symmetric reconstructions", 18:215). The "reconstruction identity" and "reconstruction comparison" of chapters 18 and 18r are the identity and the comparison for the field reconstruction `H_d(w)`.
  *Basis:* D (18:69–72) for `H_d`; D (18:83–86) for the symmetrised `A_d`, `B_d`; R (18lp:266–279, a prose construction) for `𝒫_D`; R (18r:4–7, 42, 61–62 with 18lp:289, 293) for `𝒫_D = H_D`. *Where:* 18lp:266–279; 18:69, 83, 151, 215, 230, 231; 18r:7, 36. *Proposed:* keep, define once (*projection onto `F_D` along the fixed probes*), with one symbol.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:151–161` (Definition "Finite correlation projection", `def:D31`): one biorthogonal system `ℓ_α`, `u_α`, a reconstruction map `D_j : ℂ^{𝒫_j} → F_j` with `D_j ev_j = id_{F_j}`, and for a word `w` separated from the probes `P_j^raw w = D_j((S(w, B_{j,γ}))_γ)`; `:168` (`def:D32`, "Symmetric projection"). Both v3 passages render this one definition.
3. **Fourier inversion.**
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 5:819; 17m:239 (now "Fourier inversion"). *Adopted:* *Fourier inversion*.
4. **Exact recovery** of a field or a density from its parts ("it reconstructs the original fine field on every retained link support", 6:1384; "Exact reconstruction always uses the full density", 11:613–614; "an exact reconstruction of every stencil value", 11:1831; "It remains to reconstruct the coarse representation", 11R:340). Ordinary.
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 6:1384; 11:613, 1831; 11R:340. *Proposed:* keep (ordinary); *recover*.
*Across chapters:* sense 1 in chapters 1, 12, 14–19; sense 2 in 18lp, 18, 18r; sense 3 (now "Fourier inversion") in chapters 5 and 17m; sense 4 in chapters 6 and 11. For sense 2, 18lp:266–279 is a prose construction without a formula (basis R), while chapter 18 defines `H_d` and its symmetrisations by formulae (18:69–72, 83–86; basis D). `𝒫_D` (18lp) and `H_D` (18) are the same map: both are the low-degree component in a biorthogonal system built by the same successive subtraction (18lp:270–276; 18:54–65), 18lp:293 calls its coordinates `b_α` "the fixed probe coordinates", and the proof 18r:4–7, 29–44, 61–62 obtains the statement for `H_D` from Proposition (ch18:mixed-bound), which is stated for `𝒫_D`. v3 never writes the equality and should use one symbol. Other occurrences, not classified: 3:761 ("reconstructs Wick's rule"); 6:1568 ("Reconstruction of the exact block density"); 7:145 ("preserve the reconstruction").
*See also:* replacement; raw; contact projection.

#### reference label
*Now:* partly replaced by *reference scale* (for "reference level"); "reference label", "reference coefficient", "reference insertion", "reference limit" and "reference coordinates" remain (11:899, 949, 961, 1079; 11E:120, 153; 13:396; 13ba:203, 279; 18gq:86, 107, 113).
*Variants:* reference scale; reference coefficient; reference insertion; reference limit; reference coordinates; no longer in the text: reference level.
- **Meaning.** The reference scale `r(d)` is the fixed scale at which coefficients of degree `d` are normalised ("coefficients normalized at one reference scale", 12:136; "The coefficient at its reference scale is the prescribed label", 12:148). A reference label (coefficient) is the coefficient vector expressed at that scale, as opposed to its coefficient `x_l(v)` after transfer to another scale `l` or to the cutoff ("Let `x_l(v)` be the coefficient of a reference label `v ∈ V_t` after transfer to scale `l`", 18gq:12–13). The map `𝖹_{N,p,d}` "transfers a cutoff coefficient to its fixed reference scale" (11:886–887) and is defined as the composition of the single-insertion coefficient maps from `N` to the reference scale (11:1052–1054); the text calls it "the coefficient map `𝖹`" (11:1141; 11E:183), and the inverse coordinates under it the *cutoff-scale coordinates* (11:888). A reference label may depend on the cutoff (`y_{N,p}`, 18gq:86; "The matched coefficients need not be bounded", 18gq:106–108); a "reference limit" (18gq:113) is a limit of such labels.
  *Basis:* D for the map `𝖹_{N,p,d}` (11:1052–1054); R for the label and the level (11:886–887; 12:148). *Where:* 11:886–888, 949–950, 961, 1052–1055, 1080, 1141; 11E:9, 153, 183; 12:23, 136, 148; 13ba:203, 279; 18gq:12, 86, 107, 113. *Proposed:* *label (coefficient) at the reference scale `r(d)`*; *scale of normalization* for "reference level"; for `𝖹_{N,p,d}`, *coefficient map from the cutoff scale to the reference scale*.
*Across chapters:* one sense. The label is fixed in scale, not independent of the cutoff (text read: 11:884–889, 1050–1055; 12:135–137, 147–149; 18gq:10–15, 112–114). Not *fixed label*: a reference label may depend on the cutoff. "Reference scale" is a particular scale, not a synonym of "scale" (the index of a lattice in the sequence).
*See also:* reference rows; row; trial encoding; terminal map.

#### reflected seminorm directions
*Formerly:* *reflected normalized directions*.
*In the text:* none; the phrase was replaced on 25 November 2026 (sentence repair) by "the normalized affine directions of the activity seminorm, restricted to the microscopic neighborhood", and on 26 November 2026 (from Scott `part2/D-section.tex:417–425`) by "Original small-field logarithmic coordinates and the directions admitted by the activity seminorm (ch04:local-seminorm), restricted to the cube `N_{w̄}` about the localization site and carried to the reflected periodic extension (… the cube `N_r(x)` is used there without a definition), are bounded by a polynomial in `B` times `t_m`" (9s:303–305), with a margin note: all directions of the seminorm are meant, and Scott says the chart requirement on the reflected torus remains under verification. The phrase no longer occurs.
- **Meaning.** The directions in which the activity seminorm takes derivatives (tangent link fields `A` with `|A(e)| ≤ t(1 + dist(e,o))^ϖ`, 4:622–624), restricted to the reflection cube `N_{w̄}(x)` and extended to the auxiliary torus `Λ_i` by the coordinatewise fold `q ↦ z + π_{w+i}(q)` of 9:323–331, with the sign change on reversed links, in the same way as the field `U_{i,z}`. Their size is at most `2t(1 + w̄)^ϖ`, which is the "polynomial in `B` times `t_m`" of 9s:303–305.
  *Basis:* S for "reflected"; R (4:622–624) for the normalisation; R since 25 November 2026 that the reflection is the passage to the reflected periodic extension (9s:304), I that this is the fold of 9:323–331. *Where:* formerly 9s:304. *Adopted in substance:* "the directions admitted by the activity seminorm (ch04:local-seminorm), restricted to the cube `N_{w̄}` about the localization site and carried to the reflected periodic extension" (9s:303–304, 26 November 2026). `N_r(x)` is defined nowhere in v3 (merge-2026-11-26.md).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:425`: "A direction of that definition, restricted to `N_{w̄}(x)` and reflected, is bounded by `2t(1+w̄)^{ϖ_{J_m}}`"; `:417` "Reflected perturbations retain the retracing property." Lean `YM.RG.BudgetPoint.dirBound`, `YM/RG/Masks.lean` (definition read): `∀ e, ‖A e‖ ≤ threshold · (1 + separation e.1 o)^power`, the condition on the directions in `supBounds` (definition read). No Lean form of the fold was sought.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence, now replaced. v3 still does not state the bound `2t(1+w̄)^ϖ`.
*See also:* normalized directions; auxiliary tori.

#### reflection plane
*Formerly:* *seam*.
*In the text:* (of the tiling).
*Variants:* site seams, link seams (source); no longer in the text: seam links; strip seams.
- **Meaning.** A reflection hyperplane of the chessboard tiling: for the tiling of 1:284–289, the hyperplanes `x_a ∈ ℓℤ` through lattice sites ("the planes at multiples of `ℓ`"; "without observables on the reflection planes of the tiling", 1:284). The cells are the sets of sites lying strictly between consecutive planes. The links with at least one endpoint on a plane are now "links meeting a reflection plane"; an observable that depends only on links with both endpoints in the open cell "reads no link meeting a reflection plane" (1:286–287), and this is the support condition under which reflection positivity (Proposition ch01:lattice-rp) applies. "The reflection planes bounding the strips" (1:317) are the two planes bounding a strip of the one-coordinate chessboard argument.
  *Basis:* R (1:284–289, 316–317) for the planes; S for the two kinds and for the precise set of links meeting a plane. *Where:* 1:284, 287, 317, 323. *Adopted:* *reflection planes of the tiling*; *links meeting a reflection plane*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/centered-estimates.tex:32–37`: "All seams have the same kind: put `δ = 1` for link seams and `δ = 0` for site seams. … Its strict chamber consists of the sites whose relative coordinates `r_i` satisfy `0 ≤ r_i < ℓ` for link seams, and `0 < r_i < ℓ` for site seams. Observables are complex, bounded, measurable and gauge invariant, and depend only on links with both endpoints in the indicated strict chamber"; `:56–60`: the reflection at the seam `(p,a)` is `x_a ↦ 2(b_a + ℓ p_a) − δ − x_a`; `:125–126` "no link crossing a seam is introduced". The two kinds are the site and link reflections of 1:242–247; the tiling of 1:284–289 has site seams.
*Across chapters:* in this sense chapter 1 only; "reflection plane" in the ordinary sense, the fixed plane of a reflection, stood before the conversion at 3:313, 13:295 and 14:862. At 1:322–323 ("explicit control of support, reflection planes and divisibility") the three conditions are: support of each observable in the open cell, the kind and position of the reflection planes, and divisibility of the side of the torus by twice the cell length.
*See also:* slot; strip; placement (sense 2).

#### regrading
*Now:* replaced by *automorphism `R_d`* (2e:52, "The automorphism `R_d` is essential").
*Variants:* no longer in the text: regrading `R_d`; triangular regrading.
- **Meaning.** The automorphism `R_d` of the space `V_d` of polynomial labels with `R_d p − p` strictly higher in (factor count, scaling dimension); `R_d = I + T_d` with `T_d` nilpotent (2e:229–233). The source name refers to the grading of `V_d` by the pair (factor count, scaling dimension): a regrading is a linear change of labels that is unipotent with respect to this grading, that is, it adds to each bihomogeneous label only terms of strictly later bidegree. The object is defined in v3 (2e:27–36), and 2e:52 calls it "the automorphism `R_d`".
  *Basis:* R (2e:27–36, 229–233) for the object; S for the name. *Where:* 2e:27–36, 52; also 13:139 (the symbol `R_d` in a formula; "label automorphism" does not occur). *Adopted:* *unipotent (triangular) automorphism `R_d`* (as "the automorphism `R_d`").
  *Source:* Scott `part2/A-section.tex:169`: "Order bidegrees `(w,k)` by the lexicographic order of `(k,w)`. A triangular regrading (a unipotent change of labels) is a complex-linear map on `V_d` whose difference from the identity sends each bihomogeneous polynomial into strictly later bidegrees. There are finitely many bidegrees, so this difference is nilpotent and the map is invertible; the map and its inverse preserve the filtration by minimum factor count."
*Across chapters:* one object; `notation.md` (line 193) calls it "Triangular automorphism of polynomial labels"; 2e:52 says "the automorphism `R_d`", which needs no further explanation.

#### regular
*Now:* unchanged.
1. **The regular term `E_reg` and what is built from the localized terms.** `E_reg` is the term in the exponent of `Z_ord = 𝒞 exp[−βS − 𝓛 − E_reg]` (17m:106–115) built from the localized terms `E_i^reg` of 4:479–480 ("A *localized term* of the regular part of the action consists of a *localization domain* `X_i`, a base point `o_i ∈ X_i`, and a real Borel gauge-invariant function `E_i^reg` local on `X_i`"); "regular norm", "regular error", "regular power gain", "the regular local terms of the differentiated kernel" (17m:193, formerly "regular local insertions"; the local expressions `div_Haar Y − D𝓛[Y]` etc. whose Taylor coefficient is extracted) refer to it. Paired against "large-field" (the dichotomy of 4:479–487, and of the remainders at 11:353, 379–380), not against "small-field" ("small-field score", 17m:112), which is the whole small-field part. At 17w:78 ("The regular and large-field source recurrences") the adjectives name the two norms, regular and normalised large-field, in which the one-step estimates for the coefficients of the source variables are stated; the recurrences are the two weighted step estimates of chapter 11, `z_{j+1} ≤ (α+2) z_j` on the upper part of the window (11:1547–1550, proved at 11:1649, "the upper recurrence") and `z_{j+1} ≤ α z_j + H^{1/2} z_j²` (11.lower-weighted-step) on the lower part (11:1572), each with its large-field bound (11:1575, 1639–1648, 1664–1667); their "strict negative powers" are the bounds `H^{−q}`, `H^{−3/4}`, `H^{−1/2}` they propagate.
  *Basis:* R (17m:106–115, via 4:479–480); S for 17w:78. *Where:* 4:479, 496; 12:33, 70–77; 13ba:151–152; 17m:114, 115, 132, 166, 193, 265, 290, 291, 303, 307; and 17w:78. *Adopted:* *the regular part `E_reg` of the action*, defined once (4:479, 496), its terms being the *localized terms* (see *regular activity*); not *small-field*; at 17w:78 *the step estimates 11:1547–1550 and (11.lower-weighted-step) in the regular and the large-field norm* (17w:78 now says "source recurrences" and cites neither).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:98`: "its source recurrence (`eq:E-source-step`) has total linear loss `M_n^{o(1)}`"; Scott `part2/E-Gaussian-sources.tex:167–171` (`eq:E-source-step`): "let `S_i` majorize the corrected singleton terms, and `P_i` the corrected terms with at least two marks, in the weighted regular norm at mark weight `w_t` … Use the same quantities for the forced norm after division by its positive source normalization, and take the larger values. For `k ≤ i < l` … `S_i ≤ K_j^src S_{i+1} + 𝓜^{1/2} S_{i+1}²`, `P_i ≤ K_j^src P_{i+1} + 𝓜^{1/2}(S_{i+1} + P_{i+1})²`" ("forced" is v3's "large-field"; `𝓜` is v3's `H`, `K_j^src` is v3's `α`).
2. **Non-singular.**
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 17m:221, 227. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
*Literature:* the word has two uses in Bałaban. Sense 1 (`E_reg`, regular activities) agrees with "the regular part of the action" `E_k` (B88b p. 259; see *regular activity*). But in B85a, B85b, B85c, B85d and B87 **regular configuration**, **regularity condition**, **spaces of regular field configurations** `𝔘_k({Ω_j}, α_0)` mean what v3 calls small-field: a bound on plaquette variables (B85b p. 77: "Now we can introduce the following spaces of regular field configurations"; B85d pp. 277–278, `|U(∂p) − 1| < ε_0(L^jη)^2`; B87 p. 254: "regular configurations U, i.e. configurations satisfying bounds |U(∂p) − 1| < ε_0"; B85c p. 396, regularity conditions for the background). B85a also speaks of configurations "on which the averaging operations are regular (e.g., analytic)". So "regular" is supported for sense 1 and is a name clash for configurations (see `Bad_m(U)`). Adopted (23 November 2026): "regular" stays for `E_reg`, *the regular part of the action*, whose terms are *localized terms*; the small-field condition becomes *regularity condition*. The book then has the two uses of "regular" that Bałaban has (regular part of the action; regularity condition, regular configuration), and both must be defined. The clash with "regular activity" is removed, that object being renamed *localized term*.
*Across chapters:* A wider reading of 17w:78, "the whole non-large-field part", is not supported: the sentence pairs "regular" with "large-field", the pairing of sense 1 (4:479–487; 11:353, 379–380), and the source confirms it (regular norm and forced norm). 17w:78 ("The regular and large-field source recurrences", restored after a period in which it cited only (11.lower-weighted-step)) cites no label; the identification rests on the equal form of Scott's (`eq:E-source-step`) and of 11:1572 (`S_i ≤ K S_{i+1} + 𝓜^{1/2} S_{i+1}²` against `z_{j+1} ≤ α z_j + H^{1/2} z_j²`) and on 11:2140 ("The upper and lower recurrences then give incidence and site bounds"). The induction (11.higher-induction) at 11:513, `H_c ≤ C_e{e^{−B/64} H_f + ζ}`, is not the recurrence meant: it carries no power of `H` and concerns only the terms with at least two insertions. Scott's recurrence is stated on the lower part of the window (`k ≤ i < l`); that 17w:78 also covers the upper recurrence 11:1547–1550 is inferred from the plural "recurrences" and from 11:2140. At 17m:161, 166–169 the symbol `E_reg` is reused for an error coefficient. Count in chapters 17–19: 12 (17m 9, 17w 1, 18lp 2).
*See also:* regular activity; regular expression; ordinary; polynomial-source propagation constants.

#### regular activity
*Now:* replaced by *localized term* (sense 1); *polymer activity* (sense 2).
1. **Local term of the small-field action (chapters 4, 9, 12–13, 17).** A triple `(X_i, o_i, E_i^reg)`: "A *localized term* of the regular part of the action consists of a *localization domain* `X_i`, a base point `o_i ∈ X_i`, and a real Borel gauge-invariant function `E_i^reg` local on `X_i`" (4:479–480). It enters the exponent additively; it is not a polymer activity.
  *Basis:* D (4:477–482). *Where:* 4:477–482, 496, 597; 9:133, 869; 12:33, 70–77; 13ba:151–152; ch. 17 through `E_reg`. *Adopted:* *localized term* (of the regular part of the action), on a *localization domain* `X_i`.
2. **Polymer activity of the gas without large-field sites (chapter 8).** The activities `z_γ`: "In addition to the polymer activities `z_γ`, introduce large-field activities `K_η`" (8:288–289). Chapter 9 calls this gas "the polymer gas without large-field sites" (9:151) and its polymers and factors "small-field" (9:154, 173).
  *Basis:* R (8:288–289). *Where:* 8:288, 321, 325, 334, 336. *Adopted:* *polymer activity `z_γ`*; not "regular activity".
*Literature:* **localized terms** `E^{(j)}(X,U)` of the effective action (B87 p. 256: "The functions E^{(j)} are represented as sums of localized terms"; p. 257, (0.24): `E^{(j)}(U) = Σ_{X∈D_j} E^{(j)}(X,U)`, "analytic and gauge invariant functions of U, depending on U restricted to X"); "interaction terms" `𝒫_j(Y_j,U_k)`, "potentials" `V_k(Y,B)` (B88a p. 15); terms `E^{(j)}(X; U_k, z)` of **the regular part of the action** `E_k`, with **localization domain** `X ∈ D_j` and a point `z` (B88b p. 259: "The term `E_k` is the regular part of the action. It has the same properties as the effective action constructed in [I] for the small field approximation, but localized properly", [I] being B87; pp. 259–260, text layer only: "the last sum is over localization domains `X ∈ D_j` contained in `Λ_j`"); **localized functionals** `E_k(X, φ)` (D1 p. 1330010-17: "We will assume the local structure E_k(φ_k) = Σ_X E_k(X, φ_k) where E_k(X, φ_k) only depend on the restriction of φ_k to X"; D2 p. 092301-28: "are the main corrections to the bare action"); "terms of the localization expansion" (B95). Sense 1 is the same object up to the regularity class; it was classified "analogue" against B87, "same object (role)" against D1 and "same up to regularity class" against B88b, and these describe the same differences: the literature's terms are analytic on complex neighbourhoods `U^c_j(X, α_0, α_1)`, labelled by the step `j` that produced them, evaluated on the background `U_j`, one per connected localization domain, with a sup bound `E_0 e^{−κ d_j(X)}`; v3's are real Borel with finitely many derivatives, anchored, with arbitrary supports, summed in a weighted `ℓ¹` norm. The support `X_i` corresponds to the **localization domain** (B87 p. 257: "Such a domain is a union of a connected, finite family of cubes from π_j"). The word "regular" for this part of the action is Bałaban's (B88b p. 259); "activity" is not his word for these terms. Three wordings were suggested, *localized term of the effective action* (B87), *localized functional* (D1), *term of the regular part `E_k` of the effective action* (B88b); they are compatible, and the last is the most specific. Adopted (23 November 2026): *localized term* (of the regular part of the action), on a *localization domain* `X_i` (Bałaban's `E^{(j)}(X)`, B87 (0.24), B88b (2.26)). The differences above are stated at first use: v3's terms are real Borel with finitely many derivatives, anchored, with arbitrary supports, summed in a weighted `ℓ¹` norm.
*Across chapters:* a real change of meaning between chapter 8 and chapters 4 and 9 (text read at 8:287–290). Sense 1 is defined and is used in more chapters; by the decision of 23 November 2026 it is renamed *localized term*, and sense 2 is *polymer activity*, so that "regular activity" is no longer the proposed name of either.
*See also:* regular; ordinary; activity.

#### regular logarithms with holes
*Now:* not applied.
- **Meaning.** Probable reading: the logarithms `𝓛_{Y(B)}(z)` in `Z_D = e^{𝓛(z)} Σ_B (∏ K_η) e^{−𝓛_{Y(B)}(z)}` (8:314–318), that is, the logarithm of the regular polymer gas with the set `Y = Y(B)` deleted. "Hole" does not occur in chapter 8.
  *Basis:* I (11R:366–370 with 8:314–318). *Where:* 11R:366–370. *Proposed:* *the logarithm `𝓛_Y` of the gas with the set `Y` deleted*.
*Literature:* **polymer with holes**; **cluster expansion with holes**: the holes are the large field region `Λ_k^c`, in which decay is not required, with weight `d_M(X, mod Ω_k^c)` (D2 p. 092301-19: "A variation is a polymer with holes … The idea is that decay in these regions (holes) will be taken care of elsewhere"; p. 092301-83, App. F: "a special version of the cluster expansion in which there are holes for the large field region"). An analogue of `𝓛_Y(z)`: in both the hole is the large-field set removed from the small-field expansion; Dimock's hole lies inside a polymer, v3's is a deletion from the gas. This explains the word, which does not occur in v3 chapter 8. For the identity in which these logarithms occur see *exact reassembly*. Suggested: keep the formula-based rendering; cite D2 App. F as the source of "holes".
*Across chapters:* one occurrence (with "the regular logarithm" at 11R:352); "regular" here is the chapter 8 sense of *regular activity* (sense 2), which chapter 8 now calls the polymer activities `z_γ` (8:288), so chapter 8 no longer says "regular" for this gas.
*See also:* raised hole correction; regular activity.

#### regularity-stage index `J_m`
*Now:* replaced by *stage `J_m` in force at scale `m`* (4:694).
*Variants:* `J(m)`; `J_i = J(i+1)`; stage index (4:694).
- **Meaning.** A stage `j ≥ 1` "specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds" (10:25–29). `J(m) = j` for `A_j ≤ m < A_{j+1}`, with `k_j = c_j + 2A_j + 1`, `A_{j+1} = A_j + b_{j+1} + 2k_j + 1` (10:130–135): a nondecreasing map from levels to stages. "`J(m+1)` is the stage used for this step" (10:51); `L_m = 𝓛_{J(m+1)}` (10:145); "`J(m)` is the stage at scale `m`" (10:811); "so `L_i = 𝓛_{J_i}` with `J_i = J(i+1)` in the scale convention of Chapter 10" (17w:15–16). In chapters 4–6 it appears only at 4:694: "`q, ϖ, σ` may depend on the *stage* `J_m` in force at scale `m` (a stage specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds; see Section (ch10:choices)); the stage index is different from the scale index `m`" (4:694–695).
  *Basis:* D (10:25–31, 130–135). *Where:* 4:694; 9:30–36, 111, 423 (subscript `j`, "stage"); 10:25–31, 51, 130–135, 145, 811; 13sb:28, 58; 13ba:266; 17w:15–16. *Adopted:* *stage `J(m)` in force at scale `m`*; "stage `j`" is kept, for the stages of 10:25 only (never for a scale index `m` or for a step).
*Across chapters:* one sense; chapter 10 defines it, and 4:694 glosses it with a forward reference to Section (ch10:choices). Caution: the letter `j` is the smoothing order in chapters 4, 5 and 7 (4:16; 7:609; `C_j` at 7:673; inferred for chapter 7 throughout) and the stage in chapters 9–10, where 10:125 writes `ȷ_j` for the smoothing order used in stage `j`. Not *regularity level*: it collides with "level `m`".
*See also:* stage; request.

#### relaxed
*Now:* unchanged; the phrase "relaxed small-field condition" (or "test") is now *relaxed regularity condition*, defined at 4:533.
*Variants:* relaxed regularity condition; `χ^rel`, `R^rel`; no longer in the text: relaxed small-field condition; relaxed small-field test.
- **Meaning.** The regularity condition with the exponentially weighted threshold `t_m e^{dist/R^rel}`, and its indicator `χ^rel` (4:527–531): "We call the condition in (ch04:relaxed-test) the *relaxed regularity condition* at `x`: the regularity condition on the whole lattice, with `t_m` replaced by the threshold `t_m e^{dist(x,y)/R^rel}` growing exponentially with the distance from `x`" (4:533). The first use after chapter 4 is "the indicator of the relaxed regularity condition (ch04:relaxed-test)" (6:111–112).
  *Basis:* D (4:527–533). *Where:* 4:527–533; 6:111–112, 236, 1423; 9:550, 842, 855, 864, 891; 10:98; 11R:105; 13ba:36–40 ("the small-field indicator"), 220. *Proposed:* *exponentially weighted regularity condition*.
  *Source:* for 10:98 and 13ba:36–37: Scott `part2/E-bounded-real.tex:14–17`: "the bounded coarse polynomial with coordinate `v` is `𝖵_h(v;U) = a_h^{-d}(v_0 + 𝟙_{Σ_d healthy} P_d[t_h^{-#} v°](U))`. … Its inspected stencil has a fixed radius, including the links needed for the relaxed threshold test"; Scott `part1/notation-index.tex:98`: "`clip_t`, `χ^rel_{m,x}` clip, relaxed threshold test". Git history of `chapters/10-common-trajectory.tex` and `chapters/13-bounded-approximations.tex`, commit `4ebb64ea` (diff read): "relaxed small-field guard" → "relaxed small-field smooth cutoff"; "the local guard" → "the local smooth cutoff"; "The guarded nonconstant part" → "The nonconstant part multiplied by the smooth cutoff".
*Across chapters:* one sense. At 10:98 ("On that chart the indicator of the relaxed regularity condition is one") and 13ba:36–37 ("the small-field indicator is identically one on the small-field chart") the factor is named as an indicator. It is the indicator in the bounded coarse trial, `V_h(v;U) = a_h^{-d}(v_0 + 𝟙_{small-field stencil} P_d^{loc}[S_{1/t_h} v°](U))` (13ba:216–220), whose stencil "includes the links needed by the relaxed regularity condition" (13ba:222–223). So there is no conflict with 4:527–531: the factor is an indicator, equal to one on the small-field chart. The `notation.md` remark "not a smooth cutoff" is said of `clip`, not of `χ^rel`.
*See also:* clip; plaquette whose relaxed small-field condition is not automatic.

#### remainder
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* regular remainder; large-field remainder; vanishing-jet remainder; full remainder (12:67, 116); small-field remainder (11:441, 943); remainder with insertions (12:67; 17m:176); remainder array; remainder map; no longer in the text: complete remainder; ordinary remainder; marked remainder.
1. **The part of a term with one insertion that is not its local polynomial part (chapters 11, 12, 18lp).** A term with one insertion is described by a coefficient vector `x ∈ V_d` of a label and a remainder; the remainders are of two classes, regular (with zero extracted polynomial, hence "vanishing-jet") and large-field: "the regular and large-field remainders" (11:353); "an incoming linear graph of regular vanishing-jet and large-field remainders, with norm at most `s_f` per coefficient" (11:379–380). They form the normed space `𝓡_m` in which an admissible graph `G : V_d → 𝓡_m` takes its values (12:82–83). "Full" means both classes together: "the full regular and large-field remainder on common supports" (12:116–117; section title "Contraction of the full remainder with insertions", 12:67).
   *Basis:* R (11:353, 379–382; 12:82–83, 116–117); I that the remainder is what is left after extraction of the local polynomial (cf. 11:1187; 18lp:27–40). *Where:* 11:353, 379–382, 447, 943, 1187, 1496; 12:37–39, 67, 82–95, 116; 18lp:27, 36, 40, 114, 115. *Proposed:* keep *remainder*, saying each time which class is meant (*regular remainder*, *large-field remainder*, or both).
2. **Named remainders of other chapters.** Each has its own entry: the "cutoff remainder" of chapter 6 (6:840–849); the "equation remainder" `(x_u − Π_u x_u)/(1 + ‖Π_u x_u‖)` (13:197–205; 18gq:111); the "Haar remainder" (9:128), see *Haar logarithm*; "the nonlinear remainder of the component" (6:988), see *base*; "the remainder with insertions" (17m:176), named only.
   *Basis:* as in those entries. *Where:* 6:745, 840–849, 988; 9:125–134; 13:197–205; 17m:176; 18gq:111. *Proposed:* as in those entries.
*Literature:* for sense 1 and for the regular remainder with vanishing extracted polynomial: a **normalized** functional, `E(X,0) = 0`, `E_2(X,0;1,1) = 0`, `E_2(X,0;1,x_μ) = 0`, required for small polymers, space `K_k^norm` (D1 p. 1330010-22, (134)–(136)); **irrelevant** terms, against "relevant and marginal expressions" (B95 p. 119; B87 p. 259). The same object in role. Dimock's **tiny remainder** `R_{k,Π}`, bounded by `λ_k^{n_0}` (D2 p. 092301-28; "Removal of tiny terms", Lemma 3.20, p. 092301-65), is another object. Suggested: *normalized (irrelevant) part*.
*Across chapters:* sense 1 is one notion in chapters 11, 12 and 18lp. "Remainder" is not a synonym of "nonprincipal" or "nonleading" (the note's cluster "its complement: nonprincipal; nonleading; remainder" is not kept): by 11:285–291 the factors fall into three classes, those that prescribe large-field sites (`t_C = m`), the nonprincipal ones without prescribed sites (`t_C = l`) and the purely principal ones (`t_C = 1`), and the large-field remainders belong to the first (text read at 11:285–291, 351–353, 376–382; 12:80–84, 114–117). The "remainder map" is `R_G` (11:381–382) or `J_G` (12:90–92), not the graph `G`. The word occurs on about 110 lines of the chapter files (by grep); occurrences other than those listed are not classified in the old note, which has no row for the bare word.
*See also:* graph; linear graph; principal; complete; ordinary; vanishing-jet remainder; remainder with vanishing extracted coefficient; unreparametrized remainder map; cutoff remainder; equation remainder; Haar logarithm; base.

#### remainder with vanishing extracted coefficient
*Now:* unchanged; the words are reordered, and on 25 November 2026 "norm" became "norm at most" and "size" became "norm at most": "a remainder of norm at most `r_l` whose extracted coefficient vanishes" (18lp:27), "a remainder of norm at most `q` with vanishing extracted coefficient" (18lp:36).
- **Meaning.** The remainder part of a local density with insertions in the decomposition "column coefficient plus remainder" of chapter 11: "A local degree-`t` density with insertions consists of a column coefficient `x_l` and a remainder of norm at most `r_l` whose extracted coefficient vanishes … These conventions are those of Section `ch11:one-graph`" (18lp:26–31). It is the sum of a regular part whose extracted local polynomial is zero, that is, whose radial Taylor polynomial through degree `t` vanishes (18lp:38; "all regular remainders have zero extracted polynomial", 11:1187), and a large-field part, which has no Taylor characterisation and is measured with the factor `κ^{−1}`, the inverse square root of the large-field bound ("the large-field term retains half the suppression of its original prescribed large-field set", 18lp:39–40; the norm at 11:360–366; "normalization by the square root of the large-field bound in this remainder norm", 18lp:31–32).
  *Basis:* R (18lp:26–40 with 11:360–366, 379–380). *Where:* 18lp:27, 36, 40, 114, 115. *Proposed:* *remainder* in the sense of Section `ch11:one-graph`, defined once there (*regular term with vanishing Taylor polynomial of degree `t`, plus large-field term*); for the regular part alone, *term with vanishing Taylor polynomial of degree `t`*.
*Literature:* see *remainder*.
*Across chapters:* the same object as the "regular vanishing-jet and large-field remainders" of 11:379–380; 18lp:30–31 identifies the two by referring its conventions to Section `ch11:one-graph`. The phrase "with vanishing extracted coefficient" is accurate for the regular part only; for the whole remainder it means that the column coefficient has been separated off.
*See also:* recentering (sense 2); residual; vanishing-jet remainder.

#### remote
*Now:* replaced by *far from the large-field set* in sense 1 ("far from the location of `A`", "far from `A`" in chapter 6; 11R:267 "the bounds for the corresponding action terms far from the large-field set"); remains at 3:873 (sense 2).

Also "nonlinear action remainders far from `A`" (6:1255); "a large fluctuation-field event far from the index triple" (9:281); "for event indicators far from the large-field set" (11:709); "the bounds for the corresponding action terms far from the large-field set" (11R:267).
  *Basis:* R (6:956–957 with 6:1015). *Where:* 6:1015, 1255, 1257; 9:281; 11:709; 11R:267 (all "far from …"). *Adopted:* *far from the large-field set* (at distance greater than `30B`).
2. **At a fixed distance.** "Remote spectators" (3:873): spectators kept at a fixed distance from the insertions.

#### replica
*Now:* partly replaced by *pull-back* (chapters 5–6: "their pull-back under the parent map is `(rep V)_e = …`", 5:924; "the pull-back `rep V` of the coarse field", 6:185); remains at 11:180, 196, 345, 1474; 13ba:53, in "replica cell(s)", the unrelated chessboard use (18lp:91 now says "reflected cells").
*Variants:* `rep V`; no longer in the text: replicated field.
- **Meaning.** The fine field `rep V` equal to `1` on links inside blocks and to `V` on links between blocks (5:924–933): the pull-back of the coarse field `V` under the block projection, which the text calls the parent map.
  *Basis:* D (5:924–933). *Where:* 5:924–933; 6:185, 346 ff., 1382. *Adopted:* *pull-back of `V` under the block projection* (as "pull-back under the parent map"; not "block-constant extension", which 5:1147 uses for something else).
*Literature:* no name; the configuration `V_0` with `V_{0,b} = V_{b'}` for `b ∈ B(b')` and `V_{0,b} = 1` on the remaining bonds (B85d p. 279: "For example we can take `V_{0,b} = V_{b'}` for `b ∈ B(b')`, `b' ∈ Λ_k` and `V_{0,b} = 1` for remaining bonds of `B(Λ_k)`"). The same formula as `rep V`, with a different use: the start of an induction over `k`, not the centre of a coordinate chart. In the linear scalar setting the analogue is the transpose `Q^T` of the average (D1 p. 1330010-5: "Q^TQ is a projection operator onto the range of Q^T which is functions constant on the cubes"). "Replica" is not supported by any paper read; the dictionary's proposal stands.
*Across chapters:* this sense in chapters 5–6 only. From chapter 10 on, "replica" (in "replica cell") and "replication" refer to the reflected copies of the chessboard estimate, an unrelated use (see *reflected replica cell*, *replicate*).
*See also:* reflected replica cell; replica census; replicate; parent.

#### replica census
*Now:* replaced on 25 November 2026 by *finite set of reflected copies* (15:263) and *set of cells* (13ba:173); since upstream's merge of 26 November 2026 neither phrase is in the text: 15:262–263 read "there are still only two insertions per cell, however many copies are used", and 13ba:176 reads "Let `𝓘` index the cells of the reflected tiling" (grep).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: cell census `𝓘`.
- **Meaning.** A census is a finite set of markers together with a family of allowed subsets of it that contains the empty set and all singletons and is closed under passing to subsets; the full census allows all subsets. In a replica census the markers are the reflected copies (one marker per copy). Until upstream's merge of 26 November 2026 the text said "the two-insertion estimate is used for an arbitrary finite set of reflected copies, not rerun with arity `2j`"; it now says "there are still only two insertions per cell, however many copies are used" (15:262–263): the estimate with at most two insertions per cell is applied for an arbitrary finite set of reflected copies; "only the lower bounds on the cutoff and on the translations depend on that fixed number" (15:264–265). At 13ba:176 `𝓘` indexes the cells of the reflected tiling.
  *Basis:* R for the index set (13ba:173); S for "census"; I that 15:263 uses the word in the sense of the sources. *Where:* 13ba:173; 15:263. *Adopted:* *for any finite set of reflected copies* (15:263); *set of cells `𝓘`* (13ba:173).
  *Source:* Martin existence/centered-birth-receipt.tex:5: "Let `𝒱` be a finite marker set and let `𝖡` be a downward-closed family of allowed subsets containing the empty set and all singletons. Its elements are the census modes."; existence/actual-marked-portfolio-calibration.tex:849: "`U_j` is the `j`th translated/reflected census copy". Lean `YM.Marker.Census`, YM/Marker/Console.lean (definition read: `choices : Finset (Finset V)` with `∅ ∈ choices`, `{i} ∈ choices`, and closed under subsets); `YM.Stock.census`, YM/Overlay/Terminal.lean (definition read: all subsets of a finite `V`).
*Across chapters:* chapters 13ba and 15. "Replica cells" (13ba:53) and "reflected cells" (18lp:91) are the cells themselves; see *reflected replica cell*.
*See also:* reflected replica cell; uniform in the number of reflected copies; cell census.

#### replicate
*Now:* replaced by *place a copy in each reflected cell*.
- **Meaning.** As a verb: place one copy of an observable in each cell of a reflected tiling and consider the product of the copies. At 13ba:287 ("Place a copy of the discrepancy in each reflected cell before applying the kernel") this forms the product of the copies over the reflected cells (13ba:273–275, 287–286: "the resulting residual" is "the product of the pullback discrepancies"); no estimate is applied in that sentence. At 17m:429 ("Place a copy in each reflected cell at the first backward crossing of `B_n²`") the tiling is the one at the scale `m < n` with `B_n² ≤ a_m/a_n ≤ L_*B_n²`, and the product is then bounded by the estimate `(11.replicated-bound)` (11:806–814, cited at 17m:430–431), whose root over the cells is `(11.root-bound)`: "A reflected tiling at scale `a_m`, stopped at `a_k`, has `(a_m/a_k)⁴` sites per cell. Taking the number-of-cells root …" (11:817–822); the cost `L_*⁴B_n⁸q_n + 6` of 17m:433 is `(a_m/a_n)⁴ q_n + 6` per cell.
  *Basis:* R for the estimate (11:806–822; 17m:429–433); S for the verb. *Where:* 13ba:287; 17m:429. *Adopted:* *place a copy in each reflected cell*; at 17m:429 *apply (11.replicated-bound) with the reflected tiling at the first scale `m < n` with `a_m/a_n ≥ B_n²`*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/E-several-mark.tex:188–195`: "A stopping pair is a pair of levels `ref(d) ≤ m ≤ k` with `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k`. Lemma [Replicated source bound] (`lem:E-replication`): There are mark weights `w_k > 0`, independent of `p`, such that, for each stopping pair, … `w_k^{|𝒞_m^tile|} |⟨∏_{C∈𝒞_m^tile} (O(c))_C⟩_{N,p}| ≤ e^{|Λ_{n_{p,k}}| q_k + 6|𝒞_m^tile|}`": the expectation of the product of one copy of the observable in every cell `C` of the tiling at level `m`, evaluated at level `k`.
*Across chapters:* one sense. `B_n` at 17m:429–435 is the chapter 4 support radius `⌈(log β̂_n)²⌉` (4:457), not the restarted radius (see *restart*). In chapter 11 the verb occurs only in the labels `ch11:replicated` (11:780) and `ch11:replicated-bound` (11:814); v3 should say once, at 11:781, that the "`n` copies" are the copies of the insertion in the cells of a reflected tiling.
*See also:* reflected replica cell; replication costs; root estimate; first crossing.

#### representative
*Now:* unchanged.
*Also in the text for:* the former *lift* (see those entries).
1. **Gauge representative.** A choice within a gauge class: of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration ("The smooth representative of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration is `W_a` …; its representative in the block axial gauge is `W_F`", 7:583; "The smooth representative `W_a` and the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge", 5:1161; "the smooth representative `W = W_a`", 17c:54, and 17c:113; "the forest representative `W_F`", 17c:50); of the critical configuration ("the representative of its critical configuration", 7:513); of a quotient solution (7:939); "squared curvature representative" (6:1412); "plaquette and contour-variable representative" (17m:32). For the linearization the representatives are three operators differing by fine gradients: the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge (5:1161; 9s:193–195), which is the derivative of the critical-configuration map in the block axial chart (5:1157–1160); the smooth representative `W_a = W_s − d_{0,f}ERW_s` (5:1118); and `W_s`, "the operator `W` built with the linear averaging operator `M`" (5:1094).
  *Basis:* R (5:1157–1161; 7:583; 9s:193–195). *Where:* 5:1161; 6:1412; 7:513, 583, 588, 893, 939, 966; 9s:194–196; 10:320; 11:1223, 1353; 13sb:174; 17c:50, 54, 113; 17m:32. *Proposed:* keep (standard), always saying of what and in which gauge.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:473` "Write `W_ax v = (v, Dψ(0)v)` for the axial tangent, and retain `W_0` for the smooth free interpolation before axial gauge. They are distinct coordinate representatives"; `B-section.tex:529` "the centred tangent `(W_s v, 0)` … The joint gauge transformation with parameter `I_ℓ(𝓕_m W_s v)` changes this pair to `(W_r v, 0)` … the tree projections of the two fine fields alone need not coincide". Lean `YM.Precision.extracted`, `YM/PREC/TreeMatch.lean` (definition read) for the forest representative; `YM.Stationary.soldier_known`, `YM/Next/STATIONARY/Joint/Regulator.lean` (statement read): the regauged germ `soldier` has derivative `(uniformM W).prod 0`, that is tangent `(W v, 0)` with zero coarse-frame component, the centred representative. The correspondence of `extracted S F W_s` with `W_F` is by agreement of formulas (see *actual stationary tangent*, sense 2).
2. **Representative point of a group of marks.** "A group is a set of these insertion points with a common representative" (18lp:71–72).
  *Basis:* D (18lp:71–72). *Where:* 18lp:72, 79, 93–95. *Proposed:* keep.
3. **"Protected local representative".** A finite difference written as an insertion of one degree higher, `a_N^{d+1} Δ_α O(x) = a_N^d O(x + a_N e_α) − a_N^d O(x)` (11:1068–1073): the right side is a trial of degree `d+1` on a fixed stencil that represents the same lattice function. "Protected" is the word of *protected trial*: the trial satisfies the two bounds growing slower than every power of `a_N^{-1}`, one for its derivatives on small-field configurations and one for its supremum on all configurations. At 11:2311 the text now says "a trial at degree `e = d+|l|` satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)" instead of "protected trial".
  *Basis:* R for the formula (11:1068–1073); S for "protected". *Where:* 11:1068, 2311. *Proposed:* *the finite-difference expression (11:1068–1073), a trial with filtration index `d+1` and subpower bounds*.
  *Source:* see *protected trial* (Martin `existence/actual-insertion-derivative-relay.tex:24–35`, "We call these the protected bounds"; "protected local bounds" at `:40`).
*Across chapters:* the word distinguishes the gauge representatives `W_a`, `W_F` (and `W_s`) of one linearization; it is not a name for the operator `W` (7:583, 588, 893, 939). Of the three, `W_F` is the derivative of the critical-configuration map (17c:49–51); `W_a` and `W_s` are representatives chosen for their bounds. `W_F` is called "the representative in the block axial gauge" at 5:1161, 1246; 6:954; 7:583; 9s:194; 11:642, and "the forest representative" at 17c:50. `notation.md` (line 242) now distinguishes "the straight-average `W_s`, the smooth representative `W_a = W_s − d_f E R W_s`, and the forest-coordinate `W_F`", in agreement with the text; its earlier wording "the actual forest-coordinate response `W_a`" is gone. Sense 3 is not a gauge representative.
*See also:* response (sense 4); stationary tangent; lift; protected trial.

#### request
*Now:* partly replaced by *requirement on the schedule* (sense 1 in chapter 10: 10:67, 69, 75) and by *prescribed* for "requested" (6:1562; 10:192, 748; 17m:88, 285; 18:146); "requested" stands again at 10:123 (since the merge of 26 November 2026 upstream's "a requested number of consecutive scales at stage `j`", before "a requested length for a stage plateau"; a minimum length, which "prescribed" would read as the exact length); remains on 29 lines in chapters 11, 11E, 11R, 13, 13ba, 14, 14lc, 15, 17, 17w, 18lp (all three senses).
*Variants:* numerical, finite, degree, derivative, compact-set, comparison, admissible request ("arity request" no longer in the text since 26 November 2026); lower-scale request; requested (power, derivative, difference); no longer in the text: window request; threshold request; lower-level request; requested window.
1. **Condition on the schedule.** A finite numerical requirement that a later argument adds to the choice of the stage constants: "Future applications may prescribe countably many finite numerical requirements on the schedule, provided their analytic estimates have already been established for a fixed stage. At stage `j` take the maximum of the first `j` such requirements" (10:66–69); "countably many finite degree requests to the single schedule of lower bounds on the reference coupling" (13ba:100–101); "Make all finite requests before choosing the stage orders" (11:2089). "Requested" is "prescribed": "through the prescribed derivative order" (6:1562); "the fixed requested finite power" (11R:297).
  *Basis:* R (10:66–69). *Where:* 6:1562 ("prescribed"); 10:67, 69, 75 ("requirement"), 123 ("requested"), 189, 745 ("prescribed"); 11:356, 1640, 1782, 2089, 2095, 2213; 11R:297 ("requested"); 11E:13, 30; 13ba:100; 18lp:103, 151. *Proposed:* *requirement on the schedule*; *prescribed (order, power)* for "requested".
  *Source:* Martin existence/common-scale-selection.tex:141–159 (subsubsection "Countably many requests on that same sequence": "Let `F_{n,i} ∈ ℝ` be a countable family of numerical requests selected before constructing the sequence. Define `E_j = 1 + Σ_{n≤j} Σ_{i≤j} |F_{n,i}|`. Include `exp(exp E_j)` in `d_j` before choosing `β_*` … `|F_{n,i}| ≤ E_{J(m+1)} ≤ 1 + log log β̂_m`"): a request is a real number, fixed in advance, which the stage constants are made to dominate from some stage on.
2. **Finite set of data.** A fixed finite tuple (number of insertions, degrees, derivative order, compact set of configurations, error) for which constants or thresholds are then chosen: "Fix `n ≥ 1`, finitely many real polynomial labels of bounded degree, and a compact set of point configurations … The selected stage requirements can be imposed for this finite request" (11:2057–2062); "All constants … are chosen for this one finite request" (14lc:9); formerly "Fix a finite degree, arity and derivative request" (17w:10; the line now reads "Fix the maximum scaling dimension of the insertions, their number, and"); in the same wording "Fix the finite degree and derivative requests and the comparison window" (11R:218), continued by "for the fixed requests" (11R:242).
  *Basis:* R (11:2057–2062; 14:229–232). *Where:* 11:2062; 11R:218, 242; 14:229, 230, 232; 14lc:9, 81, 110; 17:140; 17w:10, 14, 73, 85; 17m:88, 285 ("prescribed"), 142 ("finite derivative orders and degrees"); 18:146 ("prescribed"). *Proposed:* *fixed finite data `(n, D, K, ε)`*; *for the given orders*.
3. **Prescribed lower bound on a scale.** "a requested lower scale" (13:98–99); "the lower-scale request" (13ba:340; 15:209).
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 13:98; 13ba:340; 15:209. *Proposed:* *lower bound on the scale*.
*Across chapters:* three uses of one scheduling word, never defined in v3; the source defines the first (a countable family of real numbers `F_{n,i}`, fixed before the schedule and built into the stage constants), which is the content of 10:66–69. 11:2062 is the data of sense 2, not a condition of sense 1 (text read: 10:65–70; 11:2057–2063); 11R:218, 242 are the data of sense 2 as well, by their wording (that of 17w:10). With 10:66–69, 11:2057–2062 and 14:229–232 the basis is R also in chapters 17–19, whose uses are sense 2. "Compact set" at 17:140 (formerly "compact-set request") is the compact set of separated configurations of 14:230–231 ("the number of insertions, degree, compact sets and errors"; "arity" until 26 November 2026).
*See also:* regularity-stage index `J_m`; stage; schedule; diagonalize.
