#### rescaled interacting fields
*Formerly:* *moving comparison fields*.
*In the text:* (3:576: "quantitative convergence of the rescaled interacting fields to free fields").
- **Meaning.** Local fields whose label depends on the scale (or cutoff) index and converges, in the finite-dimensional space of field labels, to a fixed free-field label; the "quantitative estimates" are the convergence of the correlations of these varying labels to the free correlations of the limit label. At 3:575–576 the fields are the rescaled, pulled-back interacting trace fields `a_i = U_i^{-1}(B_i r_i^4 Θ)`, which converge to `4 d_2 O`, a multiple of the free curvature square. The phrase occurred once in the book and was not defined there; it is sense 1 of *moving*.
  *Basis:* S; ? for the v3 text (3:576). *Where:* 3:576. *Adopted:* *scale-dependent fields converging to free fields*; for the sentence, "quantitative convergence of the rescaled interacting fields to their free limits".
  *Source:* Martin `existence/trace-asymptotic.tex:192–195` (`eq:trace-moving-label`): "the selected centered trace `Θ` has the same limit `a_i := U_i^{-1}(B_i r_i^4 Θ) → 4 d_2 O`"; Martin `existence/trace-scribe-producer.tex:1456–1459`: "At two separated points, the moving-label correlation comparison and (trace-reference-normalization) consequently give the coefficient `S_0(−O,−O) = 3 dim 𝔤/π^4` at unit separation." Lean `YM.OPE.Cards.variation`, `YM/OPE/Cards/Pressure.lean` (statement read): labels `w : ℕ×ℕ → C.book.Vector d` converging componentwise to `p` along a filter finer than the extraction filter have correlations converging to the limit value at `p`. This is the general mechanism; the Lean statement for the particular trace label `a_i` was not located, so the correspondence with 3:576 is partial.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. It announces the comparison carried out for the trace in the later chapters (the "convergent sequences of free fields" of 14:243, 255 and 17:97). 3:576 now says "the rescaled interacting fields" but still not which fields; Martin's "the selected centered trace `Θ` has the same limit", with its formula, would say so.
*See also:* moving.

#### reserve
*Now:* partly replaced by *margin* ("strict width margin", "margin in the support exponent"); *keep aside* for the verb; *one additional derivative (order)*; remains at 9:34; 10:112, 429, 494, 532, 679, 763, 816; 11E:103, 116 (including "reserved band", "attachment reserves", "reserved mass").
*Variants:* reserved; numerical reserve (10:429); attachment reserve (10:763); reserved band (10:532, 679); reserved mass (11E:103, 116); no longer in the text: width, support, derivative, energy, weight, exponent reserve; reserved fraction, factor; "reserve four units".
- **Meaning.** A strict margin in an exponent, a width, a decay rate or a derivative order, left unused by one estimate and used by a later one; as a verb, to set aside part of a decaying factor ("Keep `e^{−u}` aside per selected site factor", 11R:171). The word is never defined. The one precise instance is the width margin: if `Σ_γ |c_N(γ)| e^{w'ℓ(γ)} ≤ C` with `w' > w`, the tails at width `w` and length greater than `r` are bounded by `C e^{−(w'−w) r}` ("a useful precise version of the strict width margin", 10:378–384); "common bound at width `w > v` … A strict width margin" (12:48, 62). A derivative reserve is one or more derivative orders beyond the order of the output norm ("through one order beyond the outgoing order. This is one additional derivative order for the integration kernels", 10:740–742; "one additional derivative" in chapter 17, 17m:103, 282). A support(-weight) reserve is the extra `δ > 0` in a bound `‖z‖_{α+δ} ≤ γ_0` (8:147–152; "a margin in the support exponent", 8:151).
  *Basis:* R (10:378–384; 10:740–742; 12:48, 62); I for the uses not tied to a displayed inequality. *Where:* 8:151–152, 365; 9:34, 440, 921; 10:37, 112, 378, 429, 494, 532, 597, 679, 741, 763, 816; 11:170, 227, 507, 521, 528, 940, 1602; 11R:9, 171, 181; 11E:103, 116; 12:62, 127, 279, 283; 13ba:78, 144, 148, 153; 18lp:177; 17w:84; 17m:49, 103, 198, 282 (the word itself now only at 9:34; 10:112, 429, 494, 532, 679, 763, 816; 11E:103, 116). *Proposed:* *strict margin*, printing the inequality (*a strict margin `w' − w > 0`*; *one additional derivative*; *a strictly smaller rate*; *we keep four units of the exponent*).
*Literature:* no noun; the **improved bounds**, larger analyticity spaces and decay `(1+4β)κ` kept after `T` to be used in `R` (B88b p. 262: "the newly created expressions … are defined on slightly larger spaces, with the coefficients in their definition bigger by `β` multiplied by a corresponding number, and they have better decay properties, with the number `κ` replaced, for example, by `(1+4β)κ`. Such improved bounds are needed for the R-operation"); the splitting `exp(−κd) = exp(−δκd)·exp(−(1−δ)κd)` (B88a pp. 16, 18). An analogue: the same device. No noun was found in B87, B88a, B85e or D1–D3. Suggested: *strict margin* stands; no literature noun.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout. 11:495 has no "reserve" (it reads "Retain two cover units …"). "Room" (13ba:197) is geometric and is not slack in an estimate (see *room*). `excess` and `loss` are not synonyms of "reserve": they are what the margin absorbs. "Margin" is now the word for this sense in chapters 8–18; in chapter 11 the uses of "margin" at 11:2344, 2356 are spatial. The reading of 9:34 ("derivative reserves") through 10:740–742 is inferred.
*See also:* room; retain; margin; width; cost.

#### reset
*Now:* replaced by *coupling constant renormalization* (and *vacuum energy renormalization* for the constant per site); the word survives only in `C_reset` (9:599, 601), in labels, and, since 26 November 2026, in the margin note at 10:629, which cites the source's symbol `c^reset` (grep).
*Variants:* `C_reset`; scalar reset, coupling reset (sources); no longer in the text: the reset.
- **Meaning.** The replacement, at the end of one step, of the input inverse coupling `β′` and of the constant per site by their output values: "The output inverse coupling and the constant per site are now fixed by the coupling constant renormalization and the vacuum energy renormalization: `β = β′ + α + Δ`, `v_sc = τ − |Λ|^{−1} Σ f_i(1)`" (9:719–723, equation `ch09:reset`); "the increment of the inverse coupling is the coefficient `α` fixed by the matching plus the coefficient `Δ` of the local quadratic subtraction" (9:725). "There is a second, intrinsic way to identify the coefficient `Δ`" (9:750) names `Δ` alone: the exact density identity, evaluated at one small-field configuration `U_*` with `𝒦(U_*) > 0`, determines `Δ` as the unique zero of the affine function `f(d)` (9:751–764). `C_reset` (9:599–601) is the constant in the regular bound for the terms produced by the local subtraction that precedes the reset. Chapter 10 now calls `q_m` "the coefficient `Δ` of the coupling constant renormalization of the step" (10:424–425, with `q_m = β_m − β_{m+1} − α_{N,m}` = `Δ`, 10:422; since 25 November 2026), but still uses the name for `Δ` or for the map from the input data to it at 10:449, 654 ("The coupling constant renormalization is linear on finite parameter evaluations"), 772, 842–843, 902; also 13sb:26.
  *Basis:* D (9:719–723); R (9:725, 750–764) for `Δ` as the quantity identified; confirmed by S. *Where:* 9:599, 601, 719; 10:424, 449, 654, 775, 819, 845, 905; 13sb:26. *Adopted:* *coupling constant renormalization* for the definition of the output coupling `β = β′ + α + Δ` (chapter 9); *vacuum energy renormalization* for that of the constant part `v_sc`; *the coefficient `Δ`* at 9:750. The author decided on 25 November 2026 (decision 52) that the name is the operation's and `q_m` is "the coefficient `Δ` of the coupling constant renormalization" (10:424, 819); 10:449, 654, 775, 845–846, 905 and 13sb:26 still use the name for `Δ = q_m` (see *coupling constant renormalization*).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:574` "The parameter `ϑ` is the free coupling correction of the scalar reset. Lemma D5 shows that `ϑ = Δ_u` gives the density identity at every configuration"; `:663` "The reset gives a second description of the same coefficient: evaluating the identity at one configuration with positive kinetic energy identifies `Δ_u` as the unique root of an affine scalar equation"; `:671–676` Lemma "Coupling reset": `|Δ_u| ≤ 1`, and `β_u = β′_u + α_{N,m} + Δ_u` is continuous. Martin `existence/coupling-reset-selection.tex:1–8` ("Selecting the coupling and the vacuum constant … Two healthy configurations suffice to select the two scalar parameters"); `existence/physical-reset-reorganization.tex:1` ("Reorganizing the actual return before resetting the coupling"), `:322–326` `C_reset = e^{81b}C_sub`, the subtraction constant `C_sub` with the factor for the enlargement of the support by a radius-two halo.
*Literature:* **coupling constant renormalization** and **vacuum energy renormalization**; the **renormalization group equation** defining `g_{k+1}` (B87 p. 268: "Finally we perform the coupling constant renormalization", (2.15); (0.18): `1/g_1² = 1/g_0² − β_1(g_0)`; p. 258: "there is one more renormalization counterterm needed, it is a vacuum energy counterterm. It is contained in the normalization factors"; B88b p. 279: "The vacuum energy renormalization is performed by subtracting the values of `E^{(k+1)}` and `R''^{(k+1)}` at the configuration `U_{k+1} = 1` … The coupling constant renormalization is performed by subtracting `β_{k+1}(g_k) A(φ_{k+1}, U_{k+1})`"); in D1 the flow equations `ε_{k+1} = L³ε_k + L_1E_k + ε*_k`, `μ_{k+1} = L²μ_k + L_2E_k + μ*_k` (pp. 1330010-28/29, Theorem 14: "The starred terms are the effect of the fluctuation integral"). An analogue, close: the same two redefinitions per step; Bałaban defines `g_{k+1}` by the β-function, v3 defines `β = β′ + α + Δ` by the matched coefficient plus a projected remainder `Δ`. "Reset" has no source. Adopted (23 November 2026): *coupling constant renormalization*; *vacuum energy renormalization* for the constant part. The difference is stated at first use: Bałaban defines `g_{k+1}` by the β-function, v3 defines `β = β′ + α + Δ` by the matched coefficient plus a projected remainder `Δ`.
*Across chapters:* the former word had one sense (text read at 9:718–724, 750–764); its successor *coupling constant renormalization* names two objects: the whole operation `β = β′ + α + Δ` in chapter 9 (9:719–725), and, until 26 November 2026, `Δ = q_m` alone in chapter 10 (10:449, 654, 775, 845, 905) and at 13sb:26, which now say "the coefficient of the coupling constant renormalization"; at 10:424 and 819 the text says "the coefficient `Δ` (`q_m`) of the coupling constant renormalization" (25 November 2026). Chapter 9 now calls `Δ` alone "the coefficient `Δ`" (9:750, formerly "the coupling constant renormalization `Δ`"). 9:599 and 9:601 are the two occurrences of `C_reset`.
*See also:* residual scalar inverse coupling correction `q_m`; trial inverse coupling correction; one-step integral identity.

#### residual
*Now:* partly replaced by *remaining linear (quadratic) term* (sense 2, 6:675, 1220) and *replacement error* (sense 6, 14:362); "stationary residual" is now "residual of the mean equation" (9:77) and "mean-equation residual" (9:131); "nonlinear residual squares" (6:1411) is rewritten; remains in about 60 places, in all six senses.
1. **What is left of an identity or equation.** "Its residual vanishes at zero" (5:1082); the residual of a column of the approximate inverse outside its window (6:570); "the derivatives of the residual `𝖠m_Y + f_Y`" (6:645); the "residual of the mean equation" (9:77; "mean-equation residual", 9:131), which is the coefficient `η = −g^{-1}(𝖠 m_Y + f_Y)` of the linear term in the exponent of (ch06:gaussian-identity), the amount by which the mean `m_Y` built from the window inverse fails the equation `𝖠 m + f_Y = 0` (see *stationary residual*).
  *Basis:* R (5:1082; 6:570); R with S for the stationary residual (6:621–629, 666–675). *Where:* 5:1082; 6:570, 581, 645; 9:77, 131. *Proposed:* keep (standard), saying of which equation.
2. **Leftover linear or quadratic term in an exponent.** Now "the remaining linear or quadratic term in the exponent" (6:675) and "A remaining linear term" (6:1220); "linear Gaussian residual" remains at 6:1263.
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 6:675, 1220, 1263. *Proposed:* *remaining linear (quadratic) term*.
3. **"Residual Gaussian density"; "nonlinear residual squares".** The residual Gaussian density is the factor `exp{η·z + ½ z^*(Γ^{-1} − 𝖠) z}` of (ch06:gaussian-identity), 6:666–671: the density of the exact Gaussian weight with respect to the reference law `γ_Γ` ("The residual Gaussian density in (ch06:gaussian-identity)", 6:1096; "The residual Gaussian density, the exponential factor in (ch06:gaussian-identity)", 6:1086; "the remaining linear or quadratic term in the exponent", 6:674–675). The nonlinear residual of a fine or block-average row is the nonlinear component minus its comparison term (the `B_p(U,V)` of 6:898–899); "The energies `E_f` and `E_n` equal the squares of their nonlinear components minus comparison terms, plus the nonnegative difference between the squared distance from the identity and the squared curvature representative" (6:1410–1412) is, on a retained component below its threshold, the identity energy `= ½|B_p|² + a·(χ(U_p)² − |F(U_p)|²)/2`; the word "residual" no longer occurs in that sentence.
  *Basis:* R (6:666–675, 1096) for the density; S for the squares. *Where:* 6:1086, 1096; 6:1411, 1413. *Proposed:* *the factor `exp{η·z + ½ z^*(Γ^{-1} − 𝖠)z}`*; *the square of the row minus its comparison term* (applied at 6:1410–1413).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:1277`: "Dividing the resulting density by the normalized `γ_Γ` density gives both the linear residual and the quadratic correction in the displayed identity"; `:1308` "The unbounded exponentials come from the residual Gaussian density and its local covariance comparisons." Martin `existence/packet-annulus.tex:209–212`: "Define the actual and affine residuals `v = 𝒞(U,V) − g`, `v_0 = 𝒞(V^↑,V) − g + A_R^V u`" (`g` the coarse guide row, v3's comparison term); `:223` "`flaw(q) = (r(q)² − ‖F(q)‖²)/2`"; `:243–246` "On a kept fine row below its threshold the fine energy is exactly `a_f flaw(q_f) + ½ Σ_j ‖v_{f,j}‖²`".
4. **Trial residual; residual coefficient.** The trial residual is the trial at the ultraviolet cutoff minus one normalised local insertion density, the reference coefficient of the latter being chosen so that the coefficient at the coarsest scale vanishes ("Subtract one normalized local insertion density from the trial at the ultraviolet cutoff, choosing its reference coefficient so the residual coefficient at the coarsest scale is zero", 11:898–900). Transferred through the steps it has at scale `i` a local-insertion coefficient `x_i`, "the residual coefficient", and a remainder bounded by `c_i` (11:902–905).
  *Basis:* R (11:897–905). *Where:* 13ba; 18lp (e.g. 18lp:46–47 "the transferred residual coefficient"); 11:899 ("residual coefficient at the coarsest scale"), 899. *Proposed:* *difference between the trial and its approximant*.
5. **Residual profile; residual response.** The residual profile is `f − 𝒞_{m,ρ} f`, a frequency profile after subtraction of the annular correction `𝒞_{m,ρ} f`, which is built by Lagrange interpolation so that the first `2m` moments of the difference vanish (14:465–471). The residual response is its Laplace transform `𝓡_{m,ρ} f(E)` (14:472–477; see *response*, sense 9).
  *Basis:* D (14:465–478; "the *residual profile* `f − 𝒞_{m,ρ}f`", 14:471). *Where:* 14:465, 471, 472, 527, 538, 574, 667, 747, 755. *Proposed:* *profile with its first `2m` moments subtracted* (the number of moments as in 14:465–478); keep the symbols `𝒞_{m,ρ}`, `𝓡_{m,ρ}`.
6. **Replacement error.** At 14:362 the text now says "the replacement error"; at 18lp:307–336 "residual" remains ("bounds its residual paired with any …", 18lp:307).
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 14:362; 18lp:307–336. *Proposed:* *replacement error*.
*Across chapters:* the word means "what is left" each time, of a different operation. The senses listed are those of chapters 3–6 and 12–16; the list was not checked for completeness in the other chapters. In sense 5, `𝓡_{m,ρ} f` is the Laplace transform of the residual profile `f − 𝒞_{m,ρ} f`, not of the annular correction itself (text read at 14:463–478: "Then the *residual profile* `f − 𝒞_{m,ρ}f` has its first `2m` moments zero. Interpolation of `(p²+E²)^{-1}` gives its exact Laplace transform"). Compound terms with their own entries: *residual energy*, *residual scalar inverse coupling correction*; "residual weight `ϖ`, `ω^res`" belongs to *weight*.
*See also:* remainder with vanishing extracted coefficient; replacement; response (sense 9); trial.

#### resolution heights
*Now:* not applied.
- **Meaning.** The two limits `θ = lim τ_m/T` and `θ_+ = lim τ_j/T`, where `T = log(1/r)` (18lp:300) and `0 ≤ θ_− < θ < θ_+` are chosen with levels `k, m, j` such that `τ_k/T → θ_−`, `τ_m/T → θ`, `τ_j/T → θ_+` (18lp:223–224). In general the height of a sequence of levels `m(T)` is `lim τ_{m(T)}/T` with `τ_m = log(1/a_m)`, so that `a_m = e^{−θT + o(T)}`; `θ` is the height of the extraction level `m` and `θ_+` that of the grid level `j`. "Letting the two resolution heights tend to one" (18r:55–56) is "Finally let `θ ↑ 1` and `θ_+ ↓ 1`" (18lp:347–348); it yields the exponent `D + 1 − W`.
  *Basis:* R (18lp:223–224, 347–348). *Where:* 18r:55–56 (the only occurrence of the phrase). *Proposed:* *the parameters `θ` and `θ_+`*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:222`: "A level `k` has height `b` when `s_k/T → b`; thus `a_k = e^{−bT+o(T)}`"; `J-section.tex:304`: "Choose levels `k,m,j` of heights `0 ≤ θ_− < θ < θ_+`". Lean `YM.OPE.Height` (`YM/OPE/Height.lean:18–20`; definition read): `Height S l T m c` has fields `grows : Tendsto m l atTop` and `pace : Tendsto (fun i => S.scale (m i)/T i) l (𝓝 c)`; lemma `found` (`Height.lean:58`, in namespace `YM.OPE`; statement read): for a `Gentle` schedule and `T → ∞` there is a level sequence of every height `a ≥ 0`.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence, settled by chapter 18lp (text read: 18r:53–57; 18lp:221–226, 346–349): the two parameters sent to one are `θ` and `θ_+`. The word "height" is not defined in v3 in this sense; v3 should restore the definition "A level `k` has height `b` when `τ_k/T → b`; thus `a_k = e^{−bT+o(T)}`" at 18lp:223, or drop the word at 18r:55.

#### resolvent identity for the determinant
*Formerly:* *determinant inverse identity*.
*In the text:* ("The other rows follow from the resolvent identity for the determinant", 9:141).
- **Meaning.** The step by which the determinant factor of the local expansion is bounded: the resolvent identity `A^{-1} − A_0^{-1} = A^{-1}(A_0 − A)A_0^{-1}`, applied to each principal compression of the actual and the flat precision matrices, inserted in the integral that defines the local logarithm of the determinant, `log det A = ∫_0^1 tr((A − I) A_s^{-1}) ds` (6:1203–1204). Since the two matrices differ by `O(B^a t_f)` on a local window, this gives the row "local determinant differences `C_k B^{a_k} t_f`" of the table at 6:1253–1272, proved at 6:1291–1295 ("The resolvent identity for each principal compression transfers this to the diagonal integral defining the local logarithmic normalization"), which is the row "centered determinant variation `P_j(t_{m+1}+g)`" of 9:127. The sentence 9:141–143 assigns one argument to each of three rows: this identity to the determinant row, "the second-order vanishing of the Haar correction" to the Haar row, "the window errors" to the covariance and stationary residual row.
  *Basis:* R (9:127, 141–143 with 6:1259, 1291–1295); S for the former wording. *Where:* 9:141. *Adopted:* *the resolvent identity applied to the determinant, as at 6:1291–1295* (9:141 does not cite 6:1291–1295).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:162`: "For the determinant, subtract its flat value and the quadratic term already assigned to `α_{N,m} 𝒬_m`. The inverse identity bounds the remaining variation by `P_j(t_{m+1}+g)`"; "inverse identity" is used in the same manuscript for the identity giving the derivative or the difference of an inverse (Scott `part2/B-section.tex:1115`: `D(𝖠_Ω^{-1}) = −𝖠_Ω^{-1}(D𝖠_Ω)𝖠_Ω^{-1}`; `part2/C-section.tex:348` "The inverse bounds follow by differentiating the inverse identity"). Which of the two forms Scott means at D:162 is not displayed there.
*Across chapters:* a pointer from chapter 9 to chapter 6. It is not the pair of series at 6:1198–1209 ("The exact inverse and trace expansions … This determinant identity"): those control the difference between the window covariance and the exact inverse, are exponentially small in `B`, and belong to the third row ("window errors"). v3 should still cite 6:1291–1295 at 9:141.
*See also:* Haar logarithm; stationary residual.

#### response
*Now:* partly replaced by *linearization of the critical configuration* (sense 4); *critical configuration* (sense 5); *correlation functional* (sense 8); *Laplace transform* (sense 9); removed in sense 10; remains on 45 lines in senses 1–3, 6 (as "curvature response"), 7, 11 and for the values in sense 8.
1. **Two-point function with a linear source (chapter 3).** `y ↦` the two-point function of the linear field `ℓ_P(F)(0)` with `F(y)`.
  *Basis:* D (3:409). *Where:* 3:409–451, 899, 975. *Proposed:* *two-point function with source `ℓ_P`*.
2. **Candidate infinitesimal variation (chapter 3).** A linear map on local fields giving an infinitesimal symmetry variation.
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 3:657, 1084, 1086. *Proposed:* *infinitesimal variation*; *linear map on local fields*.
3. **A term of the Ward sum (chapter 3).** "The third response".
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 3:964. *Proposed:* *third term*.
4. **Stationary fine field of a coarse field, and the linear map giving it.** "Let `a = W_F h` be the fine field that the linearization of the critical configuration, in its representative `W_F` of (ch05:stationary-tangent), assigns to a coarse logarithmic field `h`" (6:960–961): here the object is the image field `a`, the linear image of `h` under `W_F`. At 6:979 ("The operator `W_F` has a bounded row norm at fixed `L`") it is the operator. The operator is the representative `W_F` of chapter 5 in the block axial gauge, so written at 6:954 ("the representative `W_F`, in the block axial gauge, of the linearization of their critical configuration"), 953, 967, 972, 976, 1493, 1545 ("does not replace `W_F` by the representative in a different gauge"): the fine critical configuration in tree coordinates as a linear function of the coarse input, equal to `W_s` plus the fine gradient that makes it vanish on the tree. In later chapters the operator is called the linearization `W` of the critical configuration: "For the linearization `W` of the critical configuration, taken in its representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge" (11:642, with the identities `KW = Q^*K'`, `AW = bQ^*`, `DW = JD'`); "the linearization of the critical configuration" = `W_a` at 17m:193 (with 17m:263, "The smooth representative of the linearization of the critical configuration is `W_a = W_s − d_f E R W_s`"); "the linearization of the critical configuration on polynomials" = `W_s` (17m:202); "Exact polynomial preservation by the linearization of the critical configuration" (19:163) is `W_s`: it repeats "controlled by exact polynomial preservation" (17m:188–189), and the proof it refers to begins at 17m:202 and then passes to `W_a` (17m:263). 6:852 is a different object, now "the derivative of the averaging operation": the first-order variation of `Q_e^pred` in the fine fluctuation, that is, the rows `D_e^pred` of the derivative `𝖣` (6:508), which with the mean `m_Y` and the cutoff factors decides whether a cutoff factor equals one (6:850–853).
  *Basis:* R (6:960, 979; 11:642; 19:163 with 17m:188–202, 263); S for the identification of the source's `𝒰_F` with `W_F`; R for 6:852 ("derivative of the averaging operation"). *Where:* 6:954, 960, 974, 979, 1500, 1552; 11:642; 17m:193, 202, 263; 19:163 (all now "linearization" or `W_F`). *Adopted:* for the field `a` of 6:960, *the fine field that the linearization of the critical configuration, in its representative `W_F`, assigns to `h`* (the linear image of `h`, not the nonlinear critical configuration; the earlier "linearized critical configuration" was a third name and is withdrawn); for the operator, *the linearization `W` of the critical configuration*, saying which representative is meant: `W_F` at 6:960, 979, 983 (the text now writes `W_F`), `W_a` at 17m:193, `W_s` at 17m:202; no symbol is renamed, and the representative is written wherever `W` is unqualified: `W_s` at 5:527–535, `W_F` in chapter 11 (11:642), `W_a` in `17-current-contraction.tex`.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/local-mean.tex:11–14` "Write `𝒰_F b` for the fine stationary field in tree coordinates with coarse input `b`. It is the tree-straightened installed linear response"; Lean `YM.Precision.extracted`, `YM/PREC/TreeMatch.lean` (definition read). Details and the limits of the identification under *`𝒰_F`*. For 6:852: the wording before commit `4ebb64ea` was "Verifying this implication uses the actual mean, predictor response, and masks" (diff read); Martin `existence/actual-reader-tree-covariance.tex:63–65`: "The fine linear response in channel `s` is `D P_s`, where `P_s` is the signed permutation on link cochains. The predictor response is the signed permutation of `Qu` on coarse bonds" (at zero background, so the response of the predictor to a fluctuation `u` is the linear block average `Qu`). That 6:852 means this derivative at the actual field is inferred; no source sentence defines "predictor response" in general.
5. **The stationary nonlinear fine field.** Now "The nonlinear critical configuration" (17m:278).
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 17m:278. *Adopted:* *the (nonlinear) critical configuration*.
6. **Curvature response.** `J = H_{0,f}^{−1} T H_{0,c}`, where `T` is the induced map on curvatures and `H_{0,f}`, `H_{0,c}` the unmodified diagonal operators (11:646–648), and its installed form `Ψ_i` with `Δ_w Ψ_i = Q_{i,w} Δ_w` (11:1734–1740); "response paths" (11:1778); "the exponential response bound" (11:1780); "curvature-response row constants", "curvature-response estimate", "curvature responses", "the product of the subsequent curvature responses" (17w:12, 60, 67, 68).
  *Basis:* D (11:646–648). *Where:* 11:647, 1734, 1735, 1755, 1778, 1780; 17w:12, 60, 67, 68. *Adopted:* keep *curvature response*, defined once; never bare "response" (bare "response" remains at 11:1778, 1780).
7. **Dependence of a determinant or operator on the background field.** A log-determinant as a function of the background ("Its determinant response is `Π_μ = ½ log det A_μ − log det G`", 7:282; "blocked response", 7:801); an operator with its background derivatives ("the Wilson response", 7:374; "left-coordinate response", 7:633; "The kinetic response cancels", 7:753); "All three response layers" `a`, `b`, `c` (7:461–462); the second-order coefficient in the background field ("normalized quadratic response of `Γ_μ`", "regulated response", 17t:93–94).
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 7:282, 374, 461, 633, 753, 801; 17t:93, 94. *Proposed:* *dependence on the background field through second order*; for 17t, *second-order coefficient in the background field*.
8. **One-slot response.** "For `c ∈ V_d`, a fixed spectator list `v`, and a separated smooth test function `f`, define the correlation functional `L_{v,f}(c) = ∫ f(x_0,x) S_{n+1}(c(x_0), v(x))`" (13:121–124): a smeared correlation as a linear functional of one label. "Spectator responses", "separated responses", "limiting responses" (13:9–10, 153–185; 18gq:112–131; 18:185) are the values of these functionals; RG:18 says "by equality of their responses in all separated correlations", as 13:8–9.
  *Basis:* D (13:121–124). *Where:* 13:9, 10, 122 ("correlation functional"), 151, 152, 161, 177, 183, 210, 265; 18gq:112, 114, 131; 14:413, 999; 18:185; RG:18. *Proposed:* *correlation functional `c ↦ L_{v,f}(c)`* (and *its value* for the number); the first part is now in the text (13:122).
9. **Spectral response.** Two objects: the Laplace transform `ℒf(E)` of a frequency profile and its corrected form `𝓡_{m,ρ} f(E)` ("its exact Laplace transform", 14:472), functions of `E` (14:457–458, 472–477); and the integral of that function against the spectral measure, the number `Resp_i(g)` (14:510–512). The text now says "Laplace transform" for the functions (14:472, 537, 695, 704, 747, 768) and "values" for the numbers (14:661, 679); "response" survives only in the symbol `Resp_i`.
  *Basis:* D by formula (14:457–458, 472–477; 14:510–512). *Where:* functions: 14:472, 537, 695, 704, 747, 768; numbers: 14:510–512, 661, 679. *Adopted:* *Laplace transform of the profile*; *its integral against the spectral measure* (as "value").
10. **Shell integral.** The integral `−∫ ∂_μ V_c S(J_{μc}, A)` over the shell. The text now calls the quantity "the angular Ward sum" at 14:783 and 14:803 ("Conservation and the local flux identities express the angular Ward sum, the left side of (ch14:line-ward) below, as `−∫ ∂_μ V_c S(J_{μc}, A)`", 14:783–784; "whereas the angular Ward sum is independent of `λ`", 14:803).
  *Basis:* R (14:783–784). *Where:* 14:783–784, 803. *Adopted:* *the angular Ward sum* ("Ward sum" defined at 3:915; "the normalized angular Ward sum", 14:848). Not *flux integral*: "flux" is not the text's word for it (14:783 has "local flux identities" for the identities used).
11. **"Anchored vector response".** Read as the Hessian kernel of an anchored vector function.
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 17:226. *Proposed:* *Hessian kernel of the anchored vector function*.
*Literature:* see *stationary tangent* for sense 4 (`a = W_F h`) and *background insertion* for the second background derivative of the Gaussian contribution; the other senses have no counterpart in the papers read.
*Across chapters:* eleven unrelated objects (ten if senses 2 and 3 are counted as one); lines with the word now: chapter 3, 9; chapter 7, 6; chapter 11, 6; chapters 13–14, 11 (9 / 2); chapters 17–19, 12; RG, 1. (a) At 6:960 the object is the image field, at 6:979 the operator (text read: 6:958–961, 977–984); both are recorded in sense 4. (b) The operator `W` is no longer called a response: 11:642, 17m:193, 202, 263 and 19:163 say "linearization of the critical configuration". (c) In sense 8 the object defined at 13:121–124 is a functional of `c`: *correlation functional*, with *value* for the number; not *correlations with all other fields*. The phrase "response bound" at 10:629 is now "the fixed fraction `ε`" (see the next entry); "the exponential response bound" (11:1780) belongs to sense 6. Sense 1 is called "curvature response" at 3:409, the name of the unrelated sense 6 of chapter 11. For sense 4, the text now uses `W_F` at 6:960 and 6:983; before 24 November 2026 it had `𝒰_F` there, without the source definition ("Write `𝒰_F b` for the fine stationary field in tree coordinates with coarse input `b`. It is the tree-straightened installed linear response").

#### response bound `ε`
*Now:* replaced by *fraction `ε`*; since 25 November 2026 (sentence repair) the line also said what it is a fraction of ("the fixed fraction `ε≤1/16` of `C_st x^{−11/10}` allotted to the principal regular bound (and `2ε` to the complementary one)"). Since 26 November 2026 (decision on `C_st`) it reads: "where `C_st = c_j^pre` is the stage constant of (ch09:early-bounds) and `x^{-11/10} = ε_m^reg`, so that the first term is the regular bound `H_pre` there with `θ = 3ε`. … The fraction `ε≤1/16` can be made as small as desired before choosing the lower bound on the reference coupling" (10:629–630); the split into principal and complementary bounds is dropped (margin note).
*Variants:* response parameter (source).
- **Meaning.** A fixed small constant `ε ≤ 1/16`: a fraction of `E = C_st x^{-11/10}`, `x = β̂_m`; in the source the principal regular bound of the one-step output gets `εE` and the complementary one `2εE` (the text dropped this split on 26 November 2026); their sum is the leading term `3ε C_st x^{−11/10}` of `𝒩(H(t)) ≤ 3 ε C_st x^{−11/10} + O(x^{−23/20+o(1)})` (10:623–629). It is chosen before the lower bound on the reference coupling (10:629–630, quoted under *Now*). This is the "arbitrarily small fraction of `ε_m^reg`" of the chapter 9 remainder estimate (`ε_m^reg = β̂_m^{−11/10}`, 9:168; 9:376–381). "Response" is only the source's name for the parameter; no response function is involved.
  *Basis:* R (10:629 states `ε ≤ 1/16`; since 26 November 2026 also `C_st = c_j^pre` and `θ = 3ε`, the allotment to a principal and a complementary bound being dropped); S for the source's word. *Where:* 10:629. Left open by the review of 25 November: `C_st` and the "principal" and "complementary regular bound" are defined nowhere in v3 (`C_st` already at 10:625); settled on 26 November 2026: `C_st = c_j^pre` (10:629, inferred from matching formulas, margin note), the two bounds dropped. *Adopted:* *the fraction `ε`* (*the constant `ε ≤ 1/16` of (the chapter 9 remainder estimate)*, cited by number); drop "response".
  *Source:* Martin existence/background-test-prices.tex:83–99 ("`b(x) = 3t C_st x^{-11/10} + R(x)`, where `t > 0` is a small response parameter and `C_st > 0` is the fixed stage conversion constant … There the principal and complementary regular bounds are purchased as `E/16` and `2E/16`, with `E = C_st x^{-11/10}`; here they are purchased with the fraction `t ≤ 1/16` in place of `1/16`"), :129–131 ("the response parameter is chosen after it, and the coupling threshold after all those choices"). Lean: the parameter was not located; `YM.RG.Calendar.allowance` (YM/RG/History.lean:84; definition read: `hatCoupling m ^ (11/5)`, i.e. `β̂_m^{-11/10}`) is the quantity `ε_m^reg`.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence; the link to 9:168, 376–381 was inferred from the v3 text (read at 10:627–630 only) and agrees with the source; the text does not cite chapter 9 there.
*See also:* response.

#### restart
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* restarted history; restarted representation(s); restarted threshold; restarted small-field indicator; restarted family.
1. **Restarted history.** The auxiliary sequence of densities `D_k = ρ_{N,p,k}`, `D_i = 𝓑_{i,β} D_{i+1}`, with `∫D_i = Z_{N,p}` (11R:232–235), in which the inverse coupling is frozen at `β = β_{N,p,k}` below the comparison scale `k` (11R:224–225): "A useful auxiliary history, the *restarted history*, keeps the inverse coupling constant below a comparison scale while retaining the paths, adjacent quadratic identities, and block geometry" (11:736–738).
  *Basis:* D (11:736–741); D for the densities (11R:216–236, Proposition "One restarted history on the comparison window"). *Where:* 11:26, 734–765, 1161, 1226, 1315, 1669, 1972, 2063, 2095, 2203; 11R:2, 7, 216–236, 378, 391; 17w:102; 19:49. *Adopted:* keep *restarted history*, defined once as *the history with the inverse coupling frozen below the comparison scale `k`* (not "sequence", "trajectory" or "schedule": *history* is the kept word).
2. **Restarted representation.** The local representation of the densities along that history ("Constructing the restarted representations", 11R:2), with new radius and threshold: "The new representation at scale index `i` has radius `B_i = b(x_i)²` and threshold `ϑ(x_i)`" (11R:18–19), where `b(x) = ⌈(log x)²⌉` and `x_i = β̂_i` (11R:12–18).
  *Basis:* D (11R:12–18). *Where:* 11R:2–243; 11:1157–1162; 17w:33. *Proposed:* *local representation along the restarted history*.
*Across chapters:* same two objects in chapters 11, 11R, 17 and 19. Two radii carry the letter `B` in chapter 17: `B_n` at 17m:429–435 (and `B_k` at 17m:332, 413) is the chapter 4 support radius `B_m = ⌈(log β̂_m)²⌉` (4:457), so `B_n = O((log β̂_n)²)` at 17m:435; `B_n` at 17w:33 is the restarted radius `b(x_n)²` ("Here `B_n` is the radius of the restarted representation", read). Chapter 11 says so itself: "The original insertion norm uses radius `M`, whereas the restarted representation uses radius `B`. These are different radii" (11:1157–1162, read). Caution: "auxiliary history" is not one object across chapters; in chapter 10 it is the zero-terminal-array history (10:827–830, 921), in chapter 11 the restarted one.
*See also:* recording scale; re-expression of the endpoint; comparison level; history.

#### restoration levels
*Now:* replaced by *middle scale* ("This bounded-cover assertion is used at the middle scales", 11:1411).
- **Meaning.** The middle scales `ℓ` of the three scales `k > ℓ > w` of the restart argument, one for each comparison scale `k`: the scale at which the source weight is raised from `ω_−` to `ω` ("the larger source weight"), the principal terms are replaced by their corrected form, and the lower interval begins ("If the corrected principal coefficients at the middle scale are at most `H^{−31/32}`, their contribution to the incidence bound at the larger source weight …", 11:1557–1559; "On the lower interval … at the larger source weight", 11:1570–1575; "the *upper interval*, from the comparison scale to the middle scale", 11:1416). 11:1411–1413 contrasts them with "the separated opening sites": the bound `R_f` for the prescribed supports (11:1396–1401) holds where the insertions of one cell lie in one ball of radius `AB`, which is the situation at level `ℓ` and not that of the sites of distinct cells at level `k`.
  *Basis:* S; I from the v3 text (11:1411–1413 with 11:1557–1559). *Where:* 11:1411 (also "middle scale" at 11:1416, 1557, 1652, 1891). *Proposed:* *the scales `ℓ`*, after naming the three scales once by the symbols `k, ℓ, w`.
  *Source:* Martin existence/allarity-marked-propagation.tex:248–265 ("From the launch at the middle level `ℓ` down to the output torus of the replica estimate, the weight is `ω = H^{1/(8u)}`. On the leading part of the interval, from the top `k` down to `ℓ`, the recurrence above is run at the smaller weight `ω_−` … The weight is changed exactly once, at the launch"), :1876–1879 ("At the middle level `ℓ` … the marker weight is raised from `ω_−` to `ω`"); `audit/chapter-11-weight-restoration-review.md`:23 ("this fixed-cover geometry applies at the middle/restoration levels, where the same-cell readers have contracted, not at the separated opening level").
*Across chapters:* chapter 11 only. The plural is read as one scale `ℓ` for each comparison scale `k` (inferred). The lemmas "Regular remainders at the larger source weight" (11:1442) and "Large-field activities at the larger source weight" (11:1477) name the operation; the section label is still `ch11:weight-restoration`.
*See also:* restart; weight restoration.

#### rooted
*Now:* partly replaced by *incidence bound* (11:1443, 1446; 12:237–238) and by *the norms of (ch04:weighted-sums)* (12:179); remains for rooted sums, estimates and derivatives (about 40 occurrences).
*Variants:* rooted component estimates; rooted derivative; rooted cluster sums; marker-root sum (source); rooted budget (source); no longer in the text: rooted activity norm; rooted majorant sums.
1. **Rooted sums and norms.** A sum over supports, clusters or polymers pinned at one site, as in the rooted form of the Kotecký–Preiss theorem; a "rooted activity norm" is the corresponding norm. Three normalisations occur and each use is one of them. (a) At 12:179, "Summing the norms of (ch04:weighted-sums) over the finitely many sites gives uniform convergence of the regular sum and every total large-field activity" (12:179–181), the norms are the two weighted sums of (ch04:weighted-sums), 4:639–644: `𝓔_m = sup_x Σ_{i: o_i = x} e^{σ cov(X_i)} e_i` for the localized terms (each counted at its base point) and `𝓚_m = sup_x Σ_{i: x ∈ Y_i} e^{σ cov(Y_i)} k_i` for the large-field activities (each counted at every site of its support); "Summing … over the finitely many sites" (12:179–180) is `Σ_i ‖E_i‖ ≤ |Λ| 𝓔_m`, `Σ_i sup|K_i| ≤ |Λ| 𝓚_m` (4:655–657), applied to differences of the activity arrays at two cutoffs, whose convergence in these norms is the hypothesis of 12:31–34. (b) In chapter 11 a support may be rooted "at one of its fine sites or insertion points" (11:268–273). (c) The "incidence bound at `(ω, e)`" of the lemma "Regular remainders at the larger source weight" (11:1442–1446) and the "incidence bounds at most one at support exponent `σ_m`" of 12:237–238 are pinned at an insertion: the supremum over insertions `j` of `Σ_{γ: j ∈ I(γ)} ω^{|I(γ)|} e^{e·c_B(X_γ)} b_γ`, i.e. the incidence bound with source weight `ω` and support exponent `e`.
  *Basis:* R for the cluster sums (standard); R for 12:179 (12:31–34 with 4:639–657); S for the readings of 11:1443–1446 and 12:237. *Where:* 8:15, 117, 171, 180; 9:180, 198, 687, 798, 896; 11:1443, 1446, 1558, 1897, 1941; 12:179, 237; 17m:80, 87, 118, 119, 400; 18lp:214. *Adopted:* keep for cluster sums; at 12:179 *the norms `𝓔_m`, `𝓚_m` of (ch04:weighted-sums)*; at 11:1443–1446 and 12:237 *incidence bound at weight `ω` and support exponent `e`*.
  *Source:* for 12:179, Martin existence/fixed-rung-convergence.tex:193–196, 212–219: "the background activity arrays are Cauchy in their common norm of rooted ordinary derivative bounds and forced value bounds"; "For the activity arrays, sum a rooted budget over the finitely many sites. Every ordinary term has its designated site, and every forced term has a nonempty marked support, so each term is counted at least once. If `V` is the number of sites and `b, k` are the fixed two activity bounds, the resulting uniform evaluation bounds are `Vb‖A‖` for the ordinary sum and `Vk‖A‖` for a forced profile"; Lean `YM.RG.Activities.EBound`, `YM.RG.Activities.KBound`, YM/RG/Activities.lean (definitions read: there are bounds `b_i` on the activities such that for every site `x`, `Σ_{i: site_i = x} mass(support_i, b_i) ≤ budget`, respectively `Σ_{i: x ∈ support_i} mass(support_i, b_i) ≤ budget`), with `YM.RG.BudgetPoint.mass P c = exp(supportExponent · coverNumber B P) · c`, YM/RG/Masks.lean (definition read), and `YM.RG.SumBudget` (definition read: nonnegative, summable, sum at most `c`). For 11:1443–1446, Martin existence/allarity-marked-propagation.tex:1953–1978 (lemma "Raising the regular marker weight": "Suppose the marker-root sum of letters with `t(I)=1` is at most `p_1` at weight `ω_-` and support exponent `e` … Then the marker-root bound at weight `ω` and support exponent `e` is at most `H^{Un}p_1 + p_2`", proved by "Summing at each fixed marker"); this is the source of v3's lemma at 11:1442–1447 (same weights `ω_-`, `ω`, same exponent `Un`). For the insertion-rooted sums, Lean `YM.Extra.Multi.Rooted`, YM/Extra/MULTISOURCE_BOUNDS/Root.lean (definition read: `Rooted mode X M a f c` says that for every marker `s`, `Σ_{i: s ∈ mode i} exp(a · coverNumber M (X i)) · f i ≤ c`; docstring "Marker-rooted cover budget"); that this declaration is the one behind 12:237 is a match of formula, not established through a theorem.
2. **Rooted derivative.** A mixed derivative with decay measured from one index.
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 5:1217, 1357. *Proposed:* *mixed derivative with decay measured from one index*.
3. **Rooted coordinates of the frame.** See *rooted coordinates*.
*Across chapters:* the support-weighted norms are three normalisations (anchored, containing-site, pinned at an insertion; see *containing-site bound*): 4:646–649 and 9:515–520 distinguish anchored from containing-site bounds, and "root-to-site conversion" (11:1923) is the passage between them. At 12:179 both of the first two are meant, the anchored one for the regular activities and the containing-site one for the large-field activities; the source's "rooted" covers both ("Every ordinary term has its designated site, and every forced term has a nonempty marked support"). 12:179 now refers to (ch04:weighted-sums).
*See also:* root; rooted coordinates; site conversion; incidence.

Rooted: the block coordinate is the local gauge transformation at the block root, extended over the block by the minimizing transformation normalized there (`h_o = 1`) (Martin `predictor-branch.tex:169–170, 214–223, 270`; Scott `B-section.tex:553, 625`; Lean `YM.Stationary.enroll`, `Chart.lean:367`, "to rooted"). In v3 the normalization is at 4:46, 62, 95 and 5:1007, the rooted scalar coordinate `r_root` at 7:702–705. The change to centered coordinates is triangular with identity diagonal (Martin `selected-stationary-linear-data.tex:119–126`; Lean `YM.Stationary.shear`, `shear_det`, `Regulator.lean:413, 457`; v3 7:540, 683–685, 708–709). `M_core` is computed in rooted coordinates (Martin `thermal-contact-cancellation.tex:130`; v3 7:530–536).
*Across chapters:* chapter 7 only. Other uses of "rooted" in chapters 6, 9, 11 were not checked by the trace.
*See also:* recentering (sense 1); rooted; root; `M_core`, `M_act`.

#### row
*Now:* partly replaced by *component* (sense 1); *kernel* (sense 2); *operator* (sense 4); *factorization* (sense 5); *vector* (sense 7); *free test* (sense 8); remains on 53 lines: in senses 6, 9 and 10 (kept), at 7:359, 989, 990, 1006, 1181 (sense 1), 12:55 (sense 2), 5:609, 624 (sense 3), and at 7:1072.
1. **Component of the action vector.** One component, indexed by its plaquette or edge, of the stacked vector whose half-square is the action; by extension the same component of its linearisation and of its affine approximation `Du + b_Y`. The text now says "plaquette and path components" (6:104), "coarse components" (6:112), "The vectors `Φv_c` and `Φ_n v_c`" (6:191), "complement component" (6:208, 1415), "the Gram matrix of the components" (11:668), "quadratic path components", "pairs of quadratic path components" (11R:102, 123); the "exterior row … bounds" of 11R:267 are now "the bounds for the corresponding action terms far from the large-field set": the bounds for the components not assigned to a selected large-field component (see *exterior row*). "Row" in this sense remains in chapter 7: "the row squares" (7:359), "rows of `ρ`", "the transported rows" (7:989–990), "the row coefficients of `J`" (7:1006), "rows and the cubic/quartic families" (7:1181).
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 5:853, 1064–1065; ch. 6 (e.g. 6:104, 112–115, 191, 460, 1404–1405, 1441); 7:359, 989, 990, 998, 1006, 1181; 9:546, 570, 837, 842; 10:359; 11:668, 710; 11R:102, 103, 123, 267 ("component" except in chapter 7 and at 11R:267). *Adopted:* *component* (of the curvature vector `X_f(p)`, of the affine map); *plaquette component*, *path component*.
2. **Convolution kernel.** The matrix-valued kernel `K_ab(z)`, `z ∈ ℤ⁴`, of a translation-invariant operator on the infinite lattice, or one displacement-indexed coefficient of it ("Write a translation-invariant kernel as `K_ab(z)`", 5:711). The kernel of an operator between adjacent scales has the positions within the block included in the index sets (5:712–713). "Convergence of … quadratic kernels" (10:357) cites the chapter 5 proposition; 12:55 ("For a row their length is `|x|_1 + 4`") is read in this sense by inference and still says "row".
  *Basis:* R (5:711–713); I for 12:55. *Where:* 5:711–713, 738, 751, 826, 844, 849, 854, 1391; 10:357; 12:55 (all "kernel" except 12:55). *Adopted:* *kernel* (of a translation-invariant operator); *two-scale kernel*.
3. **Symbol.** The same object as a matrix-valued Fourier multiplier with exponentially summable coefficients.
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 5:609, 624. *Proposed:* *symbol with exponentially decaying kernel*.
4. **Operator.** A specific linear operator (`R`, `K`) with finite range or exponential decay.
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 5:858, 1134; 6:150 (now "operator", "finite-range operator `R`", "exponentially local operator `K`"). *Adopted:* *operator*; *finite-range operator*.
5. **Factorisation.** The factorisation `C_ν^* C_ν = H_ν` and the identities written through it, now "factorization of the metrics", "factorization hypothesis" (6:128, 140, 169, 382). 9:570 "component coefficient matrix `S(0)`" with `c_dir I + S(0)^* S(0) = I` is the same factorisation written with the letter `S`, where 7:987 writes `ρ`.
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 6:128, 140, 169, 382; cf. 9:570. *Adopted:* *factorization `C^*C = H`*.
6. **Row of a matrix or of a kernel at a fixed output index.** Literal, as in row and column sums (5:1006; 11:1218; 17c:238, 349: "row sum"). In chapter 17 all ten uses are of this kind and the kernels are not translation-invariant: rows of the curvature response `Ψ` (17w:12–13 "the curvature-response row constants", cf. 11:1740 `sup_x Σ_y |Q_{i,w}(x,y)| ≤ R L_i^{−|w|−2}`); rows of `W_s` (17m:237 "Let `A_x^{ab}(z)` be the physical row from coarse direction `b` at `⌊x/L⌋ + z` to fine direction `a` at `x`", 245, 249, 260); rows of `M_{ef}` (17c:337 "Its row sum is `L`", 349, 367) and of `R_0` (17c:281, "a rough row along the root contours"); row of the triangular matrix of the recursion (17c:217) for the norms `e_r` ("each row sum, including the below-diagonal terms, is at most `1/2`", 17c:238). In chapters 13–14 the rows are those of a matrix each of whose rows is a correlation functional (13:170, 184; 14:282).
  *Basis:* R. *Where:* 3:628; 5:882, 1006, 1358; ch. 6, about 13 (e.g. 6:222, 245, 285, 335, 560, 642, 818, 834, 913, 979, 1001, 1508); 7:721; 9s:197, 202; 11:684, 1216, 1218, 1268, 1736, 1754, 1760; 13:170, 184; 14:282; 17w:13; 17c:238, 281, 337–369; 17m:237–260. *Proposed:* keep; in chapter 17 *row of the kernel* or *for fixed output index* (not *kernel* alone: these kernels are not translation-invariant, and "kernel" is the equivalent of sense 2).
7. **Member of a finite list of coefficient vectors.** "The vectors `(I − Π_i) u_{j,i}` are bounded, hence admissible" (11:2258); "bounded vectors have uniformly subpower cutoff-scale coordinates" (13:161–162).
  *Basis:* R (11:2258). *Where:* 11:2258; 13:161. *Adopted:* *vectors* (of the finite family).
8. **Reference rows: the tests of the finite free family.** A row is one test of the finite family that separates the free fields of degree at most `d`: a one- or two-point configuration with fixed free labels, a singleton `u` and an optional spectator `v`; the tests index the rows of the matrix of free correlations whose columns are indexed by a basis of the free field space `𝓜_d^Max`. "Reference" means free (Maxwell). "The free moments of each test" (15:277) are the free moments `s = G_{u}`, `s' = G_{v}`, `G_{u,v}` of the labels of one test at its unscaled configuration; "a fixed constant depending on the finitely many free tests" (15:277); "The finitely many free tests use fixed free labels and convergent configurations without coincident points" (15:280–281). The text now calls them tests; the dictionary's reading, a row of the matrix transferred to the test that produces it, explains the earlier word.
  *Basis:* D since 26 November 2026 (15:277: "the finitely many free tests (the rows of the separating family: a label `u` with at most one further label `v`, at fixed points; the two-point rows are those of Corollary ch03:detectors)", List 2, item 1, in the reviewer's wording); I from the v3 text before (15:277–281); S for the object. *Where:* 15:277 (twice), 280. *Adopted:* *test* (member of the finite separating family); *the free moments of each test*; for the family, *separating family* (since 26 November 2026 named in the gloss at 15:277).
  *Source:* Scott part2/H-section.tex:160: "Use the rows of Lemma `lem:E2-free-tests` … Each row of trial `ℓ` consists of a singleton `u` and optional spectator `v`, placed at the comparison points `r_ℓ y^{ℓ,i}`. Write `𝒢_I^ℓ` for the Maxwell moment of the row labels in slots `I` at the unscaled points `y^{ℓ,i}`, and set `s = 𝒢_{u}`, `s' = 𝒢_{v}` and `c = 𝒢_{u,v} − ss'`"; part2/E-section.tex:490–499 (free test matrix `𝒢_{ij}`, test `i` against basis element `𝔪_j`; Lemma `lem:E2-free-tests`: "there are finitely many one- or two-point tests at generic configurations, with every second label a basis element, for which the matrix has rank `dim 𝓜_d`"). Lean, partly: `YM.Push.Corrected.Row X := Fin X.amount` and `AxisX X := Fin (X.dim+1)`, YM/Push/CORRECTED_COLUMNS/Program.lean (abbreviations read; module docstring "Mark `i` below is a *row*, the other index a column of the full free matrix"; docstring of `Tests`: "Rows fixed independently of both cutoffs"); the structure `Columns`, which holds the rows, was not opened.
9. **Row of a displayed table.**
  *Where:* 9:141, 146. *Proposed:* keep.
10. **Row vector.** See *row transport*.
  *Where:* 1:80.
*Across chapters:* a real change of meaning, by chapter: senses 2–5 belong to chapters 5–6 (with 10:357 and 12:55), sense 1 runs from chapter 5 to 11R, sense 6 is everywhere and is the only one in chapter 17. Lines with "row" now: ch. 1, 1; ch. 3, 1; ch. 5, 5; ch. 6, 13; ch. 7, 8; ch. 9 and 9s, 4; ch. 11, 7; ch. 12–14, 4; ch. 17, 10. 13:170, 184 and 14:282 are placed in sense 6: rows of a matrix each of whose rows is a correlation functional. The reference rows of sense 8 are, by the source text, the tests that produce the rows of such a matrix (the free test matrix); whether the matrices of 13:170, 184 and 14:282 are built from the same family of tests was not checked. 7:1072 "the prescribed coarse quadratic row" is doubtful (singular; presumably the whole quadratic term `J`; read, not decided) and is left out of sense 1.

### S

#### safe chart
*Now:* unchanged; 9s:144–146 now introduces it as "a fixed closed coordinate ball of the chart, the *safe chart*".
*Variants:* safe radius; no longer in the text: fixed safe chart.
- **Meaning.** The set of fine configurations whose chart coordinates are bounded by a fixed radius `r_s`: with the chart `U = 𝒟_x(y)` (the logarithms `y` of the free links relative to the replicated coarse field with coordinates `x`), it is the inverse image of the closed ball `max(‖x‖_∞, ‖y‖_∞) ≤ r_s`. It is convex in the coordinates, which is what the Taylor argument following 9s:146 uses (both endpoints and the segment joining them lie in it), and `r_s` is fixed before the lower bound on the reference coupling ("fixed"). "By the estimate (ch05:nonlinear-tree) in the block axial gauge, a fine configuration lies in a fixed closed coordinate ball of the chart, the *safe chart*, whenever its fine plaquettes and the deviations of the coarse links from the values of the averaging operation are below a fixed `δ > 0`" (9s:144–146): by the estimate (ch05:nonlinear-tree), 5:1019–1025, such a configuration has every free link within `(C_0 s + 1)δ` of its pull-back `rep V`, hence coordinates of size at most `r_s` once `δ` is small.
  *Basis:* D (9s:144–146) for the ball; S for its norm; R (9s:144–146, with 5:1019–1025) for the statement. *Where:* 9s:144–146, 237. *Adopted:* *the coordinate ball `max(‖x‖_∞, ‖y‖_∞) ≤ r_s` of the stationary chart*; for the sentence, "by (ch05:nonlinear-tree), a configuration with fine plaquettes and mismatches below `δ` lies in this ball".
  *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:81–91`: "On the common safe chart assume the fine Hessian satisfies `D_y²φ ≥ (γ/2)I`. … Here the safe chart is the inverse image of the closed combined coordinate supremum ball, while the displayed quadratic lower bound uses the Euclidean norm on `Y`. Both endpoints lie in that chart, and its convexity contains their entire joining segment"; `:22–23` "The combined chart norm is `max(‖x‖_∞, ‖y‖_∞)`"; `:111–118`: "For a prescribed safe coordinate radius `r_s > 0`, choose `δ ≤ min{r_0/(C_0 s+1), r_s/(C_log(C_0 s+1))}`. Taking the logarithm of each relative free bond now yields `U = 𝒟_x(y)` with `‖y‖_∞ ≤ r_s`. The coarse coordinates are already inside the safe radius."
*Literature:* no name. Two analogues in B85b: the conclusion `|V′ − 1| < 4d²α_0 + α_1` of Lemma 1 (p. 79), and the **regular part of the surface** (1.27) with the image set `Σ_k` and the conditions (1.36), `U_1 = e^{iηA}`, `|A| < B_1(α_0+α_1)(L^jη)^{-1}` on `Ω_j` (p. 81: "The unique gauge transformations described in it define a mapping of the set (1.28) into the regular part of the surface (1.27). Let us denote the image set of this mapping by `Σ_k`"). An analogue: a coordinate neighbourhood of the background in which every regular configuration with nearby averages has a representative; in B85b the gauge is the Landau gauge, in v3 the tree gauge. Suggested: an optional remark only, "the analogue of the conclusion of B85b Lemma 1".
*Across chapters:* occurs only in `09-stationary-remainder.tex`. The estimate it invokes is the nonlinear estimate 5:1019–1025 (subsection "The estimates in the block axial gauge and the Hessian", 5:1010), not the linear inequality 5:1046–1050, which is derived from it. 9s:145 now says "a fixed closed coordinate ball of the chart"; the norm of the ball (the combined supremum `max(‖x‖_∞, ‖y‖_∞)` of the source) is not stated.
*See also:* stationary chart; chart recognition; logarithm.

#### same-data restart conditions
*Now:* replaced by the sentence "The restarted representation keeps the original path and clipping coefficients and Gaussian law (Section (ch11:restart-construction))" (11:1672).
*Variants:* same-data requirement (source).
- **Meaning.** The requirement that every local estimate used at a step of the restarted history be proved for the very data entering that step's density identity: the original path coefficients and clipping coefficients, the original block kernel and the Gaussian law of the step, with only the threshold, the radius and the activity arrays changed. In v3 these are the conditions of Section ch11:restart-construction: "Its piecewise quadratic–linear function has the original two coefficients, evaluated at this new threshold. Its path coefficients and block-kernel branches are the original ones" (11R:19–23) and "The local chart, clipped inhomogeneous term, Gaussian precision and large fluctuation-field events are those of Chapter 6 with reference parameter `r(x_i)` and threshold `ϑ(x_i)`" (11R:44–46, upstream's wording since the merge of 26 November 2026). It is a set of hypotheses, not a further estimate.
  *Basis:* R (11:1672, which now names the conditions and cites Section ch11:restart-construction); S for the source term. *Where:* 11:1672. *Adopted:* *The restarted representation still uses the original path and clipping coefficients and the same Gaussian law (Section ch11:restart-construction)*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/restarted-rank-history.tex:603–612 ("Retain the two original beds and the original tube at this step. Their path attachment, diagonal identity, tower roll, metric floors and path bounds are properties of those paths and clips, not of the additive or forced coefficients. … so the upward path and high clip of this actual tube are exactly those of its incoming representation. This verifies the same-data requirement of the local handoff"); existence/actual-local-compiler-handoff.tex:4–7 ("The local estimates must hold for the very matrices and profiles used in the marked density identity … it does not introduce a new Gaussian law or replace the selected history"). No Lean declaration located.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. The sentences of 11:1670–1671 ("It does not transfer a bound from a different Gaussian law or change an incoming bound after the history is fixed") state the same requirement in v3's own words.
*See also:* restart; restarted history.

#### section
*Now:* unchanged.

#### sector allocation weights
*Formerly:* *sector allocation indicators*.
*In the text:* no longer; 9:81–82 now reads "retain all the weights defining the sectors", in chapter 6's words (a sector is defined by these weights, 6:85).
*Variants:* weights defining the sectors (9:81–82); no longer in the text: allocation indicators; sector allocation weights.
- **Meaning.** The factors by which the integrand is decomposed into sectors (6:67–89), kept as factors of the expanded integrand when the exponentials are expanded: for the index triple, the weight `∏_{p∈A_f} ϑ_f(r_p^f) ∏_{p∉A_f} (1 − ϑ_f(r_p^f))` and its analogue for the deviations of the coarse links, which sum to one over all pairs `(A_f, A_n)` (6:71–78), together with the condition that `A_c` is the coarse large-field set of the configuration (6:77–79) and the probability weights of the auxiliary index. "Expand exponentials as `e^V = 1 + (e^V − 1)` and retain all the weights defining the sectors" (9:81–82) says that these factors are not expanded or bounded away, so that the sum over sectors still reproduces the original integral. The weights for `A_f`, `A_n` are smooth functions; for `A_c` the factor is an indicator.
  *Basis:* R (9:81–82 with 6:67–89); S for the wording. *Where:* 9:81–82. *Adopted:* *the weights defining the sectors* (not *partition of unity*, which covers only the `ϑ` factors of 6:67–76).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:105`: "The formula is used only on compatible sectors; their sum retains the exact allocation indicators"; Scott `part2/B-section.tex:908–915` (Definition "Selections and allocation sectors"): "An *allocation sector* fixes these selected tests, their assignment to connected components of their neighbourhoods, a block tree, and the frame and predictor tags."
*Literature:* see *allocation* (sense 1).
*Across chapters:* a chapter 9 name for a chapter 6 object. Not the partition-of-unity weights alone: the auxiliary index, the trees and the coarse set belong to the sector as well.
*See also:* sector; allocation; allocation sector; likelihood.

#### seeded sector
*Now:* replaced on 25 November 2026 (sentence repair) by the index triple: "It does not compare the Gaussian law of a sector whose index triple has nonempty `A_f` or `A_n` with the law of the sector with `A_f=A_n=∅`" (6:1551); "Thus no comparison has been made between unrelated event indicators, or between the Gaussian law for an index triple with nonempty `A_f` or `A_n` and the law for `A_f=A_n=∅`" (9:284–285). "Seeded" and "unseeded" no longer occur in the chapter files (grep).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: unseeded law; seeded / unseeded.
- **Meaning.** A *seed* is a selected large-field element: a fine plaquette in `A_f`, a coarse edge in `A_n` (with the coarse sites `A_c`, these make up the large-field index triple `A = (A_f, A_n, A_c)` of 6:49–64). A *seeded sector* is an allocation sector whose selection is non-empty in the region concerned; its Gaussian law has the precision, mean and set of active coordinates determined by that selection. The *unseeded law* is the Gaussian law of the sector with `A_f = A_n = ∅` and `A_c` the actual coarse large-field set, on the same forest, with all free bonds active. Both v3 sentences are negative; before 25 November 2026 they read "It does not compare a seeded sector to an unseeded law" (6:1551) and "no comparison between unrelated event indicators or a seeded and an unseeded law has been made" (9:284–285), now as quoted under *Now*. They say that the comparison of the nonlinear and linear local laws is made only where the windows are clean, "a window meeting a large-field component of the index triple is attributed to that component" (9:280–281).
  *Basis:* S for "seed"; I for the two v3 sentences, which have no single source sentence. *Where:* formerly 6:1551; 9:284–285. *Adopted:* the index triple `A` with nonempty `A_f` or `A_n` / the law for `A_f = A_n = ∅` (the dictionary's proposal in substance). Left for the author by the review: the source's "seeds" also include coarse sites, and its reference law is formed at the identity coarse field (`repairs-review.md`, item 6).
  *Source:* Lean `YM.Pressure.Stores`, `YM/Pressure/Seeds.lean` (definition read): three finite sets `costs` (fine plaquettes), `aisles` (coarse bonds), `flags` (coarse sites); `YM.Push.SectorMeasure.Seeded`, `YM/Push/SECTOR_MEASURE/Cells.lean` (definition read): the two-sided threshold implications with `t_f/4`, `t_f/2`, `W t_f`, `2W t_f` at every fine plaquette and coarse bond, and `flags` equal to the actual coarse large-field set; the empty selection `YM.AnalyticBridge.LocalGaussianLaws.bareStores = ⟨∅,∅,∅⟩`, `YM/AnalyticBridge/LOCAL_GAUSSIAN_LAWS/Distinct.lean` (definition read). Martin `existence/gaussian-reassembly.tex:14–17`: "The reference `A_0` is formed at the identity coarse field with no seeds and the same forest: all free bonds are active"; Martin `existence/actual-reader-dawn-selection.tex:175–177`: "fix the seed-free store: both its seed sets are empty, and its flag set is exactly the set of flags of the actual coarse field".
*Across chapters:* undefined in v3 wherever it occurs; the reading rests on the uniform meaning of "seed" in the source manuscript and the formalisation. v3 now uses the index triple `A` of 6:49–64 in place of "seeded"/"unseeded". The "shared frame seed" of 13ba:251, 274 (now "auxiliary random variable") is a different use of "seed".
*See also:* shared frame seed; selected.

#### selected
*Now:* partly replaced by *index triple* (sense 1 in chapters 6 and 9: "A *large-field index triple*, for short an *index triple*", 6:49); *retained* (sense 3); *subfamily* (sense 4, 4:500, 659); *common trajectory*, *same family of measures*, *chosen* in several places of senses 2, 8 and 9; *fixed phase* (sense 7, decision of 26 November 2026: MT:91, 17:31, 353); remains on 102 lines with `select*` (none in chapter 6), in sense 1 in chapters 11 and 11R and in the other senses elsewhere (grep, labels excluded, 27 November 2026).
*Variants:* selection; select; selects; unselected (11R:314); no longer in the text: selector.
1. **Belonging to the large-field index triple.** A large-field index triple is a triple `A = (A_f, A_n, A_c)` of fine plaquettes, coarse edges and coarse sites ("A *large-field index triple*, for short an *index triple*, `A = (A_f, A_n, A_c)` consists of fine plaquettes, coarse edges, and coarse sites", 6:49–51); as such it satisfies no condition. `A_f`, `A_n` are chosen indices; a *consistent* index triple ("An index triple is consistent if", 6:54) requires `r_p ≥ t_f/4`, `n_e ≥ W t_f` on them and at most `t_f/2`, `2W t_f` off them (6:54–59); `A_c` is determined by the configuration (6:62–63, 77–78). In chapters 11 and 11R a "selected" large-field support, component, site factor or cutoff condition is one belonging to the large-field index set of the term; "unselected" (11R:265, 314) is its complement; chapter 6 now writes "not in `A_f`", "`e ∉ A_n`" (6:1348–1349) and "not retained" (6:1444). "`A_M` is the part of the index triple belonging to `M`" (9:109; "a single large-field condition of the index triple", 9:442): the index triple of the large-field component contained in the connected product `M`, and `|A_M|` in (ch09:joint-input) is its number of elements (S). The "selected site factor `X_z`" of 11R has its own entry.
   *Basis:* D (6:49–51). *Where:* ch. 6 (now "index triple", "in `A_f`", "not retained"); 9:109, 154, 280, 442 ("index triple", "chosen"); 11:141, 151, 153, 156, 250, 340, 425, 434, 520, 761, 926, 1938; 11R:64, 160, 171, 183, 287, 289, 302, 306, 313, 317 ("unselected" 11R:265, 314); 11E:81 ("large-field selection") (ch. 11 files about 25, still "selected"). *Proposed:* *large-field index triple `A`*; *belonging to `A`* (applied in chapters 6 and 9). Keep it distinct from `Bad_m(U)`.
   *Source:* for `A_M`: Scott part2/D-section.tex:170 ("Large-field components are the connected components of the neighbourhoods of the selected large-field tests … Their selections `A = (A_f, A_n, A_c)` consist of the selected fine plaquettes, mismatch edges and coarse flags; each retains `exp(−κ_B β'_u t_{m+1}² |A|)` before integration"; the bound displayed there, `∫ g_A dν ≤ P_j(𝔟)(1+s_A)^{d_j} e^{−κ'_B β'_u t_{m+1}² |A|} ∏ f_a`, is (ch09:joint-input) of 9:97–104).
2. **Belonging to the one history fixed by the construction.** "Selected trajectory / schedule / history / stage requirements / block kernels / plateau": the object fixed once in chapter 10 (and, in chapters 5–7, by the construction in hand); also the graph produced by the trajectory (12:135, 140). The selected history is, for every cutoff `N` and period `p`, the sequence of densities at the levels `m ≤ N` obtained from the Wilson density at level `N` by the block steps, with the bare coupling chosen so that the level-0 coupling is the prescribed `β̄`, and satisfying at each level the bounds of the schedule (coupling in `[β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`, increments `β_{m+1} − β_m − κ_G log L_m` within the stage tolerance). The "selected family" (13:397) is the family of Wilson measures on that history with its insertions; the "selected scale-`h` polynomial coordinates" (13ba:31; formerly "level-`h`") are the level-`h` coefficients of a trial in the same history, `J_h` being its coefficient map to level `h`.
   *Basis:* I from the v3 text; S for the conditions and for the assignment of 13:397 and 13ba:31. *Where:* (5:738 and 10:886 without the word since the titles of 26 November 2026, "Convergence of the Gaussian kernels at a fixed scale" and "… on the common trajectory") 5:858, 1390; 6:138, 170, 182, 367, 1564; 7:291, 562, 585, 676, 1215; 9:569; 10:926; 11:113, 617, 1050, 1064, 1206, 1407, 1970, 2061, 2181, 2187, 2299; 11R:90; 11E:34; 12:124, 134, 135, 140, 299, 372; 13:309, 397; 13sb:50; 13ba:19, 31, 50, 198, 203, 308; 17:11; 17w:22; 17c:136; 18:175; 19:19, 31. *Proposed:* delete, or *fixed*; where the object must be named, *the history fixed in Chapter 10* and *the same family of measures*; at 13ba:31 *their scale-`h` polynomial coordinates in the same history*.
   *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.History.Selected`, YM/RG/History.lean (definition read; fields `path_shared`: path data at level `m ≤ N` independent of the period; `represents`: `Conv N p m` for `m ≤ N`, i.e. the level-`m` bounds and `β_{N,p,m} ∈ [β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`, definition of `Conv` read; `starts`: at level `N` zero scalar and the bare Wilson density at `β_{N,p,N}`; `steps`: for `m < N` the level-`m` density is the block transform of the level-`(m+1)` density and `|β_{m+1} − β_m − κ_G log L_m| ≤ drift`; `reaches`: `β_{N,p,0} = β̄`; `running`: for every `ε > 0`, eventually in `m`, `|β_{N,p,m} − β̂_m| ≤ ε · S.scale m`); `YM.Family` and `YM.Family.Makes`, YM/Source/Construction.lean (definitions read in part; file title "Single Wilson family"; `Makes` has the field `wilson : C.path.Selected` and further fields on the local sections, reference levels and stencils). Martin existence/actual-phase-grid-approximants.tex:11–46: "Fix the selected family `C` … We use the paid selected-history data … the coefficient transport on this history"; :136–146: "a coefficient `b_s` in the same history's coefficient transport such that `‖e_s − I_k b_s‖_1 ≤ 1/4` … `I_k` is the coefficient identification at `k`". The identification of `J_h` (13ba:31) with Martin's `I_k` is by the matching bound and is inferred.
3. **Retained component.** A component of an affine map, or of a stencil, that is kept; now "retained component" ("the retained plaquette components and the retained components containing the averaging operation", 6:498).

#### selected slot
*Now:* removed; 11:424–425 now reads "The large-field factor carrying this input lies in no purely principal component".
*Variants:* forced slot, marked slot (source).
- **Meaning.** The place of one large-field activity in the polymer representation of the step, identified by its index: the support of the activity together with its prescribed set of large-field sites and its conditions. A large-field remainder of an insertion sits in one such place, where the activity is replaced by the factor carrying the insertion. "Its selected slot has no purely principal component" (11:424, now "The large-field factor carrying this input lies in no purely principal component") says that the factor carrying the insertion lies in no connected component made of small-field (principal) factors only ("component" being a connected union of terms, 11:331, 608; the source says "no ordinary principal cluster"), because that factor is itself a large-field factor; hence no principal bound is needed and only the nonprincipal and large-field estimates apply. The intermediate wording "gives no purely principal term" made a different claim (term for component) and has been withdrawn.
  *Basis:* S (11:424 gives no gloss). *Where:* 11:424. *Adopted:* *The large-field factor carrying this input lies in no purely principal component*; for the noun, *the index (support and prescribed set of large-field sites) of the large-field activity carrying the insertion*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/heading-history-handoff.tex:313–321 ("For an allowed forced slot `s`, let `f ≠ 0` be its local, gauge-invariant measurable insertion, with the slot's support and eligibility conditions … Its input profile equals `f` at the original support–inventory address and zero at every other address. It has no ordinary principal cluster: the marked slot is flagged, whereas that cluster requires an ordinary insertion. The nonprincipal and forced bounds thus give the zero-leading-coefficient bound without a principal bound"). Lean `YM.Source.Coefficient` with field `forced : ℕ → Config G n → ℂ`, `YM.Source.Coefficient.marked`, `YM.Source.Coefficient.Format` with fields `forcing`, `carried`, `supported` (YM/Source/Insertion.lean:27–61; definitions read: `marked R b U = Σ_{i∈b} forced i U · ∏_{j∈b.erase i} K_j U` on admissible `b`, and `forced i` is tied to the `i`-th large-field address of the representation). The structure `ForcedAddress` itself was not opened.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. This is a third sense of *slot*, distinct from the strips of chapter 1 and from the argument positions of chapters 13–18. The word "selected" there is counted under sense 1 of *selected*.
*See also:* slot.

#### separating family
*Now:* unchanged; "detecting families" at 14:226 is now "Finite free separating families".
*Also in the text for:* the former *detecting family*; *detection* (see those entries).
*Variants:* finite separating family; separating families; free separating family; quantitative separating families; (labels only) detector; no longer in the text: detecting family (14:226).
- **Meaning.** A finite family of correlation functionals, each the correlation with fixed insertions at fixed points, that is injective on a space of fields. Chapter 3 gives two: for a basis `(P_1, …, P_s)` of `M_d^Max` and fixed distinct points `x, y`, the map `P ↦ (S_2^Max(P, P_j; x, y))_{j=1}^s` is injective (Corollary "Polynomial positivity and finite separating families", 3:484–495); and there is a finite `D_*` with `𝒩_{D_*} ∩ 𝔓^G = {0}`, where `𝒩_D` is the set of polynomials whose correlations with every separated word of insertions `P_i ∈ M_D^Max` vanish (Proposition "A separating family of insertions of bounded scaling dimension", 3:797–809). Later chapters estimate the interacting correlations along such a family and call the result "the bound from a finite separating family" (11:29; 11E:182); "A common localization map for the separating family" (11:1146) is the map `T`; "bounded lifts of the separating family" (15:258) are polynomial preimages of its free fields.
  *Basis:* D (3:482: "A family of correlation functionals, each the correlation with fixed insertions at fixed points, is a *separating family* for a space of fields if no nonzero field of that space lies in the kernel of all of them", added by the conversion); R (3:484–495, 797–809). *Where:* 3:482, 484, 775–779, 806; 11:29, 989, 1083, 1102, 1146, 1354, 1593; 11E:169, 170, 182; 13:14, 397; 14:226, 839; 15:18, 252, 258; 19:27, 52, 100. *Proposed:* keep *separating family*, defined once in chapter 3; use it also for "detecting families" (14:226), "detection" (3:830; 11:963, 979; 11E:170) and "rank detection" (13sb:9). Applied at 14:226, 3:830 ("the separating property"), 11:979 ("to separate the quotient"), 11E:170 ("separating-family estimates") and 13sb:9 ("the separating families"); "detection" remains in the title of 11:963.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/E-section.tex:493–499`: "Choose finitely many one- or two-point tests. In test `i`, the first label is the variable `𝔪_j`; the optional second label is a fixed basis element. … The free test matrix is `𝒢_{ij} = S^Max_{n_i}(𝔪_j, test i spectator; y^i)`. The next lemma supplies a finite family that distinguishes every free field of degree at most `d`. Lemma (Free tests). … there are finitely many one- or two-point tests at generic configurations, with every second label a basis element, for which the matrix has rank `dim_ℂ 𝓜_d`"; Scott `part2/H-section.tex:160`: "Each row of trial `ℓ` consists of a singleton `u` and optional spectator `v`, placed at the comparison points `r_ℓ y^{ℓ,i}`."
*Across chapters:* one sense from chapter 3 to chapter 19. Not *nondegeneracy*: the text's own word is "separating family" (3:484, 806), which is kept. "Separated" (at pairwise distinct points, 1:359; 3:104, 144–145) is a different word and stays. The members of the family are functionals; the probes of chapter 18 are the words that define such functionals, and the "free tests" of 15:277–280 are the tests of the finite free family, which index the rows of the matrix of these pairings (see *row*, sense 8). The source states the family in this matrix form: for a real basis `𝔪_1 = 1, 𝔪_2, …` of the free field space, finitely many one- or two-point tests at generic configurations, each with a variable first label and an optional fixed second label, such that the matrix `𝒢_{ij}` of free correlations of `𝔪_j` in test `i` has rank equal to the dimension of the space.
*See also:* detection; detector; detecting family; probe; reference rows; separation; separated; spectator; lift; top polynomial extraction.
