#### shared frame seed
*Now:* replaced by *auxiliary random variable* (13ba:234–235, 274) and *shared auxiliary random variable* (13ba:251).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: frame seed; frame seeds; shared seeds.
- **Meaning.** The auxiliary random variable by which the gauge frame (local gauge transformation) at a coarse site is chosen in one block step. The block kernel is a mixture over a finite auxiliary index `α` of "all choices made for the local gauge transformations and for the averaging operation", with joint probability `λ(U,α)`; "The choices for the local gauge transformations are made first, followed by conditionally independent choices for the averaging operation" (4:230–232). 13ba realises these choices by "independent auxiliary random variables for those choices and for each coarse-link sample" (13ba:234–235). It is *shared* because the frame at a site enters every coarse link issuing from that site, so that coarse links are not conditionally independent given the fine field: "This does not assert that coarse links remain conditionally independent after a shared choice of local gauge transformation has been averaged out. The full cones, including that choice, must be disjoint" (13ba:244–246). Hence the ancestor cone of a stencil must contain "every input link and every shared auxiliary random variable for an output link" (13ba:251; without "shared" the claim would cover the coarse-link samples of 13ba:235 too), which lie within distance `(j_i+7)a_i` of its initial endpoint (13ba:252).
  *Basis:* R (13ba:233–246, 251; 4:230–232). *Where:* 13ba:235, 251, 274. *Adopted:* *the random variable choosing the frame at a coarse site* (*auxiliary random variables of the block step* for the collection).
*Across chapters:* 13ba only. It is unrelated to "seeded / unseeded" (6:1551; 9:284): there a seed is a selected large-field element (see *seeded sector*); here it is a source of randomness. The term and the requirement come from the review of the v3 draft, not from a source manuscript: `audit/bounded-coarse-approximation-review.md` item 1 ("Conditional factorization requires full random-seed cones. The actual block kernel is a mixture over shared frame choices, not a product in coarse links conditional only on the fine field. Include the independent frame seeds, predictor seeds, and link-noise seeds … in each ancestor cone"), recorded there as a correction to Scott part2/E-bounded-real.tex:23, which has only "the block kernels are products in the coarse-link variables given the preceding field". No Lean declaration was matched.
*See also:* seeded sector.

*Now:* replaced by *the estimate (ch18:signed-transport)* at 18:177, and by *signed local transfer* in the subsection title (18lp:24).
- **Meaning.** A nickname, cited once (now "Its construction requires the estimate (ch18:signed-transport), the stronger anchored marked support bound, and the graded quotient comparison", 18:176–178), for the estimate (18.signed-transport) of the subsection "Signed local transfer" (18lp:24–65). A local degree-`t` density with insertions at scale `l` is a column with coefficient `x_l` plus a remainder whose extracted coefficient is zero and whose remainder norm is at most `r_l`; the densities at successive scales of a sufficiently late interval `[k_*, m]` are related by one step with insertions, `H_l = L_l^t 𝓑_l H_{l+1}`. If a free column parameter at the finest scale `m` is chosen so that `x_{k_*} = 0`, then `r_l + |x_l|_1 ≤ 4(1+C_m) q_fin (a_m/a_l)^{1/8}` for `k_* ≤ l ≤ m` and `r_m ≤ 2(1+C_m) q_fin`, where `q_fin` is the combined coefficient and remainder bound of the original density at level `m`, before the column is subtracted. "Signed" is sense 2 of *signed*: the column is subtracted from the density as an equality of densities, before norms are taken ("The sign of the local difference has been retained throughout", 18lp:65; cf. 18:131–133).
  *Basis:* R (18lp:24, the subsection title; 18lp:48–55, the estimate). *Where:* 18:177; 18lp:24 (title). *Adopted:* *the estimate (18.signed-transport)*, cited by number. If a noun is wanted, moving a quantity through the block steps is *transfer* in this book, not *transport* (the title at 18lp:24 now says "transfer").
  *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:45–56`: "The next estimate retains the signed difference produced by subtracting a column. A transported family on `[k_*,m]` is a sequence of local marked expressions `c_l(b_l)+R_l`, `k_* ≤ l ≤ m`, in which `R_l` has coefficient zero and each term arises from the next finer one by one marked integration step … Its measured coefficient is `x_l = C_l b_l`, and `r_l` is its remainder bound"; Lemma "Signed local transport" (`lem:J-signed-local`), part (b): "If `x_{k_*} = 0`, then, for `k_* ≤ l ≤ m`, `r_l + μ(x_l) ≤ 4(1+C_m) q_fin (a_m/a_l)^{1/8}`, `r_m ≤ 2(1+C_m) q_fin`". Lean `YM.Bid.G09` (`YM/Bid/Loan.lean:133–136`; statement read), proved as `YM.Work.G09.answer` (`YM/Work/G09.lean:224`): for a `YM.Bid.Duet` on the levels `[k,o]` satisfying `YM.Bid.Duet.Woke` with parameter `w ≥ 0` (`Loan.lean:105–126`; definitions read: exact density relation between consecutive levels, zero coefficient at level `k`, `cost o ≤ w + C_o(w + |x_o|)`), and under the stage inequalities `roomCost`, `Bank` (`Loan.lean:36–46`; definitions read), `gainChart H o i · (cost i + |x_i|) ≤ 4(1+C_o) w` for `k ≤ i ≤ o`, where `gainChart H o i = exp((1/8)(scale o − scale i)) = (a_i/a_o)^{1/8}`; `YM.Work.G09.cost_finest` (`G09.lean:210–213`; statement read): `cost o ≤ 2(1+C_o) w`; `YM.Work.G09.cone_cost` (`G09.lean:183–188`; statement read): `32(1+C_i)² |x_i| ≤ cost i`, the cone of 18lp:61. The hypotheses `direction`, `Format`, `remBound` of `Woke` were not opened.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence of the nickname; the constants `4(1+C_m)`, `2(1+C_m)`, the exponent `1/8` and the cone constant `32(1+C)²` agree in v3, Scott and Lean.
*See also:* signed; transfer; anchored marked support bound; graded quotient comparison.

#### site conversion
*Now:* partly replaced by *change of cover radius* (sense 2: 11:515, 527–528; 11R:282, 322; 18lp:112); remains in sense 1 (9:515; 11:268, 502, 1923) and in sense 2 at 11R:143 ("the support conversions").
*Variants:* root-to-site conversion; support conversions (11R:143); no longer in the text: support conversion; support conversion cost `T_l`; support conversion constants.
1. **Site conversion (root-to-site conversion).** The passage from a bound for supports anchored (rooted) at a point to a bound for supports containing a given site, at the cost of one unit of the support exponent and a factor `𝒲(B)`: "The conversion of anchored bounds to containing-site bounds is explicit … An additional margin in the support exponent absorbs this polynomial" (9:515–519); "The site bound is `Σ` at exponent `v+1`. To see the latter conversion, root a support at one of its fine sites or insertion points …" (11:267–273); "Root-to-site conversion contributes only the factor `𝒲(B) = H^{o(1)}`" (11:1923).
   *Basis:* R (9:515–519; 11:267–273, 1923). *Where:* 9:515; 11:268, 502, 1923; 13ba:145. *Proposed:* *passage from anchored to containing-site bounds*.
2. **Support conversion.** The change of the exponential support weight from one cover radius or scale to another: `e^{(v+2)c_{B_c}(X^↑)} ≤ T_e e^{σ_f c_{B_f}(X)}` with `T_e = exp(15⁴(e+7))` ((ch11:cover-transfer), 11:230–240), from the fine cover number at radius `B_f` to the coarse cover number of the enlarged support. "Its full factor for the change of cover radius is `T_l ≤ L_l`, as in (ch11:cover-transfer)" (18lp:112–113). `T_e` is the constant of this step, not the cost of sense 1. In 11R the plural covers this and sense 1 together: "Eventually its old exponent absorbs this new exponent and the extra unit used to turn an anchored bound into a site bound. These are the support conversions" (11R:141–144).
   *Basis:* R (11:230–240; 18lp:112–113; 11R:141–144). *Where:* 11:515, 527–528; 11R:143, 282, 321–322; 18lp:112–113 ("change of cover radius" except at 11R:143). *Adopted:* *change of cover radius, (ch11:cover-transfer)*.
*Across chapters:* two operations: sense 1 in chapters 9, 11 and 13ba, sense 2 in chapter 11, 11R and 18lp; 13ba and 18lp use them without explanation and are settled by chapters 9 and 11 (11:228–240, 265–273 read). "Site bound" and "site sum" are the sums over the terms containing a site and belong under *containing-site bound*. The "incidence" bounds of chapter 11 (sum over terms containing a given insertion) are contrasted with the site bound.
*See also:* incidence; containing-site bound; connected covering number.

#### slab
*Now:* unchanged.
*Variants:* slab word; slab insertion; slab operator `B_h(w)`; reflected slab word `w^♯`; slab bounds; slab width; slab kernel; no longer in the text: slab margins (14:103 now "with buffer `r`").
- **Meaning.** "A word `w` lies in a slab of width `h` if `0 < x_i^μ < h` for each of its points. Its reflected slab word is `w^♯ = τ_hθ_μ w`" (14:89–91). Slab operators are the operators `B_h(w)` built from such words (14:101–108). The distances of the times `x_i^μ` from the two faces of the slab are covered at 14:103 by "with buffer `r`, `0 < r ≤ 1`", the buffer of 13:337 ("We call `r` its buffer in the slab of width `h`"). In chapter 11 a "slab kernel" is one of the factors `B_i` of the cyclic product of transfer operators `tr ∏ B_i T^{H_i}/Z`, the slab having width `w` (11:845–848).
  *Basis:* D (14:89–91, 101–108); R for the slab kernel (11:845–848). *Where:* 13:337, 393 (before the definition); 14:86–145; ch. 15; 16:35–37 (24 in chapters 12–16); 18:273; 19:93, 104; RG:44. Also 11:847–849, 879 ("`B_i` is a local slab kernel, the slab width is `w`"; "reflected-copy bound for a slab"). *Proposed:* keep; move the definition before 13:337 or refer forward.
*Across chapters:* one sense from chapter 13 on. That the slabs of the transfer words of 11:847–879 are the same notion is inferred.
*See also:* buffer; strip; transfer word.

*Now:* unchanged.
See *stationary tangent*. `W_a = W_s − d_{0,f}ERW_s` (5:1118) is a representative of the stationary tangent (the linearization `W` of the critical configuration) chosen for its fine-difference bounds; it is not the derivative of the critical-configuration map, which is the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge (5:1157–1160). The text says so at 7:583 ("The smooth representative of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration is `W_a` …; its representative in the block axial gauge is `W_F`"), at 17m:263 ("The smooth representative of the linearization of the critical configuration is `W_a = W_s − d_f E R W_s`") and at 17c:49–54 ("The first derivative of the nonlinear critical-configuration map … is the forest representative `W_F`").

#### smoothing order
*Now:* unchanged; since 25 November 2026 it also replaces "fine kernel order" and "coarse kernel order" at 11:351–352 ("fine smoothing order at least `d+2`, and coarse smoothing order at least `d+3`"), formerly "kernel level".
*Variants:* smoothing order `j`, `j_i`; fine, coarse smoothing order (11:351–352); no longer in the text: averaging order (5:303–305 now "smoothing orders"); fine kernel order, coarse kernel order (11:351–352); kernel level.
- **Meaning.** The number of box convolutions in the averaging weight of the averaging operation: "fix a positive integer *smoothing order* `j` (the number of convolution factors in the averaging weight `w^av` of Section (ch04:kernel-section))" (4:16). The local gauge transformation at each endpoint then reads a box of fine-lattice radius `(j_i+3)L_i` (13ba:248–249).
  *Basis:* D (4:16); S for 11:351–352 (the fine and coarse smoothing orders are the smoothing orders of the present step and of the step one scale coarser). *Where:* 4:16, 198, 349; 5:196–202, 303–305, 312; 7:609, 673 (`C_j`, inferred); 10:125 (`ȷ_j`); 11:351–352, 1685, 1747; 13ba:233–263; 17c:65 ("Here `j` is the smoothing order of the averaging weight, and `j≥5`"); 17m:230, 239, 251. *Adopted:* keep *smoothing order `j`*, defined once (4:16); *fine* and *coarse smoothing order* at 11:351–352 (decision 45 of 25 November 2026).
  *Source:* for 11:351–352, Martin existence/heading-history-handoff.tex:10–12 ("let `j,t ≥ 4` be the adjacent fine and coarse kernel levels"), :347 ("For each `d` with `d+3` at most the coarse kernel level"). Lean `YM.RG.Patch.J` with `order_cut : 4 ≤ J`, `YM.RG.Patch.Rolls`, `YM.RG.Patch.radius` (YM/RG/Patch.lean:29–62; definitions read), `YM.RG.Calendar.J`, `.adm`, `.params`, `.op` (YM/RG/History.lean:64–92; definitions read: the step from level `m+1` to `m` has `patch.J := J (m+1)`); hypotheses `d+3 ≤ H.levels.clock.J (r d)` in `YM/Next/FOUNDATIONS/Primary.lean:183` and `d+3 ≤ A.B.a.clock.J m` in `YM/MergeProof/Rosin.lean:79` (statements read at those lines only).
*Literature:* name clash; the object itself has no counterpart, since in all papers read the averaging weight is uniform over one block, `L^{-d}`. In Bałaban the **order** of a block, of an averaging operator or of a renormalization transformation is the number of composed steps: "block of an order j" (B85a p. 17), "k-th order averaging" (B85a p. 24: "if k-th order averaging `Ū^k` is defined at bonds of Ω^(k), then `Ū^{k+1} = \overline{(Ū^k)}`"), "averaging operators of different orders", "renormalization transformations of different orders" (B84b p. 223), "block of k-th order `B^k(y)`" (B87 p. 267). "Order of the averaging kernel" for `j` would therefore be misread. Adopted (23 November 2026): keep *smoothing order `j`*, defined at 4:16 as the number of box convolutions in the averaging weight; the earlier proposal "order of the averaging kernel" is withdrawn, for the reason just given. The letter `j` clashes with the stage index.
*Across chapters:* one sense. The letter `j` is also the stage index (chapter 9; defined 10:25); chapter 10 writes `ȷ_j` for "the largest smoothing order used in stage `j`" (10:125). That the `j` of chapter 7 is the smoothing order at every occurrence is inferred.
*See also:* stage.

#### source
*Now:* partly replaced by *insertion* (sense 4, e.g. 11E:83; 13sb:66; 13ba:123, 158; 18lp:29, 180), *inhomogeneous term* (sense 5) and *differentiated kernel* (17m:68, 155, 391, 400, 412, 440, 456); remains on 131 lines (labels excluded; 137 after the merge and the decisions of 26 November 2026, grep of 27 November, some in margin notes citing the sources), mostly in senses 1 (source variable, source degree, source weight) and 6, and in sense 4 at 11:135, 769; 12:285; 13sb:73, sense 7 at 18:414 and RG:82, sense 8 at 13sb:15, 64, 74; 17w:13, 78.
1. **Source variable.** The nilpotent variables `z_i` (`z_i² = 0`) of the source algebra, generating variables for the insertions; "linear in the sources", "source monomial `z_S`", "source degree".

2. **Source weight.** See *source weight*.
3. **Source algebra.** See *squarefree source algebra*.
4. **The inserted factor itself.** The source polynomial, the inserted observable or its density ("corrected source", 11:769; "the regular source at the ultraviolet cutoff", 11:135; "full-source", 12:285); an insertion; in `17-marked-trace-rates.tex` the inserted differentiated-kernel factor `𝒟_Y k` and the former "regular local insertions" (now "the regular local terms of the differentiated kernel"), the local expressions (`div_Haar Y − D𝓛[Y]` etc.) whose Taylor coefficient is extracted. The text now says "insertion" or "density with insertions" in most of these places ("the full transferred negative insertion", 13ba:158; "the dimensionful density with insertions", 18lp:29, 180) and "differentiated kernel" for `𝒟_Y k` and, since 25 November 2026, for the regular local insertions ("the regular local terms of the differentiated kernel", 17m:193) (17m:68, 155, 391, 400, 412, 440, 456; "the full differentiated kernel", 17m:68).

5. **Inhomogeneous term.** `b_Y`, the inhomogeneous term of the affine map of chapter 6, with `f_Y = D*b_Y` the linear coefficient of the quadratic form ("The inhomogeneous term `b_Y` in (ch06:actual-matrix)", 6:589); and the inhomogeneous term of a linear recursion ("No constant inhomogeneous term", 17c:133; "the equal-order inhomogeneous term from `J`", 17c:382).
   *Basis:* R (6:455–456, 587–618; 17c:133). *Where:* 6:455–456, 587–618; 9:926 ("clipped frozen inhomogeneous term"); 10:903; 11R:44; 17c:133, 226, 246, 382, 384, 387. *Adopted:* *inhomogeneous term*; *linear coefficient* for `f_Y`.

   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 8:255, 269, 271, 272, 367. Chapter 3 has the word only in the physicists' "source-free" (Maxwell equations without current: 3:69, 163, 554); 3:409, cited here before, does not contain it. *Proposed:* keep (standard).

#### sparse stopping scale
*Now:* replaced by *stopping scale* ("The stopping-scale argument", 18lp:159; "at the stopping scale `k=k(m)` of Section (ch13:sharp-section)", 10:175, on 25 November 2026). "Sparse" no longer occurs with it (grep).
*Variants:* sparse stopping; sparse-stopping argument.
- **Meaning.** The stopping scale is the level `k = k(m)`, "the first scale `k ≥ m` with `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k`" (13sb:105–106), for which `(a_m/a_k)⁴ q_k^site ≤ (L_{k−1}B_{k−1}²)⁴ q_k^site = o(τ_k)` (13sb:105–110); the last condition of the schedule (10:170–175) is imposed so as to "make the per-cell normalization cost `o(τ_k)` at the stopping scale `k=k(m)` of Section (ch13:sharp-section)" (10:174–175; until 25 November 2026 "keep replication costs subpower at a nearby sparse stopping scale"). "Nearby" is `τ_k/τ_m → 1` (13sb:118). "Sparse" refers to the grid of reflected insertions seen from level `k`: one insertion per cell of the reflected tiling of scale `a_m`, so that at level `k` the insertions ("reflected insertion points at the stopping scale") are `a_m/a_k ≥ B_k²` lattice units apart (13sb:86–87), far more than the support radius `B_k`. The condition `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k` is the definition of a *stopping pair* `(m,k)` in the source.
  *Basis:* R for the level (13sb:105–110); S for "sparse", with I for the last step: the source says "sparse insertion grids" and gives the spacing, but no sentence defines "sparse stopping scale". *Where:* 10:175; 18lp:159 ("stopping-scale argument", which refers to 13sb:105–118). *Adopted:* *the stopping scale `k = k(m)`*, citing the section of 13sb; "sparse" dropped (10:175, 25 November 2026).
  *Source:* Scott part2/E-section.tex:111–117: "The following choice gives both the sparse insertion grids and the windows used for free comparison", followed by Lemma "Scale and period choices", whose last requirement is `(a_m/a_{k(m)})^4 q_{k(m)} = o(s_{k(m)})`; part2/E-several-mark.tex:188, 208: "A stopping pair is a pair of levels `m ≤ k` with `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k`"; "The reflected anchors at level `k` have spacing `a_m/a_k ≥ B_k²` … Since `B_{i+1}² ≤ 2B_i²` and `ℓ_i ≥ 3`, their spacing is at least `B_i²` at every finer level"; part2/E-section.tex:362: "the stopping level `k = k(m)` of Lemma E1.1; the choice of `k(m)` makes the per-cell site cost negligible against `s_k`".
*Across chapters:* a forward reference in chapter 10 (10:172–175, formerly with the "Haar-ball normalization argument" and the "replication costs"; since 25 November 2026 with references to (ch11:replicated-bound) and Section (ch13:sharp-section)) settled by chapters 11 and 13. Martin's text does not use "sparse" in this sense. No Lean declaration was searched for.
*See also:* Haar-ball normalization argument; replication costs; stopping.

#### spectator
*Now:* partly replaced by *exterior function* (sense 2: 2e:41, 195, 205, 213, 221); remains in sense 1 as adopted, now defined at 3:705 (69 lines, chapters 3–19; 66 after upstream's merge of 26 November 2026, grep of 27 November, labels excluded). At 2e:254, before the definition, "all spectators" is now "all other insertions of the correlations" (the words of 3:705).
*Variants:* spectator fields, list, legs; spectator word; quadratic spectator; no longer in the text: exterior spectator.
1. **The other insertions in a correlation.** The insertions (fields, word) other than the distinguished one, against which a correlation is evaluated: in a correlation `S(A, x; B, y)` of two concatenated lists, the list `B` at the points `y`, kept at a fixed distance from the points `x`. Two labels represent the same field when their correlations with every spectator list agree. Defined at 3:705: "lists of *spectators*, the remaining insertions `P_1, …, P_n` of the correlation". From 3:837 the "quadratic spectator" is brought close to `P`, so it is not passive there.
   *Basis:* D (3:705). *Where:* 3:705, 782, 824–873; 11:1033, 2098, 2187, 2281; 11E:74–74, 162, 168; ch. 12–16, 33 (13: 10; 18gq: 2; 18lp: 3; 14: 15; 14lc: 1; 16: 2); 17t:144; 17m:67, 394–418; 18:7, 75, 118, 143, 156, 185, 234; 18r:45; 19:29. *Adopted:* keep *spectators*, defined once as the remaining insertions of the correlation.
   *Source:* Scott `part1/02-definitions.tex:216`: "two labels represent the same field when every spectator sees the same answer. The response `ι_d[c]` records those correlations against every spectator list … Write `v(x) = (v_1(x_1), …, v_n(x_n))` for a spectator word"; `:293`: "The product expansion replaces a cluster of nearby fields by fields at one point, inside correlations with distant spectators. … write `S^ζ(A, x; B, y)` for the correlation of the concatenated lists … spectators `y` are `δ_sp`-clear if `|o − y_j| ≥ δ_sp`".
2. **Exterior function.** In `02-equation-section.tex` the bounded measurable function `S` "depending only on links with both endpoints farther than `r_d` from `o` (an *exterior function*)" (2e:39–41).
   *Basis:* D (2e:39–41). *Where:* 2e:41, 195, 205–206, 213, 221 ("exterior function"). *Adopted:* *the function `S`*; *exterior function*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/A-section.tex:180`: "An exterior spectator outside `𝔹_r(y)` is a bounded measurable function of the positive links having both endpoints outside `𝔹_r(y)`; it need not be gauge invariant."
*Literature:* name clash. In D2 **spectator variables** are the fields left in holes from earlier stages and no longer integrated (D2 p. 092301-61: "holes which localize spectator variables left over from the early stages of the expansion"), the analogue of v3's frozen links (see *frozen*), not the other insertions of a correlation (sense 1), which have no counterpart. Suggested: keep v3's defined sense, and do not use "spectator" for frozen or conditioning variables.
*Across chapters:* sense 2 only in 2e, where the word no longer stands (2e:254 now says "all other insertions of the correlations", in sense 1; whether only the exterior functions `S` were meant there is left to the author); sense 1 from chapter 3 to chapter 19. The word is kept rather than replaced by *the remaining insertions* or *auxiliary insertion*: it is used throughout, and "exterior word", "exterior insertions", "external positions" reduce to it.
*See also:* spectator responses.

#### stage
*Now:* unchanged; "regularity-stage index" is replaced by *stage* (4:694), "adjacent pair of stages" by *pair of stages of one step* (5:689) and *stage pair* (10:30).
*Variants:* stage `j`; stage index `J_m`, `J(m)`; stage bound, constant, threshold, requirement, orders; stage pair; adjacent stage pair; change of stage; fixed-stage tail; plateau (10:124); no longer in the text: stage plateau (since the merge of 26 November 2026); regularity stage; regularity-stage index; stage floor.
- **Meaning.** "A stage `j ≥ 1` specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds" (10:25–26); the stages are nested, and at a fixed stage there are only finitely many permitted "*stage pairs* (the stages of the two scales of one step)" (10:28–31). The stage in force at level `m` is `J(m) = j` for `A_j ≤ m < A_{j+1}` (10:130–135); "`J(m+1)` is the stage used for this step" (10:51); `L_i = 𝓛_{J_i}` with `J_i = J(i+1)` (17w:15–16). It is not a renormalisation step and not a scale: "the *stage* `J_m` in force at scale `m` (a stage specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds; see Section (ch10:choices)); the stage index is different from the scale index `m`" (4:694–695). The uses in chapters 5 and 6, which precede the definition, have this sense: the "pair of stages of one step (Section (ch10:choices))" of 5:689 is the pair of stages of the fine and the coarse side of one step, and "Fix a stage" (6:21), "the fixed stage" (6:99) fix this numerical data, on which the constants may depend.
  *Basis:* D (10:25–31; index 10:130–135; recalled with a forward reference at 4:694); S for the use at 6:21, 99. *Where:* 4:694; 5:689; 6:21, 99; 7:22, 843, 1069, 1080, 1082, 1085, 1216; 9:111, 423, 429, 930, 937; 9s:88, 219; files 10 / 11 / 11R / 11E: 32 / 27 / 7 / 7 lines; ch. 12–16: 26 lines, one of them the idiomatic "at this stage" (14:67); ch. 17–19: 26 (17:132; 17w:2, 7, 14, 15, 49, 50, 69, 71, 97, 125; 17c:12, 108, 136, 239; 17m:39, 141, 197, 301, 346, 347, 427; 19:30; RG:34, 35). *Proposed:* keep *stage `j`*, defined once at 10:25 ("A stage `j ≥ 1` specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds") and referred to at first use in each chapter, with a forward reference at 5:689 and 6:21; never for a scale or a step.
  *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.Stage`, `YM/RG/History.lean` (definition read): a record of a cutoff profile `clip`, `order ≥ 6`, `power ≥ 2`, `supportExponent`, `width`, `paths`, `drift`, `columns`; `YM.RG.Calendar` in the same file (definition read): `stage : ℕ → Stage`, `J : ℕ → ℕ`, `params m := stage (J m)`, the step `op m p` built with patch order `J (m+1)`, and `Fits.stepSlow : J (m+1) ≤ J m + 1`. For chapter 6: `YM.Pressure.Teller`, `YM/Pressure/Seeds.lean` (definition read) has two stages `top`, `below` and an index `j`, and `Teller.Funds` requires the patch order to equal `j` and the two cutoff profiles to be those of `top` and `below`.
*Literature:* name clash; v3's object (a stage `j`, which specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds, 10:25–31) has no counterpart, since `L`, `M` and one set of constants are fixed for all steps (B87 p. 264, Theorem 3; D1 p. 1330010-28). In D2, D3 a **stage** is a step of the iteration (D2 p. 092301-19: "At the kth stage of the iteration we will introduce not one but two new small field regions"; D3 p. 2133: "a sum over the choice of large and small field regions at each stage"). Adopted (23 November 2026): keep *stage `j`*, restricted to `j` and described as the text does at 10:25 ("A stage `j ≥ 1` specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds"), never as a "regularity class" or "regularity stage": "regular" is kept for Bałaban's two uses (the regular part of the action; regularity condition, regular configuration). Add a note that in Dimock "stage" means step.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout. Not *regularity class `j`*, *regularity stage* or *regularity level*, as names or as descriptions: "regular" is kept for the regular part of the action and for the regularity condition, and the third also collides with level `m`. The conditions for entering a stage ("stage entrance") are the lower bounds on the starting scale. 17w:97 ("imposed at the stage of the coarsest scale of the interval of scales, … not multiplied once per step") uses the word for the stage in force at a scale. The letter `j` is shared with the smoothing order; in the formalisation the smoothing order of the step `m+1 → m` is the stage index `J(m+1)`, so the two letters denote the same number there.

#### stationary background
*Now:* replaced by *critical configuration* (5:7, 14; title 5:1166), glossed at 5:7 as "the critical configuration, the background field for the nonlinear action"; "the background" remains at 5:1234, 1299.
*Variants:* background.
- **Meaning.** The critical configuration of chapter 5, called there "the critical configuration, the background field for the nonlinear action" (5:7); "the background" at 5:1234 and 5:1298–1299, the action "whose germ at zero defines the background".
  *Basis:* I; R for 5:7. *Where:* 5:7, 14 ("critical configuration"), 1156 (title), 1222, 1287 ("background"). *Proposed:* *background field*.
*Literature:* **background field** (B85d p. 277; B85c p. 389, abstract: "These propagators depend on an external gauge field configuration, called a background field"; B85e p. 259; D2 p. 092301-42: "hence on the background field φ⁰_{k+1,Ω}(□*) and the fluctuation field W_k"; BIJ85 p. 308: "expand (3.24) into background and fluctuation parts"). The same object in role; the differences are those stated under *stationary graph*: Bałaban's background field is a `k`-step minimiser under a delta-function constraint, and the effective action is a function of it (B87 (1.3)), whereas v3's is the one-step critical point of action plus penalty. Adopted (24 November 2026): *background field*, as in the first decision of 23 November 2026. The later change of that day to *critical configuration* is reverted for this entry, because it rested on an inference: the text does not define "stationary background" (basis I). *Background field* is the word for any configuration about which one expands, or at which operators are evaluated or differentiated (Bałaban's "propagators in a background field"; v3 chapter 7); *critical configuration* remains the word for the stationary field `ρ(v)` (see *stationary graph*). The difference from Bałaban's background field is stated at first use (see *stationary graph*): his is a minimum at fixed averages (his "minimal configuration"), v3's a stationary point of fine action plus block penalty for one step.
*Across chapters:* chapter 5; "background insertions" in chapter 17 belong to the entry *background*.
*See also:* stationary graph.

#### stationary graph
*Now:* replaced by *critical-configuration map* (the map `ρ`: 5:979, 1155, 1178, 1321, 1340, 1348, 1385; 7:526, 962, 966, 1163, 1165; 9s:43; 10:925, 927; 17c:49) and *critical configuration* (its value, and the former "branch": 5:1166; 7:509, 561–562, 776; 9:293; 9s:40; 10:923; 17c:10, 141, 186–187, 397–398).
*Also in the text for:* the former *stationary branch* (see those entries).
*Variants:* critical-configuration map; critical configuration; jets of the critical configuration; no longer in the text: stationary branch; selected branch; stationary solution; stationary jets; stationary formula.
- **Meaning.** The locally unique solution `ψ = ρ(v)` of the stationarity equation `D_ψ f = 0`, as a function of the coarse field: "write `ρ(x)` for its critical configuration and `A(x) = D_y²φ(x, ρ(x))` for its positive Hessian" (9s:40–41). The "jets of the critical configuration" are its Taylor coefficients (10:720; "implicit-differentiation formula", 10:339).
  *Basis:* D (5:1155–1192); R (9s:40). *Where:* 5:979, 1155–1192, 1321, 1340, 1348, 1385; 7:509, 526, 561–562, 776, 962, 966, 1165; 9:293; 9s:40, 43; 10:339, 720, 923–927; 17c:10, 141, 186–187, 397–398 (all with "critical configuration" or "critical-configuration map"; 10:339 with "implicit-differentiation formula"). *Adopted:* *critical configuration* for the value `ρ(v)`; *critical-configuration map `ρ`* for the field as a function of the coarse field. *Background field* is kept for any configuration about which one expands, or at which operators are evaluated or differentiated; `ρ(v)` is called a background field only in that role. At first use state the difference from Bałaban's background field: his is a minimum of the action at fixed averages (his "minimal configuration"), for `k` steps at once; v3's is a stationary point of fine action plus block penalty, for one step. Not *minimizer*: what this entry records is the stationarity equation `D_ψ f = 0` and the words "positive Hessian" (9s:40–41), not a proof that `ρ(v)` is a minimum. For "stationary jets", *Taylor coefficients of the critical-configuration map*.
*Literature:* **background field**, **minimal configuration** `U_k(V)`, **critical configuration**, **critical point**, **critical orbit**, **minimal orbit**, the solution of "the variational problem" (B85d p. 277, abstract: "we prove that there exists a minimum of this action. The minimum is unique up to gauge transformations. This minimal configuration is called a background field"; p. 278: "Elements of the minimal orbit are called minimal configurations"; p. 279: "Minimal configurations will be denoted by `U_k(V)`, or `U_k`"; B84b p. 226: "exactly one critical configuration, which is of course, a minimum"; B87 p. 256: "These critical configurations are the minimal configurations investigated in [15] … These configurations are the background fields"; p. 265: "there exists the exactly one critical point … denoted by V^{(k)}"; B85e p. 259: "the minimal configuration U_1 is called a background field"); **minimizer** (B88a p. 1: "propagators and minimizers"; D1 p. 1330010-8: "expand around the minimizer. We write Φ_k = Ψ_k + Z", one-step `Ψ_k(Φ_{k+1}, φ)`, composite `φ_k = a_kG_kQ_k^TΦ_k`; B95 p. 110: "there exists exactly one critical point of the function A_k. This point is a minimum … We denote this minimal configuration by φ_k"); **classical field** (BIJ85 p. 301). The dependence on the coarse field: "`U_k = U_k(V)` … an analytic function of `V`", with expansion function `ℋ(B)` (B85d p. 305). Two classifications were given. Against the gauge-field papers (B84b, B85d, B87, B85e) it is an analogue: Bałaban minimises the Wilson action on the finest lattice over configurations with fixed averages `Ū^k = V` (delta-function constraint, `k` steps at once, on a gauge orbit) and proves a minimum; v3 solves a stationarity equation for fine action plus block penalty, for one step, on one chart. Against D1, B95, B96 it was called the same object in role: there the kernel is Gaussian as in v3, and in B95, B96 the minimiser is nonlinear and obtained by contraction as in v3 (in D1 it is linear and global). The reading taken here is "analogue" for a gauge-theory reader, with the scalar papers as the closest model, because v3's field is a gauge field and its graph is a one-step object. Calling `ρ(v)` "the background field `U_k(V)`" without qualification would mislead (hard against soft constraint; `k`-step against one-step). The dictionary's caution "say minimiser only where a gap is proved" agrees with Bałaban's own distinction between critical and minimal configurations. Adopted (23 November 2026): *critical configuration* for the value `ρ(v)` and *critical-configuration map `ρ`* for the map, in place of the earlier *critical-point map `ρ`*; this refines the decision of the same day, which had *background field* for both. *Background field* is any configuration about which one expands, or at which operators are evaluated or differentiated (Bałaban's "propagators in a background field"; v3 chapter 7); *critical configuration* is the specific one determined by the coarse field, the stationary point of action plus penalty. "Minimal configuration" (Bałaban) and "minimizer" (Dimock) only where minimality is proved. The difference from Bałaban's `V ↦ U_k(V)` (delta-function against Gaussian constraint, `k` steps against one step, minimum against stationary point) is stated at first use.
*Across chapters:* one object, named *critical-configuration map* (the map) and *critical configuration* (its value) in chapters 5, 7, 9, 10 and 17c: 10:923–925 names "critical configuration" and "critical-configuration map" in consecutive sentences for the same datum of a history, and 9s:40, 43 writes `ρ(x)` for the critical configuration and calls `ρ` the critical-configuration map (both read). "Branch" in the sense of a case of a piecewise definition does not occur here; "a common analytic branch" (5:952) is a branch of an analytic continuation. A different object from the "graph" `G` of 11:379–382 and 12:82–95, which keeps that name.
*See also:* stationary chart; stationary tangent; stationary substitution.

#### stationary residual
*Now:* replaced by *mean-equation residual* (9:131) and *residual of the mean equation* (9:77).
*Variants:* mean-equation residual; residual of the mean equation; linear Gaussian residual; no longer in the text: stationarity residual; linear residual.
- **Meaning.** The vector `η = −g^{-1}(𝖠 m_Y + f_Y)`, `g = β^{-1/2}`: the coefficient of the linear term `η·z` in the exponent of the exact Gaussian identity (ch06:gaussian-identity), 6:666–671. It measures by how much the mean `m_Y = −P^* f_Y`, built from the window inverse `P`, fails the stationarity (mean) equation `𝖠 m + f_Y = 0` of the quadratic form `Q_Y`, and it vanishes when `m_Y = −𝖠^{-1} f_Y`. Since `𝖠 m_Y + f_Y = (I − 𝖠P^*) f_Y`, it is bounded by `C g^{-1} t_f e^{−cB}`, which is exponentially small in `B` because `g^{-1} t_f` grows slower than `e^{εB}` (6:621–629); this is the majorant `P_j 𝔟^{c_j} e^{−c'_j B}` of the row "covariance and mean-equation residual" (formerly "covariance and stationary residual") at 9:131–132, the "covariance" part being the quadratic term `Γ^{-1} − 𝖠`. At 9:76–77 it is one of the local exponential factors kept after the flat determinant is extracted. Not defined in chapter 9; 6:1263 calls it "linear Gaussian residual", 6:674–675 "the remaining linear … term in the exponent".
  *Basis:* R (6:621–629, 666–675; 9:131–132); S for the name. *Where:* 9:77 ("residual of the mean equation"), 130 ("mean-equation residual"). *Adopted:* *the residual `η = −g^{-1}(𝖠 m_Y + f_Y)` of the mean equation*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:1088–1096` (Lemma "Window covariance bounds"): `|D^r[g^{-1}(𝖠_Y m_Y + f_Y)]_i| ≤ C_k e^{−cB} υ_i^r`; `:1087` "Its mean and stationarity-residual bounds"; `:1269` `η_Y = −g^{-1}(𝖠_Y m_Y + f_Y)`; `:1277` "the exponents of the retained factor vanish exactly when `m_Y = −𝖠_Y^{-1} f_Y` and `Γ = 𝖠_Y^{-1}`"; Scott `part2/D-section.tex:154`: row "Gaussian-density and stationarity residuals `P_j 𝔟^{c_j^res} e^{−c_j^tail B}`"; `:162`: "The covariance and sector mean-equation residuals are exponentially small by Lemma B-windows; their rescaling introduces only the displayed fixed power."
*Across chapters:* a chapter 9 name for a chapter 6 object. It is not a residual of the stationarity equation of the full action (the stationary point `ρ(x)` of chapter 9s), but of the mean equation of the sector quadratic form.
*See also:* residual (senses 1, 3); determinant inverse identity.

#### stationary tangent
*Now:* replaced by *linearization of the critical configuration* (5:528, 1091, 1246; 6:954, 960; 7:583, 790, 892; 11:642; 17c:8, 211; 17m:263); its representatives are *the smooth representative `W_a`*, *the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge* (5:1161, 1246; 6:954; 7:583; 9s:194; 11:642), and *the representative `W_s` built with the linear averaging operator* (5:1094; 7:1125).
*Variants:* linearization (`W`) of the critical configuration; `W_a`, `W_s`, `W_F`; smooth representative `W_a`; representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge; forest representative `W_F` (17c:50); no longer in the text: (actual, straight, smooth) stationary tangent; tangent `W`; linearized critical configuration (6:960); representative in the block axial chart (5:1246; 9s:194).
- **Meaning.** The derivative at zero of the stationary graph, a linear map from coarse to fine link variables: "The first derivative of the nonlinear critical-configuration map, from coarse to fine link variables with block ratio `L`, is the forest representative `W_F` of (ch05:stationary-tangent)" (17c:49–51; before 24 November 2026 the text had "Let `W` be the actual stationary tangent from coarse link variables to fine link variables … The first derivative of the nonlinear stationary substitution is this `W`"). In the forest coordinates, in which the critical-configuration map `ψ = ρ(v)` is constructed, this derivative is the forest representative `W_F`: `rep v + ι_F Dρ(0)v = W_F v` (5.stationary-tangent, 5:1157–1160); "Its linearization is the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge of Chapter 5" (9s:194–195). `W_F v` is `W_a v` plus "the unique gradient `d_{0,f}φ` whose site potential is zero at every block root and makes all tree edges vanish" (5:1149–1151). Two further operators represent the same tangent modulo fine gradients and have the same curl: `W_s`, "the operator `W` built with the linear averaging operator `M`" (5:1094), which satisfies `K_f W_s = M^*K_c`, `M W_s = I − b^{-1}K_c` (5:1097); and `W_a = W_s − d_{0,f}ERW_s` (5:1118; "Its difference from `W_s` is a fine gradient", 17m:263–264), which satisfies the same identities with `𝒬 = M + d_{0,c}R` in place of `M` and "`W_a` is the smooth representative of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration, whereas `W_F` is its representative in the block axial gauge" (5:1246; also 5:1161; 7:583). The present text names the derivative `W_F` at 17c:49–51 and computes with the smooth representative: "Since `W_F − W_a` is a fine gradient, the Ward identities of `E_b` allow us to compute with the smooth representative `W = W_a`" (17c:53–54; also 17c:113–114), so the letter `W` of 17c is `W_a`. A radial `W^rad` is named with them and not glossed.
  *Basis:* D (5:1155–1192; 17c:49–51) for `W`; R for `W_s`, `W_a` (5:1094, 1118) and for `W_F` as the derivative in forest coordinates (5:1157–1160; 9s:193–195); S for the statement that the stationary map of chapter 17 is the forest-coordinate one. *Where:* 5:528, 535, 1091, 1094, 1118, 1155–1192 (1151), 1234; 6:960; 7:583, 790, 892; 9s:194; 11:642; 17c:8, 49, 53–56, 63–65, 67–68, 84, 113, 188, 211, 350; 17m:263–264; 17t:165 (chapter 17 list redone on 25 November 2026: 17c:56–84 now compute with `W_s`; 17c:324 no longer names the linearization). *Adopted:* *the linearization `W` of the critical configuration*, defined once as the derivative `W_F` at zero of the critical-configuration map `ρ` (5.stationary-tangent); keep the symbols `W_s`, `W_a`, `W_F` and say each time which of the three is meant: `W_F` the derivative itself, in forest coordinates; `W_a` *its smooth representative*; `W_s` the operator built with the linear averaging operator `M`. At 7:583 and 17m:263, where the text had "the smooth representative of the actual (stationary) tangent is `W_a`", it now has "The smooth representative of the linearization (`W`) of the critical configuration is `W_a`" (applied). No symbol is renamed, and the representative is written wherever `W` is unqualified: `W_s` at 5:527–535, `W_F` in chapter 11 (11:642), `W_a` in `17-current-contraction.tex`. Do not call `W_F` "axial gauge minimizer" or `W_a` "Landau gauge minimizer": that pairing with BIJ85 is an unchecked conjecture (see *Literature*) and may be mentioned only as such.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:473`, `483` (Lemma B3(ii): "`rep v + ι_ax Dψ(0)v` is the tree representative of `W_0 v`"), `386–389` (`W_r = W_s − d_f I_ℓ(𝓕_m W_s)`, `W_0 = W_r`); `part2/I-section.tex:162`. Lean (all in namespace `YM.Precision`): `mean`, `fixRoot`, `probe := mean S + d 0 c * fixRoot S`, lemma `root_gradient` (`probe (d_f v) = d_c (v restricted to block roots)`), `YM/PREC/FrameResponse.lean` (definitions and statement read: `M`, `R`, `𝒬` and (5.actual-Q)); `Inputs`, `straighten`, `extracted`, `stays`, `stationed`, `action`, `YM/PREC/TreeMatch.lean` (definitions and statements read); `Critical`, `Guessed`, `YM/PCalc/Chart.lean` (definitions read); `YM.Work.F04.tangent`, `YM/Work/F04.lean` (statement read). Table of correspondences: v3 `W_s` = Scott `W_s` (centred) = the Lean matrix `W` satisfying `Inputs`; v3 `W_a` = Scott `W_r = W_0` (rooted, smooth) = no Lean counterpart found; v3 `W_F` = Scott tree representative / `W_ax` = Lean `extracted S F W`. The first and third Lean correspondences are by agreement of formulas; what is established and what is inferred is set out under *actual stationary tangent* (sense 2).
*Literature:* the **operator `H_k`** (later `H`, `H(U)`, `H_1`), with no noun in Bałaban's gauge papers: the "minimum" or "minimal configuration" of the quadratic form at fixed average, `H_kB = GQ*(QGQ*)^{-1}B` (B84a p. 26: "With this integral an operator of fundamental importance is connected … its value on such a configuration is equal to a configuration `A` on `T_η` minimizing the form `½⟨∂A,∂A⟩` under the conditions `Q_kA = B`, `R∂*A = 0`"; p. 34, (1.103); B85c p. 417, (3.109)–(3.110): "we define `H(U)B`, or simply `HB`, as a minimal configuration of the functional"; B85d p. 285; B85e p. 263: "`𝓗(B) = HB + A_1`, where HB corresponds to a linearized theory"; B88a p. 2, (1.2)); in BIJ85 the linear operators are called **axial gauge minimizer** `H_{k,Ax}` and **Landau gauge minimizer** `H_k`, with `Q_kH_kB = B` (pp. 309–312: "We introduce a transformation H_{k,Ax} which maps B into such a minimizing configuration for axial gauge, and we call H_{k,Ax} the axial gauge minimizer"); in D1 the operator `a_kG_kQ_k^T`, unnamed. An analogue: Bałaban's `H_k` satisfies the hard constraint `QH_kB = B` exactly, for `k` steps at once and in a Landau-type gauge `R∂^*H_kB = 0`; v3's `W = A^{-1}bQ^*` satisfies `QW = I − b^{-1}K_c` and is a one-step object. That `W → K_f^{-1}Q^*(QK_f^{-1}Q^*)^{-1}`, the form of B84a (1.103), as `b → ∞` is an inference, not in the papers. The two representatives: `W_a` (smooth) against `W_F` (forest) correspond in role to `H` in the Landau gauge against the minimal configuration in the axial gauge (B85d p. 309, Prop. 9: "The minimal configuration `U_k(V)` … in the axial gauge … transformed to the Landau gauge is, by the definition, equal to `exp iηℋ(B)`"); the pairing `W_F ↔ H_{k,Ax}`, `W_a ↔ H_k` of BIJ85 is a conjecture and was not checked against v3's formulas, and v3's smooth representative is built by a gradient correction with a cardinal partition of unity (5:1110–1118), not by a Landau condition. The identification of `W` with `H` from B85e and B88a alone was an inference from the roles; B84a, B85c and B85d, where `H` is defined, confirm it. Letter clash: in D1, D2 `W` is the unit-covariance fluctuation variable. Adopted (23 November 2026): *the linearisation `W` of the critical configuration*, in place of the *linearised background field `W`* of the earlier decision of the same day, keeping the symbols `W_s`, `W_a`, `W_F` and saying which is meant; at first use "the soft-constraint analogue of Bałaban's operator `H_k`, for one step". `W_F` is not called "axial gauge minimizer" and `W_a` is not called "Landau gauge minimizer": the pairing with BIJ85 recorded above is a conjecture not checked against v3's formulas, and may be mentioned only as such.
*Across chapters:* the symbols are consistent in chapters 5, 7, 9s, 17; before 24 November 2026 the phrase "actual (stationary) tangent" named `W_a` at 7:583 and 17m:263 and `W_F` at 17c:49, 113; the present text says "the smooth representative of the linearization (`W`) of the critical configuration is `W_a`" at 7:583 and 17m:263. `W_F` is "the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge" (5:1161, 1246; 6:954; 7:583; 9s:194; 11:642) and "the forest representative" (17c:50); 6:960 says "the linearization of the critical configuration, in its representative `W_F` of (ch05:stationary-tangent)". "Representative" means gauge representative and is not a further name of `W`. Not *parallel transport* and not *transfer*: those name other operations. `𝒰_F`, which stood at 6:960 and 6:983 before 24 November 2026, was `W_F` under another letter; the text now writes `W_F`. 17c:150–151 writes `T u = (u, Dz(0)u)` for the tangent "on the slice of the block axial gauge", the form of Scott's `W_ax v = (v, Dψ(0)v)` (B:473). Since 25 November 2026 the proof of preservation of the order of vanishing computes with `W_s`: "we pass once more to a gauge-equivalent representative, the linearization `W_s` built with the linear averaging operator `M`" (17c:56), using `W_a − W_s = −d_{0,f}ERW_s` and the bounded potential of `W_F a − W_a a` (17c:56, 63); see *polynomial field*. In the Lean formalisation the potential that takes `W_s` to the forest representative is built in one step (`straighten`: tree-path integral minus the root value of `fixRoot`), without the intermediate smooth `W_a`.
*See also:* stationary graph; stationary identification; straight; actual stationary tangent; `𝒰_F`.

#### stationary units
*Now:* removed; 9s:170–171 now displays the bound: "the exterior integrand is bounded by `Ω e^{−Φ(x)} e^{−Δ+o(M²)}`".
- **Meaning.** After division by the stationary weight `Ω e^{−Φ(x)}`: the exterior integrand `U_x(U)` satisfies `U_x(U) ≤ Ω e^{−Φ(x)} e^{Y_*}` for `U` outside the retained region, with `Y_* = −N log[c_H(√(2π)g)^{dim 𝔤}] − Δ + (loop, Haar and determinant bounds)`; "the exterior integrand is bounded by `Ω e^{−Φ(x)} e^{−Δ+o(M²)}`" (9s:170–171) is this inequality with `e^{Y_*} ≤ e^{−Δ+o(M²)}`. The term `−N log[c_H(√(2π)g)^{dim 𝔤}]` of 9s:165–166 ("the normalization term") is the price of expressing the bound relative to `Ω = π_{β′}(√(2π)g)^n c_H^N`.
  *Basis:* S; I from the v3 text (9s:163–171). *Where:* 9s:170 (the bound, without the phrase). *Adopted:* write `≤ Ω e^{−Φ(x)} e^{−Δ+o(M²)}` (proposed: *relative to `Ω e^{−Φ}`*; better, the displayed bound).
  *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:156–165`: "To express it in stationary units, put `m_H = c_H(√(2π) b)^{dim 𝔤}`, so `Ω = π_β m_H^N`, and define `Y_* = −N log m_H − Δ + W B_loop + p + t_W`. Then `U_x(U) ≤ Ω e^{−Φ(x)} e^{Y_*}` (`U ∉ 𝒮_x`)."
*Across chapters:* one occurrence; formed like "Gaussian units" (9:243, rescaled by `g`). "Unit" here is not the identity field. The inequality is now stated at 9s:170–171.
*See also:* Gaussian units.

#### stencil
*Now:* partly replaced by *link support* (defined at 6:460; 11:150–152, 163, 922, 925, 941; 11E:15, 79–80, 94; 13sb:139; 18gq:103) and *support of the expression* (4:550); remains in the finite-difference sense (12:347, 364, 391–392), at 13:238, 13ba:219–254, 301, 11:1788–1834, 11E:162, 17m:119, and for the finite stencils `Σ_d` of chapters 1, 2, 2e, 7, 10 and 17c (37 lines in all, labels excluded).
*Variants:* link support; union of the link supports; support of the expression; no longer in the text: footprint; insertion stencil; complementary stencil.
- **Meaning.** The set of links a term or an insertion is built from: "its *link support*, the fixed set of links from which its expression is built" (6:460). Not the full dependence set: "The support of the expression contains the contours, plaquettes and base point; this indicator may read additional adjacent plaquettes" (4:550–551). In chapter 12 also a finite-difference stencil in the standard sense.
  *Basis:* R (4:549–551); D (6:460). *Where:* 4:550 ("support of the expression"); 6:460, 466 ff.; 11:150–152, 163, 922, 925, 941; 11E:15, 79–80, 94; 13sb:139; 18gq:103 ("link support"); 12:347, 364, 391, 392; 13:238; 13ba:219–254, 301 ("stencil"). *Proposed:* *support of the expression*, kept distinct from the *dependence set*.
*Across chapters:* the earlier reading of one set under two names, "support of the expression" (4:550) and "link support" (6:460 and later), does not hold: the link support "contains the links on which the averaging operation depends and every endpoint of a retained path" (6:466), so it is larger than the declared support of 4:549–550, and the text does not identify them. Chapter 4 itself has two names for its set ("declared support", 4:549; "support of the expression", 4:550). The finite-difference stencil of chapter 12 is the ordinary numerical term.

#### step
*Now:* unchanged; the variant "update" (6:176) is replaced by *step*.
*Also in the text for:* the former *update* (see those entries).
*Variants:* nonlinear step; block step (10:236); renormalization step (7:4; 8:335; 9:911; chapter title 9:2); no longer in the text: update.
- **Meaning.** One renormalisation (block) transformation, from level `m+1` to level `m`; occasionally its index. "The constants may depend on the fixed step" (6:957); "the nonlinear step" (5:1392–1393); "The step in Theorem (ch09:step-theorem)" (6:176); "A renormalization transformation, called a step, is first an exact integration" (4:5).
  *Basis:* I; D (4:5). *Where:* 4:5; 5:1392; 6:176, 957; throughout the later chapters. *Adopted:* *step* for the map; at first use "renormalization transformation, called a step"; *scale index* for the index.
*Literature:* **renormalization transformation** `T`, `T_k`; **step** (B87 p. 254: "Now we consider renormalization transformations, which have the general form (Tρ)(V) = ∫dU t(V,U)ρ(U)"; p. 256: "Thus we obtain after k steps"; D1 p. 1330010-6: "After k steps we will have a density ρ_k(Φ_k)"; B95 p. 107: "Thus applying k renormalization and scaling transformations yields a density ρ_k"); "RG transformation" (D1). The same object in role. Differences: in B84a, B95 and D1 each step is followed by a rescaling `S` to the unit lattice, which v3 does not have; Bałaban's kernel is a delta function (see *kernel*, *penalty parameter*); and in D2, D3 a step is also called a "stage" (see *stage*). Adopted (23 November 2026): *step*; at first use "renormalization transformation, called a step", with the differences above stated there (no rescaling after a step in v3; Gaussian kernel against delta function).
*Across chapters:* one sense. `stage` is not a synonym. "Update" no longer occurs in chapters 3–6 (6:175–177 read).
*See also:* stage; scale; suffix.

#### stop backwards
*Now:* the sentence at 17w:30–33 is upstream's explicit rule since the merge of 26 November 2026, which superseded the repair of 25 November: "move backwards from scale `n`, adding `log L_i` at each step. Stop when this sum first reaches `(b+2) log H_n`. Starting from that scale, continue until the additional sum first reaches `10 log B_n`"; "stop backwards" and the formula `log(a_{n'}/a_n)` are no longer at 17w:31 (grep); "stopping integers" stands at 17w:105; the variant "stopping levels" is replaced by *stopping scales* (17w:102).
*Variants:* stopping integers; stopping scales (chapter 17); no longer in the text: stopping levels.
- **Meaning.** Starting from level `n`, pass to coarser levels until a difference of `τ_m = log(1/a_m)` first exceeds a target: "stop backwards from `n` at the first scale `n'<n` with `log(a_{n'}/a_n)≥(b+2)log H_n`, and then at the first scale `n''<n'` with `log(a_{n''}/a_{n'})≥10 log B_n`" (17w:31–33; until 25 November 2026 "at the first crossing of `(b+2) log H_n`, and then at the first crossing of another `10 log B_n`"); "Place a copy in each reflected cell at the first backward crossing of `B_n²`, so `B_n² ≤ a_m/a_n ≤ L_*B_n²`" (17m:429–430). At 17m:421–422 the crossing is towards finer scales ("`τ_{k(n)} − τ_n ≥ T_n` is the first crossing"). At 17w:31 the crossing quantity is now named, `log(a_{n'}/a_n)`.
  *Basis:* R (17m:421, 429–430; 17w:31–33 since 25 November 2026). *Where:* 17:138, 142; 17w:31–36, 102, 105; 17m:422, 429, 466. *Adopted:* *the first scale `n' < n` with `log(a_{n'}/a_n) ≥ …`*, printed at 17w:31–32 (25 November 2026).
*Across chapters:* chapter 17; the rule of 17m:429 is that of 13sb:105–106. The "middle and output stopping scales" of 17w:101–102 are the two backward stops of 17w:31–33 (inferred from the parallel with 11:2090–2093).
*See also:* stopping.

#### stopping
*Now:* replaced in sense 1 by *(the scale at which) terms of higher source degree are deleted* (decision of 26 November 2026, chapter 12 only: 12:10 "an estimate for deleting the terms of higher source degree at an intermediate scale"; title 12:226 "An estimate uniform in the scale at which terms of higher source degree are deleted"; 12:252 "the later scale `m` at which the terms of higher source degree are deleted"; 12:305 "The expression (ch12:stopped)"); the word remains in chapter 12 only in the labels `ch12:stopped`, `ch12:stopping` (12:217, 227). Sense 2 unchanged ("stopping scale" of chapters 10, 11, 13, 17, 18): "stopping level" is replaced by *stopping scale* and "stopping pair" by *pair `(m,k)` of cell scale and stopping scale* (11:948–949; 11E:65; 17m:466); "stopping scale" also at 11:806, from the second round of merge corrections (grep).
*Variants:* stopping scale, representation (11:781, "the representation at the stopping scale"), data; pair `(m,k)` of cell scale and stopping scale; stopped at `a_k`; no longer in the text: stopping level; stopping pair; stopped expression; stopping errors; stopping estimate.
1. **Deletion at an intermediate level (chapter 12).** Evaluation at an intermediate level `m` after setting to zero all terms with two or more source variables: "Keep the full terms of source degree one and set only these terms of higher source degree to zero", giving the expression `C_{N,p,m}(v;x)` (12:208–216), formerly the "stopped expression"; formerly "the two stopping errors" (12:303), now "the error in Lemma (ch12:omission)" (12:303–304).
   *Basis:* R (12:208–216). *Where:* 12:10, 226, 252, 305. *Adopted:* *the scale at which the terms of higher source degree are deleted* (decision of 26 November 2026; the dictionary had proposed *the correlation with the terms of source degree ≥ 2 deleted at scale `m`*). Not *truncated correlation*.
2. **The level at which the block evolution is halted and the chessboard bound applied.** Nothing is deleted ("We keep all incoming joint components with insertions", 13sb:9–10). "A reflected tiling at scale `a_m`, stopped at `a_k`, has `(a_m/a_k)⁴` sites per cell" (11:817–818); a "pair `(m,k)` of cell scale and stopping scale" (11E:65) is (scale of the reflected tiling, level at which it is stopped). In 13sb the level is `k = k(m)`, "the first scale `k ≥ m` with `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k`" (13sb:105); in 13ba the letters are exchanged ("Fix `m ≥ k` with `B_m² ≤ a_k/a_m`", 13ba:215; "We instead stop at one fixed coarse scale", 13ba:8–9); in 18lp it is `k_*` (18lp:154–159); at 12:251–252 the base level `r` played this role ("evaluated at `r`, not at the later stopping scale `m`"; since 26 November 2026 "not at the later scale `m` at which the terms of higher source degree are deleted", sense 1).
   *Basis:* R (11:817–818; 13sb:105). *Where:* 10:175; 11:781, 806, 817–818, 948–949; 11E:65; 13sb:86, 103, 138; 13ba:8, 196; 18lp:159; 17w:101–102; 17m:466. *Proposed:* *the scale `k(m)` at which the bound is applied*; *pair (cell scale `m`, evaluation scale `k`)*; the text has "pair `(m,k)` of cell scale and stopping scale" (11:949; 11E:65; 17m:466).
*Across chapters:* a real change of meaning: sense 1 in chapter 12 only, sense 2 in chapters 10–11, 13, 17, 18lp. The word suggests stopping times, which are not meant. The chapter 11 lines fix sense 2; the gloss "the level `k = k(m)`" fits 13sb only (11:780–819, 12:250–253, 13ba:8–9, 214–216, 13sb:103–107 read). Count in chapters 12–16: 11 lines with "stop", "stopped" or "stopping" before 26 November 2026, now 6 (12: 0; 13sb: 3; 13ba: 2; 18lp: 1) (grep).
*See also:* sparse stopping scale; stop backwards.

#### strip
*Now:* unchanged in senses 1 and 3; in sense 2 the text now writes *coincident-coordinate strips* (14:183, 201; 17:122, 128; 17w:118), not the proposed wording.
1. **Strip of analyticity.** The set `|Im p| < σ` in momentum space; its width is the exponential decay rate.
   *Basis:* D (7:41–49). *Where:* 5:279, 316, 413, 445, 593, 611, 685, 896, 899 (its "width" at 5:744–745, 854, 1392); 7:41–49, 121; 17t:130; 17c:165, 180, 182, 197, 283. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
2. **Coordinate-equality strips.** Neighbourhoods of width `4δ_k`, `δ_k = M_k^c`, of the set where two distinct points share a coordinate ("coincident coordinates which are not coincident points", 14:211–212), outside which the gradient bound is required (14:183–205: "The gradient bound is required outside the coincident-coordinate strips").
   *Basis:* R (14:183–205). *Where:* 14:183, 201, 211, 376; 17:122, 128; 17w:118 ("coincident-coordinate strips"; 14:211, 376 "coincident coordinates"). *Proposed:* *neighborhoods of width `4δ_k` of the coincident-coordinate set*.
3. **Strips of the chessboard tiling.** The `2q` slabs obtained by cutting one coordinate into intervals of length `ℓ` (1:284–285; "The slots are the `2q` strips in that coordinate", 1:314–315). In chapter 13 the strips to be avoided near the cell boundaries of a reflected tiling ("a translation avoids all these strips", 13:86; "strip count", 13:370; 13ba:251); that these are the same strips is inferred.
   *Basis:* R (1:314–315); I for chapter 13. *Where:* 1:315, 317, 318; 13:86, 370; 13ba:251. *Proposed:* keep, with the definition of 1:284–285.
*Across chapters:* three unrelated uses (chapters 5, 7, 17; chapters 14, 17; chapters 1, 13); chapter 17 has the first two.
*See also:* cell; seam; slab; slot; strip bound; strip removal.

"The supplied construction" (3:547; 5:195) was the construction of the manuscripts from which v3 was written (and of the formal source behind them), that is, the construction this book presents: at 3:546–547 the sign of `T^Max` "is chosen to match the flux convention (ch03:flux) used below", the normalisation of the stress tensor by its shell flux; at 5:195 "The smoothing used in this construction is `ŵ_L(θ) = …`" introduces the symbol of the uniform weight on the centred box.

("supplies"); 1:408, 456; 2:10, 392; 2e:55; 7:116, 999; 9:872, 967; 11:686, 1041, 1079, 1593; 17:17, 249; 17t:455; 17w:103; 17c:327; 17m:476; 18:27, 187, 189, 273; 19:36, 45, 48, 104, 164 (all now "gives" or "give"; 2:392 "come from"; 9:872, 967 "given"); 11:250 ("covered by"); the verb "supply" remains on 29 lines (chapters 4–6, 8–11, 14; e.g. 9:873 "the direction factors supply"). *Adopted:* *gives*; *the present construction* (3:547: *the shell-flux convention of Section …*, written "the flux convention (ch03:flux) used below"; 5:195: *The smoothing used in this construction is*).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/G-section.tex:120–128` (shell flux of Definition `def:D13`; "the requirement that the flux be the derivative fixes both the normalization and the sign of the stress tensor"); Scott `part2/B-section.tex:194–196` ("`ŵ_ℓ(θ) = ∏_a ℓ^{-1} Σ_{|s| ≤ (ℓ−1)/2} e^{isθ_a}` … the symbol of the uniform weight on `𝔹_{(ℓ−1)/2}`"). The chapter note `audit/ch03-maxwell.md:30` uses the parallel phrase "the supplied source derivation". Both sentences are in the first v3 commit `89c513b3`; no source sentence contains the phrase, so the reading rests on what the two sentences refer to.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout; the word survives in labels ("parameter-supplier", "cutoff-supplier", "coarse-residual-supplier", "current-suppliers") and in the titles 5:1244 ("Supplying the local derivative estimates"), 8:352 ("What an application must supply") and 14:851 ("Analyticity supplied by a positive Gram kernel").

#### support compression
*Now:* replaced by *passing to the coarse image of the support* (9:232); the inequality is still not stated.
- **Meaning.** The comparison of covering numbers before and after blocking. A coarse support `Y` contained in the `rB`-neighbourhood of the coarse image of a fine support `X` has `L·cov_B(Y) ≤ (L + 10·cov(X))·T_r` with `T_r = (2r+13)^4`. Hence, if `20 t T_r ≤ Lσ`, where `σ` is the incoming support exponent, `t·cov_B(Y) ≤ t T_r + (σ/2)·cov(X)`: the outgoing weight `e^{t·cov(Y)}` uses at most half of the incoming exponential decay. This is the condition on "the scale ratio and the incoming support exponent" of 9:231–233 ("so that, after passing to the coarse image of the support, the outgoing weight uses at most half of the …").
  *Basis:* S; ? for the v3 text (9:232). *Where:* 9:232 ("passing to the coarse image of the support"). *Proposed:* *after passing to the coarse image of the support, whose covering number is smaller by a factor of order `L`*; better, state the inequality.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/nonlinear-singleton-inheritance.tex:216–219`: "The support compression estimate gives, provided `20 t t_{r_0} ≤ LA`, `t q_i' ≤ t t_{r_0} + ½ A q_i`." Scott `part2/D-section.tex:291–300`: "For support compression, fix an integer `r` with `Y_i ⊂ N_{rB_m}(parent(X_i))` and put `T_r = (2r+13)^4`. Choose the ratio to satisfy `20(σ+3)T_r ≤ ℓ_m σ_{J_{m+1}}`. Together with `B_{m+1} ≤ 2B_m`, this leaves half the incoming exponent: `(σ+3) cov_{B_m}(Y_i) ≤ (σ+3)T_r + ½ σ_{J_{m+1}} d_i`." Lean `YM.PhysicalNext.JointLoad.Heir.Release.compressed`, `YM/PhysicalNext/V9_JOINT_ENDPOINT_LOAD/Heir/Fusion.lean:60–67` (statement read: `t·coverNumber P.B Y ≤ base t r + (B.supportExponent/2)·coverNumber B.B X` under `accepts r B.supportExponent t L`, i.e. `20·base t r ≤ L·A`, with `base a r := a·toll r`, definitions read in the same file), with hypothesis `Walled` (`Y ⊆ halo (r·radiusB x) (X.image parent)`, `YM/PhysicalNext/V9_JOINT_ENDPOINT_LOAD/Heir/Depth.lean`, definition read); it uses lemma `YM.Lattice.Corona.collapse`, `YM/Corona/Spend.lean:73–75` (statement read), whose constant is `((s+6)+(s+6)+1)^4`. The constant is `YM.Planned.AtomRegular.toll`, `YM/Planned/ATOM_REGULAR_ESTIMATE/Geometry.lean:50` (definition read): `toll r := ((r+6)+(r+6)+1)^4 = (2r+13)^4`, in agreement with Scott's `T_r`. That the `toll` used in `compressed` is this declaration is read from the `open … Planned.AtomRegular` of `Fusion.lean` and from the fact that it is the only `toll` in the tree with a single natural-number argument and natural-number value; nothing was elaborated.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. Unrelated to *compression* (chapters 15, 18). v3 should restore the inequality from Scott D:291–300.
*See also:* support exponent.

#### tag
*Now:* replaced by *auxiliary index* (sense 1, defined at 4:230) and *filtration index* (sense 2, defined at 2:96); the word survives only in the label `ch04:tag-law`.
*Variants:* auxiliary index; filtration index; tag law (label `ch04:tag-law` only); no longer in the text: frame tag; live tag actions.
1. **Random index `α`.** The auxiliary discrete variable `α` with law `λ(U,α)` recording which case of the frame and block-average definition is used: "Collect all choices made for the local gauge transformations and for the averaging operation in a finite *auxiliary index* `α` and denote their joint probability, the probability weight of `α`, by `λ(U,α)`" (4:230–231); the same object as "label" in its random-index sense. A *live* tag is a value `α` with `λ(U,α) > 0`, a *dead* one has weight zero; the *action* of a tag is the fine action plus the block-kernel penalty computed with the block average of that tag (see *live tag actions*). *Basis:* D (4:230); S for "live" and "tag action". *Where:* 4:86, 222–230, 350; 5:952–977, 1348; 6:63, 87, 368, 493, 1114, 1351; 9:83, 85; 9s:132, 139, 226, 247; 11:246, 679; 11R:359–360 (all now "auxiliary index", "index" or "value of the auxiliary index"); none in ch. 12–16. *Adopted:* *auxiliary index `α`*; drop "tag".
   *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:48–61` (the tagged integrand `Σ_k π_β λ_k(U) e^{−β[a(U) + n_k(U,V(x))] − ℓ(U)} 1{fine field healthy}`; "The nonnegative tag weights satisfy `Σ_k λ_k(U) = 1`; a dead tag has zero weight"; "all live tag actions there equal `φ`"); the Lean declarations are cited under *live tag actions*.
2. **The index `d` of `V_d`.** In the observable label `v = (d,c)`: "The same polynomial `c` can occur with different filtration indices `d`" (2:97–98). *Basis:* D (2:96, "whose index `d` we call the *filtration index*"). *Where:* 2:96, 98, 99. *Adopted:* *filtration index `d`*.
*Across chapters:* the meaning changed between chapter 2 (sense 2) and chapters 4–11 (sense 1); the two senses now have different names.
*See also:* live tag actions; tag-count factor; tag-coincidence radius; uniform mass; weight.

#### tag-coincidence radius
*Now:* replaced by a description: "the ball on which the actions for all values of the auxiliary index with positive probability weight coincide" (9s:226).
- **Meaning.** A fixed radius of the coordinate ball around the stationary point within which the actions of all tags `α` with `λ(U,α) > 0` are equal to `φ` (see *live tag actions*), because the block average does not depend on the tag there. It is not a radius within which the tags of two configurations coincide. "The common chart and the ball on which the actions for all values of the auxiliary index with positive probability weight coincide contain these regions because `h+gD → 0`" (9s:226–227): the retained regions shrink into the chart and into this ball.
  *Basis:* S; R for the ball (9s:226). *Where:* 9s:226. *Proposed:* *the radius within which the average `Q_e(U)` (the value of the averaging operation) is independent of the tag*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:259–262`: "The same conditions place the entire region inside the Haar chart and inside the region where all tag actions coincide"; `:282–283`: "It is eventually smaller than the fixed safe radii, the action-coincidence radius and one". The source states that such a radius exists and does not prove it in the passage read; no Lean constant was located.
*Across chapters:* one place. The source word is "action-coincidence radius"; the text now describes the ball instead of naming its radius.
*See also:* tag; chart; live tag actions.

#### tag-count factor
*Now:* replaced by *factor counting the values of the auxiliary index* (11R:359–360; 9s:139).
*Variants:* tag multiplicity, number of tag choices (source).
- **Meaning.** The number of values of the random index `α` (the cardinality of the finite set of tag arrays), as a factor. It appears when the tag weight is written as a mask: the "physical" likelihood is the number of tags times the probability `λ(U,α)`, so that on a minimising branch, where the tag is uniform with mass the reciprocal of the number of tags, it equals one; the reciprocal of the number of tags then stands outside as a uniform average over tags. Hence at 11R:359–361 "the event indicators retain the finite factor counting the values of the auxiliary index; it cancels the denominator of the normalized average over that index when the slices are summed". At 9s:139 no such factor occurs because the integrand is written with the probabilities themselves: "The probability weights of the auxiliary index sum to one, so there is no additional factor counting its values".
  *Basis:* I (9s:139; 11R:359–360); S for the mechanism. *Where:* 9s:139; 11R:359–360. *Adopted:* *number of values of `α`*, written "factor counting the values of the auxiliary index".
  *Source:* Martin `existence/actual-corrected-body-compiler.tex:70–81`: "Its factors are the actual factors in the block integral, including the finite tag count in the site and bond factors. Precisely, `Π_j mask_j = profile · #Choices · likelihood · interfaces`. This tag multiplicity is present in the pointwise sliced identity; it cancels the denominator of the normalized tag average when the block integral is reconstructed"; `existence/gaussian-reassembly.tex:194–199`: "The complete product of physical tag likelihoods equals the number of tag choices times the original normalized likelihood. Thus a single factor `|𝒯|^{-1}`, where `𝒯` is the tag-array space, remains outside the product. This is the uniform tag average"; `existence/warning-safety.tex:115–118`: "On a minimizing branch the chosen tag is uniform: its mass is the reciprocal of the number of tags. The physical likelihood multiplies by that number, so its value is exactly one"; `existence/stationary-exterior-receipt.tex:69–74`: "the tag sum is one … No tag-count factor occurs."
*Across chapters:* same use in 9s and 11R; undefined in both. v3 should restore the source's sentence on `#Choices` at 11R:358.
*See also:* tag; tag average; uniform mass; live tag actions.

#### tangent
*Now:* replaced by *linearization of the critical configuration* (senses 1 and 2; 5:528, 1091, 1246; 7:583, 790, 892; 11:642; 17c:8; 17m:263); the word remains only in other senses (tangent space, the tangent of a curve at 7:514).
*Variants:* linearization (`W`) of the critical configuration; no longer in the text: stationary tangent; actual tangent; actual stationary tangent; smooth tangent; straight stationary tangent.
1. **The operator `W_a`.** The smooth representative `W_a = W_s − d_{0,f} E R W_s` (5:1118) of the derivative at zero of the critical-configuration map `ψ = ρ(v)` (5:1155–1192), where `W_s` is "the operator `W` built with the linear averaging operator `M`" (5:1094); the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge is a different operator (5:1161), and it, not `W_a`, is that derivative (sense 2). "The smooth representative of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration is `W_a`" (7:583); "The smooth representative of the linearization of the critical configuration is `W_a = W_s − d_f E R W_s`" (17m:263–264); before 24 November 2026 the text had "The actual stationary tangent is `W_a` …; its forest representative is `W_F`" (7:583) and "The actual tangent is `W_a = …`" (17m:263). *Basis:* R (7:583; 17m:263). *Where:* 5:1094, 1118, 1161; 7:583, 790, 892, 1056, 1167; 17m:263. *Adopted:* *the smooth representative `W_a` of the linearization `W` of the critical configuration*; one name for `W` throughout (*the linearization of the critical configuration*), stating the representative (`W_F`, `W_a` or `W_s`); no symbol is renamed, and the representative is written wherever `W` is unqualified: `W_s` at 5:527–535, `W_F` in chapter 11 (11:642), `W_a` in `17-current-contraction.tex`.
2. **The derivative of the stationary substitution (17c:49–51), the forest representative `W_F`.** "The first derivative of the nonlinear critical-configuration map, from coarse to fine link variables with block ratio `L`, is the forest representative `W_F` of (ch05:stationary-tangent) … Since `W_F − W_a` is a fine gradient, the Ward identities of `E_b` allow us to compute with the smooth representative `W = W_a`" (17c:49–54); "Recall that `W = W_a` is the smooth representative; the quadratic Ward identities annihilate its gradient difference from `W_F`" (17c:113–114). Quotations updated to the present text, in which the letter `W` of 17c is `W_a`; before 24 November 2026 the text had "Let `W` be the actual stationary tangent … The first derivative of the nonlinear stationary substitution is this `W`", an unqualified `W` that was `W_F`. The derivative of the stationary graph in forest coordinates is `W_F` (5:1157–1160; 9s:193–195), and `W_a − W_F` is a fine gradient. *Basis:* D for the derivative of the stationary substitution, which the present text states to be `W_F` (17c:49–51); R that this derivative is `W_F` in forest coordinates (5:1157–1160; 9s:193–195); S that the stationary map of chapter 17 is the forest-coordinate one. *Where:* 17c:49, 113. *Adopted:* *the linearization `W_F` of the critical configuration, that is, the derivative of the critical-configuration map `ρ` with respect to the coarse field (5.stationary-tangent)*; in `17-current-contraction.tex` the computation uses its smooth representative `W_a`, and the representative is written wherever `W` is unqualified there.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:473`, `483`; `part2/I-section.tex:162`. Lean `YM.Precision.Guessed`, `YM/PCalc/Chart.lean` (definition read); `YM.Precision.extracted`, `YM/PREC/TreeMatch.lean` (definition read); `YM.Work.F04.tangent`, `YM/Work/F04.lean` (statement read). See *actual stationary tangent* (sense 2) for the quotations and for what is inferred.
*Across chapters:* the symbols `W_s`, `W_a`, `W_F` are used consistently in chapters 5, 7, 9s and 17; the phrase "actual tangent" was not, before 24 November 2026 (it named `W_a` at 7:583 and 17m:263 and `W_F` at 17c:49); the present text says "the smooth representative of the linearization (`W`) of the critical configuration is `W_a`" at both places and names `W_F` at 17c:49–51 (text read at 17c:47–54, 111–114). 11:642 has "the linearization `W` of the critical configuration, taken in its representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge"; "transport", "lift" and "response" no longer name these operators at the lines cited here. `notation.md` line 242, which once called `W_a` "the actual forest-coordinate response", now reads "the smooth representative W_a = W_s - d_f E R W_s, and the forest-coordinate W_F (the derivative of the stationary map)", in agreement with 5:1161–1162 and 7:583. "Representative" is not a further name for `W`: it means a gauge representative (7:583, 588, 939).
