1. **Prescribed value.** A prescribed value or location (6:923, 940); "Choose a prescribed value `β̄ > 0` of the coupling at unit scale, the *coarse endpoint*" (10:154). *Basis:* D (10:154); I for 6:923, 940. *Where:* 6:923, 940 ("target"); 10:154 ("prescribed value", "coarse endpoint"), 209, 268, 813 ("coarse endpoint"). *Adopted:* *prescribed value* (at 10:154).
2. **What is to be reached in the current step.** The statement or exponent to be proved ("derivative target", "grid target", "target exponent"). *Basis:* I. *Where:* 13:254, 262; 18lp:341, 344. *Proposed:* *the required bound*.
3. **Right-hand sides of the lift equations.** The "finite target list" (11:1370) is the finite list `v_1, …, v_r` of real representatives of the free separating family, the right-hand sides of the equations `S_{g/θ} T u_j = W_ρ v_j`, (ch11:simultaneous-detector-lifts) (11:1353–1359). The former "normalized target columns" (11:1243) were the vectors belonging to the solutions `u_j` of these equations, for which `‖Au_j‖` is bounded by a fixed power of `H`; since 25 November 2026 the text says so: "For the solutions `u=u_{j,N,p}` of the lift equations (ch11:simultaneous-detector-lifts) below, which satisfy `‖Au‖≤H^{bd+c_d}`" (11:1243–1244).
   *Basis:* S; R since 25 November 2026 for 11:1243. *Where:* 11:1370 (11:1243 until 25 November 2026). *Proposed:* *the list `v_1, …, v_r`*. *Adopted:* *for the solutions `u_j` of (ch11:simultaneous-detector-lifts)* (11:1243).
   *Source:* Martin existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:208–217 ("For every `i` solve `S_{t_{k,N,p}}T_{k,N,p}u_i = W_{ρ_k}v_i` … All columns are therefore normalized simultaneously, with their actual unit and real structure"), :1026–1028 ("For a solved lift … `|Au|_1 ≤ H^{bd+q_*+2}` eventually, on a fixed bounded target set"), :1074 ("eventually for a fixed bounded set of targets"). Lean `YM.Next.Rank.Price.Solves`, `.solve`, `.shrink`, `.columns`, `.awake` (YM/Next/RANK/Matrices.lean:26–30, 104, 126–131; definitions and the statement of `solve` read; docstring of `Solves`: "The exact solving condition, not a comparison drift of the target labels in k-units").
4. **Limit configurations.** "These moments remain bounded as the rounded, rescaled configurations approach their fixed separated limit configurations" (11:2210–2212): the fixed configurations of separated points which the rounded, rescaled lattice configurations approach.
   *Basis:* R (11:2210–2212). *Where:* 11:2212 ("limit configurations"). *Adopted:* *their limit configurations*.
   *Source:* Lean `YM.Next.Rank.Ship.targets` (YM/Next/RANK/Allowance.lean:64–65; definition read: the cumulants evaluated at the fixed tested configuration); the correspondence with 11:2212 is inferred from the context, not from a formula.
*Across chapters:* four loosely related uses. In chapters 17–19 only the ordinary "the excess over the target" (17:142; 17w:36), in sense 2, and "coarse endpoint" (19:23); ordinary uses also at 1:407, 9:168, 14:271. The exponents at 11:1244 (`‖Au‖ ≤ H^{bd+c_d}`, `D > bd + c_d + v`) and at 11:1369 (`H^{bd+c_d}`; also 11:1847, 1930) agree. The source and the formalisation both have the term `bd`. Martin existence/allarity-coordinate-calibration.tex:232–244: "Let `q_*` be the maximum connection degree in the fixed frame … `|Tu|_1 ≤ (2H)^{q_*} r^d |v|_1`, `|𝓗u|_1 ≤ 2^{q_*+1}|v|_1 H^{bd+q_*+1} ≤ H^{bd+q_*+2}` eventually … The finite loss `q_*+2` is chosen before the amplification exponent `b`"; existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:1027–1029: "`|Au|_1 ≤ H^{bd+q_*+2}` eventually, on a fixed bounded target set. Thus any fixed `D > bd+q_*+2+v` makes this error at most `H^{−v}`". Lean `YM.Next.Rank.Atlas.income` (YM/Next/RANK/ParticleGate.lean:46–49; statement read): for `b > 0`, eventually in `k`, for all `N ≥ k`, all `p` and every solution `u` of the lift equation with `ρ = H^b`, `H · coeffSize(awake u) ≤ H^{b·d + saves C d}`, where `saves C d = leash + 2` and `leash` is the maximum over the frame of the second grade of a basis element (:42–44; definitions read), `bill a s = exp((log log s)² a) = H^a` (YM/Next/RANK/Reign.lean:22–25; definitions read) and `awake = a_k^{−d} · columns` is the map `A` (YM/Next/RANK/Matrices.lean:26–30; definitions read). So 11:1369 is the correct statement, with `c_d = q_* + 2` and `q_*` the largest factor ("connection") degree of a basis element ("depends on factor counts", 11:1370); 11:1244 now reads `‖Au‖ ≤ H^{bd+c_d}`, `D > bd + c_d + v`, in agreement with it. The letter `c_d` also denotes a different constant at 11:1292–1304, that of `‖v‖_1 ≤ c_d‖𝓔v‖_coeff`; the source has `c_d` for that constant (existence/actual-rank-purchases.tex:549–551) and `q_*+2` for the exponent.
*See also:* column; trial.

#### terminal
*Now:* partly replaced by *at the ultraviolet cutoff* (sense 1: 5:705–706; 6:180; 10:102–112, 731, 893; 11:135, 168, 898, 913; 11E:77) and *cutoff-scale* (13:161, 219); in sense 2 by "its constants" (17m:423); remains on 20 lines in chapters 10–13 (10:435, 442, 450, 784, 864; 11:112, 149, 159, 173, 525, 926, 958, 1081, 1333; 13ba:61, 77, 123, 153, 175; 13sb:93); the title at 12:132 was "Independence of the graph at the ultraviolet cutoff" from 25 November 2026, upstream's "Independence of the terminal graph in the cutoff limit" after the merge, and is since 26 November 2026 "Cauchy convergence of the graphs at a fixed scale" (decision on titles).
*Variants:* terminal column; terminal attachment bound; terminal insertion; terminal arrays; terminal density; joint terminal construction; no longer in the text: terminal graph (12:132); terminal cutoff; terminal scale; terminal fine metric; terminal trial; terminal source; terminal value norms; terminal delays.
1. **At the ultraviolet cutoff level `N`.** The finest scale of a history: "increase only the ultraviolet cutoff `N`. … the sequence with ultraviolet cutoff `N+1` extends the sequence with ultraviolet cutoff `N` at its fine end" (5:705–707). The word names the level at which the renormalisation flow starts. The "fine metric at the ultraviolet cutoff" (6:179–180) is unmodified (`ζ_f = 0`). The "terminal graph" of the former title "Forgetting the terminal graph" (12:132, since 26 November 2026 "Cauchy convergence of the graphs at a fixed scale") belongs here: it is the graph at the fine end of the history with cutoff ("terminal index") `N`; the proof replaces the graph at level `m+h` (12:140–141) and shows that the level-`m` graph depends on it by at most `2^{1−h}`. *Basis:* R (5:705–706; 13ba:123 "its terminal insertion satisfies the joint attachment bound at `N`"); S, with I, for 12:132 (see *forgetting*). *Where:* "at the ultraviolet cutoff" or "at the cutoff": 5:705–706; 6:180; 10:102–112, 731, 893; 11:135, 168, 898, 913; 11E:77; "cutoff-scale": 13:161, 219; "terminal": 10:435; 13sb:93; 13ba:61, 77, 123, 153, 175 (7 occurrences in ch. 12–16; 12:132 until 25 November 2026); 11E:57 now has "the attachment … bound" without the adjective. *Proposed:* *at the ultraviolet cutoff `N`*.
   *Source:* for 12:132, Martin existence/fixed-rung-convergence.tex:92–94: "Write `G_{m,N}` for the selected graph at scale `m` in the history with terminal index `N`".
2. **At the fine end of a comparison that does not start at `N`.** The "terminal norm bounds" of 17m:423, which referred to the fine end `k(n)` of a backward comparison; the line now reads "before multiplication by its constants". *Basis:* R via 11:913–919 for 17m:423. *Where:* 17m:423 ("its constants"). *Proposed:* *at the fine end (scale `k(n)`)*.
*Across chapters:* chapters 5–6 use the word in the same sense as chapters 10–13 (5:705–706, text read). The only real shift is sense 2. The former title at 12:132 was sense 1 by the source text; the new title says "at the ultraviolet cutoff".
*See also:* terminal map; terminal norm bounds; trial; Wilson initialization.

#### test
*Now:* partly replaced: sense 2 by *pairing* ("paired with", "pairing with") and *values of the correlation functionals* (11:2238–2325; 13:274; 14:247, 1023; 15:245, 250; 16:46; 18lp:307–330); sense 3 by *condition* ("loop condition", "condition on the minimum", "Borel conditions", 4:69–114, 222; 5:974; 6:83, 694; at 4:116 upstream's new sentence of 26 November 2026 had "loop test", changed to "loop condition" in the merge; upstream's "loop inequalities" at 4:281–282 was left as written, merge-2026-11-26.md); sense 4 by *indicator of the relaxed regularity condition* and *event indicator* (6:111–112, 236, 1423; 9:543, 549); senses 5 and 6 by *variables* and *plaquettes and edges* (6:325, 342, 610); sense 8 by *evaluation* (7:220), *checked* (10:113) and *curvature coordinates* (2e:60); remains in sense 1 (test function, kept as proposed), at 11:117 and 14:212 (sense 2), 11:402, 413 (sense 7), 9s:229, 11:355, 1019 (sense 8), "free tests" (15:277, 280), "the tested function" (16:220, sense 1), in "test configurations", "test link variables", "test connection" (2:13, 118, 150, 416; see *test configuration*), and in labels.
*Variants:* tested; testing; tested links; free tests; no longer in the text: test against; tested correlation; tested neighborhood; loop test; eligibility test; minimum-cost test; relaxed small-field test; curvature tests.
1. **Test function.** Standard. *Basis:* D (1:359 for "separated test function"). *Where:* ch. 1 (1:353–393, 7 lines); 3:147, 319; 11:117, 1760; ch. 13–16 (30 lines: 13:43, 44, 111, 121, 195, 244, 293, 297; 14:17, 202, 229, 514, 517, 619, 621, 773; 16:96, 98, 158, 166, 175, 181, 220, 287, 301, 317, 364, 368, 391, 465); 17:69, 70; 18:8, 260, 307, 323, 342, 367, 408, 417, 418. *Proposed:* keep; reserve *test* for this sense (as `notation.md` does).
2. **Pairing.** "Tested against" = paired with all spectators, exterior words or word vectors; "tested correlation" = the value of a correlation functional on an insertion; "tested / testing" = smeared with a test function or paired with fixed spectators. The text now writes "paired with", "pairing with" (13:274; 15:245, 250; 16:46; 18lp:307, 310, 320), "the values of the correlation functionals" (11:2325; 14:1023), "free correlation functionals whose values give an injective map" (14:247) and "smeared with test functions" (16:91). *Basis:* R. *Where:* 11:2238, 2240, 2281, 2293, 2325; 13:274; 18lp:218, 307, 310, 320, 330; 14:212, 247, 1023; 15:245, 250; 16:46, 91, 121, 154, 155, 306; 18:7, 218, 251; 18r:37 ("test" or "testing" now only at 11:117 and 14:212). *Adopted:* *value of the correlation functional*, naming the pairing each time.
3. **Borel condition on the configuration.** A condition deciding which case of a definition applies ("loop condition" (4:69), "eligibility conditions" (6:83), "every loop condition and every condition on the minimum of the objective" at 5:974, comparing the minimum of the block-average objective `P_e` with `ε_pred`, 4:435); at 4:533–536 the single-plaquette inequality of (4.relaxed-test), now called "the *relaxed regularity condition*" (4:533). "The cutoffs and large-field indicators in the sector definition are fixed Borel conditions" (6:694). *Basis:* R (6:693–694); D (4:533). *Where:* 4:69–114, 222 ff., 483–493; 5:974; 6:83, 694, 1347 (all "condition"). *Adopted:* *condition*; *smallness condition* (written "regularity condition").
4. **Indicator of such a condition.** `χ^rel = 1{χ(U_p) ≤ t_m e^{dist/R^rel} for every p}` (defined 4:527–531) is "the indicator of the relaxed regularity condition (4.relaxed-test)" (6:111–112); "The retained indicators of the relaxed regularity condition also equal one" (6:1423). Not a smooth cutoff. The adjective "tested" (restricted by this indicator) is now "restricted by its event indicators" (9:543, 549). *Basis:* D (4:527–531 with 6:111–112). *Where:* 6:111–112, 236, 782, 926, 1330, 1423; 9:543, 549 (no longer "test" at any of them). *Adopted:* *indicator of the regularity condition*; the text's own *event indicator*.
5. **Variable.** The numbers `r_p`, `n_e` compared with thresholds ("If every variable `r_q^f` or `n_e` in their fixed macro-box is at most …", 6:325). *Basis:* R. *Where:* 6:325, 342, 610 ("variable", "plaquettes and edges"). *Adopted:* *plaquette and edge variables*.
6. **Location.** The plaquette or mismatch edge itself; the most frequent sense in chapter 6, now written "plaquettes and edges" or "elements of `A`" ("The set `D ⊂ A_f ∪ A_n` consists of the plaquettes and edges whose variables `r_p^f`, `n_e` exceed `t_hi`", 6:89). *Basis:* R. *Where:* 6:19, 54, 79, 89, 328, 421, 1162, 1168, 1335, 1356 (no "test" remains in chapter 6 prose). *Adopted:* *plaquettes and edges*.
7. **Dependence set.** "Tested links", "tested neighborhood" = the links (sites) on which a function depends. *Basis:* R. *Where:* 11:402, 413; 11R:108 (now "the neighborhood on which it depends"). *Proposed:* *the links on which … depends*.
8. **Evaluation or check.** "One transverse evaluation determines that scalar" (7:220); "only finitely many degrees are checked" (10:113); "tested" at 11:355, 1019; "each tested coarse configuration satisfying the regularity condition" = under consideration (9s:229, inferred); "Curvature coordinates avoiding a prescribed link" (2e:60, title). *Basis:* R; I at 9s:229. *Where:* 2e:60; 7:220; 9s:229; 10:113; 11:355, 1019. *Proposed:* *evaluation*; *check*; *curvature coordinates*.
9. **Classical test connection.** See *test configuration*.
*Literature:* for sense 3 (a Borel condition on the configuration and its indicator, 4:533–536; 5:974): **characteristic function** `χ`, `χ_k`, `χ({…})` (B87 p. 256: "The characteristic function χ_k restricts the integral to small fluctuation fields"; p. 266, (2.9); "small field characteristic functions", "large field characteristic function(s)", B88b; D1 p. 1330010-28: "we add some characteristic functions"). The same object. Notation clash: in Bałaban `χ` is a characteristic function, in v3 the distance from the identity. Suggested: *characteristic function (indicator) of the condition*; drop "test" for this sense.
*Across chapters:* the meaning changed by chapter group; senses 3–6 no longer use the word, which now stands in sense 1 throughout, in sense 2 at 11:117 and 14:212, in sense 7 at 11:402, 413 and in sense 8 at 9s:229, 11:355, 1019; "free tests" (15:277, 280) are the free correlation functionals. 4:527–537, 6:83, 6:694 and 6:1347 are conditions, not indicators (text read at 4:531–537, 6:82–84, 693–695, 1346–1348). For sense 2, not *correlation functional*: the phrase names a value.
*See also:* test configuration; event indicator; cutoff; likelihood.

#### thermal
*Now:* replaced by *the coefficient of the Gaussian contribution (ch07:thermal)* (7:774–775); the word survives only in the label `ch07:thermal`.
*Variants:* label `ch07:thermal`; thermal term, thermal function, thermal determinant (sources); no longer in the text: thermal coefficient.
- **Meaning.** "Thermal" names the part of the logarithm of the stationary Gaussian integral that does not carry the factor `β`: the Gaussian (one-loop) contribution `T(v) = 𝓛_{m+1}(U_v) + ½ log det Q(v) − log J_Haar(v)` of 7:236–238, marked by the label `ch07:thermal`. The "thermal coefficient" is its marginal quadratic coefficient `α(T)`, in the sense of (ch07:alpha): "The preceding contact proof identifies the coefficient of the Gaussian contribution (ch07:thermal)" (7:774–775) says that the coefficient `α` of the actual `T(v)` equals that of the determinant term in which the full Hessian of the block penalty has been replaced by its constraint pullback (the block average contact term removed), so that "the comparison concerns the same density, averaging operation and critical configuration throughout" (7:775–776).
  *Basis:* I (7:236–238, from the label); S for "thermal" and for which coefficient. *Where:* 7:775 ("the coefficient of the Gaussian contribution"); label at 7:237. *Adopted:* *the coefficient `α` of the Gaussian contribution `T(v)`*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/thermal-contact-cancellation.tex:83–88` "`½ log det H_tree − log j(y) = ½ log det M_act − log det Γ`. Adding the inherited loop gives the thermal term of the stationary Gaussian integral with exactly its original normalization"; `:268–287` "We have proved that the actual and the core one-loop determinant terms … have the same leading quadratic coefficient. … the thermal term of the stationary integral is the sum of the first of these and the inherited loop evaluated on the stationary branch. … the thermal term and the core determinant term have the same leading quadratic coefficient"; `existence/stationary-output-construction.tex:410–413` "the thermal function `ϑ(x) = 𝓛_U(x,ρ_k(x)) + ½ log det D_z²𝒯(x,ρ_k(x)) − log Π_b J(ρ_k(x)_b)`".
*Literature:* "terms of the order 0 in the coupling constants"; **normalization factor** `Z^{(k)}`; Haar density `σ(A)` (B87 p. 260: "We have written explicitly terms of the order 0 in the coupling constants"; p. 267: "Terms of the order 0 in g_k are (2.11) … This quadratic form defines the k-th normalization factor Z^{(k)}(U_{k+1})"; B85e p. 260: "we express the Haar measure dU′ as dU′ = σ(A′)dA′"). An analogue of `T(v) = 𝓛_{m+1}(U_v) + ½ log det Q(v) − log J_Haar(v)`. "Thermal" has no precedent. Suggested: *zeroth-order (in the coupling) term: fluctuation determinant and Haar density*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 7 only (text read at 7:234–239, 773–776). The word survives only in the label `ch07:thermal`.
*See also:* contact term; prescribed coarse classical action.

*Variants:* small-field threshold; lower bound on the reference coupling; lower bound on `N`; lower bound on the period; upper bound on `r`; approximation thresholds (13ba:311); no longer in the text: coupling-threshold (13ba:262, 265); coupling threshold; inverse coupling threshold; coupling entry threshold; mesh threshold; period threshold; cutoff / convergence / translation thresholds.
1. **Lower bound on `β̂`.** "Coupling threshold": a lower bound imposed on `β̂` at a stage ("for `β̂` sufficiently large"); now written "the lower bound on the reference coupling" ("after increasing the lower bound on the reference coupling", 6:327; 9:203), at 9s:212, 224 "the lower bound on `z`". *Basis:* R. *Where:* 6:327, 437; 7:1203; 9:146, 203, 432, 711; 9s:212, 224; 10:38–39, 104–105, 110, 630, 646; 11:279, 443, 711; 11R:10; 11E:32; ch. 12–16 (about 14; the former "coupling-threshold" of 13ba:262, 265 belonged to sense 4); 17:134; 17w:24, 42, 74, 76, 95; 17c:142, 235, 237, 386, 388; 17m:142–143, 174, 185, 315, 346–347, 365, 427; 19:20 (19 in ch. 17–19). *Adopted:* *lower bound on `β̂`* ("for `β̂` sufficiently large, depending on `j`, `L`"), written "lower bound on the reference coupling".
2. **Small-field threshold `t`.** An upper bound on the field size (`t_m = β̂_m^{-1/2} M_m^cut`, 4:454–458, label `ch04:thresholds`; also `ε_pred`, `t_f`); in chapters 11 and 11R also the restarted threshold `ϑ` ("The restarted large-field threshold is `ϑ`, not `t`", 11:749). *Basis:* D (4:454–458). *Where:* 2:326, 449; 4:454–458, 464, 578, 614; 9:19; 10:107, 648, 729, 737, 902; 11:749, 795, 1226, 1319; 11R:19–23, 46–47, 72, 188; 11E:114; 13sb:63; 13ba:75; 18lp:179; 17c:317; 17m:153, 272, 304, 378, 424. *Proposed:* keep *small-field threshold `t_m`*; reserve the unqualified word for it.
3. **Lower bound on the cutoff `N`.** "Mesh threshold" ("once the mesh is sufficiently fine relative to the fixed cell in continuum units", 11:1128–1129; "one lower bound on `N` ensures the required nonwrapping", 11:1134–1135); cutoff, convergence and translation thresholds (an `N_0`), now "lower bound(s) on `N`", "on the cutoff and on the translations". At 13ba:311 "approximation thresholds may depend on each fixed pair" is kept: the approximation holds "on the ordered cutoff and volume tails" (13ba:210), whose thresholds bound both `p = P(k)` and `N = n(j)` (13:215–216), so "lower bounds on `N`" would narrow the statement. *Basis:* R (11:1128–1136; 13ba:210, 337–339). *Where:* 11:1124, 1134–1136, 1820, 2356; 12:266, 397; 13:27, 390; 13sb:140; 13ba:311 ("approximation thresholds"); 15:264; 18:168; 18r:21. *Adopted:* *for `N` large enough*, written "lower bound on `N`"; *thresholds* where both cutoff and volume are bounded (13ba:311).
4. **Lower bound on the starting scale of a stage.** See *threshold for the starting scale*, now "lower bound on the starting scale" (in chapters 10–11: 10:63, 609, 695; 11R:80, 220). The former "coupling-threshold requirement" and "coupling-threshold conditions" of 13ba:262, 265 were of this kind: the condition `b_q log 3 ≥ 2 log(ȷ_q+7)` is on the minimum starting scale `b_q` (10:122–127); the text now reads "a permitted finite requirement on the starting scale" (13ba:262) and "among the conditions on the starting scales of Section (ch10:schedule)" (13ba:265), on 25 November 2026 (decision 48).
5. **Lower bound on the period.** "Enlarge one lower bound on the period" (2e:210). *Basis:* R (2e:210). *Where:* 2e:210. *Adopted:* *lower bound on the period*.
6. **Upper bound on the radius `r`.** "Small-`r` threshold", now "the upper bound on `r`" (18:168; 18r:71); "The constants and threshold are uniform" (18:208) keeps the word. *Basis:* R. *Where:* 18:168, 208; 18r:71. *Proposed:* *for `r` small enough*.
*Literature:* no word; for the small-field threshold `t_m = β̂_m^{−1/2} M_m^cut`, `M_m^cut = exp((log log β̂_m)²)`: **`ε_1 = g_k p(g_k)`**, `p(g) = b_0(1 + log g^{−1})^{p_0}` (B85e p. 257: "we take ε_1 = g_0 p(g_0), where p(g) = b_0(1 + log g^{−1})^{p_0}, p_0 > 2 and b_0 is a sufficiently large absolute constant"); `ε_j = g_j A_0 (log g_j^{-2})^{p_0} = g_j p_0(g_j)`, with fluctuation thresholds `δ_j = g_j A_1 p_0(g_j)`, `δ'_j = g_j A_1 p_1(g_j)`, `p_1 < p_0` (B88b p. 255, (2.4); pp. 247–248; B89a p. 183); `p_k = (−log λ_k)^p` (D1). An analogue of the same form, coupling times a slowly growing function: Bałaban's uses the actual coupling and a power of the logarithm; v3's uses the reference coupling `β̂_m`, which does not move when `β` is varied (4:458–465), and a factor growing faster than every power of `log β̂`. In B87 the threshold is a fixed small `ε_0`, `ε_1`, with the alternative `γ_k = C log(L^kε)^{−1}` (p. 266) the only scale-defined threshold; in B85a, B85b it is a fixed small constant `α_0 ≤ c_2(d,L)` with no dependence on the coupling. Suggested: cite B85e (7) and B88b (2.4) as the model of `t_m`; where `M_m^cut` is described add "the role of Bałaban's `p_0(g_k)`".
*Across chapters:* chapters 1–9 have senses 1, 2 and 5 (text read at 2:326, 9:19, 2e:210); senses 3, 4 and 6 are added from chapter 10 on, and chapters 10, 11, 11R and 11E continue to use senses 1 and 2. The word now stands mainly in sense 2. At 4:215, 224 and 450 the text now also says "threshold" ("Choose the threshold `ε_pred`", 4:215; "Equality with either threshold", 4:224; "The threshold used to distinguish small from large fields", 4:450). 17m:197 "stage orders and thresholds" is not assigned to a sense. Other occurrences in chapters 10–11, not classified (mostly "the threshold" or "stage threshold" without qualifier): 11:221, 523, 939, 1192, 1344, 1402, 1605, 1850, 1909, 2043, 2249, 2340; 11R:250, 266; 11E:115. At 10:158–159, 698; 11:464, 723 the text now says "lower bound … on the reference coupling" (sense 1), and 11E:112 "These conditions"; the word no longer stands there.
*See also:* threshold coordinates; threshold for the starting scale; floor; cutoff; tail events.

#### tolerance exponent
*Now:* replaced by *exponent `q` of the initial remainder bound* ("it is unrelated to the fixed exponent `q` of the initial remainder bound", 11:1679).
- **Meaning.** The fixed exponent `q ≥ 6` in the bound `H^{−q}` on the regular remainder with which the recurrence on the interval `k → ℓ` starts (the "tolerance"); in v3 it is the `q` of "For `H^{−q} ≤ z ≤ H^{−4}`" (11:1612) and of the terms `H^{−q}` at 11:1632, 1641. Each step multiplies the bound by at most `α + 2`, and `q` is taken so large that after the `k − ℓ` steps a prescribed negative power of `H` remains. "The density `q_k` with insertions … is unrelated to the fixed exponent `q` of the initial remainder bound" (11:1677–1679; "The source density" before the conversion) only warns against the clash of letters.
  *Basis:* S; R for the occurrences of `H^{−q}` (11:1612, 1632, 1641). *Where:* 11:1679. *Adopted:* *the exponent `q` of the initial remainder bound `H^{−q}`*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/allarity-marked-propagation.tex:197–200 ("Let the tolerance exponent be `q ≥ 6` and the regular step multiplier be `α ≥ 0`. Set `d_0 = H^{−q}`, `d_j = (α+2)^j d_0`"), :207–209 ("the initial marked representation has regular remainder bound `d_0`"), :289–291 ("If the later propagation requires an extra factor `H^{uV+2}` in the regular bound, purchase `q ≥ κ + uV + 2`"). No Lean declaration was sought.
*Across chapters:* one place.

#### trajectory
*Now:* partly replaced: in sense 1 "renormalization trajectory" is written *renormalization-group trajectory* as proposed (1:208, 488; 2:436; 4:20; 8:377; 9:975; MT:63); in sense 2 "selected trajectory" is replaced by *common trajectory* (11R:90; 12:134, 372), and "trajectory" remains there, not the proposed "construction of Chapter 10".

Sense 1 (the sequence of densities and couplings at one cutoff) is the same object. "Trajectory" has no support in the papers read. #### translation semigroup
*Formerly:* *heat*.
*In the text:* (and "semigroup", 14:865; 16:454–499); "energy" for "heat energy" (14:421); the word survives only in labels (`ch14:heat`, `ch14:heat-pairing`, `ch16:heat-function`, `ch16:heat-decay`).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: heat semigroup, operator, energy, orbit, analyticity, damping, limit, pairing, intertwiner.
- **Meaning.** `E_μ(t) = e^{−tH_μ}`, `t ≥ 0`: the self-adjoint, strongly continuous contraction semigroup induced on the reflection Hilbert space of the axis `μ` by translation of positive-time words by `t e_μ`: "On formal word sums put `T_t c = [τ_t c]_μ` … The operators descend and extend to self-adjoint contractions `E_μ(t)` … `E_μ(t) = e^{−tH_μ}`" (14:39–58). In chapter 14 there is one for every coordinate axis `μ`. "Nonnegative energy" (14:421, formerly "heat energy") is the spectral variable of `H`; "this elementary analyticity of the translation semigroup" (14:83, formerly "heat analyticity") is the holomorphy of `z ↦ e^{−zH_μ}` in `Re z > 0`. "Heat" is the name the source texts and the formalisation give to this semigroup; no heat equation or Laplacian appears in v3, in the sources or in the Lean definition.
  *Basis:* R (14:39–58; named at 15:27). *Where:* 14:83, 421, 442, 862, 865; ch. 15 (6 uses); ch. 16 (7 uses); 18 uses in all, now "translation semigroup", "semigroup" or "energy". *Adopted:* *the translation semigroup `e^{−tH_μ}`*, `H_μ` the Hamiltonian (general knowledge: the Euclidean time-translation semigroup of Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction); *energy* for "heat energy"; *analyticity of the semigroup in `Re z > 0`* for "heat analyticity".
  *Source:* Scott part2/G-section.tex:475: "*The heat semigroup.* On the span of positive words, `‖τ_{te_4}v‖² = ⟨v, τ_{2te_4}v⟩ ≤ ‖v‖ ‖τ_{2te_4}v‖` … Spectral calculus … defines `H_4^OS = ∫_{(0,1]} −log v dP(v)` from the spectral measure `P` of the time-one heat operator"; :488 for the other axes. Martin existence/physical-ward-analytic-continuation.tex:7 "positive-time heat evolution". Lean `YM.OS.Semigroup`, YM/OS/Flow.lean (definition read; file title "Heat operators on actual GNS spaces": `E : ℝ≥0 → H.Op` with `E 0 = id`, `E(t+s) = E t ∘ E s`, `‖E t‖ ≤ 1`, `(E t)† = E t`, `t ↦ E t v` continuous, and commuting isometric transverse translations `U`); `YM.OS.Chamber`, YM/OS/Dynamics.lean (definition read: `GNS.plant (travel v t) = flow.E t (GNS.plant v)`); `YM.OS.travel`, YM/OS/Schwinger.lean (definition read: every point of the positive word `v` is translated by `t` times the basis vector of the axis); `contract`, YM/OS/Flow.lean (statement read: `‖timed X t p‖ ≤ ‖X.stems p‖`, the bound of 14:45–52).
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 14–16. First prose use of the name is 14:83 ("This elementary analyticity of the translation semigroup"), before 15:27 names the semigroup (text read at 14:82–84, 15:27). Not *transfer semigroup*: *transfer* is the word for moving a density, coefficient or current through the block steps.

#### transport
*Now:* partly replaced by *contour variable* and *holonomy* (sense 1: 4:26, 38, 52, 355; 5:1013, 1018; 7:652; 17m:32; 2e:80), *linearization of the critical configuration* and *induced map on curvatures* (sense 2: 5:453, 528; 7:1101, 1149; 9s:175, 197; 11:648), *transfer* (sense 3: 11:886, 1875, 1963; 12:278; 18gq; 18lp; 17t:3; RG:17) and *conjugated* or *image* (senses 4 and 5: 11:1793, 1818; 17w:68; 14:953; 6:973), *conjugated derivatives* for "Derivative transport" (sense 4: title 14:234 "Conjugated derivatives and smooth comparison", 14:307; decision of 26 November 2026); in upstream's new text of chapter 4 "transport" was replaced by *contour variable* at 4:28, 115, 386 (second round of merge corrections, 26 November 2026); remains for parallel transport (1:80–81, 153; 2:171; 6:184–222, "parallel-transport"; 7:150, 988, 1191), at 11:336 and 11:1054 ("transporting supports …", "the transport part of Hypothesis (H)", since 25 November 2026; the sense of part (d) of Assumption `ch09:forest-assumption`, the bijection of labels under a lattice symmetry, close to sense 5), at 9:915 ("exact transport identities"), 10:357 ("free transports") and 11:1756 ("exact exterior-transport identities"), in "transported curvature(s)" (chapters 2, 2e; 4:541, 546; 7:150, 354, 1022; 10:316), at 14:826 (sense 6), on 18 lines of `09-forest-average.tex` (e.g. 9f:17, 265 "*Transport.*", 575, 941: transport of terms and activities by the lattice symmetries, sense 5) and in labels; 95 lines in all (92 before the merge of 26 November 2026), labels excluded, many of them "transporter(s)" (see *connector*).
*Variants:* transported; row transport; curvature transport; two-form transport; free transports; exterior-transport identities; polynomial transport steps; derivative transport; transporting all coefficients together.
1. **Parallel transport.** Holonomy along a path, introduced as `T_U(x→y;o)`, now "the contour variable along the contour which changes coordinates in order `o`" (4:38–39); "transported kernel" = flat kernel made gauge covariant by parallel transport along fixed paths; "transported (covariantised) rows" (7:988–990); "row transport" (1:80) is a convention, stated after the definition of *contour*, *contour variable* and *holonomy* (1:78–80). *Basis:* R (4:38). *Where:* 1:153–154 and ch. 1, 2, 2e throughout; 2:171–176; 2e:80–83; 4:26, 38, 52, 355, 541, 546; 5:1013, 1018; 6:184–191, 222; 7:150, 354, 652, 1018–1022, 1191; 10:316; 17m:32. *Adopted:* *contour variable* for the product of the link variables along a *contour* (4:38); *holonomy* only when the contour is closed (2e:80; 4:52); *parallel transport* for the action ("Parallel-transport the coefficients", 6:184); *covariantized kernel* (not checked).
2. **Stationary-field map.** `W`: coarse field ↦ stationary fine field of the Gaussian block step (`QW = I − b⁻¹K_c`, with `b` the penalty parameter; "sends a coarse field to the fine critical configuration", 5:105), and its companion `T` on two-forms ("the induced map on curvatures", 9s:175; "the induced map `T` on curvatures", 9s:197, with `d_{1,f} W_a = H_f^{-1} T H_c d_{1,c}`, 9s:199). The word was attached in particular to `W_s`, now "the operator `W` built with the linear averaging operator `M`" (5:1094), which solves `K_f W_s = M^*K_c`, `M W_s = I − b^{-1}K_c` (5:1097) with the straight average `M`; the derivative of the stationary map in forest coordinates is `W_F`, which differs from `W_s` by a fine gradient. *Basis:* R (5:105; 5:1094–1097). *Where:* 5:453–534 and about 20 further; 6:139; 7:1101, 1125, 1149, 1154, 1214; 9:915; 9s:175, 197; 10:357; 11:648, 651, 1756; 17t:164; 17m:213, 221 (now "linearization", "representative", "induced map"; "transport" remains at 9:915 and 10:357). *Adopted:* *the linearization `W` of the critical configuration*, stating the representative (`W_s` where the operator built with the linear averaging operator `M` is meant, `W_a` or `W_F` otherwise); no symbol is renamed, and the representative is written wherever `W` is unqualified: `W_s` at 5:527–535, `W_F` in chapter 11 (11:642), `W_a` in `17-current-contraction.tex`; *induced map `T` on curvatures*.
   *Source:* Lean `YM.Precision.Inputs`, `YM/PREC/TreeMatch.lean` (definition read): the two hypotheses `K H * W = (mean S)ᵀ * K H'` and `mean S * W = 1 − penalty⁻¹ • K H'` on a matrix `W`, which are the identities of 5:1097 with `mean` (`YM/PREC/FrameResponse.lean`, definition read: weighted average over patch points of straight path sums) in the place of `M`. That the Lean matrix is v3's `W_s` is inferred from this agreement; `Inputs` is a hypothesis, and the particular matrix supplied for it was not read.
3. **Transfer through the block steps.** Propagation of a marked density, coefficient or current down the levels by the block maps; "`𝖹_{N,p,d}` transfers a cutoff coefficient to its fixed reference scale" (11:886–887); "transfer steps", "polynomial transfer norm" = the action of one step on polynomials (11:1875, 1963). *Basis:* R; I at RG:17. *Where:* 11:886, 1875, 1963; 12:278; 18gq:13, 77, 85; 18lp:24, 47, 197, 216; 17t:3; 17c:323; 17m:377, 381; 18:132; RG:17 (all now "transfer"); 18:177 only in the label `ch18:signed-transport`. *Adopted:* *transfer (through the block steps)*; "in the direction of the transfer" (11:1349, from 25 to 26 November 2026; now "the coefficient of one transferred insertion").
4. **Image under, or conjugation by, linear maps.** "the mean `μ = 𝓛u` and the conjugated coarse covariance `B_0 = 𝓛κ_ℓ𝓛^T`" (11:1793–1794, 1817–1818); "each conditional covariance is conjugated by the product of the subsequent curvature responses" (17w:67–68); conjugation by the comparison maps `U_{k,d}` (14:234, 307, 953) and their application to a field array (14:286, 287); the "derivative-transport argument" (17:128) is the proposition now titled "Conjugated derivatives and smooth comparison" (14:234–243; formerly "Derivative transport and smooth comparison"). *Basis:* R. *Where:* as listed. *Proposed:* *image under …*; *conjugation by …* (adopted at 14:234, 307 as *conjugated derivatives*, decision of 26 November 2026).
5. **Image under a lattice symmetry.** "each signed orientation with the image of the spanning trees under the symmetry" (6:973). *Basis:* R (6:973). *Where:* 6:973. *Adopted:* *image of the forest under the symmetry*.
6. **"Carries over".** Ordinary. *Where:* 14:826.
*Literature:* **`U(Γ)` for an oriented contour `Γ`** (B85a p. 18, (9): "For an oriented contour Γ … we define U(Γ) = ∏ U(x_i,x_{i+1}), where the order of factors in the product is the same as the order of bonds in Γ"), in particular the contours `Γ_{y,x}` (B84a p. 18, (1.7): "In each block `B(y)` we introduce a family of contours `Γ_{y,x}` connecting the points `y` and `x`"; B85a p. 24: "`Γ_{y,x} = [y,(y_1,…,y_{d-1},x_d)] ∪ … ∪ [(y_1,x_2,…,x_d),x]`"); **contour variable** `U(Γ)` (B85c p. 393: "the contour variables `U(Γ)` were defined by (52), (53) in [5]"; B87 p. 253: "averaged contour variable"); the adjoint action is written `R(U)X = UXU^{-1}` (B85c p. 390). Sense 1 (parallel transport, holonomy, route) is the same object for the single coordinate order that Bałaban uses; v3 uses all 24 orders and an arbitrary root. The phrase "contour variable" occurs in B85c and B87 but not in the text of B85a or B85b, where `U(Γ)` has no noun; neither "holonomy" nor "parallel transport" (as a noun for `U(Γ)`) occurs in B85a, B85b. Adopted (23 November 2026): *contour* for "route", the path of a parallel transport, and *contour variable* `U(Γ)` for the product of links along it ("route matrices"); *parallel transport* stays for the action. At first use: Bałaban has one contour system with a fixed coordinate order, v3 all 24 orders and an arbitrary root. *Holonomy*, the text's own word in chapters 1 and 2, names the same group element. Adopted (24 November 2026): *holonomy* only for a closed contour, *contour variable* for the product along any contour; *path* only in "path action" and "path coefficients" and for paths that are merely counted or summed over.
*Across chapters:* the meaning changed between chapters. Chapters 1–2 have sense 1 only; chapters 4–9 senses 1, 2 and 5; chapters 10–11 senses 1–4; chapters 12–16 senses 3 and 4 (no parallel transport); chapters 17–19 senses 1–4. In the present text the word stands mainly in sense 1. Sense 1 is introduced at 4:38; *parallel transport* stays for the action, and the product of the link variables is the *contour variable* (*holonomy* when the contour is closed). For sense 3 the one word is *transfer*, not *propagation*.
*See also:* transfer; tangent; terminal map; lift; response.

#### tree comparison
*Now:* replaced by *the estimate (ch05:nonlinear-tree) in the block axial gauge* (sense 1: 4:330; 9s:144; title 5:1010 "The estimates in the block axial gauge and the Hessian") and *Poincaré-type inequality* (sense 2: 6:495; 5:1302, 1387); "common-tree comparison" remains at 6:1386.
1. **Nonlinear tree estimate.** The bound `χ(U_e (rep V)_e^{-1}) ≤ C_{j,L} 𝒫_y(U) + 1{e crosses blocks} χ(V_{y,μ} Q_{y,μ}(U)^{-1})` for a fine edge joined to the block roots along the chosen trees (5:1012–1025, equation `ch05:nonlinear-tree`). It is what 4:330–331 announces ("The later estimate (ch05:nonlinear-tree) in the block axial gauge of Chapter 5 needs the averaging operation on both of its branches, including configurations far from the identity") and what 9s:144–146 uses ("By the estimate (ch05:nonlinear-tree) in the block axial gauge, a fine configuration lies in a fixed closed coordinate ball of the chart, the *safe chart*, whenever …"). *Basis:* R (5:1012–1025). *Where:* 4:330; 5:1010–1025, 1034; 9s:144, 237. *Adopted:* *the nonlinear estimate (5.nonlinear-tree) in the block axial gauge*, cited by equation.
2. **Linear inequality.** `‖a‖² ≤ B_{j,L} ‖d_{1,f} a‖² + C_{j,L} ‖𝒬a‖²` for `a = ι_F z`, i.e. vanishing on tree links (5:1044–1050, equation `ch05:tree-comparison`). *Basis:* D (5:1046–1050). *Where:* 5:1046–1050, 1302, 1387; 6:495, 519 ("Poincaré-type inequality"). *Adopted:* *Poincaré-type inequality in the block axial gauge* (the text reserves "coercivity" for the resulting Hessian bound, 5:1153).
*Literature:* no name. Sense 2, `‖a‖² ≤ B_{j,L}‖d_{1,f}a‖² + C_{j,L}‖𝒬a‖²` for `a` vanishing on tree links (5:1044–1050): **Lemma 2.4** of B84b, p. 245, (2.128): for `B` with `B(Γ_{y,x}) = 0`, `L^{d−2} Σ_c |(Q_1B)(c)|² + Σ_p |(∂_1B)(p)|² ≥ (12d²)^{-1} L^{-d-1} ‖B‖²`; the same statement, with Bałaban's `Q_1` and comb trees in place of `𝒬` and arbitrary trees, and an explicit constant. Sense 1, the nonlinear estimate `χ(U_e (rep V)_e^{-1}) ≤ C_{j,L}𝒫_y(U) + 1{e crosses blocks} χ(V_eQ_e(U)^{-1})` (5:1012–1025), and the "chart recognition" of 9s:144–146: **Lemma 1** of B85b, p. 79: "Let `V_0`, `V′V_0` satisfy the condition (1.7) for k = 1 and L arbitrary, and let `(R(V_0)V′)(Γ_{y,x}) = 1` for x ∈ B(y), `|\overline{V′V_0} − \overline{V_0}| < α_1` on Ω_1^(1). Then for α_0, α_1 small the configuration V′ is also small, more precisely we have the bound `|V′ − 1| < 4d²α_0 + α_1`" (quoted from the text layer with symbols restored); a close analogue: both bound a link, in the block axial (tree) gauge relative to a background, by plaquettes plus the deviation of the block average, Bałaban in the sup norm with a regular background `V_0` and the deviation between two averages, v3 with sums over a macro-box, the background `rep V` and the deviation `χ(VQ(U)^{-1})`. For sense 1 nothing was found in B84a, B84b, B85c, B85d; the counterpart is in B85b, so the two findings concern different papers and do not conflict. Adopted (23 November 2026) for the word: *block axial gauge*. Sense 2: *Poincaré-type inequality in the block axial gauge*, citing B84b Lemma 2.4 as the prototype; sense 1: cite B85b Lemma 1 as the antecedent of (5.nonlinear-tree).
*Across chapters:* the subsection title 5:1010 ("The estimates in the block axial gauge and the Hessian") covers both. 4:330 and 9s:144 cannot mean the linear inequality (text read at 4:328–332, 5:1008–1026, 1044–1051, 9s:142–147).
*See also:* tree slice; safe chart.

#### tree slice
*Now:* replaced by *block axial gauge* (5:934; 6:477; 7:560, 1131; 9s:38, 119), *slice of the block axial gauge* (7:901; 17c:151) and *block axial chart* (5:915, 934, 1301); 9s:194 says "the representative `W_F` in the block axial gauge"; "tree coordinates" remains (6:497, 688).
*Also in the text for:* the former *tree gauge* (see those entries).
*Variants:* block axial gauge; block axial chart; slice of the block axial gauge; tree coordinates; no longer in the text: tree gauge; tree slice; tree-straightened; tree-coordinate inverse; tree-gauge representative.
- **Meaning.** The gauge slice on which the links of the chosen trees equal the identity: "The *block axial chart*, the chart of the block axial gauge (the gauge in which the links of the chosen spanning tree of each block equal the identity)" (5:934).
  *Basis:* I; D (5:934). *Where:* 5:919 ff.; 6:473–497, 979, 1499; 7:560, 583, 877–879, 900–902, 1131; 9:74, 240, 926; 9s:38, 119, 194 (now "block axial gauge", "block axial chart" or "slice of the block axial gauge"; at 6:979, 1499 the line names `W_F` only; 9:240, 926 keep "forest"). *Adopted:* *block axial gauge* (*axial gauge* where the blocks are understood), defined once as "the links of a chosen spanning tree of each block equal the identity"; at first use say that v3 allows any spanning tree rooted at the block center, where Bałaban has the tree of the contours `Γ_{y,x}` rooted at a block corner, and that v3 works in this gauge as a chart. It is a different construction from the axial gauge of the patch frames of chapter 4 (base point `z`, coordinate order `o`; see *frame*, *eligible*, *macro-box*): where both occur, say which is meant.
*Literature:* **axial gauge** in blocks: "Axial (Ax) gauge fixing conditions `A(Γ_{y,x}) = 0`, `x ∈ B(y)`, `x ≠ y`", `δ_Ax(A) = ∏_y ∏_{x∈B(y), x≠y} δ(A(Γ_{y,x}))` (B84a p. 19: "we remove it by introducing Axial (Ax) gauge fixing conditions"); "axial gauge conditions in blocks: `(R_{0,y}V′)(Γ_{y,x}) = 1`, x ∈ B(y), x ≠ y" (B85a p. 27); relative to a background, the gauge condition **`Ax_k(𝔅_k, U_0)`** (B85b p. 79, (1.19): "The conditions (1.19) determine uniquely an element in each orbit given by the subgroup (1.14). We denote this gauge condition by `Ax_k(𝔅_k, U_0)`"; B85d p. 281); **block axial gauge** (B87 p. 254); "axial gauge", fixed on "a maximal tree T(y) in each block B(y)" built from "standard contours Γ_yx" (BIJ85 pp. 302–303, for `U(1)`); **tree graph** fixing a gauge (B89a pp. 195–196: "We fix the gauge putting the bond variables equal to 1 for bonds belonging to the tree graph"). The same object up to the choice of tree: the contours `Γ_{y,x}` of B84a (1.7) together form a comb-shaped spanning tree of the block rooted at the corner `y`, so `U(Γ_{y,x}) = 1` for all `x` says that the tree links are `1` (an inference from the definition of the contours; BIJ85 and B89a state the tree explicitly); v3 allows any spanning tree rooted at the block centre. B87 alone was classified "analogue (inferred)", in a row that treats the chapter-4 frames and the tree gauge together without the v3 frame construction having been read; the four other identifications agree and are taken as right. Two cautions: in Bałaban the axial gauge is a delta-function gauge fixing that is then traded for a Landau-type gauge by the Faddeev–Popov procedure (B84a p. 20; B87 pp. 255, 265) and is called the "preliminary gauge condition" (B85b p. 81), whose bound is "too weak" for large `L` (B85b p. 80), whereas v3 works in the tree gauge as a chart (5:935–936); and v3 also uses "axial" for the patch frames of chapter 4, which in Bałaban are the same axial gauge at a different size. Adopted (23 November 2026): *axial gauge* (*block axial gauge*), in place of "tree gauge", "tree slice" and "forest gauge"; the two cautions above are stated at first use, and the block axial gauge of chapter 5 is kept apart in words from the axial patch frames of chapter 4.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 5–7 and 9, now written "block axial gauge" throughout, and in the same sense at 4:330; 11:617, 631, 642; 11R:248 ("block axial charts"); 17c:151; "forest" remains for the spanning forest itself (9:240, 926).
*See also:* tree comparison; forest.

#### trial
*Now:* not applied; "trial" stands throughout; the variants "terminal trial" and "fixed-stencil trial" are replaced by *trial at the ultraviolet cutoff* (11:898, 913) and *trial with fixed link support* (11:922), and "protected trial" (11:2311) by "a trial … satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)"; "protected trial construction" remains at 13:231.
*Variants:* local trial; trial at the ultraviolet cutoff; trial with fixed link support; difference trial; protected trial construction; bounded coarse polynomial trials; coarse trial `V_h`; inclusion trial; trial residual; trial columns; no longer in the text: terminal trial; fixed-stencil trial; protected trial (alone).
- **Meaning.** A candidate local observable: a family `F_{N,p}` which assigns to each cutoff `N`, period `p` and lattice site a function of the gauge configuration on the corresponding torus (e.g. `f = a_N^e F`, 11:922), and which is to be approximated by a normalized local insertion `O_{N,p}(e,v)` (11:952); its image under the block maps is compared with that insertion ("Subtract one normalized local insertion density from the trial at the ultraviolet cutoff", 11:898). The coarse trial `V_h` is given by formula (13ba:216–220); "trial columns" are images of basis vectors under `J_h` (13ba:279–282). A "protected trial" (now only in "the protected trial construction", 13:231; at 11:2311 "a trial at degree `e = d+|l|` satisfying the hypotheses of (ch11:trial-error)") is a trial on a fixed finite stencil with two bounds growing slower than every power of `a_N^{-1}`, one for its derivatives on small-field configurations and one for its supremum on all configurations (see *protected trial*); the finite difference written at the higher degree `d+1` (or `e = d+|l|`), where the factor `a_N^{|l|}` "in the normalization at its filtration index cancels all inverse mesh powers" (11:1068–1073, 2310–2313; 13:231–234), is an example.
  *Basis:* I (the noun is never defined in v3); S for the kind of object; D for `V_h` (13ba:216–220); S for "protected". *Where:* 10:95, 99 ("The value of the trial outside that chart", since 25 November 2026); 11:27, 893–960, 1068, 1079, 2240, 2281, 2299, 2311–2316, 2334, 2354; 11E:93, 147; 13:231, 234, 241, 396; 13ba:12, 17, 26, 31, 48, 157, 216, 280 (11 lines with "trial" in ch. 12–16; 18gq:106 and 18lp:34 cite the backward comparison of a trial without the word); 17m:441–467. *Proposed:* *candidate local observable* (to be approximated by a normalized local insertion).
  *Source:* Lean `YM.Extraction.Lease.Trial C` (YM/Lane/Lease.lean:17; definition read: `(N p : ℕ) → Site (C.side N p) → Config G (C.side N p) → ℂ`), the type of the argument `F` of `RawProtected`; "local" and "candidate" are not in the type and come from the hypotheses put on a trial. For "protected", Martin existence/actual-insertion-derivative-relay.tex:24–35 and Lean `YM.Push.RelayDifference.RawProtected` (YM/Push/RELAY_DIFFERENCE/RawTop.lean:34; definition read); see *protected trial*.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 10–13, 17, 18. "Protected trial" is not *trial with small-field cutoff* and not the "protected change of variables" sense: the text at 11:1067–1073, 2309–2314 and 13:230–235 mentions no cutoff (text read).
*See also:* trial descent; trial encoding; trial inverse coupling correction; terminal; protected; protected trial.

#### trial descent
*Now:* replaced by *backward comparison* (11:948, 2316; 11E:124, 147; 13:241; 17m:458, 466; 18gq:106; 18lp:34); the label `ch11:trial-descent` is unchanged.
*Variants:* backward comparison; bulk bound of the backward comparison (11E:124); no longer in the text (in this sense): descent; bulk descent bound.
- **Meaning.** The propagation of the trial at the ultraviolet cutoff from fine to coarse through the block steps and its comparison with a normalized insertion, giving `c_i + |x_i| ≤ 4(1+C_N) w e^{−(τ_N−τ_i)/8}` (11:916–918). The induction on the cone condition "starts at the coarsest scale with zero coefficient" (11:912); it is not a downward induction.
  *Basis:* R (11:893–920). *Where:* 11:27, 893–920, 948, 2316; 11E:120, 124, 147; 13:241; 17m:458, 466; 18gq:106; 18lp:34 (all "backward comparison"). The section at 11:893, "Backward comparison of a local trial", has the label `ch11:trial-descent`; 13:232 and 18lp:49 cite that label only. *Adopted:* *backward comparison of a local trial (Section 11)*, cited by number.
*Across chapters:* one sense (11:893–920). Not *propagation of the terminal trial down the block steps*: the section title's own wording, backward comparison, is kept.
*See also:* trial; terminal norm bounds; transfer.

#### tuning of the bare coupling
*Formerly:* *shooting*.
*In the text:* ("the bare coupling `β_{N,p,N}` of the Wilson measure is tuned so that it gives the prescribed coarse endpoint `β̄`", 19:21–23; "the choices made in tuning the bare coupling", 10:821).
*Variants:* no longer in the text: shooting parameter.
- **Meaning.** The choice of the bare coupling at the cutoff scale `N` so that the finite trajectory ends at the prescribed coarse value: `β_{N,p,0} = β̄` (10:246–254); "At cutoff `N` and period index `p`, the bare coupling `β_{N,p,N}` of the Wilson measure is tuned so that it gives the prescribed coarse endpoint `β̄`" (19:21–23). The section 10:212 ff. is titled "Tuning a finite history to the coarse endpoint".
  *Basis:* R (19:21–23). *Where:* 10:276, 821; 19:21–23. *Adopted:* *tuning of the bare coupling* (as at MT:62); "shooting" is acceptable with one sentence, as in the shooting method for boundary-value problems.
*Literature:* unnamed in Bałaban: the existence of a bare coupling with prescribed coupling at the unit scale, part of the "coupling constant renormalization" (B87 p. 259, Theorem 2: "there exists a bare coupling constant g_0 = g_0(ε,g) such that the sequence of the effective coupling constants g_k is contained in the interval ]0,γ], and g_K = g"; its proof is deferred, "will be given in a separate paper"); **tuning**, "non-perturbative renormalization" (D1 p. 1330010-42: "To accomplish this tuning we do not at first specify the initial values for ε_k, μ_k but instead specify final values … This is non-perturbative renormalization"; p. 1330010-41, footnote: "This section is not particularly due to Balaban"). The same object (the same statement). v3 proves it by an intermediate-value argument (10:235–254), D1 by a contraction on sequences with prescribed final values. "Shooting" is not used in any paper read. Suggested: *tuning of the bare coupling by prescribing the coupling at the unit scale (B87 Theorem 2)*.
*Across chapters:* one sense; 19:21–23 is an explicit sentence (text read), hence basis R.

#### uniform mass
*Now:* replaced by *uniform probability weight* (4:85, 221–222; 5:977); "positive mass" and "likelihood" (of tags) by *positive probability weight* (4:350; 6:64, 1352) and *normalized weights of the auxiliary index* (6:926, 1023).
*Variants:* uniform probability weight; positive probability weight; normalized weights of the auxiliary index; no longer in the text: uniform branch masses; positive mass (of tags); likelihood (of tags).
- **Meaning.** "Mass" was the probability weight of a tag (now of a value of the auxiliary index): of a frame tag in `𝔹_R × S_4` at a coarse site, or of a block-average tag in `𝔹_R` at a coarse edge; the product of all of them is the weight `λ(U,α)` of the random index `α` (4:231–234). "Uniform mass" is the weight `1/(number of tags)` given to every tag on the minimising branch, where the frame, respectively the block average, does not depend on the tag ("On the minimizing branch give all pairs the same uniform probability weight, but let each pair specify the same minimizing gauge transformation", 4:80–86; "assign uniform probability weight to the redundant values `z ∈ 𝔹_R` of the index of the averaging operation", 4:221–222). On the other branch the eligible frame tags have equal mass and a block-average tag `z` has mass `w_z^av`. A tag has "positive probability weight" when its weight is not zero (6:63–64; 4:350). For tags, "mass" and "likelihood" named the same weights, both now "probability weight" ("Every chosen value of the auxiliary index of Chapter 4 for a local gauge transformation must have positive probability weight", 6:63–64; "The retained values of the auxiliary index for the local gauge transformations have positive probability weight", 6:1351–1352); as a factor of the expansion the likelihood is the weight relative to the uniform law on tags, that is, multiplied by the number of tags, so that it equals one on the minimising branch.
  *Basis:* R (4:80–86, 221–223, 231–234); S for the normalisation of the likelihood. *Where:* 4:85, 222, 350; 5:977; 6:63–64, 678, 1113, 1351–1352 (all "probability weight(s)"). *Adopted:* *probability weights `λ(U,α)`*; *the uniform weight* for "uniform mass", written "uniform probability weight".
  *Source:* Scott `part2/B-section.tex:90`: "and every tag has mass `|𝔹_R × S_4|^{-1}`"; `:95` "eligible tags have equal mass"; `:100`: "predictor tags have uniform mass on `𝔹_R`. Otherwise a tag `z` selects `Q_e^pred = Y_{e,z}`, with mass `w_z^av`. The product of frame and predictor masses is `λ^tag(U, α_tag)`"; `:1193`: "Reference tags are independent uniform tags; their actual likelihoods are included among the factors"; `:1182` "This includes the likelihood relative to uniform tags" (said of the amplitude bound `M_w = 2 + |𝔹_R × S_4| + |𝔹_R|`). Lean `YM.RG.Patch.frameMass`, `YM.RG.Patch.predictorMass`, `YM/RG/Patch.lean` (definitions read): `frameMass` is `1/|FrameTag|` on the minimising branch, otherwise `1/|eligible|` on eligible tags and `0` on the others; `predictorMass` is `1/|Points|` on the minimising branch, otherwise the averaging weight of the tag.
*Across chapters:* chapters 4–6, and "positive probability weight" / "probability weights of the auxiliary index" again at 9s:132, 139, 226 and 11R:362. The "normalized weights of the auxiliary index" of 6:926, 1023 (formerly "likelihood tests" and "likelihood factors") are these same tag weights, taken per coarse site and per coarse edge and normalised by the number of tags; they are not the allocation weights `ϑ_f`, `ϑ_n` (see *likelihood*, sense 2).
*See also:* tag; weight; mass; likelihood; `Q^pred`.

#### unit
*Now:* partly replaced by *identity field* (sense 1, at all the places listed); "stationary units" is removed (9s:170) and "level-`k` units" is now *scale-`k` units* (17m:331, 416); remains in senses 2–5 ("unit vacuum", 14:34; 15:26; 16:463; "units of the support exponent", "cover units", 11:396–533, 942, 1452; 17m:332, 413; units of measurement; "two unit bounds", 11:792).
*Variants:* identity field; unit vacuum; cover units; units of the support exponent; Gaussian units; scale-`k` units; no longer in the text: the unit (sense 1); unit field; unit insertion; unit coordinate; unit column; distinguished unit; exact unit rule; stationary units.
1. **Identity field.** The constant polynomial `𝟏` and the constant function 1 ("The identity field illustrates the simplest section: `P_d^loc[𝟏] = 1` for every `d`", 2:400); as an insertion, the constant field `e_0` and its coefficient (11:89–92); in the continuum, the class of the constant polynomial 1 ("The identity field is fixed at degree zero", 14:225; "preserving reality and the identity field", 14:981). The former "unit column" (2:259–260, now "The column of the identity field is one") is the basis column `P_d^loc[b_{d,i}]` belonging to the basis element `𝟏`, which is the constant function 1. *Basis:* R (2:400; 14:225). *Where:* 2:192, 281, 400; 2:259–260; 2e:227, 236; 3:126, 190, 925, 999, 1032, 1069 (also "kill the unit"); 11:89–92, 389, 451, 1055; 13:60; 14:225, 288, 415, 981; 17:32, 40, 82, 403; 17m:380; 18:111, 385, 433; 19:63 (all now "identity field"; 3:999, 1069 now "annihilates the stress"). *Adopted:* *identity field*.
2. **Of norm one.** In "unit vacuum" (`Ω_μ = [∅]_μ`). *Basis:* I (14:34). *Where:* 14:34; 15:26. *Proposed:* *unit vector `Ω`*.
3. **Unit of the support exponent.** One unit in the exponent multiplying the covering number `c_B(X)`: "Retaining two units of the support exponent bounds these terms by `C exp[−2R/(2B_k+1)]`" (17m:413–414); "Retain two cover units" (11:495); "Keep aside four units" (13ba:144). *Basis:* R (17m:413–414). *Where:* 11:396, 495, 502, 528, 533, 942, 1452; 11R:142; 13ba:144; 17m:332, 413. *Proposed:* *keeping the factor `e^{−2n}` for covering number `n`*; print the inequality.
4. **Unit of measurement.** Ordinary; "scale-`k` units" (17m:331, 416); "Gaussian units" = rescaled by `g` (9:243), inferred; "stationary units" (relative to `Ω e^{−Φ}`) no longer occurs at 9s:170. *Where:* 9:243; 10:129; 11:704, 864, 2306; 17m:331, 416. *Proposed:* keep; *in units of `g`*.
5. **"Unit bounds".** Bounds by one ("two unit bounds", 11:792). *Proposed:* *bounds by one*.
*Across chapters:* sense 1 is the same object throughout; *identity field* is the one equivalent (not *the constant polynomial `𝟏`* or bare *identity*), with "identity insertion `e_0`" where the insertion is meant. The "column of the identity field" (2:259–260) is a basis column in the sense of *column* (text read at 2:257–260).
*See also:* unit endpoints; unit removal; vacuum; column.

#### unit endpoints
*Now:* replaced by the sentence "The identity-field parts of the two endpoint values are equal and cancel" (17m:471).
- **Meaning.** The two end terms of a telescoping sum, in their parts proportional to the identity field. The trace is a forward difference of a degree-three primitive `q`, "whose invariant projection is a multiple of the identity field" (17m:379–380), that is, a multiple of the identity field `𝟏`, the same multiple at both ends. Averaging over `m` consecutive differences telescopes to the difference of the two endpoint values divided by `m a_k`; the identity-field parts of the two endpoint values are equal and cancel, and what remains is at most twice the matching error `C a_k^η`, divided by `m a_k`: "The identity-field parts of the two endpoint values are equal and cancel, leaving at most `2Ca_k^η/(ma_k) = O(a_k^{η/2})`" (17m:471–472).
  *Basis:* R (17m:379–380, 464–472), confirmed by S. *Where:* 17m:471 (once). *Adopted:* *the identity-field parts of the two endpoint values are equal and cancel*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:447` "the transferred trace of `L` is a forward difference. Its degree-three projection is a unit, since simplicity leaves no nonconstant invariant below degree four"; `I-section.tex:451` "In physical units the average of `m` consecutive forward differences telescopes to the difference of the two endpoint values divided by the window length `m a_k`. The unit parts of the two endpoints are equal and cancel, leaving at most twice the endpoint error".
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. The source sentence is now in the text (17m:471); the reason "since simplicity leaves no nonconstant invariant below degree four" is still not given at 17m:380.
*See also:* unit.

#### unmarked gas
*Now:* replaced by *exact-cover gas of the density without insertions* (18lp:186), itself now *sum over disjoint covering families of the density without insertions* (decision of 26 November 2026).
*Variants:* sum over disjoint covering families of the density without insertions; no longer in the text: unmarked gas; exact-cover gas; exact-cover gas of the density without insertions.
- **Meaning.** The exact-cover gas of the density without source variables: the factor `𝒢(U) = Σ_b ∏_{i∈b} K_i(U)` of that density, summed over exact covers `b` with the large-field activities `K_i` that carry no source variable (the degree-zero coefficients). It is a function of the configuration and only one factor of the density; the partition function is the integral of its product with the exponential of the regular action (12:173–184; "The sum over disjoint covering families is a finite polynomial in the latter activities and the fixed indicators of the eligibility conditions", 12:181–183). "Unmarked" said that the activities are those without source variables; "exact cover" names the summation condition; the object is the same.
  *Basis:* R for the exact-cover gas (12:181–184); S that "unmarked gas" names it. *Where:* 18lp:186 ("so this operation never divides by the sum over disjoint covering families of the density without insertions"); 12:181. *Adopted:* the text's "exact-cover gas", with "of the density without insertions" added at 18lp:186, then "exact-cover gas" replaced by "sum over disjoint covering families" (decision of 26 November 2026) (proposed: *the large-field polymer sum without insertions*, or "exact-cover gas" with "of the density without sources").
  *Source:* Martin existence/terminal-marked-construction.tex:127–142: "Its sum is exactly `f_v` times the old gas … Here `R(U)` denotes the value at `U` of the unmarked density of the terminal representation … There is also an identity before multiplication by the unmarked gas." Scott part2/G-section.tex:289: "the scalar, unmarked forced gas, and regular and forced source sums". Lean `YM.RG.Activities.gas`, YM/RG/Activities.lean (definition read), as a factor of `YM.RG.Rep.eval`, YM/RG/History.lean (definition read). The Lean declaration of the density with sources used in the passage 18lp:178–186 was not located, so the statement that the gas there is `Activities.gas` of the density without sources rests on the source wording.
*Across chapters:* one place. "Partition function without insertions" and "density without insertions" are rejected equivalents.
*See also:* unmarked; exact cover; exact-cover gas; vacuum; mark.

#### vacuum
*Now:* replaced in sense 2 by *per-site normalization exponent* (12:248; 13sb:25; 17m:436) and *denominator without insertions* (12:287); remains in sense 1 (14:34; 15:26; 16:452), as proposed, in the standard phrases "uniqueness of the vacuum", "vacuum expectations", "vacuum functional", "vacuum state" (1:418; 14:1034; 15:143–327; 15sp:17; 16:71–499; 18:210; 18r:68; 19:72–143; MT:38, 50, 79), and in sense 3 (9:719; 10:425 "It is not the vacuum energy renormalization", formerly "the vacuum normalization"; 10:821–822 "additive vacuum normalizations").
*Also in the text for:* the former *ground vector* (see those entries).
*Variants:* unit vacuum; vacuum energy renormalization (9:719; 10:425); additive vacuum normalizations (10:821–822); no longer in the text: vacuum denominator; vacuum bound; vacuum normalization (10:425).
1. **The vector `Ω`.** `Ω = [∅]`, the class of the empty word in the reflection Hilbert space. *Basis:* R (14:34). *Where:* 14:34; 15:26; 16:452. *Proposed:* keep, for `Ω` only.
2. **The lattice integral without insertions.** `Z⁰`, as in "vacuum normalization bound" and "vacuum denominator", now "per-site normalization exponent" (12:248; 17m:436) and "denominator without insertions" (12:287). *Basis:* I. *Where:* 12:248, 287; 17m:436. *Proposed:* *normalization without insertions*.
3. **The additive normalization constant** (the constant per site `v_sc`): "The output inverse coupling and the constant per site are now fixed by the coupling constant renormalization and the vacuum energy renormalization" (9:719); "It is an identity of the densities … including the additive normalization constant. That constant is not asserted to converge" (10:268–269); "No convergence of additive vacuum normalizations is asserted" (10:821–822). The sentence "`q_m` is the coefficient `Δ` of the coupling constant renormalization of the step. It is not the vacuum energy renormalization" (10:424–425; "the coefficient `Δ` of" added on 25 November 2026) contrasts `q_m` with this constant; the former wording "vacuum normalization" there meant this constant, not `Z⁰` (sense 2), as this entry used to say. *Basis:* R (9:719–722; 10:268–269, 821–822). *Where:* 9:719; 10:425, 821. *Adopted:* *vacuum energy renormalization* (Bałaban's name, 9:725).
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes between chapters 10–12, 17 (sense 2, no longer with the word), 9–10 (sense 3) and 14–16 (sense 1). The word must not be used for `ker H`, which need not be one dimensional (15:48–49, which now says "zero-energy subspace").
*See also:* vacuum normalization bound; zero-energy subspace; unit.

#### vacuum normalization bound
*Now:* replaced by *per-site normalization exponent* (10:169; 12:248; 13sb:25; 17m:436); "vacuum denominator" by *denominator without insertions* (12:287).
*Variants:* `q_r`, `q_n`, `q^site`; per-site normalization exponent; denominator without insertions; no longer in the text: vacuum normalization bound; vacuum bound; vacuum denominator; per-site normalization cost.
- **Meaning.** The per-site exponent `q_m = 2b_act + κ_m + β b_loc(ρ) + 4D_G log(16/ρ)` at level `m`, taken with `ρ = β̂_m^{-1/2}`: the cost per lattice site of dividing a coefficient integral by the lower bound on the partition function ("positivity gives `Z ≥ e^{v_0−V[…]}`", 11:801–814, (11.replicated-bound)). `q` (11:810–813), `q_k` in (11.root-bound) (11:821), `q_r` (12:248) and `q_i^site` (13sb:24–25) are this one function of the level. The bound at 12:244, `exp{|Λ_{r,p}| q_r + n(x_r+y_r+2)}/∏w_i`, is (11.replicated-bound) at level `r`; 13sb:24–25 calls the same quantity "the per-site normalization exponent of (11.replicated-bound)", and 12:248 now says "`q_r` is the per-site normalization exponent of (ch11:replicated-bound) at scale `r`"; the exponent `(a_m/a_k)⁴ q_k` of (11.root-bound) is the `L_*⁴ B_n⁸ q_n` of 17m:433. The "denominator without insertions" (12:287) is the division by the integral `Z⁰` without sources.
  *Basis:* R via 11:801–814 for `q_n` (17m:436) and `q^site` (13sb:24–25); R (12:248) that `q_r` is the same quantity. *Where:* 10:169 (`q_{m+1}^site`); 12:248, 287; 13sb:24–25; 17m:430, 436. *Adopted:* *per-site normalization exponent `q_m`* (the per-site constant of the lower bound on the partition function, (11.replicated-bound)), under one symbol; *denominator `Z⁰`*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/fullmesh-correlation-cauchy.tex:208–218: "The normalized density estimate proved in Subsection [centered-construction] gives `|F_N(z)| ≤ C_r := exp{|Λ_{r,p}|τ_r + |V|(x_r+y_r+2)}/ω_w(S)` … Its integral and its vacuum normalization remain exactly those above" (the bound of 12:244 with `τ_r` for `q_r`); existence/centered-construction.tex:86–110 (eq. `ex-centered-sail`: exponent `s[2 exCost + κ + β baseBudget + 4d_G log(16/ρ)] + |V|(x+y+2f)`), :42 "`t_k` is the vacuum treasury per site at that depth"; existence/actual-phase-grid-approximants.tex:126 "`𝒯_m` is the vacuum treasury". Scott part2/E-section.tex:117 (`(a_m/a_{k(m)})⁴ q_{k(m)} = o(s_{k(m)})`; :44 has the schedule form `(ℓ_iB_i²)⁴ q_{i+1} = o(s_{i+1})`), :362 ("per-cell site cost"). Lean `YM.Vac.treasury`, YM/Vac/Treasury.lean (definition read; docstring "Numerical expense per site ignoring source markers": `2(δ + loopsPrice) + forcedAllowance m + β·baseBudget(clip, r, u) + 4·finrank_ℝ(G.Mat)·log(16/u)` with `u = hatCoupling m = β̂_m^{-1/2}`, `β = 2β̂_m`, `δ = allowance m`); `YM.RG.Rep.exCost`, `YM.RG.Rep.denominator`, YM/Vac/Shelter.lean (definition and statement read: `exp(scalar − |sites|(exCost + β·baseBudget) − |edges|·finrank·log(16/s)) ≤ ∫ eval`); `YM.Vac.suffices_bill` (statement read: `finalBill ≤ |sites|·treasury + q(u+c+d·b)` on a selected history); `YM.Vac.treasury_stage` (statement read: eventually `treasury A m ≤ fiat`, a stage constant plus `4·finrank·(log 16 + ½ log β̂_m)`). The Lean terms were matched to `q` formula by formula (`loopsPrice`, `baseBudget` not opened); `treasury` has `β = 2β̂_m`, the upper end of the coupling band, where 11:810 has the actual `β`.
*Across chapters:* one quantity, now under one name (per-site normalization exponent) in chapters 12, 13sb and 17m, with its source in chapter 11. Not *bound on the normalization without insertions*, which loses "per site". The letter `q_n` also denotes the sup-norm bound per site of 11R:226–255 (this clash was not examined against the sources), and `q_m` the coupling constant renormalization at 10:424. The source texts write `τ_r`, `t_k`, `𝒯_m` ("vacuum treasury per site") or `q_k` ("per-cell site cost") for it; the letters `q_r`, `q_n`, `q^site` remain.
*See also:* vacuum; value cost; positive-density estimate; cost.

### W

#### walk
*Now:* partly replaced by *contour* (4:116, 119; 5:1005, 1013, 1026; 6:185), *path* (12:54) and *sequence* (14:553); remains at 6:1310–1313 and 9:896 ("rooted spanning-walk count"), where the walks are counted or followed, not multiplied along.
*Variants:* spanning walk ("rooted spanning-walk count", 9:896); no longer in the text: route.
- **Meaning.** A lattice path ("rather than all paths of a given length", 12:53–54; the contour from a fine edge to the block roots, 5:1013). At 14:553 "a sequence `i_0,…,i_N` through `I`" is a finite sequence in an index set.
  *Basis:* I (ch. 4–6); R (12:53–54; 14:553). *Where:* 4:116, 119; 5:1005, 1013; 6:185 ff. ("contour"); 6:1310–1313 ("walk"); 9:896 ("rooted spanning-walk count"); 12:54 ("paths"); 14:553 ("sequence"). *Adopted:* *contour* where the links are multiplied along the walk (the places shared with *route*: 4:116, 119; 5:1005, 1013; 6:185 ff.); *path* where lattice paths are only counted or summed over (chapter 9; 12:54); *sequence* at 14:553.
*Literature:* name clash. In v3 a walk is a lattice path, which Bałaban calls a **contour** (B84a p. 18; B85a p. 18). In the literature a **random walk** `ω` is a sequence of cubes or localization domains in the **(generalized) random walk expansion** of a propagator (B85c p. 409, p. 413: "a random walk `ω` is a sequence"; B88a pp. 1–3, walk `ω = ((α_0,X_0),…,(α_n,X_n))`; D1 §2.4, p. 1330010-12, `G_k = Σ_ω G_{k,ω}`). Adopted (23 November 2026): *contour* for the walks along which links are multiplied, *path* for the others; "random walk" is reserved for the expansion of an inverse, which v3 does not sum (see *window*).
*Across chapters:* same sense in chapters 4–12; a sequence of indices at 14:553. The word now stands only at 6:1310–1313 and 9:896.
*See also:* path; route.

#### warning
*Now:* replaced by *cutoff remainder* (6:1483; also 6:840, 1025) and *the joint tail bound for cutoff remainders* (11:320). Since 26 November 2026 the string occurs once more, only as the source file name `gaussian-warnings.tex` in the margin note at 6:1025 (grep); not in the prose.
*Variants:* cutoff remainder; joint tail bound for cutoff remainders; no longer in the text: warning; Warnings; actual warning estimate.
- **Meaning.** A cutoff remainder at one address: a factor `w = γ·a − 1`, where `a` is an allocation weight, a tag weight or a contraction factor and `γ` a bounded smooth cutoff, or `γ_e − 1` for a chart cutoff on a fine bond. It is zero inside the compulsory region (see *compulsory*, sense 2), and outside it vanishes unless some Gaussian coordinate within `2B` of its assigned coarse site has an excursion (the event `ℰ_w` of 6:843–849). A warning is not small pointwise; what is small is the probability that all warnings of a term are nonzero. The *warning estimate* is this joint Gaussian tail bound: for a set `X` of distinct addresses the probability is at most `E^{|X|}`, with `E` decaying faster than every power of the coupling parameter; this gives the `x^{-1}` of 11:320–321. "Cutoff remainders carry the joint-event factors proved above" (6:1483) says that each remainder contributes one such factor; "A cutoff remainder, a cutoff factor minus one, is bounded but need not be pointwise small" (6:840). The two readings formerly separated, cutoff remainder and cutoff-failure event, are the factor and the event on which it is nonzero.
  *Basis:* S; I for the link between 11:320 and 11:1618. *Where:* 6:1483 ("cutoff remainders"); 11:320 ("the joint tail bound for cutoff remainders"). *Adopted:* *cutoff remainder* at 6:1483; *the joint tail bound for cutoff remainders (ch06:joint-tails)* at 11:320, without the label. The event on which a warning is nonzero is a *large fluctuation-field event*, not an event of the large-field set.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/gaussian-warnings.tex:4–8`: "A warning factor, for example, need not be small on a configuration with a large fluctuation. What is small is the probability that all warnings in a given term are present"; `:206–207` (quoted under *compulsory*); `:131–133` (`eq:warning-actual-price`): `P{Z ∈ C(X;t,2B)} ≤ E(x)^{|X|}`; `:154–161` "`E` decays faster than every negative power of `h`"; `:241–246` (`lem:warning-vanishes`); Martin `existence/actual-local-compiler-handoff.tex:254–257` "The warning estimate on the corrected alphabet". Lean `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.WarningAt` (index type, six kinds of address) and `YM.ConnectedActivityE6.Coat.detect`, `YM/AnalyticNext/CONNECTED_ACTIVITY_JETS_E6/Alert.lean` (definitions read): `detect` is `mayor` on the first five kinds and `aura` (chart cutoff minus one) on fine bonds. The Lean theorem for the probability bound was not located.
*Literature:* see *cutoff remainder*.
*Across chapters:* one object in chapters 6 and 11, now called "cutoff remainder" at 6:840, 1025 (source: "inside the compulsory region the warning is zero by definition"; since 26 November 2026 6:1025 states this convention: a cutoff factor meeting `A^{[300B]}`, a chart cutoff `A^{[304B]}`, "is kept whole as a factor of the sector, and its cutoff remainder is set to zero") and 1483 and at 11:320. The object belongs to the Gaussian-tail mechanism of chapter 6, not to the large-field set (6:7–11). 6:840 now glosses it as "a cutoff factor minus one"; the source's fuller definition ("A warning factor is either a bounded cutoff times one of these factors minus one, or a bond cutoff minus one") is not given.
*See also:* tail events; cutoff-failure event; cutoff remainder; compulsory.

2. **Exponential support or path-length weight.** The factor `e^{σ c_B}` in polymer norms, and exponential weights in path length. *Basis:* R. *Where:* 4:614; 7:168, 1012, 1095; 8:16, 78, 156, 177–178, 365; 9:180–183, 232, 284, 440, 518; 11:200, 206, 1375, 1452; 11R:189. *Proposed:* keep, as *exponential weight* with its exponent named.
3. **Fourier weights `h_l`.** With the weighted Hilbert norms built from them. *Basis:* R. *Where:* 7:598–761, 880–926 (about 20). *Proposed:* keep.
4. **Source weight `ω_i`.** "For positive weights `ω_i`, put `‖a‖_ω = Σ_S |a_S| ∏_{i∈S} ω_i` … The weights rescale source variables; they are not probabilities" (11:43–49). *Basis:* D (11:43–49). *Where:* ch. 11 (about 20; 11:43–49, 194–198, 496, 941, 956, 1558, 2135); 12:244–250; 13sb:73–76; 14lc:60–63; ch. 17–18. *Proposed:* *weights `ω_i`*.
5. **Probability or averaging weights.** The weights `λ(U,α)` of the random index, now called "the probability weight of `α`" (4:231); allocation weights (6:71); the probability weight of an orientation (6:1367, 1428); convolution weights (4:417). *Basis:* R. *Where:* 4:417; 6:71, 1367, 1428; 8:54; 10:468; 11:563, 602; 11R:113, 362. *Proposed:* *probability weights*; *averaging weights*.
6. **Numerical coefficients and density factors.** "The weights of the components" (6:601), "spatial derivative weights" (10:608), "the derivative-weight" (11:1073), non-holomorphic norm weights (5:903); formerly also "bubble weights" (7:306, now "bubble coefficients"), "fourth-difference weights" (9:356, now "fourth-difference coefficients"), "nonquadratic local weights" (9:265, now "nonquadratic local factors") and the spatial weight of 10:79 and 11:351 (now "spatial exponent(s)"). *Basis:* R. *Where:* 5:903; 6:601; 10:608; 11:1073. *Proposed:* *coefficients*; *factors*.
7. **"Encoding weights".** The factors `e^{−δℓ(γ)}` of the Hilbert encoding of the path coefficients, in which the coefficient space has the norm `(Σ_γ e^{2δℓ(γ)}|c(γ)|²)^{1/2}`; their "summability on that dictionary" is the condition `Σ_γ e^{−2(δ−w)ℓ(γ)} < ∞` under which the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality turns this `ℓ²` bound into the weighted `ℓ¹` bound at a width `w < δ`. See *Hilbert encoding*. Since 25 November 2026 the words are gone and the condition is written out at 10:385. *Basis:* S (10:384–385 gave no definition). *Where:* formerly 10:385. *Proposed:* *the weights `e^{−(δ−w)ℓ(γ)}`*, with the condition written out.
   *Source:* Martin existence/path-attachment-producer.tex:852–863 ("give its real coefficient space the Hilbert norm `‖c‖_H = Z(Σ_a e^{2δ|a|}|c_a|²)^{1/2}`, `Z = (Σ_a e^{−2(δ−s)|a|})^{1/2} < ∞` … Cauchy–Schwarz gives `Σ_a e^{s|a|}|c_a| ≤ ‖c‖_H`"); existence/background-path-convergence.tex:42–50 ("for the fixed encoding width `w_{m,q}`, use the norm `𝔫_{m,q}(C) = Σ_{a,ν} e^{−(w_{m,q}−v_m)ℓ(a)}|C(a,ν)|`, `w_{m,q} > v_m` … All weights are strictly positive").
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes with the chapter. Sense 1 no longer uses the word: the text says "scaling dimension" throughout; chapters 4–6 have senses 2, 5 and 6; chapter 7 adds sense 3; chapters 10–18 are dominated by sense 4, whose definition for all later chapters is 11:43–49.
*See also:* weight conversion; weight restoration; width; uniform mass.

#### window
*Now:* partly replaced by *interval of scales* (sense 2: 10:188, 192; 17w:2, 37, 43, 49, 102, 107, 124; 17m:426), *compact set (of separated configurations)* (sense 3: 14:177, 202, 231, 242; 14lc:6, 99; 17:140; "compact configuration set", 11:2083, 2154), *interval of radii* (sense 4: 17:129, 131, 146; 17w:6) and *averaging length* (sense 5, 17m:473); remains in sense 1 (as proposed), in sense 2 in chapters 11 and 11R (11:1468, 1681, 1800, 1970, 2096–2097; 11R:216, 219, 223, 299; 14lc:23) and in the display 17w:53–56, and in sense 5 at 11:1731.
